components.name: A2UI Renderer
components.description: Renders agent-emitted A2UI (v0.9) with Styloviz components: the basic catalog and a dashboard catalog, JSON-Pointer data binding written back as the user edits, catalog functions for validation and formatting, and actions sent back to the agent. Nothing the agent streams ever executes.
whenToUse: An agent that should answer with a form, a card or a small dashboard instead of paragraphs describing one.
Any A2UI-speaking agent (ADK, LangGraph, CopilotKit…) whose output an Angular app must show in its own design system.
For free-form agent text, sv-streaming-markdown is lighter; for tool results the agent did not design, sv-tool-call-card.

examples.title: Register catalogs once
Stream JSON Lines into a store
A catalog of your own

customization: `[messages]` (applied incrementally as the array grows) or `[store]` from `createSvA2uiStore()` for JSON Lines (`processJsonl` / `flush`).
`provideSvA2ui({ catalogs, functions, actionHandler, openUrl })` app-wide; `SV_A2UI_BASIC_CATALOG` is always on, `SV_A2UI_STYLOVIZ_CATALOG` adds Badge, Alert, Stat, Progress and Rating.
Custom catalog components take one input, `ctx: SvA2uiContext`, and read props through it — literals, bindings (relative inside templates) and function calls resolved for them.
`headingOffset` (default 1: an agent's h1 renders as an h2), `locale` for the formatting functions, `surfaceId` to pick one of several surfaces.
accessibility: The surface is a named region ("Interface from Concierge"), so a screen reader can tell where the agent's interface begins and ends inside the page.

Every component is a kit component with its own keyboard model and labels — the A2UI TextField is sv-input-field, ChoicePicker a radio group, checkbox set or pressed chips, Tabs sv-tabs, Modal sv-modal with its focus trap.
An icon-only Button takes its name from the component's accessibility.label, else the icon's name; an Image is decorative unless the agent describes it.
Heading levels move down by headingOffset so the agent's title does not compete with the page's own h1.
Validation messages appear only after the user has changed a field; a disabled button stays focusable through sv-button's own handling.
variants: A Form the Agent Could Not Have Guessed
The Styloviz Catalog — Stats, Alerts and Badges

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while waiting for the agent's first surface.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: The stream failed. Use `toSvDataError()` from `@styloviz/core` to normalise an `HttpErrorResponse`.

inputs.name: messages
inputs.description: Parsed A2UI messages, in order. Appending re-renders only what the new messages change; replacing the array with one that does not start with the previous messages starts over. Ignored while `store` is set.

inputs.name: store
inputs.description: A host-owned store from `createSvA2uiStore()` — push a JSON Lines stream into it with `processJsonl()`, share it between renderers, or read its `issues()`. Takes precedence over `messages`.

inputs.name: surfaceId
inputs.description: The surface to draw. `null` draws the newest one.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale for the catalog's number, currency, date and plural functions.

inputs.name: headingOffset
inputs.description: How far an agent's heading levels move down: at `1`, its `h1` renders as an `<h2>`, because inside an app page the agent's title is not the page's.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name for the surface. Falls back to the agent's display name.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The host should re-open the stream.

outputs.name: action
outputs.description: A component's `event` action fired — the client message to send to the agent.

outputs.name: issue
outputs.description: Something in the stream could not be used. For the developer console; the user sees a notice in place.

components.name: Accordion
components.description: Default, flush, separated and filled styles, single- or multi-expand, icon placements, badges & subtitles and disabled items. Sizes (sm / md / lg), multi-expand, CSS-grid animation and keyboard navigation are free; the separated card style is in the Pro package.
whenToUse: Job: disclosure — owns visibility of its panels in place and never navigates, so back should do nothing (compare all seven in the “Choosing a navigation pattern” guide under Guides).
Condensing long content into expandable sections (FAQs, settings, details).
You want to reduce scroll length while keeping everything reachable.
For switching between mutually exclusive views, use Tabs.

examples.title: Filterable FAQ — a search field bound to searchQuery
examples.code:
<label for="faq-search">Search the FAQ</label>
<input id="faq-search" type="search" [value]="query()" (input)="query.set($any($event.target).value)" />

<!-- Matching sections open and the hits are marked; clearing the query restores
     what the reader had open. faq.matchedIds() gives the count for a summary. -->
<sv-accordion #faq [items]="items" [searchQuery]="query()" />

examples.title: Expand all / collapse all and print
examples.code:
<button type="button" (click)="faq.expandAll()">Expand all</button>
<button type="button" (click)="faq.collapseAll()">Collapse all</button>

<!-- expandAll() needs expandMode="multi". Printing reveals every enabled panel
     and restores the reader's open set afterwards; [expandOnPrint]="false" keeps
     collapsed panels off paper (a quiz answer). -->
<sv-accordion #faq [items]="items" expandMode="multi" [expandOnPrint]="true" />

customization: Three sizes: sm / md / lg.
Single- or multi-expand via `expandMode`.
Flush and filled styles; the separated card style is Pro (`sv-accordion-pro`).
Badges, subtitles and icon placement.
expandAll() / collapseAll() for an "Expand all" control (expandAll needs expandMode="multi").
A filterable FAQ: bind a search field to searchQuery and read matchedIds() for the count.
accessibility: Headers are native buttons with aria-expanded; panels linked via aria-controls.
Keyboard: Enter/Space toggles, ↑↓/Home/End move focus between headers.

Collapsed panels are out of the tab order and the accessibility tree: hidden="until-found" where the browser supports it (so Ctrl+F still finds their text and opens the panel), inert where it does not.

Print and find-in-page contract: printing reveals every enabled panel and restores the reader's own open set afterwards (expandOnPrint, on by default); a find-in-page hit opens its panel; disabled panels stay closed in both.
searchQuery announces how many sections matched through the shared live region, so a search field beside it needs no live region of its own.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: Array of panel definitions.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Visual style.

inputs.name: expandMode
inputs.description: Whether one or many panels can be open at once.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Padding / font scale.

inputs.name: iconPosition
inputs.description: Which side the chevron appears on.

inputs.name: customIcon
inputs.description: Icon-library NAME used as the expand/collapse indicator instead of the default chevron (e.g. `'plus'`). Leave empty to use the built-in chevron. When only this is set the glyph rotates 180° on open (good for arrows). Was `customIconPath`, which took a raw `<path d="…">`.

inputs.name: customIconOpen
inputs.description: Optional alternate icon-library NAME shown when the panel is **open**. Set this alongside `customIcon` for a true swap (e.g. plus → minus). When set, rotation is disabled — the glyphs switch instead. Was `customIconOpenPath`.

inputs.name: customClass
inputs.description: Extra CSS classes applied to the root wrapper.

inputs.name: headingLevel
inputs.description: Heading level of the element wrapped around each panel header — `1`–`6`, so the panels sit correctly in the page outline and can be reached by heading navigation. A value outside `1`–`6` is clamped, with one dev warning.

inputs.name: findInPage
inputs.description: Let browser find-in-page (`Ctrl+F`) reach the text inside COLLAPSED panels, by marking them `hidden="until-found"` where the browser supports it. The browser expands the panel it matched and the open state follows. Turn it off for content that is meant to stay hidden until asked for — a quiz answer, a spoiler. Disabled panels are never findable.

inputs.name: expandOnPrint
inputs.description: Expand every enabled panel while the page is printed, and restore the reader's own open set afterwards. Turn it off for content that must stay hidden on paper (a quiz answer).

inputs.name: searchQuery
inputs.description: Reveal and highlight the panels whose title, subtitle or body contains this text. The reveal is transient: clearing the query returns every panel to the state the user left it in, and nothing is written to `openIds` or to the URL. Matching is case-insensitive substring.

inputs.name: urlKey
inputs.description: Put the open sections in the URL under this key, so one answer can be linked to and survives a refresh. Needs `provideSvNavLocation()` at the app root; multiple open sections are comma-separated.

inputs.name: openIds
inputs.description: Ids of the currently-open panels (two-way). A `model`, so the open set can be restored as well as observed: `itemToggled` reports one gesture at a time, and `defaultOpen` only ever affects panels this accordion has not seen — so binding this is how a host reopens the sections a user had left open before a route change. A bound value wins over `defaultOpen`. `defaultOpen` is applied to each new `items` array, so sections that arrive from a request can open on arrival — but only to ids this component has not seen before, which is what "default" means: a host that rebuilds its `items` on every change detection cannot reopen a section the user closed, and ids that have gone away are dropped.

outputs.name: itemToggled
outputs.description: Fires whenever a panel is opened or closed. `source` says what did it — `'user'` for a click or key, `'find-in-page'` when the browser revealed the panel itself. A transient reveal (a search query, `reveal()`) does not fire.

outputs.name: unresolved
outputs.description: Emitted when the open set named sections this accordion cannot show. Carries the set as bound, the set after pruning, and whether `openIds` was written back.

outputs.name: openIdsChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `openIds` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(openIds)]`.

components.name: Action Sheet
components.description: The phone's bottom sheet of choices for the thing you just tapped: a WAI-ARIA menu of actions with icons and second lines, destructive and disabled choices, and a separate Cancel. A choice, Cancel, Escape, a tap on the dimmed page and a swipe down all close it, and focus goes back to whatever opened it.
whenToUse: A short list of actions on one thing — a row, a message, a photo — on a phone, where a dropdown menu would be a postage stamp under the thumb.
Confirming one destructive step on mobile, with the choice within thumb reach.
Not for content or forms (use Drawer or Modal), and not for a typed or held confirmation (use Confirm Dialog).

examples.title: From a row's ⋯ button
examples.code:
<button type="button" aria-haspopup="dialog" (click)="open.set(true)" aria-label="More actions for INV-2041">⋯</button>
<sv-action-sheet
  [(open)]="open"
  title="Invoice INV-2041"
  [actions]="[
    { id: 'share', label: 'Share', icon: 'share' },
    { id: 'copy', label: 'Copy link', icon: 'link' },
    { id: 'delete', label: 'Delete invoice', icon: 'trash', destructive: true }
  ]"
  (actionSelect)="run($event.action.id)" />

examples.title: A message, second lines and a disabled choice
examples.code:
<sv-action-sheet [(open)]="open" title="Move 3 conversations"
  description="They keep their labels."
  [actions]="[
    { id: 'inbox', label: 'Inbox', description: 'Where they are now', disabled: true },
    { id: 'archive', label: 'Archive', description: 'Out of the inbox, kept for search' }
  ]" />

examples.title: A sheet only a choice can close
examples.code:
<sv-action-sheet [(open)]="open" title="Leave this workspace?"
  [closeOnBackdrop]="false" [swipeToClose]="false"
  [actions]="[{ id: 'leave', label: 'Leave workspace', destructive: true }]"
  (closed)="log($event)" />

customization: Each action takes `icon` (an icon-library name the app registers), `description` (a second line), `destructive` and `disabled`.
`cancelLabel` renames Cancel ("Keep them"); `showCancel` drops it.
`closeOnBackdrop`, `closeOnEscape`, `swipeToClose` and `closeOnNavigation` each turn one way out off.
Full width on a phone, a 28 rem card from `sm` up; never taller than 85% of the viewport, the list scrolling inside it.
Strings come from the `overlays` labels (`actionSheetName`, `actionSheetCancel`, `actionSheetDestructive`).
accessibility: A modal `role="dialog"` named by its title (or `ariaLabel`) and described by `description`; the page behind it is made inert while it is open.

The choices are a WAI-ARIA `menu` of `menuitem`s with one tab stop: ↑/↓ move and wrap, Home/End jump, a letter jumps to the next choice starting with it, Enter or Space chooses. Focus lands on the first available choice when it opens.
Tab moves between the menu and Cancel and never leaves the sheet. Escape closes it.
Disabled choices stay focusable with `aria-disabled="true"`, as the menu pattern asks.
Every way out — a choice, Cancel, Escape, the scrim, a swipe — returns focus to the opener, or to the nearest thing that survived it.
The swipe is an extra: Cancel, the scrim and Escape are the single-pointer and keyboard ways out (WCAG 2.5.7). Under reduced motion the sheet appears and goes without sliding.
Aria: `@angular/aria` is not a dependency of the kit, so the menu is the kit's own implementation of the WAI-ARIA menu pattern. Moving it onto `@angular/aria` later changes no input or output.
variants: With a Message, Second Lines & a Disabled Choice
States — Long List, Must Choose, No Title

components.name: Address Card + Form
components.description: A saved address — label, default / shipping-billing badges, and edit / remove / set-default actions — plus a companion sv-address-form whose field list comes from the country rather than the template: labels, order and required-ness are all data, so a UK address submits without a county and a Hong Kong one renders no postal code at all. Verification is a six-state enum that never blocks submit, and removing the default address asks where the badge goes next. Cards support a selectable (radio) mode for checkout address pickers.
whenToUse: The account "Addresses" page and the checkout shipping / billing address picker.
You want a consistent address display with default and type badges.
Pair the card (display) with the form (add / edit) for a complete address book.
You ship outside the United States. The form asks for what the country actually has, so nobody has to invent a county or a postal code to get past validation.
You verify addresses against a third-party service and need "we could not reach it" to be a different state from "this is wrong".

examples.title: Deleting one, and a delete that fails
Removing the default — choose where the badge goes
Your own countries — a schema is data
A correction offered as a one-press fill

customization: Label, default badge and shipping / billing kind badge on the card.
Toggle edit / remove / set-default actions individually.
Selectable radio mode with a stretched click target and check indicator.

`schemas`: each entry declares its own field list, labels, order, required-ness, autofill token, input mode and — where the subdivisions are a closed set — a dropdown of options. Twelve are built in as `DEFAULT_ADDRESS_SCHEMAS`, chosen to cover every shape rather than to be a world list.
Form wording: `countryLabel`, `title`, `submitLabel`, `cancelLabel`, and optional label / default-toggle / cancel.
Verification wording is yours: pass `message` for an already-translated sentence, or leave it out for the built-in one per status.
accessibility: Selectable cards expose role="radio" + aria-checked with a full-card click target.
The address renders in a semantic <address> element; action buttons have descriptive labels.
Form fields have associated labels, aria-invalid on error, and inline required-field messages; visible focus in light and dark mode.
Every id is instance-scoped, so a checkout showing a shipping and a billing form together does not point both sets of labels at the first form's inputs.
Optional fields say "(optional)" in words. An asterisk on the required ones leaves the reader to guess which convention is in play.

The verification strip is `aria-live="polite"`, not an alert: the verdict arrives while the person is still typing, and an assertive region interrupts them mid-field. `verifying` also sets `aria-busy`.
The remove confirmation is a `role="group"` with its own label, and it follows the trash button in the DOM so it is the next tab stop from the control that opened it.
Removing the default names that fact in the heading, and the successor dropdown has a real `<label>` — the choice is not left to a colour or a badge position.
variants: Deleting an Address, and a Delete That Fails

inputs.name: address
inputs.description: The address to display.

inputs.name: selectable
inputs.description: Radio-style selection mode (checkout address picker).

inputs.name: selected
inputs.description: Selected state (parent-controlled in a radio group).

inputs.name: showActions
inputs.description: Show the action row.

inputs.name: canEdit
inputs.description: Show the edit action.

inputs.name: canRemove
inputs.description: Show the remove action.

inputs.name: canSetDefault
inputs.description: Show the "Set as default" action (hidden when already default).

inputs.name: maskLevel
inputs.description: Print the address in full, or with its identifying parts masked — house and flat numbers, the inward half of the postcode and all but the last four phone digits.

inputs.name: confirmRemove
inputs.description: Ask before deleting. On by default. A saved address is not something the component can put back — see AddressActionEvent — and the trash button is a 32px icon sitting next to an edit button of the same size in a grid of near-identical cards. Turn it off only where the host runs its own confirmation dialog.

inputs.name: saving
inputs.description: True while a write against this address is being sent. Freezes the actions, so a slow round-trip cannot be turned into two deletes.

inputs.name: actionError
inputs.description: The last write failed. Reported on the card, because the card is still here — the host never took it out, and the badge never moved.

inputs.name: defaultCandidates
inputs.description: The other addresses that could take over as default, offered as a choice in the confirmation when THIS address is the default one being removed. The card cannot see the address book, so it cannot pick — but given the candidates it can ask, and the answer rides back on `nextDefaultId`. Left empty, the confirmation says plainly that there will be no default afterwards, which is the outcome the host then has to handle. Ignored entirely when this address is not the default.

outputs.name: addressSelected
outputs.description: Emitted when the card is chosen in selectable mode. Named `addressSelected`, not `select`: `select` is a native DOM event name (@angular-eslint/no-output-native), so an `(select)` binding is ambiguous with the native one, and `selected` is already taken by the input above. Matches the kit's `<thing>Selected` pattern (see search-bar's `suggestionSelected`).

outputs.description: Emitted when the edit action is pressed.

outputs.name: remove
outputs.description: The user confirmed deleting this address. Bind this or nothing happens: the component only asks, it never deletes.

outputs.name: setDefault
outputs.description: "Set as default" was pressed. Persist it — the badge follows `address()`.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Initial value for edit mode; the form resets when it changes.

inputs.name: schemas
inputs.description: The countries offered, and the field list each one implies — so picking Germany does not demand a state Germany has no field for.

inputs.name: countryLabel
inputs.description: Label for the country selector.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Optional form heading.

inputs.name: submitLabel
inputs.description: Submit button label.

inputs.name: cancelLabel
inputs.description: Cancel button label.

inputs.name: showCancel
inputs.description: Show the cancel button.

inputs.name: showLabelField
inputs.description: Show the label field (Home / Work).

inputs.name: showDefaultToggle
inputs.description: Show the "Set as default" toggle.

inputs.name: saving
inputs.description: True while the host is persisting a submitted address.

inputs.name: verification
inputs.description: What is known about this address, from the host's verifier. Advisory only. **No status disables submit**, `unavailable` and `failed` included. A verifier is a third party that times out, rate-limits and 500s, and a form that treats a missing answer as a failing one stops accepting good addresses the moment someone else has a bad afternoon.

outputs.name: save
outputs.description: Emitted with the assembled address on a valid submit, alongside the verification status at that moment — so the host can tell "checked and fine" from "never managed to check".

outputs.name: cancelled
outputs.description: Emitted when cancel is pressed. Named `cancelled` rather than `cancel`, which is a native DOM event name, and to match `cancelLabel` / `showCancel`.

outputs.name: countryChange
outputs.description: The country changed. The field list changed with it, so this is the moment to run a fresh verification rather than re-showing a verdict about the old shape of the address.

outputs.name: suggestionApplied
outputs.description: The verifier's suggestion was accepted and written into the fields.

components.name: Affix / Sticky
components.description: Pin an element while the page scrolls, with the placeholder that stops the jump. Optional container boundary so a pinned sidebar parks at the end of its section instead of floating over the footer.
whenToUse: Keeping a toolbar, filter bar or table of contents in view while a long page scrolls.
You need the pinned element to stop at the end of a section rather than travel the whole page.
If `position: sticky` alone does what you need, use it — this exists for the cases it cannot express (a container boundary, a measured placeholder, a mode you want to react to).
components.usage:
<!-- The affix reads scroll from the host: forward the scroll root (here, the window). -->
<sv-affix #affix [offsetTop]="16" (window:scroll)="affix.onWindowScroll($event)">
  <nav>…</nav>
</sv-affix>

examples.title: Window scroll root
examples.description: The affix does not listen to scroll itself: the host names the scroll root. For the page, forward the window scroll event.

examples.title: Shrink-on-scroll header
examples.description: The header compacts once pinned; holdRestingHeight keeps the placeholder at its in-flow height so the page below never moves while it animates.

examples.title: Detect a transformed ancestor
examples.description: A transform, filter, perspective, backdrop-filter, will-change, contain, content-visibility, preserve-3d or container-type on any ancestor makes it the containing block for position: fixed. The affix reports it (and warns once in dev mode) instead of silently pinning to the wrong box.
examples.code:
<sv-affix (containingBlockChange)="cb = $event">…</sv-affix>
<!-- cb?.element is the ancestor to fix; the placeholder also carries data-sv-containing-block="ancestor" -->

customization: Gap from the viewport top via `offsetTop`.
Stop at the bottom of any element with `container`.
Turn pinning off entirely with `disabled`, e.g. below a breakpoint.
`affixChange` reports the mode — static, fixed or docked — and only when it actually changes.

Measurement: the pinned content's height is observed automatically (`svElementSize`, at most once per frame), so content that grows or shrinks while pinned — or was hidden at init and is revealed — keeps the placeholder in step and re-reads the anchor with no host code. The SCROLL position is manual: the host calls `measure(scrollTop)` from its scroll root (or binds `onWindowScroll`). Until the first `measure()`, and while the content has no box, the element stays in flow.

Shrink-on-scroll strategy: the pin threshold is measured from the placeholder, never the content, so a header that changes height cannot move its own threshold or re-pin; height changes arrive through the observer only, never through a per-scroll read. By default the placeholder follows the live height; `holdRestingHeight` freezes it at the in-flow height while pinned.

Scroll roots and containing blocks: `position: fixed` pins to the VIEWPORT, and `offsetTop` is measured from the viewport top. Supported roots: the document (forward `window:scroll` to `onWindowScroll`, which reads the event's own `defaultView`, so it also works inside an iframe for that iframe's window) and a scroll container that starts at the viewport top, such as an app-shell main region (call `measure(el.scrollTop)`). For a scroll panel lower on the page, add its top to `offsetTop`. Only the root you feed to `measure()` is tracked; nested scrollers inside it are not. Any ancestor with `transform`, individual `translate`/`rotate`/`scale`, `perspective`, `filter`, `backdrop-filter`, a `will-change` naming one of those, `contain: paint|layout|strict|content`, `content-visibility: auto|hidden`, `transform-style: preserve-3d` or a `container-type` becomes the containing block (a `filter` on `<html>` itself does not): the element is then placed against that box and scrolls with it. The affix checks this each time it pins, exposes it as the `containingBlock` signal and `containingBlockChange` output, marks the placeholder `data-sv-containing-block="ancestor"`, and warns once in dev mode — it cannot fix it, because the property is the host's. `container` must be an element whose bottom edge is the parking line; the docked element is absolutely positioned inside the placeholder. There are no built-in breakpoints: bind `disabled` to your own media query.

Variant axes: there is no appearance input — the look is the projected content's. `offsetTop` and `container` are layout; `disabled`, `holdRestingHeight` and the floating-layer inputs are behavioural modes. Every combination is valid; `disabled` wins over all of them and also removes the placeholder.

Browser limits: without `ResizeObserver` the height is re-read on every `measure()` instead of observed, so a resize with no scroll is picked up on the next scroll. `container-type` and individual transform properties are only detected on engines that report them in computed style. Pinning is `position: fixed`, so it does not follow a pinch-zoomed visual viewport on mobile.

Floating layer (`floatingAnchor`, `floatingOrder`, `collisionOffset`): while pinned, the block registers as an occupied region (usually `'top'`), so floating controls at that edge stack clear of it, and a host banner registered before it pushes it down — `collisionOffset` is added to `offsetTop` and exposed for companions. `null` (default) registers nothing.
accessibility: A placeholder of the measured height holds the element's space, so nothing below it moves when it pins — the jump that makes a page unreadable at exactly the scroll position someone is reading.
The pinned state is described in a visually-hidden read-out, since a purely visual change of position tells assistive tech nothing.
The scroll position is read from the event target rather than a global, so the component works inside an iframe or a server-rendered page.
variants: Pinned — With the Placeholder That Stops the Jump
Bounded — Parked at the End of Its Container
Affix — In Flow, Pinned, Parked & Disabled
Affix — Sticky Table of Contents on a Long Policy

inputs.name: offsetTop
inputs.description: Gap between the viewport top and the pinned element, in px.

inputs.name: container
inputs.description: Stop the element at the bottom of this container. Without a boundary, a pinned sidebar floats over the footer — and, being fixed, over whatever the reader scrolled down to look at.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disable pinning entirely, e.g. below a breakpoint.

inputs.name: holdRestingHeight
inputs.description: Keep the placeholder at the height the content had IN FLOW while it is pinned, instead of following the content's live height. For shrink-on-scroll headers. A header that compacts from 80px to 48px once pinned would otherwise pull everything below it up by 32px mid-scroll. With this on, the page below never moves while the header animates; the pin threshold is measured from the placeholder either way, so a changing header height never moves the threshold and cannot re-pin it.

inputs.name: floatingAnchor
inputs.description: Join the shared floating layer while PINNED, as an occupied region at this anchor — usually `'top'` for a full-width bar, or a corner for a pinned card. Floating controls at that edge then stack clear of it, and regions ranked before it (a host's top banner) push it down through `collisionOffset`, which is added to `offsetTop`. `null` registers nothing and leaves the offset at 0.

inputs.name: floatingOrder
inputs.description: Rank in the floating layer; lower sits nearer the edge.

outputs.name: affixChange
outputs.description: Emitted whenever the mode changes.

outputs.name: containingBlockChange
outputs.description: Emitted when an ancestor turns out to be the containing block for `position: fixed` — a `transform`, `filter`, `perspective`, `backdrop-filter`, `will-change`, `contain`, `content-visibility`, `transform-style: preserve-3d` or `container-type` on any ancestor — so the pinned element is positioned against that ancestor and scrolls away with it. Checked each time the element pins; `null` once the viewport is the containing block again.

components.name: Agent Approval
components.description: Human-in-the-loop gate for an action an agent proposes but has not taken. Editable arguments, a risk level that arms destructive actions, a diff of what will change, a cost estimate, an expiry countdown and always-allow memory. Four variants — inline, modal, inbox queue and policy record.
whenToUse: Gating any action an agent takes that spends money, emails a customer, or writes to production.
Giving an operator a chance to correct a nearly-right action instead of denying and re-prompting.
Collecting an audit trail of who approved what, with what arguments, and under which policy.
Queuing approvals for agents that run unattended, so nothing silently blocks or silently proceeds.

examples.title: Read the corrected arguments
examples.description: The decision carries the operator’s edits. Reading request.args instead discards them.

examples.title: A queue that piled up
examples.description: Agents run unattended, so approvals arrive while nobody is looking.

examples.title: Blocking the irreversible
examples.description: Composes over sv-modal — backdrop dismissal off, focus trapped, closes on decision.

examples.title: Risk that follows the edit
examples.description: An editable argument can turn a low-risk call into a destructive one. riskFor reclassifies it.
examples.code:
<sv-agent-approval [request]="req" [riskFor]="riskOf" (decided)="onDecision($event)" />

// Pure and cheap — it runs over the visible requests on every edit.
riskOf: AgentApprovalRiskFn = (req, args) =>
  req.tool === 'delete_rows' && PROD_TABLES.has(args['table']) ? 'critical' : 'low';

examples.title: Require a reason
examples.description: reasonRequired is never (default), high-risk (high or critical, judged on the edited arguments) or always. Approve or Deny with the field empty is refused, focused and announced; the trimmed reason rides in decided and the receipt. Send a denial’s reason back to the agent so it re-plans instead of retrying.
examples.code:
<sv-agent-approval [request]="req" reasonRequired="high-risk" (decided)="onDecision($event)" />

onDecision(e: AgentApprovalResult): void {
  if (e.decision === 'deny') this.agent.reprompt(e.request.id, e.reason);   // e.reason: string | null
  else this.runTool(e.request.tool, e.args);
}

examples.title: Remembering a safe tool
examples.description: Always-allow reports the tool so a policy layer can persist it. Withheld above medium risk.

customization: `(receipt)` is the immutable record of a decision, emitted beside `(decided)`: who (`[decidedBy]` — the component has no idea who is logged in, so it is `null` rather than a guess), when, through which variant, the risk class it was approved under, the policy that routed it, and **the arguments as executed**. Frozen, arguments included: 'immutable' is a property of the object rather than a promise in a doc comment. `decided` is the instruction; this is what happened.

`inline`, `modal` and `inbox` are three shapes for **one act**, and the receipt is identical apart from `through` — an audit trail whose contents depend on which shape the operator happened to be looking at cannot be reconciled with anything. One function (`svApprovalReceipt`) builds it for every variant, which is what keeps that true.

`policySource` on a request answers 'why am I being asked?' in the dialog, in every variant. An operator who cannot tell a genuine escalation from a misconfigured threshold learns to approve everything, and the rule’s own name is the only thing that tells them apart.

The expiry countdown is a **courtesy, never the enforcement point** — it runs on `Date.now()` in the operator’s browser, which a skewed laptop clock, a slept tab or a deliberately-set system time all move. The component says so beside the timer and folds it into the timer’s `aria-label`. A host that treats 'the button went grey' as authorization having lapsed has put its access control in the client, where anybody can win an argument with it.

Redaction, from the pack-wide policy: argument values matching `provideSvAiPrivacy({ patterns })` are masked on screen — and a masked argument becomes READ-ONLY, because an input showing `[API KEY]` submits `[API KEY]`, so the operator would edit the mask and approve it as the real argument. Where the policy sets `reveal: true`, a Reveal control restores both the value and the input, and hides again. The decision receipt and the risk classifier always see the REAL arguments.
`variant` chooses the shape: `inline` in a thread, `modal` for the irreversible, `inbox` for a queue, `policy` for a read-only record of an auto-approval.
`approveLabel` and `denyLabel` carry domain wording — "Issue refund" reads better than "Approve".
`showChanges` and `showCost` hide sections a given request does not need.
`allowRemember` turns always-allow off globally; it is withheld automatically above medium risk regardless.

`riskFor` owns the risk classification. Editing an argument re-runs it, and a class change re-arms the confirmation, emits `riskReclassified`, and lands in `decided.risk` — the class approved under, not the one requested.
Each argument’s `description` renders as help text under the field, and `policyReason` explains an auto-approval.
The `RISK_ORDER`, `msRemaining`, `isExpired` and `formatCountdown` helpers are exported for sorting or thresholding a queue yourself.
accessibility: The countdown is `role="timer"` with a spoken label, so remaining time is available without watching it tick.
Arming a high-risk action surfaces a `role="alert"` explaining that it cannot be undone, before the confirm is possible.
Editable arguments are real `input` elements with `aria-label`, reachable and correctable by keyboard.
The inbox pending count is `role="status"`, so a queue that grows while the operator is elsewhere is announced.
Status is never colour-only — approved, denied and expired each carry a distinct glyph and a text label.
The modal variant inherits sv-modal’s focus trap, Escape handling and scroll lock rather than reimplementing them.
variants: Risk — Arming, and What Cannot Be Remembered
Policy — What Went Through On Its Own

inputs.name: request
inputs.description: The action awaiting a decision. Ignored when `requests` is non-empty. The expiry countdown is a courtesy, never the enforcement point. It runs on `Date.now()` in the operator's browser — a skewed laptop clock, a tab that slept or a deliberately-set system time all move it. Revalidate on the server, where the action runs: that the request has not expired, that it is still pending, and that the decider is authorized to approve it. A host that treats "the button went grey" as authorization having lapsed has put its access control in the client.

inputs.name: requests
inputs.description: A queue of requests, for the `inbox` variant. Takes precedence.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP 47 locale for dates and numbers.

inputs.name: riskFor
inputs.description: Reclassify a request's risk from its arguments as the operator edits them. Without this, `request.risk` is fixed at the moment the agent asked, and the whole point of the component is that the operator can change the call. A reviewer can be shown `delete_rows(table: 'staging')` chipped low risk, change `table` to `users`, and approve a destructive call on one click — the badge, the always-allow offer and the two-step arm all still describe the call that was requested rather than the one about to run. Supply it and every one of those follows the edited arguments. Only the host knows which values are dangerous, so nothing is inferred here.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Presentation preset.

inputs.name: open
inputs.description: Two-way open state for the `modal` variant.

inputs.name: allowRemember
inputs.description: Offer "always allow this tool". Never offered above medium risk.

inputs.name: showChanges
inputs.description: Show the before/after diff when the request carries one.

inputs.name: showCost
inputs.description: Show the cost estimate when the request carries one.

inputs.name: approveLabel
inputs.description: Label on the approve button.

inputs.name: denyLabel
inputs.description: Label on the deny button.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible label for the gate.

inputs.name: deciding
inputs.description: True while the decision is being sent. Both buttons lock — approving twice because the first click looked like it did nothing is exactly the mistake an approval dialog must not allow.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Failure recording the decision. Shown in place of nothing else changing, so the user can see the request did not land and decide again.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the `inbox` queue is being fetched. While it is true the inbox shows a loading state rather than "Nothing awaiting approval". On an approvals queue, nothing to do, not known yet and *something is waiting and you cannot see it* are three different situations, and only the last one is urgent.

inputs.name: loadError
inputs.description: Failure **loading** the queue, as opposed to `error`, which is a failure recording a decision. Both can be live at once — a decision can fail and a later refetch can fail too — so they are separate inputs rather than one.

inputs.name: decidedBy
inputs.description: Who is deciding, for the receipt. The component has no idea who is logged in, and a receipt that attributed a decision to "operator" would be worse than one admitting it does not know — so leave this unset and `decidedBy` is `null`.

inputs.name: reasonRequired
inputs.description: When the operator must write a reason before approving or denying: `'never'`, `'high-risk'` (a `high` or `critical` call, judged on the arguments as edited) or `'always'`. While it applies, the card shows a required reason field, and Approve / Deny with it empty refuses — the field is marked invalid, focused and the refusal announced — rather than emitting. The trimmed reason rides in `decided` and the receipt (`reason`); send a denial's reason back to the agent so it re-plans instead of retrying.

outputs.name: retryLoad
outputs.description: The user asked to reload the queue after a load failure.

outputs.name: decided
outputs.description: The operator decided. Read `args` from the payload, not from the request.

outputs.name: argEdited
outputs.description: An editable argument changed.

outputs.name: riskReclassified
outputs.description: An edit moved a request into a different risk class, per `riskFor`. Worth logging: it is the operator turning one call into another, and the audit trail is thinner without it.

outputs.name: alwaysAllowChanged
outputs.description: Always-allow was ticked or unticked.

outputs.name: expired
outputs.description: The countdown reached zero without a decision.

outputs.name: receipt
outputs.description: The immutable record of a decision, for the host's audit log. Separate from `decided`, which is the instruction. `decided` says what to do; this says what happened, frozen, with who and when and through which surface. A host that logged the instruction would be logging a request, not a decision.

outputs.name: openChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `open` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(open)]`.

components.name: Agent Task Queue
components.description: Inbox for work an agent is doing on its own: queued, running, done. Progress derived from a plan that checks itself off, an ETA extrapolated from observed pace, and cancel or retry per task. Four variants — inbox, compact, grouped and detail.
whenToUse: Showing work an agent is doing unattended, where the user needs to know what is running and how far along it is.
Surfacing a long-running job behind a header bell or sidebar rail, in the compact variant.
Debugging a run: the plan shows what the agent intended, the step notes show what it actually found.
Giving an operator a way to stop work that is going wrong, and restart work that failed.

examples.title: Let the plan be the progress
examples.description: Omit progress and give a plan — the steps that complete become the percentage.

examples.title: Compact, for a header popover
examples.description: One row per task when the only question is whether anything is still running.

examples.title: Triage a backlog
examples.description: Sections ordered by urgency, empty ones omitted.

examples.title: Rewind to a step
examples.description: Run a stopped task again from a finished step; the host checks the request is current and applies it.
examples.code:
<sv-agent-task-queue [tasks]="tasks()" [rewindable]="true" (rewind)="onRewind($event)" />

onRewind(e: AgentTaskRewind): void {
  const current = this.tasks().find(t => t.id === e.task.id);
  if (svTaskRewindIsStale(e, current)) return;
  this.tasks.update(list => list.map(t => t.id === e.task.id ? svTaskRewind(t, e.step.id) : t));
  this.runtime.resumeFrom(e.task.id, e.step.id);
}

examples.title: Read-only queue
examples.description: Keeps the information, removes cancel and retry.

customization: `rewindable` (off by default, needs `actionable`) puts a Rewind button on each finished step of a paused, done, failed or cancelled task that has a later step to undo (`svTaskCanRewindTo`). It asks inline first — "Run again from here? N later steps will be reset." — then emits `rewind` (`AgentTaskRewind`: `{ task, step, reset, observedStatus, at }`). `svTaskRewind(task, stepId)` returns the task with later steps pending and the task paused.
`variant` chooses the shape: `inbox` when the queue is the page, `compact` for a rail, `grouped` for triage, `detail` for one run.
`showPlan`, `showEta` and `showStats` drop the checklist, the estimate and the roll-up independently.
`actionable` false, or `cancellable: false` on a single task, removes the interrupt controls.
`priority` tints a task title so a high-priority item reads differently in a long list.

The `planProgress`, `taskProgress`, `estimateRemainingMs`, `elapsedMs`, `formatDuration` and `queueStats` helpers are exported, so a header badge or notification can use the same maths as the component.

A scale ceiling: `[maxTasks]` (200) bounds the list, windowed from the TOP because a queue is ordered by what happens next — the opposite direction from a transcript. The grouped variant windows before grouping, so sections cannot render the whole queue by splitting it up, and the summary line keeps counting the whole backlog: "12 running, 940 queued" is the number an operator acts on. `0` turns it off.

The clock stops when nobody is looking: the internal tick pauses while the tab is hidden (`createVisibilityPause`) and while the queue's own element is scrolled out of view (`createOffscreenPause`). It catches up the instant it resumes, so a reader who comes back sees the right elapsed time rather than an old one for a further second. With no `IntersectionObserver` it keeps ticking — the fallback is never a frozen queue.

`(action)` carries `observedStatus` and `at` as well as the verb: a cancel is the conditional instruction "stop this, which I was looking at as running". Compare with `svTaskActionIsStale(action, current)` and, when it is stale, treat the request as a **no-op** and push the true status back — `svTaskActionNoopMessage()` is the sentence for it. A 409 at a reader who pressed a button the queue offered them is the failure this avoids.
`pendingTaskIds` disables a task's controls while its action is in flight, which is the optimistic half: the row shows the request has been made without claiming it succeeded.
accessibility: Rewind is a separate button beside the step ("Rewind to step: {label}"); its inline confirm takes focus, Escape or Keep returns it, and the rewind is announced.
Each progress bar is `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow` and a label naming its task, so progress is available without seeing the fill.
A running task's status chip is `role="status"`, so a task starting or finishing while the operator is elsewhere is announced.
Step state is carried in visually-hidden text ("— done", "— active", "— skipped") as well as by colour, icon and strikethrough.
The plan is an ordered list labelled with its task, and its expand control is a real `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls` disclosure.
Group headings separate the label from the count with hidden text, so a screen reader reads "Running — 1 tasks" rather than "Running1".
Cancel and retry carry explicit labels naming the task, since the visible text is only the verb.
variants: Inbox — The Plan Is the Progress Bar
Compact — For a Sidebar or Popover
Rewind — Run Again From a Step

The window keeps the host's order from the top, and here that is the right end: a queue is ordered by what happens NEXT, so the rows worth rendering are the first ones.
