components.name: Barcode (1D)
components.description: Code 128, EAN-13 and EAN-8 rendered as SVG from a real encoder: mod-103 and mod-10 check characters computed rather than trusted, EAN-13's leading digit carried in the left-half parity, subset-C packing so a long serial fits the label, spec quiet zones, and a module width snapped to whole device pixels. Refuses to draw what cannot scan, and says why.
whenToUse: Printing a label, packing slip, shelf tag or ticket that a handheld scanner has to read.
You have a GTIN, SKU or serial and need the symbol drawn correctly, including the check digit.
For a 2D code holding a URL or a payload, use the QR Code instead.

examples.title: Code 128 with a long serial
examples.description: Subset C packs two digits into one symbol character, so the printed symbol is about half as wide as a subset-B-only encoder would produce.

examples.title: Handle a refusal
examples.description: A value that cannot be encoded renders the reason instead of a picture. Listen for it if the value comes from user input.

examples.title: Printing: pin the X-dimension, not the pixels
examples.description: A barcode is correct in modules and scannable in millimetres. The X-dimension — the width of one module on paper — is what ISO/IEC 15416 and GS1 specify, and CSS pixels do not survive a print dialog: "shrink to fit" rescales the symbol and the X-dimension goes with it. printModuleWidthMm pins the printed width so it measures the same whatever the dialog decides. The component also carries its own @media print block for the two other ways print destroys a correct symbol — stripped backgrounds (the white is half the contrast a scanner measures, and the quiet zone is nothing but background) and a page break through the middle.
examples.code:
<!-- EAN-13 at 100% magnification: the nominal 0.33 mm module. -->
<sv-barcode-1d value="4006381333931" symbology="ean13" [printModuleWidthMm]="0.33" />

examples.title: When the symbol is correct and too small to read
examples.description: Every other check here is arithmetic on modules; this is the one failure that survives all of it. A container that squeezes the module, or a print setting below the floor, produces bars in perfect proportion that will not scan — and the component says so in place and emits the measurements, so a label pipeline can refuse the job rather than print a roll of stickers. Worth knowing why it is reachable at all: the pixel-snap floors at one DEVICE pixel, which at dpr 1 is 0.2646 mm — a hair above EAN's 0.264 mm floor — but at dpr 2 it is half that. A finer screen lets the symbol get physically smaller, so the better display is the one that produces the unscannable label.

customization: Three symbologies: `code128`, `ean13`, `ean8`.
Three variants: `labelled` (bars + human-readable line), `bare`, and `inspect` (module count, quiet zones, check character, snapped width and the subset-C saving).
`requestedModuleWidth` + `devicePixelRatio` (snapped to whole device pixels; `widthAdjusted` says when it moved), `barHeight`, and `showQuietZone` to make the invisible margin visible.
`encodeError` reports why a value could not be encoded; `loading` / `error` / `retry` for the async shells.

`printModuleWidthMm` pins the printed X-dimension in millimetres, and the component's own `@media print` block forces `print-color-adjust: exact`, avoids a page break through the symbol, and hides the `inspect` report (a development aid, not part of the label).

`scanSizeWarning` emits `{ xMm, widthMm, heightMm, magnification, minXMm, belowMinimum }` whenever the symbol falls under its symbology's floor. `svScanSize()` and `SV_BARCODE_MIN_X_MM` are exported for a pipeline that wants to check before rendering.
accessibility: The symbol carries an accessible name naming the symbology, the encoded value and the check character — a scanner reads the bars, a person reads the label, and a screen reader gets both.
A refusal is rendered as text stating what is wrong (e.g. "EAN-13 needs 12 digits; this has 11"), not as an empty box.
EAN guard bars extend below the digit row, which is how a human recognises the symbol's start, end and midpoint.
A symbol too small to scan renders a `role="status"` warning stating the measurement and the floor, so the problem is legible rather than left to a failed scan in a warehouse.
variants: EAN-13 — The Check Digit Is Computed, Not Trusted
Code 128 — Subset C, and Why the Label Fits
Refusing — A Label That Obviously Failed Beats a Mislabelled Shipment
Inspect — The Quiet Zone Is Part of the Symbol
Correct in Modules, Scannable in Millimetres

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the value to encode is being fetched; shows a skeleton in place of the barcode.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Load failure, shown as an error panel in place of the content. Use `toSvDataError()` from `@styloviz/core` to normalize an `HttpErrorResponse`.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Bars with text, bars alone, or bars with the encoder's report.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: What to encode. For EAN, with or without the check digit.

inputs.name: symbology
inputs.description: Barcode standard `value` is encoded in: `'code128'`, `'ean13'` or `'ean8'` (check digit computed).

inputs.name: requestedModuleWidth
inputs.description: Requested width of one module, in CSS px. Requested, not final — see `moduleWidth`. A module narrower than a whole device pixel antialiases, and a scanner reads the antialiasing as different run widths.

inputs.name: devicePixelRatio
inputs.description: Device pixel ratio to snap against.

inputs.name: barHeight
inputs.description: Bar height in px, excluding the human-readable text.

inputs.name: showQuietZone
inputs.description: Draw the quiet zones as a visible margin outline. For the `inspect` view. The quiet zone is invisible by nature, which is exactly why people lay a barcode flush against a border and cannot see what broke it.

inputs.name: printModuleWidthMm
inputs.description: Physical width of one module when printed, in millimetres. `0` leaves the printed size to the browser, which is what an untouched print job does. This is the X-dimension, the quantity ISO/IEC 15416 and GS1 actually specify — and the reason it exists as its own input is that CSS pixels do not survive a print dialog. Pin it and the symbol measures the same on paper whatever "fit to page" decides.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: Emitted when the user presses the error panel's "Try again" button (retryable errors only); the host should re-run the failed load.

outputs.name: encodeError
outputs.description: Emitted whenever the value cannot be encoded, with the reason.

outputs.name: scanSizeWarning
outputs.description: Emitted when the symbol's physical size falls below the floor its symbology may be printed at. Carries the measurements, so a label pipeline can refuse the job rather than print a roll of stickers that will not read.

components.name: Bottom Navigation
components.description: The phone app bar: three to five destinations as real links with an icon and a label, aria-current on the page you are on, 48 px targets, count badges and dots, padded clear of the home indicator with env(safe-area-inset-bottom). Fixed (with its height reserved), sticky in a scroller, or static; hidden from a breakpoint up. The same MenuItem model as the sidebar, and no router dependency.
whenToUse: The primary navigation of a phone layout — a PWA, a mobile web dashboard, a store front — with three to five top-level destinations.
Alongside a desktop sidebar fed the same destinations, hidden from the breakpoint where the sidebar appears.
Not for switching views on one page (use Tabs or a Segmented Control) and not for more than five destinations (put the rest behind a "More" destination or in the sidebar).

examples.title: One model, two renderers
examples.code:
<!-- The same MenuItem[] on a phone and a desktop: the bar hides from md up, the sidebar below it. -->
<sv-sidebar-nav class="hidden md:flex" [menuGroups]="[{ groupLabel: 'App', items: destinations }]" [activeRoute]="router.url" />
<sv-bottom-nav [items]="destinations" [activeRoute]="router.url" hideFrom="md" />

examples.title: Badges and dots
Wired to the Angular router

customization: Three positions: `fixed` (pinned to the viewport, reserving its height in the flow with `reserveSpace`), `sticky` (bottom of its own scroller) and `static`.
`hideFrom` (`sm` · `md` · `lg`) hides it from a breakpoint up.
Badges take `badgeColor` (primary · accent · warning · danger — danger by default) and render as a count pill; `dot` draws an activity dot.
The current item draws the `solid` weight of its icon and the `primary-*` tokens, so a theme that remaps primary recolours it.
Icons are icon-library names the app registers (`provideSvIcons` or `registerSvIcons`); labels come from the `sidebarNav` namespace (`navigation`, `newActivity`, `external`).
accessibility: A `<nav>` landmark named by `ariaLabel` (default "Main navigation"), with a list of real `<a href>` links — Tab moves between them, Enter follows one. No `role="tab"`: a bar that changes pages is navigation, not a tablist.
The current destination carries `aria-current="page"`.
Every link is at least 48 × 48 px (WCAG 2.5.8 asks for 24).
A badge is drawn on the icon but read after the label ("Inbox, 12"); a dot is read as "new activity"; an external destination says it opens in a new tab.
A fixed bar marks itself `data-sv-sticky="page-bottom"`, so the browser keeps a focused control from being scrolled under it (WCAG 2.4.11).
variants: Phone App Bar — Fixed, with Badges
Current Label Only — Sticky in a Scroller
Routed — the Host Owns Where You Are
States — Current, Badges, No Match & External

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: The destinations — three to five. Each `MenuItem` needs `label`, `route` and `icon` (an icon-library name the app has registered); `badge`, `badgeColor`, `dot`, `id` and `external` are honoured.

inputs.name: activeRoute
inputs.description: The path the reader is on, so one destination is marked current. Controlled — a routed host writes `[activeRoute]="router.url"`.

inputs.name: position
inputs.description: Where the bar sits.

inputs.name: hideFrom
inputs.description: Hide the bar from this breakpoint up — the desktop has a sidebar for the same destinations. `null` shows it at every width.

inputs.name: labelVisibility
inputs.description: Show every label, or only the current destination's.

inputs.name: reserveSpace
inputs.description: With `position="fixed"`, render an in-flow spacer of the bar's height, so the end of the page is never hidden behind it.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: The `<nav>` landmark's accessible name. Defaults to the `navigation` label ('Main navigation').

inputs.name: surfaceId
inputs.description: Names this bar in the navigation stream when a page has several.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Per-instance overrides for the package labels.

outputs.name: itemSelected
outputs.description: A destination was picked (a plain click or tap; a modified click opens elsewhere and is not reported).

components.name: Box Plot
components.description: Distribution chart with Tukey 1.5×IQR whiskers, outlier dots, an optional mean marker, raw-samples or server-computed summaries, and a value axis that is deliberately not zero-based. Pure SVG.
whenToUse: Comparing the SHAPE of several distributions — latency by service, price by category.
Spotting outliers and skew that an average hides completely.
For a single distribution with enough samples to show shape, a histogram is clearer.

examples.title: Server-computed summaries
examples.code:
<!-- `count` and `method` are worth supplying: without them the chart cannot
     say how much data the box stands for, or which quartile rule produced it. -->
<sv-box-plot-chart
  [boxes]="[{ label: 'p90', stats: {
    min: 190, q1: 214, median: 236, q3: 262, max: 298,
    mean: 241, outliers: [412], count: 8400, method: 'linear',
  } }]"
  [showMean]="true" />

examples.title: Reconciling with Excel QUARTILE.EXC
examples.code:
<!-- Type 6, as Excel QUARTILE.EXC / Tableau / Minitab. The rule in force is
     printed under the plot either way. -->
<sv-box-plot-chart [boxes]="boxes" quartileMethod="exclusive" />

examples.title: Small-sample threshold
examples.code:
<!-- Boxes under 12 samples get a dashed edge and a sentence under the plot.
     0 turns the check off entirely. -->
<sv-box-plot-chart [boxes]="boxes" [minReliableSamples]="12" />

customization: Vertical or horizontal layout.
Tukey fence multiplier via `iqrFactor`.
Outliers, mean marker and grid each toggleable.
Box thickness via `boxRatio`.

`quartileMethod` picks the sample-quantile definition: `linear` (type 7 — R, NumPy, Excel `QUARTILE`, Sheets) or `exclusive` (type 6 — Excel `QUARTILE.EXC`, Tableau, Minitab, SPSS). They agree on the median and diverge on `q1`/`q3`, most visibly on small samples. Whichever is in force is **printed under the plot** along with the whisker convention: there are at least nine defensible quartile rules, so a chart that keeps its own to itself cannot be reconciled against anything, and a reader holding a different `q3` from their BI tool will trust the tool they already had. A summary supplied through `stats` was computed elsewhere, so the chart says so rather than claiming a rule it never applied — unless the summary declares its own `method`. When supplied summaries disagree, the line reports exactly what each declared, per rule with the boxes named (e.g. "1 linear (C), 2 exclusive (A, B), 1 not stated (D)"), and warns that boxes under different rules are not directly comparable. A supplied `count` or `dropped` that is not a whole number is left out and disclosed rather than printed as `n = NaN`.

`minReliableSamples` (default 5) marks a box with too few samples for its quartiles to describe a distribution: a dashed edge, a sentence under the plot naming which boxes and their n, the caveat in the accessible name, and a note in the data table. Below five, `q1` and `q3` are pure interpolation between two adjacent points and the fences that define an outlier are derived from that interpolation. `0` turns the check off.

A `stats` summary is checked against itself before it is drawn, because it is the one input here with nothing else to cross-check against. Out-of-order figures, or one that cannot be read as a number, mean the box is **not drawn** and is named under the plot with the reason — inverted quartiles would draw at the right size in the wrong place, and a `NaN` coordinate makes an SVG element silently fail to paint, which on screen is identical to a category that had no data. Nonsense extras are gentler: a mean that cannot be read loses its marker, an "outlier" sitting between the whiskers is dropped, and the box itself still renders.

Sample size is drawn on the category axis as `n = …`, and it is the count actually **used**: samples that could not be read are excluded from it and reported separately, so the figure never overstates how much data is behind a box.

Raw-sample cost, measured rather than guessed. Aggregating `values` is dominated by one sort per box and runs inside a single `computed()`, so it re-runs when the `boxes` array identity changes and **not** on hover, focus, resize or a theme flip. On a desktop machine: 12 boxes × 1,000 samples ≈ 3 ms, × 10,000 ≈ 30 ms, × 50,000 ≈ 190 ms, × 100,000 ≈ 460 ms. Treat **250,000 samples in total** as the ceiling for passing raw `values` — that is around the point a recompute stops fitting in a frame on a desktop, and a mid-range phone is several times slower again. Above it, aggregate server-side and pass `stats` with `count` and `method`; the wire cost of shipping the raw array is usually the worse half of the problem anyway.

The value axis is **linear only** — there is no log-scale input, and `axisMin` / `axisMax` are read as linear bounds. A log axis would move the box, the median line and both whiskers independently, so the box would not be the IQR of anything you could measure off the axis, and the 1.5×IQR fences that define an outlier would land in a different place than the ones the summary was computed with. For heavily skewed data, transform the samples before passing them in and say so in the `title` (`Response time (log₁₀ ms)`). A quantile is order-preserving, so the median and any quartile landing on a real sample are the log of the untransformed one; only the interpolated quartiles shift, because the interpolation then happens in log space. The **mean** is the exception and the one to watch: the mean of the logs is a geometric mean, not the log of the arithmetic mean, so `showMean` on transformed samples is answering a different question — turn it off, or state which mean it is.
accessibility: Each box has a slot-sized `role="button"` hit area named with its median, quartiles, range, mean, outlier count and sample size, so the mean and n reach a keyboard, not only the hover tooltip.
The plot is a labelled `role="group"`; Enter/Space emits `boxSelect` and focus emits `boxHover`.

A visually-hidden table lists each distribution with its sample size, five-number summary, mean and the individual outlier **values** — an outlier is drawn as a ring carrying no label at all. The quartile rule is stated in the table's own overview, so the alternative is no more unfalsifiable than the picture.

Anything the chart dropped, repaired or hedged is stated in the rendered output rather than logged: a rejected box, samples that could not be read, and a sample too small to support a quartile. The dashed edge on an unreliable box is never the only cue.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the distributions are being fetched.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Load failure. Use `toSvDataError()` from `@styloviz/core` to normalize an `HttpErrorResponse`.

inputs.name: emptyMessage
inputs.description: Copy for the no-data state.

inputs.name: filtered
inputs.description: True when the emptiness is caused by a filter rather than an empty set.

inputs.name: boxes
inputs.description: Distributions to plot, one box each.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: Layout direction.

inputs.name: iqrFactor
inputs.description: Multiplier on the IQR that sets the outlier fences. `1.5` is Tukey's rule; `3` marks only far outliers. Ignored for boxes that supply `stats`.

inputs.name: quartileMethod
inputs.description: Which sample-quantile definition to compute quartiles with, and the one the chart names under the plot. There are at least nine defensible definitions and they disagree, most visibly on small samples. Unnamed, this chart was unfalsifiable: a reader holding a different `q3` from their own BI tool had no way to tell whether the chart was wrong or merely using another rule, and they will trust the tool they already had. `exclusive` is the rule Excel's `QUARTILE.EXC`, Tableau and Minitab use; `linear` is R, NumPy, Excel `QUARTILE`, Sheets. Ignored for boxes that supply `stats` — those were computed elsewhere, and the chart says so rather than claiming a rule it did not apply.

inputs.name: minReliableSamples
inputs.description: Below this many samples a box is marked as too small for its quartiles to carry much meaning: drawn with a dashed edge, named under the plot, and flagged in its accessible name and in the data table. `0` turns the check off. The default is 5 because below it `q1` and `q3` are pure interpolation between two adjacent points and the IQR fences that define an outlier are derived from that interpolation — the box is a picture of arithmetic rather than of a distribution, and it looks exactly like a box over four thousand samples.

inputs.name: axisMin

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.description: 4 visual variants, 5 separator styles, a sibling-page dropdown switcher, badges, disabled crumbs, collapsible middle crumbs, a loading skeleton, and full keyboard support.
whenToUse: Job: destination links — renders real `<a href>` crumbs to levels of a hierarchy the route already defines (compare all seven in the “Choosing a navigation pattern” guide under Guides).
Showing the user's location within a nested hierarchy and offering a way back up.
Multi-level apps: settings, file systems, category drill-downs.
Use the sibling-page `menu` on a crumb when users need to jump between sibling sections (orgs, branches, workspaces) without leaving the current level.
For switching between sibling views, use Tabs instead.

examples.title: Derived from the route, not hand-passed
Router transitions instead of page loads

customization: Four visual variants: plain, contained, pills, underline.
Five separator styles, including a custom icon from the icon library (`customSeparatorIcon`).
Collapse middle crumbs behind a toggleable ellipsis on overflow, or hide them below the sm breakpoint with `collapseOnMobile`.
Optional leading icons, an automatic home icon via `showHomeIcon`, and per-crumb badges.
Sibling-page dropdown switcher via a crumb's `menu` array.
Label truncation with a tooltip via `truncateLabels`.
Customisable nav landmark label via `ariaLabel`.
Links render through `SvLinkAdapter` from `@styloviz/core` — no dependency on `@angular/router`, so it drops into an app that routes any way at all.
`svTrailFromPath(path, { labels, root, base, titleCase })` derives the trail from a URL path, with no router of its own.

`surfaceId` names this instance in the shared navigation-analytics stream (`provideSvNavTelemetry()`): a crumb or sibling page followed is `jump`, opening a crumb menu or the collapsed middle is `explore`, Escape out of the menu is `escape`. Consent and retention are the sink's; under `retention: 'none'` keys and labels are stripped.
accessibility: Wrapped in a labelled nav landmark (`ariaLabel`).
Current page marked with aria-current.
Disabled crumbs render as non-interactive elements with `aria-disabled`, outside the tab order.
The ellipsis toggle exposes `aria-expanded` and stays focusable in both states, so it can be opened and closed again from the keyboard without losing its place in the tab order.

The dropdown panel is rendered in a `document.body` portal so it always escapes ancestor `overflow`/transform clipping instead of being cut off inside scrollable cards or tables; it repositions on scroll and closes on viewport resize or outside click.

components.name: Bullet Chart
components.description: Featured measure against a comparative target and qualitative bands, horizontal or vertical, on a shared or per-row scale. Pure SVG.
whenToUse: A KPI that is only meaningful against a target — actual vs plan, SLA vs commitment.
A dense scorecard where one row per metric beats one gauge per metric.
For a single headline number with no target, use a Stat Card or a Gauge.

examples.title: Bands and targets
examples.code:
<sv-bullet-chart
  [rows]="[
    { label: 'Revenue', value: 268, target: 250, unit: 'k',
      ranges: [{ to: 150, label: 'Poor' }, { to: 225, label: 'Satisfactory' }, { to: 300, label: 'Good' }] }
  ]"
  title="Q3 performance against plan" />

examples.title: A measure the track cannot hold
examples.code:
<!-- clamp (default): the bar sits at the baseline, the track is
     outlined dashed, and -40 is still printed beside it.
     reject: refuse the set and show the error state instead. -->
<sv-bullet-chart
  [rows]="[{ label: 'Net churn', value: -40, max: 100 }]"
  valuePolicy="clamp" />

customization: Horizontal or vertical layout.
Per-row scales by default; opt into a shared or chart-wide one.
Per-row band colours, measure colour and unit suffix.
Labels, values and the target tick can each be hidden.

Reflows in a narrow container instead of scaling. `max-w-full h-auto` shrinks an SVG rather than re-laying it out, so a 520px scorecard in a 300px column draws every 11px label at 6px — unreadable, and zooming does not help because what is on screen is a shrunken glyph, not text at a size. Below 380px the label and value move to their own line above the track, which then runs the full width instead of surrendering the 104px label gutter.

The label gutter is sized to the labels rather than fixed, capped at 45 % of the chart, and a name too long for the cap is ellipsised — the full text stays in the row's accessible name, its table row and every emitted event.
`width` is the width the host asks for and is only ever capped by the container, never stretched to it: a scorecard spread across a 2000px monitor is not an improvement.

The scale mode is **always** stated under the plot, and there is no input to hide it. Per-row scales are the default, so by default each bar is a share of a different number — two bars filling half their tracks are then two entirely different results, and the drawing has no way to say so. On per-row scales each measure is additionally printed as a share of its own ceiling (`268k of 300k`) rather than bare, and the value gutter grows to hold it; with `showValues` off there is no such line, so the note lists each row's ceiling itself. On one shared scale both are dropped: the ceiling is stated once in the note instead of repeated down every row.

A measure or a target past the ceiling is still drawn clamped — there is nowhere else to put it — and then MARKED, because a clamp alone is the wrong statement: 340 against a ceiling of 300 drew exactly like 300, and a target on the rim read as "the target is the maximum". A clipped bar gets a chevron at the end of its track and a dashed track outline; an off-scale target tick is dashed; both are named under the plot with the real figure and the ceiling.

`valuePolicy` decides what happens to a measure a track starting at zero cannot hold — a negative one, or one that is not a number. `clamp` (the default) pins the bar to the baseline, outlines the track dashed and still prints the real measure, because printing `0` there would be a false measurement. `omit` drops the row, which on a scorecard silently stops reporting a metric, so it says so. `reject` refuses the set and shows the error state. `render` is not offered: a track that starts at zero has no room below it.
accessibility: Every row carries a transparent, full-track `role="button"` hit area — a 0 % row has no bar, so the bar itself cannot be the focus target.

Each row is named with its value, target, percent-of-target and band, plus its ceiling when the rows disagree on one and a caveat when its bar is not to scale; Enter/Space emits `rowSelect` and focus emits `rowHover`.

The band a measure falls in is drawn as TEXT beside the row. A fill-opacity ramp over one hue alone would leave three greys to be ranked by eye (WCAG 1.4.1). The name survives `showValues` and `showLabels` being turned off, since neither hides information the picture carries nowhere else.

Bar length against a target tick is the entire chart, so `sv-data-summary-table` publishes measure, value, target and % of target, the band where the rows have one, and a "Scale maximum" column on per-row scales — which is where two equal-LOOKING bars are not equal values. Cells carry the caveats the plot marks visually, so a row whose bar is not to scale is not readable as an ordinary one. A band the source data never named is written by its position — "Band 2 of 3" — beside the row, in its name and in the table, and a dev-mode warning asks for a label; the opacity ramp is never its only statement. A measure that is not a number falls in no band: it says "No value" rather than taking the lowest band it was plotted at.

The target tick is drawn over a background-coloured halo. It is a dark 2.5px line that lands on the measure bar whenever the two nearly agree, which on a scorecard is most of the time — against a dark bar colour it vanished, and "we hit the target" drew identically to "there is no target".

inputs.description: Put every row on ONE scale so bar lengths are comparable across rows. Off by default, which is the opposite of most multi-row charts and is deliberate: a bullet chart's rows are a scorecard, and a scorecard mixes units — revenue in thousands next to a percentage next to a 1–5 rating. On a shared scale the revenue row sets a ceiling in the thousands and every other row collapses to an invisible sliver at the left edge. Each row already carries its own target and bands, so per-row scales are the honest default; turn this on when the rows genuinely measure the same thing (sales per region, latency per service) and you want lengths comparable. Whichever is in force, the chart states it under the plot — see `scaleNote`.

components.name: Candlestick
components.description: Open/high/low/close sessions on an ordinal axis, with direction carried by the body fill as well as the colour, an optional volume pane and a logarithmic price scale. Pure SVG.
whenToUse: A price history where the open, high, low and close of each session all matter.
Any period where the RANGE within a session is part of the story, not just the closing level.
For a closing price alone, a Line Chart is read faster. For a live feed, append sessions and set `liveWindow` to follow the newest ones.

examples.title: A live feed
examples.code:
<!-- Append candles as they arrive; the newest 30 are drawn and the axis fits them.
     connection says whether the socket is up, even over the empty state. -->
<sv-candlestick-chart [sessions]="sessions()" [liveWindow]="30" [showVolume]="true"
  [connection]="socketState()" [reconnectable]="true" (reconnect)="openSocket()" />

customization: Linear or logarithmic price axis, with the scale actually in force named under the plot — including when log was asked for and could not be given. Negative prices (spreads, futures) plot on the linear axis; log is positive-only and falls back to linear over any range that reaches zero or below (or a series whose prices are all equal), naming the reason.
`splits` back-adjusts prior sessions for a split or reverse split, disclosed in the note, in each adjusted session's accessible name and tooltip, and in its table row.

`minSlotWidth` (default 3 px): when one candle per session would be narrower, consecutive sessions are merged OHLC-style (first open, highest high, lowest low, last close, summed volume) — the bar a coarser timeframe draws — and the merge is disclosed; the table still lists every session. `0` draws hairlines instead.
Optional volume pane beneath the price pane.
Up and down colours, a currency prefix, and plot size.
A session missing any of the four prices is dropped and counted rather than patched, because filling a missing close with the open invents a doji and filling it with the previous close invents a gap.
accessibility: The series is ONE tab stop: Arrow keys step session by session (clamped, not wrapping — a time series has a first and a last), Home/End jump to the ends, Enter/Space select. Each candle is a `role="button"` named with its direction as a word, its percentage move and all four prices.
Sessions are keyed by position, not label, so two sessions that share a label are both drawn, both listed, and never highlight together.

Direction is encoded three times over: colour, body fill (hollow up, solid down, which is what paper charts used before colour was available), and the word itself. Colour alone reaches nobody using a screen reader, is unreliable with a colour-vision deficiency, and is gone in print.

`sv-data-summary-table` carries every session's direction, all four prices, the percentage change and the volume — figures the body and wick geometry only ever approximates. It lists every session individually even when dense data is drawn as merged candles, and a Note column marks split-adjusted prices and widened ranges.
The volume bars are not a second set of tab stops: each belongs to a session that is already focusable.
variants: Sessions, With Direction in More Than the Colour
Volume, and a Logarithmic Price Axis
Five Years of Sessions, Merged to Fit

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the sessions are being fetched.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Load failure. Use `toSvDataError()` from `@styloviz/core` to normalize an `HttpErrorResponse`.

inputs.name: emptyMessage
inputs.description: Copy for the no-data state.

inputs.name: filtered
inputs.description: True when the emptiness is caused by a filter rather than an empty set.

inputs.name: sessions
inputs.description: Trading sessions, oldest first. The axis is ORDINAL — one slot per session you supply — so weekends, holidays and halts simply are not in the list. Do not pad them: a market has no Saturday, and a padded session is a candle that never traded. Labels are printed verbatim and never parsed, so the chart has no time zone of its own: format each session's label in the exchange's zone before it arrives, and it reads the same for every viewer. Labels need not be unique.

inputs.name: liveWindow
inputs.description: Show only the newest N sessions, so a host appending candles from a feed gets a window that moves with it. `0` draws every session. The prices are still audited (and split-adjusted) over everything you pass; only the drawing is windowed, and the axis fits the visible sessions.

inputs.name: connection
inputs.description: State of the socket / `EventSource` behind a host-fed series. A series that stops updating looks the same whether the market is quiet or the connection dropped, so the chart cannot infer this — only the host knows. `idle` renders nothing.

inputs.name: reconnectable
inputs.description: Offer a Reconnect button while `connection` is `reconnecting` or `closed`. Off by default: most hosts retry on their own, and a second manual trigger opens a second socket.

inputs.name: priceScale
inputs.description: How the price axis is spaced. `log` is the correct choice over a long history: on a linear axis a move from 10 to 20 and one from 100 to 110 are drawn the same height, though the first doubled the money and the second added a tenth. It falls back to linear when the range touches zero or every price is the same, and the chart says which it used and why.

inputs.name: showVolume
inputs.description: Draw the volume pane beneath the price pane.

inputs.name: splits
inputs.description: Share splits to back-adjust across: `{ at, ratio }`, where `at` is the label (first match) or index of the first session AFTER the split and `ratio` is new shares per old (`4` for 4-for-1, `0.1` for a 1-for-10 reverse split). Every earlier session's prices are divided by the ratio and its volume multiplied by it, so an unadjusted split does not draw as a crash nobody lost money on. The adjustment is disclosed under the chart and in each adjusted session's accessible name. Leave empty when the feed is already adjusted — adjusting twice is its own crash.

inputs.name: minSlotWidth
inputs.description: Narrowest slot, in pixels, a single session may be drawn in. When there are more sessions than fit at this width, consecutive sessions are merged into one candle each (first open, highest high, lowest low, last close, summed volume) — the bar a coarser timeframe would draw — and the merge is disclosed. `0` turns aggregation off and draws hairline candles instead.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Plot width in pixels.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Plot height in pixels, both panes included.

inputs.name: upColor
inputs.description: Colour for a rising session.

inputs.name: downColor
inputs.description: Colour for a falling session.

inputs.name: pricePrefix
inputs.description: Currency or unit prefix for prices, e.g. `$`.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Chart title, rendered above the plot.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name override. Falls back to a generated summary.

inputs.name: customClass
inputs.description: Extra CSS classes applied to the root wrapper.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The host should re-run the failed load.

outputs.name: reconnect
outputs.description: The user asked to re-open the feed.

outputs.name: sessionHover
outputs.description: Emitted when a session is hovered or keyboard-focused.

outputs.name: sessionSelect
outputs.description: Emitted when a session is clicked or activated with Enter/Space.

components.name: Carousel
components.description: Image carousel with optional autoplay — slide, fade, card or coverflow, horizontal or vertical, one slide or a row of cards — with dots, lines, numbers or thumbnails, prev/next arrows and a slide counter.
whenToUse: Cycling through a small set of images or promotional slides.
You want autoplay with arrows and a choice of indicator styles.
For browsing many images on demand, use the Image Gallery.

examples.title: Calls to action
examples.code:
<!-- slides = [
  { id: 'sale', title: 'Summer sale', image: '/img/sale.webp', cta: 'Shop the sale', ctaLink: '/sale' },
  { id: 'news', title: 'Join the newsletter', cta: 'Subscribe' },
] — a CTA with ctaLink is a link; one without is a button you handle. -->
<sv-carousel [slides]="slides" (ctaClick)="onCta($event)" />

examples.title: A row of cards
examples.code:
<!-- three in view, fewer when each would be under 220px wide -->
<sv-carousel [slides]="cards" [slidesPerView]="3" aspectRatio="4/5" [loop]="false" />

customization: Indicator styles: dots, lines, numbers, thumbnails (a strip of previews under the carousel) or none.
Autoplay with configurable interval, `pauseOnHover`, and a built-in pause/play button.
Variants: `default` (slide), `fade`, `card` and `coverflow`.
`orientation="vertical"` moves `default` and `card` slides up and down (`fade` still cross-fades), with the arrows above and below and the dots down the edge; `coverflow` stays horizontal.

`slidesPerView` shows a row of cards that steps one slide at a time and stops with the last in view; each keeps `slideMinWidth` (220px by default), so a narrow container shows fewer. Above 1, `aspectRatio` is each card's and `variant` does not apply.
accessibility: Swipe: a horizontal swipe (touch, pen or mouse; 40px or more, and more sideways than up/down) shows the next or previous slide, mirrored under `dir="rtl"`. The region is `touch-pan-y touch-pinch-zoom`, so a vertical swipe still scrolls the page and pinch still zooms it, and the click a swipe ends in is swallowed so a slide's link is not followed by accident. The arrows, dots and ←/→ remain.
Exposed as a `region` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"`; slides are labelled groups and a live region announces changes (silenced while auto-rotating).
Auto-play pauses on hover and keyboard focus and can be stopped with the pause button (WCAG 2.2.2); ←/→ navigate slides.
Prev/next, indicators and pause are labelled buttons; the active indicator exposes `aria-current`.
A vertical carousel takes ↑/↓ instead of ←/→ and a vertical swipe instead of a horizontal one; its region is `touch-pan-x`, so a sideways swipe still scrolls.
Thumbnails are buttons named by position ("Go to slide 3"), as the dots are; the preview image is decoration (`alt=""`).
With several slides in view, every slide in the row is reachable and announced; those outside it are `inert` and hidden from assistive technology, as an inactive slide always is.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the slides are being fetched.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Load failure. Use `toSvDataError()` from `@styloviz/core` to normalize an `HttpErrorResponse`.

inputs.name: emptyMessage
inputs.description: Copy for the no-data state.

inputs.name: filtered
inputs.description: True when the emptiness is caused by a filter rather than an empty set.

inputs.name: slides
inputs.description: Slides to display (image, caption, optional link).

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Visual variant. `default` slides full-bleed; `fade` cross-fades in place; `card` insets each slide as a rounded, shadowed card; `coverflow` shows the neighbouring slides scaled down either side of the active one. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` every variant keeps its layout but drops the transition.

inputs.name: indicator
inputs.description: Indicator style: dots, lines, numbers, `thumbnails` (a strip of slide previews under the carousel) or none.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: Which way the slides travel. `vertical` moves `default` and `card` slides up and down, puts the arrows top and bottom, and takes ↑ / ↓ and vertical swipes. `coverflow` and several slides per view stay horizontal.

inputs.name: slidesPerView
inputs.description: How many slides show side by side — a row of cards that steps one slide at a time. Fewer show when the carousel is too narrow for each to keep `slideMinWidth`, so a phone sees one. Above 1, `variant` is ignored and `aspectRatio` is each slide's.

inputs.name: slideMinWidth
inputs.description: The narrowest a slide may get when several share the view, in px.

inputs.name: autoPlay
inputs.description: Auto-advance slides.

inputs.name: interval
inputs.description: Auto-advance interval in ms.

inputs.name: loop
inputs.description: Wrap from last slide back to first.

inputs.name: arrows
inputs.description: Show prev/next arrows.

inputs.name: aspectRatio
inputs.description: CSS aspect-ratio for the viewport.

inputs.name: pauseOnHover
inputs.description: Pause auto-advance while the carousel is hovered or focused.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name for the carousel region.

inputs.name: priority
inputs.description: Load the first slide's image eagerly at high fetch priority. Set it when the carousel is above the fold — a hero image is usually the page's Largest Contentful Paint, and a lazy one is fetched only after layout. Later slides stay lazy either way.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The host should re-run the failed load.

outputs.name: slideChange
outputs.description: Emitted with the active slide index when it changes.

outputs.name: pausedChange
outputs.description: Emitted when the user toggles auto-play; payload is the paused state.

outputs.name: ctaClick
outputs.description: Emitted with the slide whose call-to-action was activated (click, Enter or Space). A slide with `ctaLink` still navigates; this fires first, so it suits analytics. A slide without one has no other effect — handle it here.

components.name: Cart Line Item
components.description: A single cart row: image, title, variant, quantity stepper and a computed line total, with remove and save-for-later actions. Bursts of quantity clicks settle into one write, which rolls back if the server rejects it. Stock caps the stepper rather than only hinting, and a price that moved since the item went into the cart says so. Default and compact densities.
whenToUse: Rows in the cart page and the mini-cart drawer.
A read-only line in order details / confirmation (set `editable`/`removable` to false).
You want the line total to track quantity automatically.

examples.title: Persisting one write per burst of clicks
Removed, with the undo window the host owns
A variant that stopped being buyable
Stock as a cap, and a cart that already holds too many
examples.code:
<!-- Stepper ceiling is min(max, stock): 3, not 99. -->
<sv-cart-line-item title="Aurora Runner" [unitPrice]="129" [(quantity)]="qty" [stock]="3" />

<!-- Already over the cap: the row says so and describes the stepper with it.
     It does not rewrite the quantity — correcting the cart is your write. -->
<sv-cart-line-item title="Aurora Runner" [unitPrice]="129" [quantity]="5" [stock]="3" />

<!-- stock 0 is unbuyable on its own, without a separate [unavailable]. -->
<sv-cart-line-item title="Trail Cap" [unitPrice]="35" [quantity]="1" [stock]="0" unavailableText="Out of stock" />

examples.title: A price that moved since the item went into the cart

customization: Default and compact densities.
Editable quantity stepper or a static quantity.
Optional remove and save-for-later actions.
`commitDelayMs` tunes how long a burst of clicks settles; `0` reports every step.
`unavailableText` for why a variant cannot be bought.
`stock` caps the stepper; `previousUnitPrice` turns on the repricing note, with the direction and old figure formatted in the row's own currency and locale.
Any ISO currency + locale, with minor-unit support.
accessibility: Remove, undo and save actions are real buttons with descriptive labels naming the product.
The quantity stepper is named after its line, so a five-item cart does not announce "Number input" five times — and its + / – buttons are named after the line too, not "Increase value".

Whichever note the row is showing describes the stepper via `aria-describedby`, with a per-instance id so one row is never described by another's. A quantity that outruns the stock, or a write that failed, also sets `aria-invalid` — so the red border and the announced state agree.
A write in flight sets `aria-busy` on the row and disables its controls.

A failed write is text in a `role="alert"`, never colour alone; removed and unavailable rows say so in words as well as by dimming the image. The repricing note names the direction in words, so up and down are not told apart by colour.
Image links and titles are keyboard-reachable; line total is tabular-nums text.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Product title.

inputs.name: unitPrice
inputs.description: Unit price (minor units when `minorUnits` is true).

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: Product image URL.

inputs.name: href
inputs.description: Link target for the product.

inputs.name: variantLabel
inputs.description: Variant description, e.g. "Black / M".

inputs.name: compareAt
inputs.description: Compare-at unit price for a strikethrough.

inputs.name: currency
inputs.description: ISO 4217 currency code.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP-47 locale for prices.

inputs.name: minorUnits
inputs.description: Treat prices as minor units.

inputs.name: min
inputs.description: Minimum quantity.

inputs.name: max
inputs.description: Maximum quantity.

inputs.name: stock
inputs.description: Remaining stock, as the server last reported it. `null` is "not known". This is a cap, not a hint. Stock is the number most likely to change while the row is on screen — the cart was filled an hour ago and somebody else has been shopping since. It caps the stepper (`quantityMax`), and a quantity already above the cap is stated out loud rather than silently rewritten: the cart holds what it holds, and correcting it is a write this row does not make.

inputs.name: previousUnitPrice
inputs.description: What this item's unit price was when it went into the cart, if it has changed since. A price that moves under a shopper has to say so. `unitPrice` is an input, so a host applying a fresh quote silently redraws the line total and the shopper is asked to pay a number they never agreed to — the same failure `sv-order-summary` handles with its `repriced` state, one level down. Set this to the old price and the row names the change and its direction. It is display-only: it does not affect the line total, which is always `unitPrice × quantity`.

inputs.name: editable
inputs.description: Show the quantity stepper (false renders a static "Qty: n").

inputs.name: removable
inputs.description: Show the remove control.

inputs.name: showSaveForLater
inputs.description: Show a "Save for later" control.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Density.

inputs.name: showMedia
inputs.description: Show the product image (or its placeholder) at the start of the row. `false` is for lines where the shopper is not choosing by sight — a till ticket, a returns form, a re-order list. There the empty image box is 64px of row that carries nothing, on the one screen that needs every line it can fit.

inputs.name: saving
inputs.description: True while a write for this row is in flight. The stepper and both row actions stop responding, so a second edit cannot race the first and leave `rollback()` ambiguous.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: The last write for this row failed. Rendered as a danger note under the title. Roll the quantity back as well — this input reports the failure, it does not undo it.

inputs.name: commitDelayMs
inputs.description: How long the quantity settles before it is reported, in milliseconds. `0` reports every step immediately.

inputs.name: unavailable
inputs.description: This variant cannot be bought any more — discontinued, or out of stock since the cart was filled. The row still renders, because a shopper needs to see what they are being asked to drop, but the quantity is frozen and the line total is struck: it is not part of the payable order.

inputs.name: unavailableText
inputs.description: Copy for the unavailable note.

inputs.name: removed
inputs.description: The host has removed this row and is offering a way back. The row renders as removed with an Undo control, and nothing else responds. The window is the host's to open and close — a component that started its own timer and committed the deletion when it expired would be claiming a write it never makes.

inputs.name: quantity
inputs.description: Quantity (two-way: `[(quantity)]`). Moves on every click so the stepper and the line total stay live. What to PERSIST comes from `quantityCommit`, once the clicking stops.

outputs.name: quantityCommit
outputs.description: The quantity settled. One emission per burst of edits — persist this.

outputs.name: remove
outputs.description: Emitted when the remove control is pressed.

outputs.name: undoRemove
outputs.description: The shopper pressed Undo on a removed row.

outputs.name: saveForLater
outputs.description: Emitted when "Save for later" is pressed.

outputs.name: quantityChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `quantity` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(quantity)]`.

components.name: Cascader
components.description: Multi-level cascading select for hierarchical data (e.g. Country → State → City) with searchable mode, hover/click expand triggers, partial-path selection, multi-select with removable chips, async lazy-loaded children and full keyboard navigation.
whenToUse: Selecting from naturally hierarchical data: location, category trees, org units.
You want one compact control instead of several dependent dropdowns.
For a flat list use Select Dropdown; for browsing a big tree use Tree View.

examples.title: Async lazy-loaded children
examples.description: Give branch nodes isLeaf:false and no children; loadData fetches them on expand (a spinner shows meanwhile).

examples.title: Multi-select with removable chips (Pro)
examples.description: Set multiple=true — leaf nodes become checkboxes, the panel stays open while picking, and each pick shows as a removable chip in the trigger.

customization: Feed `options` as a `CascaderNode[]` tree; the path is emitted as an array of values via `[(value)]`.
Set `expandTrigger` to `hover` or `click`, and allow partial paths with `changeOnSelect`.
Enable `searchable` for flat path search, tune `separator` for the displayed label, and pick a `size` (sm, md, lg).
Provide `loadData` to lazily fetch children on expand — mark branch nodes with `isLeaf: false` and no `children`; a spinner shows while loading.

Turn on `multiple` for multi-select: leaves render checkboxes, the panel stays open, and picks surface as removable chips. Bind `[(checkedValues)]` (a `string[][]` of value paths) and listen to `valuesChange` / `selectionsChange`.
Toggle the clear affordance with `clearable` (defaults to on) — it clears the single value or every checked chip.
Implements `ControlValueAccessor`, so single-select also binds with `[formControl]` / `[(ngModel)]` and respects `control.disable()` — `[(value)]` still works for non-form usage.
Responsive: the body-portaled panel caps its width and height to the viewport and the column strip scrolls horizontally, so a multi-column cascader never runs off-screen on a phone or tablet.
accessibility: The trigger exposes `aria-expanded`/`aria-haspopup` and is named via `ariaLabel` (announced with the selected path); each column is a `role="listbox"` of `role="option"` rows with `aria-selected`.
The popover is a non-modal `role="dialog"`; the search box is labelled; arrows move within a level and Esc closes.
In multi-select mode each leaf row reflects its checked state via `aria-selected`, and every chip has a labelled "Remove <item>" control operable with Enter/Space.
Closes on outside click and restores focus to the trigger; all panel ids are generated per instance.
variants: Touch and Narrow Screens — hover falls back, columns drill in

inputs.name: options
inputs.description: Tree of selectable nodes.

inputs.name: loadData
inputs.type: ((node: CascaderNode, signal?: AbortSignal) => CascaderNode[] | Promise<CascaderNode[]>) | null
inputs.description: Async children loader. When provided, a node with no `children` and `isLeaf !== true` is treated as an unloaded branch: clicking it calls `loadData(node)` and attaches the resolved children.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Selected value path as array of values, e.g. ['country', 'state', 'city'].

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Placeholder text.

inputs.name: changeOnSelect
inputs.description: Allow selecting intermediate (non-leaf) nodes.

inputs.name: searchable
inputs.description: Show search input in dropdown.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disabled state.

inputs.name: expandTrigger
inputs.description: Expand trigger.

inputs.name: columnMode
inputs.description: Side-by-side columns, one column at a time, or whichever fits.

inputs.name: separator
inputs.description: Path separator shown in the trigger.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Component size.

inputs.name: multiple
inputs.description: Multi-select mode (Pro). Leaf nodes render checkboxes, the panel stays open while picking, and selections surface as removable chips in the trigger. Single-select behaviour is unchanged when `false`.

inputs.name: clearable
inputs.description: Show the clear button while there is a selection.

inputs.name: checkedValues
inputs.description: Initial checked value paths for multi-select mode.

inputs.name: serverSide
inputs.description: Let the server do the searching. The supplied `options` are shown exactly as given — the flat search list is built from them without re-filtering.

inputs.name: debounceMs
inputs.description: Delay before `queryChange` fires, in ms. `0` emits immediately.

inputs.name: minChars
inputs.description: Characters required before a search is sent. Below this the panel says so instead of showing a misleading "No results".

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Failure loading the root options, rendered in place of the columns. Pair it with `(retry)`: unlike a failed branch, which the user can re-open by clicking the node again, a failed root leaves an empty panel with nothing to press.

inputs.name: stale
inputs.description: The results on screen answer an **older** query — a newer request is still in flight. Distinct from `loading`, which cannot separate the two cases it covers: the first fetch (nothing on screen — show a skeleton) and a refinement of results already visible (keep them, and say they are provisional). Blanking the panel on the second is the most jarring thing a picker can do; showing the old list with no indication is a quiet lie. Bind `svSuggestController(...).stale` from `@styloviz/data`, or `createRequestGuard().stale` from `@styloviz/core`. The results dim and report `aria-busy` while staying fully interactive.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name for the trigger / panel.

inputs.name: errorMessage
inputs.description: Client-side validation message.

inputs.name: serverError
inputs.description: A rejection reported by the server about this value. Self-expiring.

outputs.name: valueChange
outputs.description: Emitted when a value is selected (single-select mode).

outputs.name: queryChange
outputs.description: The search term changed — fetch matching paths. Debounced by `debounceMs` and never emitted twice for the same term. Pair with `serverSide`.

outputs.name: loadError
outputs.description: A branch's children failed to load. The node keeps a retry control; this lets the host log or toast as well.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The host should re-run the failed root load (see `error`).

outputs.name: selectionChange
outputs.description: Emitted with full node path on selection (single-select mode).

outputs.name: valuesChange
outputs.description: Emitted in multi-select mode with every checked value path.

outputs.name: selectionsChange
outputs.description: Emitted in multi-select mode with every checked node path.

components.name: Checkbox
components.description: Accessible checkboxes with 5 variants, 3 sizes, indeterminate state and ControlValueAccessor support.
whenToUse: Selecting any number of independent options, or a single opt-in (terms, consent).
You need an indeterminate parent for "select all / partial" patterns.
For mutually exclusive options use a Radio Group; for instant settings use a Toggle.

examples.title: Indeterminate "select all"
examples.description: Derive the parent from the children — `checked` when all are, `indeterminate` when some are — and let its `(changed)` set every child, so a mixed parent clicked selects all. The live demo above is exactly this.
examples.code:
<sv-checkbox label="Select all"
  [checked]="allChecked()"
  [indeterminate]="someChecked()"
  (changed)="setAll($event)" />
@for (item of items(); track item.id) {
  <sv-checkbox [label]="item.label" [checked]="item.checked" (changed)="setOne(item.id, $event)" />
}

// allChecked  = computed(() => items().every(i => i.checked));
// someChecked = computed(() => items().some(i => i.checked) && !allChecked());

examples.title: Required + reactive forms
examples.description: Works with formControlName via ControlValueAccessor; required sets native required + aria-required, and name/value enable plain form submission.
examples.code:
<sv-checkbox
  formControlName="acceptTerms"
  label="I accept the terms"
  description="You must accept to continue."
  [required]="true"
  name="acceptTerms"
  value="yes" />

customization: Choose a `variant` (primary, success, warning, danger, neutral) and `size` (sm, md, lg) to match your form density.
Supports an `indeterminate` state for "select all" patterns and a `description` sub-label.
Add `required`, `name` / `value`, `autofocus`; two-way bind with `[(checked)]` or a reactive control and listen to `(changed)`.
accessibility: A real, focusable native checkbox (visually hidden) owns keyboard activation (Space) and announces role/state — including `aria-checked="mixed"` for indeterminate.
A unique id is generated automatically so the `<label for>` association works without `inputId`; clicking the label toggles the box and the focus ring is clearly visible.
The `description` is linked via `aria-describedby`; `required` sets `aria-required`; use `ariaLabel` when there is no visible label.
Implements ControlValueAccessor — works with template & reactive forms; programmatic `formControl.disable()` disables the native input.

The value and the appearance are allowed to disagree, and only one of them is ever submitted: `aria-checked="mixed"` and the dash render the `indeterminate` input, while the form receives the boolean `checked`.

inputs.name: checked
inputs.description: Current checked state. Use `[(checked)]` for two-way binding.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Visible label text.

inputs.name: description
inputs.description: Smaller descriptor line beneath the label.

inputs.name: inputId
inputs.description: Explicit id forwarded to the native input. Auto-generated when omitted.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: `aria-label` override — required when there is no visible `label` so screen readers can still announce the control's purpose.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Size of the checkbox.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Active color variant.

inputs.name: indeterminate
inputs.description: Show an indeterminate (dash) state.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disable interaction.

inputs.name: required
inputs.description: Mark the control as required (sets native `required` + `aria-required`).

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: `name` for native form submission.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: `value` submitted with `name` when checked (grouped checkboxes).

inputs.name: autofocus
inputs.description: Autofocus the control on render.

inputs.name: customClass
inputs.description: Additional CSS classes on the root wrapper.

inputs.name: errorMessage
inputs.description: Client-side validation message, rendered under the box and label — e.g. "You must accept the terms".

inputs.name: serverError
inputs.description: A rejection that came back from the server about THIS value. Self-expires as soon as the value changes — see `createFieldError`.

inputs.name: pending
inputs.description: The user's change is applied on screen and its write is in flight. Not `disabled`: the tick the user just placed stays at full strength — fading a value the user chose reads as "this did not take" — and the box stays focusable. It refuses further changes while true, which is what makes `rollback()` unambiguous. Bind it for the whole round-trip.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: The write failed. Accepts an `SvDataError` or a plain string. Not `serverError`. That is the field-validation contract and it expires on the next value change — and a rollback IS a value change, so a failure routed through it would vanish in the same tick the box un-ticked. The user would watch it revert and be told nothing. Call `rollback()` as well: a message beside a box still showing the state that failed is worse than either alone.

outputs.name: changed
outputs.description: Emits the new boolean state after every change.

outputs.name: changeRequest
outputs.description: The same change, carrying what a server write needs: an idempotency key and a guarded `rollback()`. Additive — `changed` still fires first, and a checkbox that only writes to local state has no use for this.

outputs.name: checkedChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `checked` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(checked)]`.

components.name: Chip
components.description: 7 semantic variants × 3 visual styles. Supports avatar, icon, selectable and removable modes.
whenToUse: Displaying compact, discrete metadata: tags, categories, statuses, filters.
Building removable filter bars or selectable token lists.
For free-text entry of many tags, compose with Tag Input instead.

examples.title: Say what the chip is for
examples.code:
<sv-chip chipRole="status" categoryLabel="Status" label="Overdue" variant="danger" />
<sv-chip chipRole="action" label="Add label" icon="plus" (activated)="addLabel()" />

examples.title: Styles
examples.code:
<sv-chip label="Filled" variant="success" chipStyle="filled" />
<sv-chip label="Soft" variant="warning" chipStyle="soft" />
<sv-chip label="Outline" variant="danger" chipStyle="outline" />

customization: Seven semantic `variant`s across `filled`, `soft` and `outline` styles, in three `size`s.
Add a leading `icon` (an icon-library name), `avatarSrc` or `avatarInitials`; enable `selectable` and/or `removable`.
Bind selection with `[(selected)]` (two-way), `[selected]` (controlled) or leave it uncontrolled; listen to `(removed)`.
accessibility: Selectable chips use `role="checkbox"` with `aria-checked`, are in the tab order, and toggle with Space/Enter — the `selected` model keeps the visual and bound state in sync.
Removable chips expose a labelled remove button (disabled when the chip is disabled).
Disabled chips set `aria-disabled` and leave the tab order; provide `ariaLabel` for icon/avatar-only chips so they have an accessible name.

`chipRole` names the job instead of a styling flag: `status` (no role, ignores `selectable`), `filter` (`role="checkbox"`), `token` (inert body, labelled remove button) and `action` (`role="button"`, Space/Enter, emits `activated`, never carries selection). `auto` (default) resolves from the other flags: selectable → filter, removable → token, else status.

`categoryLabel` prefixes the announced name ("Status: Overdue", "Filter: Frontend") — as sr-only text on role-less chips, folded into `aria-label` on roled ones; an explicit `ariaLabel` is never prefixed.
variants: Four Roles — status, filter, token, action

Prefixing every non-interactive chip would turn a skills list into "Status: Angular, Status: TypeScript". The component cannot know which plain chips are badges and which are decoration — the host can, and this is how it says so. Rendered as `sr-only` text rather than `aria-label` for chips with no ARIA role, because `aria-label` on a bare `<span>` is not reliably announced. Roled chips fold it into their name instead.

components.name: Chip Group
components.description: A set of chips that belongs to something — one tab stop for the whole row, arrows between members, and a name for the thing they are members of.
whenToUse: Any row of selectable chips — filter bars, tag pickers, skill selectors. Two or more selectable chips side by side is already the case this exists for.
A row of removable tokens, with `selectionMode="none"` — they are not toggles but they are a set, and the set deserves a name.
A single chip does not need one. A lone chip is its own tab stop and that is correct.
Picking exactly ONE of several is not this. Use Segmented Control or Radio Group — they own single-select, with the right roles and selection-follows-focus.

examples.title: The problem it solves
examples.description: A selectable `sv-chip` is a `role="checkbox"` with its own `tabindex="0"`. That is valid ARIA and a poor control: twenty filter chips are twenty tab stops, and a screen reader announcing "Design, checkbox, not checked" has no way to say what set it belongs to, how many there are, or which one this is. The chips were never wrong individually — there was simply nothing above them.
examples.code:
<sv-chip-group label="Filter by tag">
  <sv-chip label="Design"   [selectable]="true" [(selected)]="design" />
  <sv-chip label="Frontend" [selectable]="true" [(selected)]="frontend" />
  <sv-chip label="Backend"  [selectable]="true" [(selected)]="backend" />
</sv-chip-group>

examples.title: Arrows move, Space chooses
examples.description: Movement and selection are deliberately different keys. In a radiogroup selection follows focus and that is correct — there is always exactly one answer, so moving IS choosing. In a multi-select filter bar the same behaviour silently switches on every filter the user scans past, which is a data-loss bug wearing a keyboard shortcut. Arrow and Home/End move; Space and Enter toggle.
examples.code:
<!-- Tab reaches the group once. ← → Home End move between chips.
     Space toggles the one you are on, and nothing else. -->
<sv-chip-group label="Skills" orientation="horizontal">
  @for (skill of skills(); track skill.id) {
    <sv-chip [label]="skill.name" [selectable]="true" [(selected)]="skill.on" />
  }
</sv-chip-group>

examples.title: A set that is not selectable is still a set
examples.description: `selectionMode="none"` still buys the group a name and one tab stop. A row of removable tokens is not selectable but is very much a set, and a reader arriving at it should be told what it is.
examples.code:
<sv-chip-group label="Applied filters" selectionMode="none">
  <sv-chip label="Status: open" [removable]="true" (removed)="clear('status')" />
  <sv-chip label="Owner: me"    [removable]="true" (removed)="clear('owner')" />
</sv-chip-group>

customization: `orientation` lays the chips out in a row or a column. It is visual only: the arrows move along both axes in either layout, and no `aria-orientation` is set (it is not allowed on a group).

`selectionMode` is `multiple` (checkbox chips) or `none` (a named set of non-toggles — a chip on `chipRole="auto"` is not inferred to be a filter from `selectable` there). There is deliberately no `single`.
`gap` (`xs` · `sm` · `md`, 4 / 8 / 12 px on both axes) sets the spacing between chips; `customClass` adds classes to the container.
accessibility: A `role="group"` named by `aria-label`. The arrow keys move along both axes in either layout, so `orientation` is visual only — and `aria-orientation` is not allowed on a group, so none is set.
One roving tab stop for the whole set: Tab reaches the group once, and ← → ↑ ↓ Home End move between members. Both axes are accepted, because a row that is horizontal today is vertical at 400px.

Movement never selects. Arrowing past a chip leaves it exactly as it was; Space and Enter are what toggle. This is the one behaviour that separates a multi-select chip set from a radiogroup, and getting it wrong loses the user's filters silently.
Disabled chips keep `role="checkbox"` and `aria-disabled` — a disabled control still exists — but leave the tab rotation, so the arrows step over them.
The tab stop follows the user: clicking a chip makes it the member Tab returns to.

Removable tokens count too: in a group each token is reached through its "Remove …" button, so a row of twelve tokens is still one Tab and the arrows walk the remove buttons. A focusable chip that is also removable keeps its `×` out of the tab order and is removed with Delete or Backspace (declared via `aria-keyshortcuts`).
Outside a group a selectable chip is still its own tab stop. A lone status chip must not require a container to exist.
variants: Four Roles — status, filter, token, action

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Accessible name for the set — "Filter by tag", "Skills". Without it the group is an unnamed container, which is worse than no container: a reader announces a grouping boundary and cannot say what the grouping is. Supply it, or the chips were better off loose.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: Layout direction. Visual only: both arrow axes walk the chips in either layout, so a user who guesses the wrong axis is still right.

inputs.name: selectionMode
inputs.description: Whether the chips are toggles or decoration.

inputs.name: gap
inputs.description: Gap between chips.

inputs.name: customClass
inputs.description: Additional classes on the group container.

components.name: Choropleth Map
components.description: Value-per-region map. Equal-area projection by default, quantile / equal-interval / threshold class breaks, an explicit no-data fill and legend entry, a hatch for figures the host flags as estimates, and one tab stop with arrow-key navigation. Bring your own GeoJSON or TopoJSON — adapters and a simplifier are included. Pure SVG.
whenToUse: A single number per administrative region, where WHERE is the question.
Rates, densities and shares — anything already normalised by population or area.
For raw counts, prefer a bar chart or proportional symbols: a count map mostly reproduces the population map.
For a handful of regions, a ranked bar chart is read faster and more precisely.

examples.title: Equal-interval breaks against a fixed scale
TopoJSON in, simplified for a dashboard-sized map
A figure that is an estimate

customization: Four projections, including identity for pre-projected composites such as Albers USA.
Quantile, equal-interval, explicit-threshold and continuous scales.
Seven sequential ramps, plus a configurable no-data fill and label.
A hatch overlay for figures flagged `uncertain`, with its own legend entry and `uncertainLabel` wording.

`svGeoJsonFeatures`, `svTopoJsonFeatures` and `svSimplifyFeatures` convert real boundary files into the shape the component takes. None of them fetches anything — the host loads its own file and hands over the parsed object.
accessibility: The SVG is a `role="group"` with a generated summary naming the region count, the value range and the arrow-key model (override via `ariaLabel`).

Colour is the value here, and a sequential ramp is the least precise encoding in the kit — two adjacent bands are one shade apart. `sv-data-summary-table` publishes one row per region with its figure (the column takes its name from `legendTitle`) and its band where the scale is classed, and writes "No data" in words rather than leaving a blank cell that reads as zero.

One roving tab stop for the whole map rather than one per region: Tab enters and leaves, arrow keys and Home/End move between regions in reading order, and Enter/Space emits `regionSelect`. Every region carries an `aria-label` with its name and value, and says "No data" in words where there is none.

An estimate says so in words, not only in the hatch. A texture is invisible to a screen reader and easy to miss on a small or printed map, so `uncertainLabel` travels with the figure into the region's accessible name, the tooltip and the table row.
variants: Figures the Map Is Less Sure About
Pin Map — Sites on a World Base Layer
Pin Map — Clustering On and Off
Pin Map — Tones, Highlights and a Custom Palette
Pin Map — Loading, Error, Empty and Filtered-Empty

components.name: Citation Sources
components.description: Numbered citations attached to an answer, with the coverage strip that names the passages nothing supports. 3 variants: inline chips, source cards and a side panel.
whenToUse: A RAG answer where the reader has to be able to check a claim against its source.
Any surface where the important question is not "what did it say" but "what is this resting on".
For the retrieval pipeline itself — chunks, hit scores, index health — use the RAG Knowledge Base.
customization: `[claims]` makes claim ids the **first** anchor: a citation carrying `claimId` resolves to that claim’s text before `anchorText` and before offsets, and an id that is not in the answer leaves the citation unplaced and says so rather than falling back to stale offsets. `(claimsOpened)` emits the claim ids behind a source when the reader opens it, which is what lets a host persist ‘the reader checked this’ across re-generations.
`answer`, `citations` and `sources` are inputs and all default to empty; import `DEMO_ANSWER` / `DEMO_CITATIONS` / `DEMO_SOURCES` for a demo.
Three layouts via `variant`: `inline` (superscript chips in the prose), `cards` (chips plus a source list) and `panel` (a docked source list).
A chip is a button, not a superscript — it emits `sourceSelect` with the source and the citation the reader activated.
Coverage is exposed as a strip: percentage attributed, distinct source count, and the uncited passages themselves, longest first.

`[uncitedMinChars]` (40, from the still-exported `SV_UNCITED_MIN_CHARS`) is the floor below which a gap is not worth reporting — the whitespace between two adjacent citations is not an unsourced claim. Forty characters is a sentence in English prose, two or three in Chinese and most of a bullet in a summary-style answer, so the figure is yours to set; `svCitationCoverage` takes it as an optional last argument.
Free tier: uses only free icons.

`anchorText` on a citation is the exact words of the ANSWER it covers, and it is placed by *finding* those words. Character offsets are the wrong anchor and every pipeline proves it: a trim, a collapsed double space, a markdown pass or a prepended greeting shifts every offset by the same amount, the chips slide off the claims they belong to, and nothing fails. Offsets stay as the fallback for a host that has not adopted it.

When a citation cannot be located, or lands somewhere its own offsets disagree with, the component **says so in the surface** (`[data-sv-placement-notice]`) instead of clipping it away. An answer whose citations moved is worse than an uncited one, because it looks checked.
`claimId` is identity rather than placement: the same claim re-worded keeps its id, so a host can persist 'the reader checked this' across re-generations.

`[allowedUrlProtocols]` defaults to `http:`, `https:` and `mailto:`. A source URL is model output, which is untrusted input, and Angular renders a `javascript:` href as a dead `unsafe:` link — safe, and silent. A refused URL is shown as **text** with its scheme named: that the answer cited something unreachable is evidence about the answer. Relative and protocol-relative URLs are refused rather than resolved, since this component does not know the host's base URL.

**Coverage measures attribution, not support.** The strip says so in the surface — "Attributed is not verified as supported" — because a chip records which source a passage was attributed to, not that the source actually says it. A 100 % bar over an answer its sources contradict looks exactly like a checked one. Entailment checking needs a verifier this kit does not ship; run one in your pipeline if you need it.

**Source freshness.** `SourceRef.retrievedAt` renders under each source as a relative age in the kit locale ("Retrieved 3 days ago") inside a `<time datetime>` whose title is the absolute date. Pass ISO 8601 (or epoch milliseconds); any other text ("09:41", "last sync") is rendered verbatim rather than guessed at. `svSourceFreshness(retrievedAt, locale, now?)` is exported.

**Sources the reader cannot open.** `SourceRef.access` — `available` (default), `paywalled`, `dead` or `denied` — renders a named chip beside the source and, in the passage, a sentence with the address as text **instead of a link**: a paywall, a 404 or a permission wall behind "Open the source" reads as a fabricated citation. The quoted passage still renders. The state is the host's to report — the component never fetches a source. `svSourceAccess(source, labels)` is exported; `DEMO_SOURCES_RESTRICTED` shows a paywalled, year-old source.
accessibility: Chips are real buttons with accessible names naming the source they resolve to, not bare superscripts.
The coverage percentage is stated in words as well as drawn as a bar.
Uncited passages are listed as text, so the finding does not depend on noticing an absence of highlighting.
The coverage bar is `aria-describedby` the attribution caveat, so "100% attributed" is never announced without "attributed is not verified as supported".
A source entry’s accessible name carries its access state and its age ("Paywalled. Retrieved 3 days ago"), not only the visible chip.
variants: Unsourced — An Answer With Nothing Behind It
Freshness & Access — Sources You Cannot Open
