inputs.name: claims
inputs.description: The answer's claims, as the host's pipeline structured them — an id and the claim's words as rendered. Supply these and a citation's `claimId` is its anchor, ahead of `anchorText` and the offsets. A claim id that is not in this list is reported in the placement notice as a claim the answer does not contain — never quietly re-placed by arithmetic. Leave it empty and `claimId` is identity only, handed back through `(claimsOpened)`.

inputs.name: showCoverage
inputs.description: Show the coverage strip. On by default, because the figure it carries — how much of the answer is attributed, and which passages are not — is the one thing a citation UI cannot show by drawing chips.

inputs.name: allowedUrlProtocols
inputs.description: URL schemes a source link may use. A source URL is model output, which is untrusted input. A retriever returns what the index holds and a model returns what it generated, and either can hand this component a `javascript:` URL. Angular renders that as a dead `unsafe:` link, which is safe and also silent — the reader clicks, nothing happens, and nobody learns the citation was fabricated. A refused URL is shown as text instead, with the scheme named: that the answer cited something unreachable is evidence about the answer.

inputs.name: uncitedMinChars
inputs.description: Shortest uncited stretch worth reporting, in characters. Forty is a sentence in English prose — and two or three sentences in Chinese, where a claim fits in a dozen characters, and most of a bullet in a summary-style answer. A connective is not an unsupported claim, so a floor has to exist; where it sits is a fact about the language and the answer shape, which this component cannot see.

This is how a host persists "the reader checked this". A claim id survives re-generation where offsets and wording do not, so the record still points at the right claim after the answer is rewritten.

components.name: Code Block
components.description: Read-only source display with a zero-dependency highlighter for 9 languages. Four variants — block, multi-file tabs, diff (unified or split with per-hunk accept/reject) and terminal — plus streaming-safe rendering, line numbers, soft wrap, line highlighting, copy-to-clipboard, and a render cap for files too long to draw in full.
whenToUse: Rendering AI-generated code in a chat, artifact panel or completion.
Documenting an API response, config file or install command in an admin UI.
Showing a proposed edit for review, with per-hunk accept and reject.
Displaying CI logs or agent tool output as a terminal transcript.

examples.title: Multi-file tabs
examples.description: Pass an array of files to render a tabbed viewer with roving arrow-key navigation.

examples.title: Reviewable diff
examples.description: Unified or split diff with per-hunk Accept / Reject — the AI-suggested-edit pattern.

examples.title: Streaming buffer
examples.description: The highlighter is pure, so re-running it on a growing buffer keeps a partial response correctly coloured.

examples.title: Terminal transcript
examples.description: Command, stdout, stderr and exit lines are coloured semantically. ANSI escape sequences in the text are stripped, so output pasted straight from a real tool run does not render its colour codes as `[31m` debris.

examples.title: A file too long to render
examples.description: Past `maxRenderedLines` (default 600) the block renders the first N lines and offers a "show all" control below the scroll region. Set `0` to render everything however long. The cap re-arms when a different tab or a replaced buffer arrives — but not while a stream appends to the buffer, so an expanded block stays expanded as an answer arrives — and never applies to the clipboard — copy always takes the whole file.
examples.code:
<!-- render 200 lines, with the rest one button away -->
<sv-code-block [code]="hugeFile" [maxRenderedLines]="200" />

<!-- no cap at all -->
<sv-code-block [code]="hugeFile" [maxRenderedLines]="0" />

examples.title: Computing the diff — the engine lives in core, not here
examples.description: This component RENDERS a diff and computes nothing, which is deliberate: JSON Viewer wanted a JSON diff, Tree View wanted to compare trees and Descriptions wanted to diff a record, and four private half-engines is four sets of edge cases found separately. svDiffLines() in @styloviz/core is the one engine, and its output is the DiffHunk[] this component already takes — no adapter, no mapping. A contract test renders the engine's output through this component so the two cannot drift apart. It takes ignoreWhitespace, ignoreCase and a context width, and svDiffSummary() gives you the sentence that replaces the red and green for a screen reader.

customization: Four variants: `block`, `tabs` (multi-file), `diff` (`unified` / `split`) and `terminal`.

Nine languages — typescript, javascript, html, css, json, bash, python, go, rust — inferred from the file extension or set via `language`. An extension with no rules degrades to plain monospace and says so rather than passing for a language that simply used no keywords.

Zero third-party dependencies: the highlighter is a small rule-based tokenizer that emits a token model, so the template renders it through Angular bindings — no `innerHTML`, no `bypassSecurityTrust*`.

Streaming-safe — `tokenize()` is pure, so re-running it on a growing buffer is cheap; `streaming` adds a caret after the last line. Half-received literals are handled explicitly: an unterminated string, template literal or block comment tokenises as what it is opening, so the colours do not rearrange themselves when the closing quote lands.

`maxRenderedLines` (default 600, `0` disables) caps how many lines are drawn in the `block` and `tabs` variants; the rest is one button away, below the scroll region. A cap rather than virtualisation — a windowed scroller has to own scroll position, row height and gutter alignment, and it breaks find-in-page for the rows it has not built. Copy is never truncated.

Terminal text is passed through an ANSI stripper, so a transcript pasted from real tool output renders as text instead of `[31m` fragments. Escapes are stripped rather than interpreted: `TerminalLine.kind` already drives the colour, and honouring an SGR code would mean two sources of truth for one pixel.
Toggle `lineNumbers`, `wrap`, `showHeader` and `copyable`; emphasise rows with `highlightLines`; cap the scroll region with `maxHeight` and its content with `maxRenderedLines`.
Emits `copied` (the copied text), `tabChange` (the selected file) and `hunkAction` (accept / reject with the hunk), so a host can wire it to real behaviour.
Icons come from `@styloviz/icons` (`sv-copy-icon`, `sv-check-icon`) — restyle or swap them by theming the icon library.
The exported `tokenize()`, `inferLanguage()`, `revealBidi()` and `stripAnsi()` helpers are public, so you can reuse the highlighter — and its two text-safety passes — outside the component.
accessibility: The scrollable body is a `role="region"` with `tabindex="0"` and an accessible name from `ariaLabel` or the file name, so keyboard users can reach and scroll it.
The tab strip is a true `role="tablist"` with `aria-selected`, roving `tabindex`, and Arrow / Home / End navigation.

The copy button states what it will actually copy, in both `aria-label` and `title`: the updated side of a diff without the `+` / `−` markers, the transcript without the `$` prompt, the open tab only, or the code without the line numbers. One icon meaning four different things is not guessable, and every one of those answers is something a person pastes into a terminal. Success is announced through an `aria-live="polite"` status region.

When highlighting falls back, it says so. An extension the highlighter has no rules for renders a "plain text" badge and an `sr-only` "Not syntax highlighted: no rules for .rb. Shown as plain text." linked as the region's description — the failure mode of a highlighter is silence, so it has to announce itself. An explicit `language="plaintext"`, or a name with no extension, is a request rather than a fallback and stays quiet.

The body is pinned `dir="ltr"`. Source reads left-to-right whatever it contains, and inheriting a host `dir="rtl"` would reverse the visual order of every line while leaving the text alone. Each line is additionally `unicode-bidi: isolate`, so a right-to-left run inside one line cannot reorder its neighbours.

Invisible bidirectional control characters are rendered as a visible `<U+202E>` in a warning colour, everywhere the component draws text — tokenised code, diff lines and terminal output. They occupy no width and reorder the glyphs around them, so a line can display as one statement and copy as another (CVE-2021-42574, "Trojan Source"); a diff is the highest-risk place for that, because it is where code gets approved. The clipboard keeps the host's original bytes: rewriting source on the way out would corrupt a legitimate Arabic or Hebrew string literal to defend against a rare hostile one.
Line-number gutters, diff +/- markers and the streaming caret are `aria-hidden`, so screen readers read only the source text.

The truncation notice is a real `<button>` outside the scroll region, not decoration inside it. "There is more file" has to be reachable by keyboard, and placed after the last rendered line it would sit below a screenful of source — the one place a reader has no reason to scroll to.

A diff states its own scale: the region is `aria-describedby` a summary reading "Diff: 3 hunks, 12 added lines, 4 removed lines." The size of a change otherwise reaches the page only as geometry — the header's `+12 −4` chips and the per-line tint — leaving a screen-reader user to walk every line to find out how big it is. It is a DESCRIPTION, not part of the name, so a host `ariaLabel` still names the region and gets the summary too, and the chips are `aria-hidden` because this says it better.

Added and removed lines are prefixed with an `sr-only` "Added:" / "Removed:", in both `unified` and `split` modes. A red or green tint is not information, and in split mode the two columns read as one continuous run of text without it.
Highlighting renders a token model through Angular bindings — no `innerHTML` and no `bypassSecurityTrust*`, so untrusted source is never executed as markup.
variants: Long Files, Plain Text & Invisible Characters

inputs.description: Diff layout. Ignored unless `variant` is `'diff'`.

inputs.name: lineNumbers

inputs.name: wrap

inputs.name: showHeader

inputs.name: copyable

inputs.name: highlightLines

inputs.name: maxHeight

inputs.name: maxRenderedLines
inputs.description: Rendering threshold, in lines. Beyond it the block truncates and offers a "show all" control. `0` renders everything, however long. Applies to `block` and `tabs`. A diff is bounded by its hunks and the terminal transcript by `terminalLines`, so neither needs a cap the caller has not already applied. "Show all" holds until the tab changes or the content is replaced; a buffer that only grows (a streamed answer) stays expanded.

inputs.name: streaming

outputs.name: tabChange

outputs.name: hunkAction

components.name: Color Picker
components.description: HSV gradient canvas picker with hue rail, alpha channel, hex input, preset swatches and 3 sizes.
whenToUse: Letting users pick an arbitrary color (theming, labels, calendars, design tools).
You need HSV selection plus hex entry and brand preset swatches.
For a fixed brand palette only, a swatch list or Select may suffice.
customization: HSV canvas with a hue rail and optional `showAlpha` opacity channel; `format` outputs hex, rgb or hsl.
Hex input plus configurable preset `swatches` ({ label, value }); `label`, `disabled`, three `size`s.
Two-way bind `[(value)]` or a reactive control (CVA); listen to `(colorChange)`.
accessibility: The gradient, hue and opacity controls are `role="slider"` and fully keyboard-operable: Arrow keys adjust (Shift for larger steps), Home/End jump to the ends.
Opening moves focus into the panel; Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger. Swatches expose `aria-label` + `aria-pressed`, and the hex input and sliders are labelled.
Implements ControlValueAccessor — works with `[(ngModel)]`, `[formControl]` and `formControlName`; `formControl.disable()` disables the trigger.

components.name: Command Palette
components.description: Spotlight-style launcher with four looks, 3 sizes, fuzzy search, ⌘K shortcut, grouped results, nested pages, per-command actions, a preview pane, prefix scopes, pinned and suggested commands, an Ask AI fallback, query highlighting, recent history, async/remote loading, disabled commands and keyboard navigation.
whenToUse: Giving power users a fast keyboard launcher for actions and navigation.
Apps with many commands where menus would be unwieldy.
Remote/async command sources — drive `[loading]` from `queryChange`.
For searching data records specifically, use the Search Bar.

examples.title: Remote search without the race
examples.code:
<!-- resultsFor is the host echoing back which term these groups answer.
     Without it the palette cannot tell that a slower response for "de"
     landed after the one for "del": it renders the stale list, highlights
     whatever came first, and Enter runs a command the user never saw
     offered. With it the palette keeps saying "Searching…", marks the
     listbox aria-busy, and refuses to run from a list it knows is stale. -->
<sv-command-palette
  [groups]="results()"
  [serverSide]="true"
  [loading]="searching()"
  [resultsFor]="answeredTerm()"
  (searchRequest)="search($event)" />

examples.title: Cancelling the search the user typed past
Dark variant, large, fuzzy
examples.code:
<sv-command-palette
  [groups]="commandGroups"
  variant="dark"
  size="lg"
  [config]="{ fuzzy: true, placeholder: 'Type a command…' }"
  (commandSelected)="run($event)" />

customization: Four looks (default · dark · glass · minimal), three sizes (sm · md · lg), and `top`, `center` or `spotlight` placement.

A command with `children` opens a page of its own: a breadcrumb chip per level, Backspace on an empty search goes back, and `[(pages)]` holds the stack. `actions` gives a command a sub-menu (→ or ⌘K on the highlighted row, `(subActionSelected)`).

`layout="split"` adds a preview pane for the highlighted command — its `preview` data or template. `scopes` turn a typed prefix (`>`, `#`, `@`, `/`) into a removable chip that searches only its groups.

With the search empty: `[(pinnedCommandIds)]` first (`config.pinnable` adds Pin / Unpin to every actions menu), then Recent, then `suggestedCommandIds`. `config.aiFallback` adds an Ask AI row for whatever was typed (`(aiAsk)`); `config.placeholderHints` rotate in the empty search; the list is windowed above `config.virtualizeAbove` rows (200).
Grouped, searchable commands with substring or fuzzy (subsequence, ranked) matching; recent history and badges.
Configurable/optional global shortcut, `showRecent` toggle, disabled and keep-open commands.

The open shortcut goes through the shared registry: `config.shortcutScope` puts it in the global, route or overlay band — so a palette inside a dialog outranks the app's own instead of competing on equal terms — and a second component claiming the same binding is refused and reported rather than firing alongside it.

A command's `keys` (e.g. `'mod+shift+p'`) is a real binding: it renders itself for the running platform, colliding ones are reported through `(shortcutConflicts)`, and `config.bindCommandKeys` registers them so pressing one runs the command through the same path a click takes. `shortcut` remains the display-only glyph array.
Rendered into `document.body` via a portal, so it always covers the full viewport and is never clipped by a parent `overflow`/`transform`.
Return a `Promise` from a command `action` for an inline loading spinner; remote sources use `[loading]` + `queryChange`; failures keep the palette open with an error state and emit `commandError`.
accessibility: Combobox semantics with `aria-activedescendant` on the search input tracking the active result; `role="listbox"`/`option` results with `aria-selected` and `aria-disabled`.

Full keyboard control (↑↓ skip disabled, Enter, Esc, Tab); focus returns to the prior element on close — and if a command removes that element (a navigation tearing down the old view), focus moves to a surviving neighbour or the main landmark once the exit transition ends, instead of `<body>`. Opened with nothing focused, it hands focus to the main landmark.

With `resultsFor`, rows that answer an older term — including during the debounce window, before the new term has been requested — stay on screen dimmed but `inert`, are dropped from `aria-activedescendant`, and cannot be run.
Running commands set `aria-busy`; async failures are announced via an assertive live region.
Forced colours: the panel (the glass variant included) keeps a `CanvasText` edge when its tint and ring are stripped.

inputs.name: groups
inputs.description: Command groups to display. Provide all available commands here.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Optional configuration for placeholder, empty message and recent limit.

inputs.name: portalClass
inputs.description: Classes applied to the body-portal container. The overlay is instantiated into `document.body` so its fixed backdrop escapes any ancestor `overflow`/`transform`/`filter` containment, which also means it is outside every scoped class on the host: a `.dark` on a section root or a `.tpl-*` token scope does not reach it. Pass the scopes the palette should inherit, e.g. `portalClass="dark tpl-dev"`; without them the palette opens light on a dark section and uses the kit's default accent.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Panel theme.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Panel width preset.

inputs.name: placement
inputs.description: Vertical anchoring of the panel.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: External loading flag — set true while a parent fetches remote results (drive it from `queryChange`). Shows a loading row in the results area.

inputs.name: serverSide
inputs.description: Let the server do the matching. The supplied `groups` are shown exactly as given — a palette over a large workspace searches documents and people, not just the commands already in the browser.

inputs.name: debounceMs
inputs.description: Delay before `queryChange` fires, in ms. `0` emits immediately. A palette wants this short — it is the primary interaction, not a filter.

inputs.name: minChars
inputs.description: Characters required before a remote search is sent. Below this the palette says so instead of "No results found".

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Failure loading commands, rendered in place of the list.

inputs.name: resultsFor
inputs.description: Which term the supplied `groups` are the answer to. Without this the palette cannot know its results are stale, and is exactly that. The host answers "de" and then "del"; the slower "de" response lands second and the list shows commands for a term the user has already typed past. Nothing in the markup looks wrong, and the palette has no way to tell — `groups` is just an array. And it is worse than cosmetic. The highlighted row is whatever the stale list put first, so Enter runs a command the user never saw offered for what they typed. Set this and the palette keeps saying "Searching…", marks the listbox `aria-busy`, refuses to run a command from a list it knows is out of date, and — the quiet one — does NOT say "No results found" about an answer to a different question. Echo back the `term` the palette handed you. Only consulted with `serverSide`.

inputs.name: layout
inputs.description: `'split'` adds a preview pane beside the list for the highlighted command — its `preview` template or data, or its icon, label and shortcut.

inputs.name: scopes
inputs.description: Prefix scopes: typing a scope's prefix first (`>` commands, `#` channels, `@` people, `/` pages) turns it into a removable chip and searches only its groups. Backspace on an empty search removes it.

inputs.name: pinnedCommandIds
inputs.description: Ids of pinned commands, shown first when the search is empty (two-way). With `config.pinnable`, every command's actions menu can pin and unpin.

inputs.name: suggestedCommandIds
inputs.description: Ids of suggested commands, shown after Pinned and Recent when the search is empty.

inputs.name: pages
inputs.description: The page stack — ids of the commands drilled into, outermost first (two-way). Set it to open the palette on a page; it empties on close.

inputs.name: canClose
inputs.description: Host veto over a USER-initiated close — Escape or the backdrop. The same `canClose` Modal, Drawer and Confirm Dialog take, so a half-typed multi-step command need not be lost to a stray backdrop click. Return `false` to keep the palette open; `closeCancelled` reports the refusal. `close()` stays unconditional: a host calling it IS the decision, the same rule `createCloseGuard` applies everywhere (`programmatic` is always allowed).

inputs.name: recentCommandIds
inputs.description: IDs of recently selected commands, most-recent first (two-way). A `model` because a most-recently-used list that only lives in the component is reset by every page load — the one thing an MRU list must survive. Bind it to restore what you stored, and read `(recentCommandIdsChange)` to store it. IDs that do not match a command in `groups` are ignored, so a stale saved list is safe to hand back verbatim.

outputs.name: opened
outputs.description: Emitted when the palette opens.

outputs.name: closed
outputs.description: Emitted when the palette closes (any method).

outputs.name: closeCancelled
outputs.description: A user close (Escape / backdrop) was vetoed by `canClose`.

outputs.name: queryChange
outputs.description: Emitted whenever the search query changes (debounce/fetch in the parent).

outputs.name: searchRequest
outputs.description: The same change, with a token and an `AbortSignal`. Emitted immediately after `queryChange`, for hosts that want to cancel the request the user has typed past rather than let it finish and be discarded. Ignore it and nothing changes.

outputs.name: commandSelected
outputs.description: Emitted when a command is confirmed (before its action runs).

outputs.name: commandError
outputs.description: Emitted when an async command's action rejects.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The host should re-run the failed command load.

outputs.name: shortcutConflicts
outputs.description: Two or more commands declare the same `keys`. Reported whether or not anything is bound. Duplicate shortcuts were "undetected" because `shortcut` was a list of glyphs nobody parsed — two commands could claim ⌘K and the palette would draw both. Detection is a pure check over the command list, so it does not wait for `bindCommandKeys`: two commands claiming one binding is a bug in the list either way.

outputs.name: aiAsk
outputs.description: "Ask AI" was chosen (`config.aiFallback`) — the search, as typed.

outputs.name: scopeChange
outputs.description: A prefix scope was turned on, or off (`null`).

outputs.name: subActionSelected
outputs.type: { readonly command: CommandAction; readonly action: CommandSubAction }
outputs.description: A sub-action was run from a command's actions menu.

outputs.name: pinnedCommandIdsChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `pinnedCommandIds` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(pinnedCommandIds)]`.

outputs.name: pagesChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `pages` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(pages)]`.

outputs.name: recentCommandIdsChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `recentCommandIds` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(recentCommandIds)]`.

components.name: Comment Thread
components.description: Threaded comment display with depth-limited nested replies, an inline reply box, emoji reactions, relative timestamps and an avatar/initials fallback.
whenToUse: Displaying discussion threads with nested replies and reactions.
You want inline reply, emoji reactions and relative timestamps out of the box.
For inline @-references inside a single field, use the Mention input.

examples.title: Persisting a reaction, and putting it back
examples.description: The pill lights up and its count moves on press — it does not wait for you, because a reaction that needs a round trip reads as a dead button. That leaves the component holding the only copy of the pre-toggle value, so the event carries rollback(). Bind busyIds: it locks the comment while the write is in flight, which is what keeps rollback() unambiguous. Send requestKey so a retried request cannot count the same reaction twice.

examples.title: Product reviews (rating + verified + helpful)
examples.description: variant="review" renders each entry as a product review: a star rating, a verified-purchase badge and a helpful-vote button.

examples.title: Deleting a comment that has replies
examples.description: Dropping the node drops the replies with it. That is fine for a leaf and it is data loss for a parent, because the author asked for their own words to go and not for everyone else's. Mark the parent deleted and leave it in the array: the component renders a tombstone in its place — content, identity, reactions and every action withheld, timestamp kept so the conversation still reads in order — and the replies render underneath it.

examples.title: Reporting a failure on the comment that caused it
examples.description: error renders once, at the top. In a thread of forty that puts the message a screenful away from the button that produced it, and a second failure overwrites the first. commentErrors is keyed by comment id, renders beside the comment, and reaches nested replies. Key a failed reply by the parentId — the reply itself was never posted and has no id yet.

customization: Replies below `maxDepth` are flattened into one list at the last level, in thread order, each with a "Replying to <name>" line — never dropped. `collapseReplies` puts every reply list behind a "Show N replies" disclosure (N counts every depth). `timeZone` (IANA) sets the zone absolute times are written in; the zone is always named.
Cap nesting with `maxDepth` and toggle the inline `showReplyBox`.
Identify the viewer via `currentUserId` to reveal inline Edit and Delete on their own comments.
Handle `reply`, `react`, `edit` and `delete` outputs to persist changes.
Reactions are optimistic: the pill and its count move on press and are reconciled against the next `comments` value you supply, so nothing has to be re-rendered to make a press feel immediate.
`busyIds` locks one comment's controls mid-write and reaches nested replies automatically; `error` reports a failed action above the thread, `loading` / `loadError` / `retryLoad` cover the fetch.
Comment bodies wrap long words and URLs (`break-words`) so they never overflow the bubble on narrow screens.
A `review` variant renders comments as product reviews (star rating, verified-purchase badge and helpful votes); the Comment type gains `rating`, `verified` and `helpfulCount`.
`deleted: true` renders a tombstone in place of a comment — withheld content and identity, no actions, timestamp kept, replies intact — and `deletedMessage` supplies the wording.
`commentErrors` is a map of comment id to failure, rendered beside that comment and passed down to nested replies; `error` stays for a failure that belongs to no comment on screen.
accessibility: Every timestamp is a `<time datetime>` with the absolute date, time and zone as its tooltip and in the spoken text ("30m ago, October 24, 2026 at 11:30 AM UTC"); the relative label refreshes once a minute. The reply toggle is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`.

Reaction toggles expose `aria-pressed` and a descriptive label (emoji + count), so state is not conveyed by color alone — and both track the optimistic value, so the announced state matches what is drawn.
A comment in `busyIds` disables its pills, Delete and Send and marks them `aria-busy`, so an in-flight write is announced rather than only implied by an unresponsive button.
Opening reply or edit moves focus into the textarea, which carries an explicit label; Edit exposes `aria-expanded`.
Timestamps expose readable values and avatars fall back to initials with an accessible name.

Focus is never dropped: posting a reply returns it to that comment's Reply button, saving or cancelling an edit returns it to Edit, and a failed delete returns it to Delete. Each of those controls destroys the element that had focus, and the browser's only fallback is the top of the page.

A confirmed delete moves focus to the comment that took its place — the previous one when the last comment goes, the thread itself when none is left — and announces the removal in a polite live region, since a comment simply ceasing to exist is otherwise silent.
variants: Persisting a reaction, and putting it back
Deleting a parent, and a delete that fails

inputs.name: comments
inputs.description: Array of top-level comments with optional nested replies.

inputs.name: currentUserId
inputs.description: ID of the currently logged-in user (for "edit/delete own" logic).

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP 47 locale for dates and numbers.

inputs.name: showReplyBox
inputs.description: Show inline reply box below each comment.

inputs.name: maxDepth
inputs.description: Maximum nesting depth. Replies below it are not dropped: they are FLATTENED into one list at the last level, in thread order, each saying who it replies to.

inputs.name: collapseReplies
inputs.description: Start every reply list collapsed behind a "Show N replies" button (N counts replies at every depth). `false` shows them all.

inputs.name: timeZone
inputs.description: IANA time zone the absolute timestamps are written in, e.g. `'Europe/Berlin'`. The zone is always named, because "yesterday" and "14:05" mean nothing without it.

inputs.name: replyToNames
inputs.description: Who each comment replies to, by comment id — set by the thread itself on a list flattened past `maxDepth`; hosts leave it empty.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Display mode: threaded discussion, or a product-review list.

inputs.name: busyIds
inputs.description: Ids of actions with a request in flight. Those controls disable and show a busy state, so a double-click cannot fire the same request twice — the most common way an action button creates duplicate records.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Failure from the last action, when it belongs to no single comment. Rendered above the thread; nothing is removed from view, so the user can see what state things are in. Prefer `commentErrors` for anything that failed on a comment that is on screen — see the note there.

inputs.name: commentErrors
inputs.description: Failures keyed by comment id, rendered beside the comment they belong to. `error` above renders once, at the top. That is right for a failure with no place on the page and wrong for every failure this component actually produces: a reply, an edit, a delete and a reaction all name a comment, and a thread of forty puts the message a screenful away from the button that caused it. Worse, a second failure overwrites the first, so a user who retried two comments sees one message and cannot tell which one it is about. Key a reply failure by its `parentId` — the comment being replied to is what is on screen; the reply itself was never posted and has no id yet. Unlike `error`, this map DOES go down the tree: it is keyed, so a nested reply's failure lands on the reply and nowhere else.

inputs.name: deletedMessage
inputs.description: Copy for a comment the host has tombstoned (`deleted: true`).

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the thread itself is being fetched. Distinct from `busyIds`, which marks individual comments whose *action* is in flight.

inputs.name: loadError
inputs.description: The thread could not be loaded. The `…Load` spelling exists because `error` above is already taken, and it means something else: *the reply you just posted failed*. That is a different event with a different recovery — the control is still on screen and you retry by pressing it again, so it is deliberately not retryable. A failed *fetch* leaves nothing to press, so it gets its own error and its own retry. Same precedent as `sv-toolbar` and `sv-tool-call-card`; overloading one input with both meanings is what the rule exists to stop.

inputs.name: emptyMessage
inputs.description: Copy for the zero-comment state.

inputs.name: filtered
inputs.description: Whether a filter or search is narrowing the thread, so the empty state can say *no matching comments* rather than *no comments* — telling someone with four hundred comments that there are none reads as a bug.

inputs.name: expandedReplies
inputs.description: Ids of comments whose replies are open while `collapseReplies` is on. Two-way, so a host can restore what the reader had opened after a route change.

outputs.name: retryLoad
outputs.description: The host should re-fetch the thread. Pairs with `loadError`, not `error`.

outputs.name: reply
outputs.description: Emitted when a reply is submitted.

outputs.name: react
outputs.description: A reaction pill was toggled. The pill has already moved — persist it, or call `rollback()`.

outputs.name: delete
outputs.description: Emitted when a comment is deleted.

outputs.name: edit
outputs.description: Emitted when an owned comment is edited and saved.

outputs.name: helpful
outputs.description: Emitted when a review is marked helpful (review variant).

outputs.name: expandedRepliesChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `expandedReplies` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(expandedReplies)]`.

components.name: Confirm Dialog
components.description: Focused confirmation modal with 6 variants, 3 sizes and three icon styles, a type-to-confirm guard, an acknowledge checkbox, a countdown or press-and-hold confirm, a reason field, single-button acknowledge mode, loading state, custom labels and async support.
whenToUse: Getting explicit confirmation before a destructive or irreversible action.
High-risk deletes — use `requireText` so users type a phrase to confirm.
Informational acknowledgements — use `hideCancel` for a single-button dialog.
For reversible actions, an Undo toast is friendlier than a confirm.

examples.title: Async confirm with loading
examples.code:
<!-- keepOpenOnConfirm is REQUIRED here: without it the dialog closes
     in the same tick as (confirmed) fires and the spinner never renders. -->
<sv-confirm-dialog
  [(open)]="ask"
  variant="danger"
  title="Delete project?"
  confirmLabel="Delete"
  [loading]="deleting"
  [keepOpenOnConfirm]="true"
  (confirmed)="onDelete()"
  (cancelled)="ask = false" />

examples.title: Hand the dialog the work — [action]
examples.code:
<!-- The dialog owns the request: a second click is refused rather than
     queued, a rejection is rendered in place with a Try again button (only
     when retrying could plausibly succeed), and pendingDismissal says
     whether the user may back out while it is running. -->
<sv-confirm-dialog
  [(open)]="ask"
  variant="danger"
  title="Delete project?"
  confirmLabel="Delete"
  [action]="deleteProject"
  pendingDismissal="abort"
  (actionCompleted)="toast('Project deleted')"
  (actionFailed)="log($event)" />

examples.title: The action itself
Type-to-confirm guard
examples.code:
<sv-confirm-dialog
  [(open)]="ask"
  variant="danger"
  title="Delete this project?"
  requireText="DELETE"
  confirmLabel="Delete project"
  [showClose]="true"
  [keepOpenOnConfirm]="true"
  (confirmed)="onDelete()" />

examples.title: Acknowledge (single button)
examples.code: <sv-confirm-dialog [open]="ok" variant="success" [hideCancel]="true" title="You're all set" confirmLabel="Got it" (confirmed)="ok = false" />

customization: Six semantic variants (danger · warning · info · success · primary · neutral) and three sizes (sm · md · lg).
Type-to-confirm guard (`requireText`), single-button acknowledge mode (`hideCancel`), optional close (×) button.
Custom confirm/cancel labels, custom or hidden icon, and configurable initial focus.

The look: `iconStyle` (`ring` · `tile` · `plain`), `align` (`start` · `center`), `footer` (`plain` · `inset`), `backdrop` (`blur` · `dim` · `none`), `buttonLayout` (`inline` · `stacked`) and `mobileSheet` for a bottom sheet on a phone.

Friction for the irreversible: a `consequences` list, an `acknowledgeLabel` checkbox that must be ticked, a `confirmDelayMs` countdown on the button, a `confirmHoldMs` press-and-hold, and a `reasonLabel` field (`reasonRequired`, `[(reason)]`) — each off until you set it. `error` shows a failure from a host-driven request.
Rendered into `document.body` via a portal, so it always covers the full viewport and is never clipped by a parent `overflow`/`transform`/`backdrop-filter`.
Backdrop / ESC toggles, async `loading`, manual `confirmDisabled`; scroll-lock with scrollbar-width compensation; `customClass` on the panel.

`[canClose]` is a veto over every dismissal path — Cancel, Escape, the backdrop and the × button — and it is told WHICH path it is being asked about, so a host can refuse the backdrop and allow the button. Shared with Modal and Drawer via `createCloseGuard`; there is no unsaved-changes prompt here, because this dialog holds a decision rather than a form.
`keepOpenOnConfirm` hands the close back to the host so an async confirm can show its loading state, then close (or stay open and show an error).

`[action]` hands the work to the dialog instead: first-wins (a second press is refused, not queued), a normalized error rendered in place, a Try again button only when the failure is retryable, `pendingDismissal` deciding whether the user may back out mid-flight, and `actionCompleted` / `actionFailed` reporting the outcome. One async contract, shared with the rest of the kit — `createAsyncAction` in `@styloviz/core`.
accessibility: `role="alertdialog"` + `aria-modal`, labelled/described via per-instance unique ids; body scroll locks while open.
On open, focus moves to the type-to-confirm field (if present) or the configured button and Tab is trapped; on close, focus returns to the trigger.
`opened`/`closed` fire for every transition; cancel/close are blocked while busy unless `pendingDismissal="abort"`, in which case the Cancel and × buttons stay enabled and abort the request.
If the focused trigger is removed because the action succeeded (the deleted row), focus moves to a surviving neighbour in the same list, then the main landmark — never `<body>`.
After a failed `[action]`, focus moves to Try again (or Confirm), because the button the user pressed was swapped or disabled and focus would otherwise fall out of the dialog.
A failed `[action]` is announced: the message renders in a `role="alert"` beside the buttons, so a screen reader hears the failure rather than a dialog that simply refused to close.

inputs.name: open
inputs.description: Controls visibility. Use `[(open)]` for two-way binding.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Semantic variant — controls icon, icon color, and confirm button style.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Panel size.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Dialog title.

inputs.name: description
inputs.description: Descriptive body text.

inputs.name: confirmLabel
inputs.description: Label for the confirm button.

inputs.name: cancelLabel
inputs.description: Label for the cancel button.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: Show a loading spinner on the confirm button (e.g. while async action runs).

inputs.name: confirmDisabled
inputs.description: Manually disable the confirm button (in addition to loading/requireText).

inputs.name: hideCancel
inputs.description: Hide the cancel button for single-action acknowledge dialogs.

inputs.name: showIcon
inputs.description: Show the built-in variant icon.

inputs.name: icon
inputs.description: Icon-library name that replaces the variant's default icon, e.g. 'trash'.

inputs.name: showClose
inputs.description: Show a close (×) button in the top-right corner.

inputs.name: requireText
inputs.description: Require the user to type this text before Confirm is enabled (type-to-confirm guard for high-risk destructive actions). Empty = off. The comparison is not `===`. An exact code-point comparison fails for a phrase the user typed correctly: `é` can be one code point (U+00E9) or two (`e` + U+0301), the two render identically, and which one you get depends on the keyboard, the input method and the operating system. What is compared: the phrase and the typed text, each NFC-normalized, trimmed, and with internal runs of whitespace collapsed. Only differences the user CANNOT SEE are folded away. Everything visible still counts — accents (`cafe` must not delete `café`) and, by default, case, which stays significant because slowing the user down is the guard's job; `requireTextCaseSensitive` is the way out of that.

inputs.name: requireTextLabel
inputs.description: Label shown above the type-to-confirm field.

inputs.name: requireTextCaseSensitive
inputs.description: Whether the typed phrase must match the case of `requireText`.

inputs.name: requireTextLocale
inputs.description: BCP-47 tag for the comparison, e.g. `'tr'`. Defaults to the runtime locale. Consulted ONLY when `requireTextCaseSensitive` is false, because case folding is the one part of this comparison that is language-dependent — and it matters most where it is least likely to be tested: Turkish, Azeri, Lithuanian. A host that localises `requireText` should pass the matching tag.

inputs.name: requireTextMatcher
inputs.description: Replace the built-in comparison with the host's own. For the case no normalization can reach: a phrase that is a resource NAME, shown translated. The user reads "Rechnungen" and the id is "Invoices"; no amount of case folding or NFC makes those equal, and only the host knows they are the same thing. Both arguments arrive canonical (NFC, trimmed, whitespace collapsed), so the matcher never re-implements that. A matcher that THROWS refuses the phrase — a guard on a destructive action fails closed.

inputs.name: initialFocus
inputs.description: Which control receives focus on open.

inputs.name: keepOpenOnConfirm
inputs.description: Keep the dialog open when Confirm is pressed, leaving the close to the host.

inputs.name: action
inputs.description: The work to perform when Confirm is pressed, owned by the dialog. `(confirmed)` alone is a notification: the dialog hands the intent over and never learns what happened. So a rejection has nowhere to go (the host must invent its own error surface), a second click can send the destructive request twice (`[disabled]` applies on the next change-detection pass, which is after the second click has been dispatched), and there is no retry state. Give it the work and all three fall out of `createAsyncAction`: first-wins so the double submit is refused rather than queued, a normalized `SvDataError` rendered in place, and a Try-again button — but only when the failure could plausibly succeed again, because a 403 will fail identically and offering a retry for it wastes the user's time twice. `(confirmed)` also emits, once per accepted press. Wiring BOTH means doing the work twice — pick one. ```html <sv-confirm-dialog [(open)]="confirming" [action]="deleteInvoice" pendingDismissal="abort" (actionFailed)="log($event)" /> ``` ```ts protected readonly deleteInvoice = (req: SvRequest) => this.api.delete(this.id(), req.signal); ```

inputs.name: pendingDismissal
inputs.description: May the user dismiss the dialog while the action is in flight? `'block'` (the default) keeps Cancel, Escape and the backdrop blocked while the action runs. That is right for a short request and wrong for a slow one the user has changed their mind about, where the dialog would simply stop responding. `'abort'` aborts the request through its `AbortSignal` and closes, which is only honest when the work actually passes `request.signal` to its transport.

inputs.name: retryLabel
inputs.description: Label for the retry button shown after a failed action.

inputs.name: canClose
inputs.description: The host's own veto over every dismissal path. `pendingDismissal` answers the async half — may the user back out while the action is running — and this is the other one: may they back out at all, right now, for a reason only the host knows. A wizard step that must be acknowledged, a license the user has to accept, a dialog that is the last thing standing between an operator and an irreversible batch. Same primitive as modal and drawer (`createCloseGuard`), so the three answer it identically: return `false` to refuse, return nothing to have no opinion. A veto is silent — the host refused for its own reasons and owns its own messaging. There is no unsaved-changes prompt here: this dialog holds a decision, not a form. ```html <sv-confirm-dialog [canClose]="mustAcknowledge" /> ``` ```ts protected readonly mustAcknowledge = () => this.acknowledged(); ```

inputs.name: closeOnBackdrop

inputs.name: closeOnEsc
inputs.description: Close on the ESC key.

inputs.name: customClass

inputs.name: iconStyle
inputs.description: The featured icon: a ringed disc, a rounded tile, or the glyph alone.

inputs.name: align

inputs.name: footer

inputs.name: backdrop

inputs.name: buttonLayout

inputs.name: mobileSheet

inputs.name: consequences

inputs.name: acknowledgeLabel

inputs.name: confirmDelayMs

inputs.name: error

inputs.name: labels

outputs.name: cancelled
