components.name: Context Menu
components.description: The right-click context menu built on Dropdown Menu — same items, theming and keyboard nav, opened at the cursor via `triggerMode="contextmenu"` or the public `openAt(x, y)` method instead of a click-toggled trigger.
whenToUse: A per-row or per-cell action menu in a table, list, canvas node, or file tree, triggered by right-click.
One menu instance shared across many rows — repopulate `items`/`groups` and call `openAt()` per target, rather than mounting a menu per row.
For a single wrapped element with nothing else driving it, `triggerMode="contextmenu"` is simpler than wiring `openAt()` yourself.

examples.title: One shared menu across many rows
examples.code: @for (row of rows; track row.id) { {{ row.name }} } // component onRowContextMenu(event: MouseEvent, row: Row) { event.preventDefault(); this.activeRow.set(row); this.menu.openAt(event.clientX, event.clientY); } onRowKebab(event: MouseEvent, row: Row) { event.stopPropagation(); this.activeRow.set(row); // The kebab's rect, not the click point: Enter/Space click at (0, 0). this.menu.openAtElement(event.currentTarget as HTMLElement); }

examples.title: Keep the browser menu on links and fields
examples.code: …row with a link…

customization: Everything Dropdown Menu supports — items/groups, icons, descriptions, shortcuts, badges, danger items, themes and sizes — applies unchanged.
`triggerMode="contextmenu"` disables the wrapped trigger's left-click toggle in favor of its native right-click.
`openAt(x, y)` works regardless of `triggerMode`, for menus with no rendered trigger element at all; `openAtElement(el)` anchors to an element's live rect instead — the kebab-button path.
`nativeMenuSelector` (opt-in) names the regions inside the trigger where the browser's own context menu wins — links, fields, prose — so suppression is narrow rather than blanket.

`[sheetOnNarrow]="true"` turns the panel into a bottom sheet below 640px — full-bleed, rounded at the top only, padded clear of the home indicator and lifted above the virtual keyboard. At 375px an anchored panel is clamped until it covers the thing it points at, and a context menu's anchor is a cursor POINT, which is the case with the least room of all. Off by default, because it changes how an existing app looks on a phone.

Three ways in, not one: right-click, a long press on touch (500ms, abandoned if the finger travels — a slow scroll over a right-clickable list is not a menu request), and Space or Enter from the keyboard. The keyboard path anchors the menu to the trigger rather than to a cursor, which is the APG position: there is no pointer in a keyboard interaction, and inventing one would put the menu where the user is not looking.
Nested submenus work in a context menu exactly as in a dropdown: give an item `children`.
accessibility: Same `menu`/`menuitem` ARIA roles and keyboard navigation as Dropdown Menu — a context menu opened at the cursor is still fully keyboard-operable once focus reaches it.

It can be OPENED from the keyboard, not just navigated once open: with nothing focusable projected as a trigger, the wrapper is promoted to `role="button"` with a tab stop, and both Space and Enter open the menu.

And from touch: a right-click menu has no touch path at all — there is no right button, and iOS Safari fires no `contextmenu` event for a long press on a non-selectable element — so a held touch opens it. Mouse and pen are excluded deliberately: a mouse has the right button already, and a held left press is how a drag or a text selection starts.

Set `targetLabel` to what the actions act on. Without it the panel announces itself as "Menu" and then reads "Edit, Duplicate, Delete" — every item true, and no way to tell which of forty rows they belong to. With it the panel's name becomes "Actions for Invoice 4021". A shared menu with no projected trigger (the `openAt()` / `openAtElement()` pattern) moves DOM focus into the panel on open, so that name is read as focus arrives and `aria-activedescendant` is published on the focused panel; Escape returns focus to the kebab that opened it. A promoted wrap-one-element trigger keeps focus and carries the target in its own name ("Open Actions for Invoice 4021").
Shift+F10 and the ContextMenu key open it from the focused trigger in `contextmenu` mode — the platform-standard keyboard equivalents of a right-click.

The native context menu is suppressed on the trigger whenever `triggerMode="contextmenu"` is set. Shift+right-click is not a reliable escape hatch: that bypass is Firefox behaviour, not Chromium or WebKit. Suppression has a real cost — copy, paste, open-in-new-tab and translate all go with it — so narrow it with `nativeMenuSelector` (e.g. `a[href], input, textarea`) and never suppress on a region whose value is those actions.
variants: Accessibility — a closed menu is really closed
Context Menu — One shared menu across many rows
Context Menu — Checkable, disabled & destructive items

inputs.name: open
inputs.description: Controls menu visibility. Use `[(open)]` for two-way binding.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the menu's contents are being fetched — a permissions-aware or workspace-scoped menu is a list the server owns.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Load failure. Use `toSvDataError()` from `@styloviz/core` to normalize an `HttpErrorResponse`.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: Flat list of menu items, rendered as a single ungrouped section; ignored when `groups` is non-empty.

inputs.name: groups
inputs.description: Grouped menu items. Takes precedence over `items`.

inputs.name: placement
inputs.description: Where the menu opens relative to its anchor. Same flip/clamp resolution applies whether the anchor is the trigger's bounding rect (click mode) or a point (`openAt()` / right-click) — for a point, `bottom-start` means "top-left corner of the panel at the cursor," which is the conventional context-menu placement.

inputs.name: itemAction
inputs.description: The work an item performs, run by the menu. `(itemClick)` alone is a notification: the menu emits the id and closes in the same tick, so a slow action shows nothing to say the click registered. Give the menu the work and the menu stays open, the row shows a spinner and goes `aria-busy`, a second click on it is refused rather than queued (first click wins), and a rejection is rendered in the menu. `(itemClick)` and `(itemSelect)` also emit for every accepted click. Wiring both this and a click handler does the work twice.

inputs.name: triggerMode
inputs.description: How the menu opens — left-click toggle, or right-click at the cursor. See DropdownMenuTriggerMode.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Panel theme.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Density preset.

inputs.name: offset
inputs.description: Gap between the trigger and the panel (px).

inputs.name: flip
inputs.description: Flip to the opposite side when there's no room; always clamps to viewport.

inputs.name: closeOnSelect
inputs.description: Close the menu after selecting an item (per-item `keepOpen` overrides).

inputs.name: submenuOpenDelay
inputs.description: Hover time before an item with `children` opens its submenu, in ms. Long enough that a pointer sweeping down the list does not flash every submenu it crosses.

inputs.name: submenuCloseDelay
inputs.description: Grace before an open submenu closes once the pointer moves to another item, in ms — applied while the pointer is inside the safe corridor toward the submenu (`svInSafeCorridor`), so a diagonal path to it does not close it on the way. Outside the corridor the submenu switches after `submenuOpenDelay`.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Prevent the menu from opening.

inputs.name: minWidth
inputs.description: Minimum width of the menu panel (px).

inputs.name: triggerRole
inputs.description: ARIA role for the trigger WRAPPER, or `null` to leave it generic. The wrapper is a layout `<div>` that provides the bounding rect to anchor against. That is invisible to a host — until the host is a composite whose own role requires the trigger to be one of its owned children: a `role="menubar"` must own `role="menuitem"`s, and a roleless div in between breaks that ownership. Passing `'none'` takes the wrapper out of the accessibility tree so the composite owns the button directly. `'none'` also stops the menu writing `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-owns` and `aria-activedescendant` at all, so the composite is the single writer: `panelId` and `activeDescendantId` are public for exactly that, and `sv-menubar` binds all five itself. In the default case the menu writes its state on the projected trigger — the element that takes focus — not on this wrapper.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible label for the menu (role="menu").

inputs.name: targetLabel
inputs.description: What these actions act ON — a row, a file, a record.

inputs.name: nativeMenuSelector
inputs.description: Right-clicks inside an element matching this selector keep the BROWSER's context menu.

inputs.name: customClass
inputs.description: Extra CSS classes merged onto the menu panel.

inputs.name: sheetOnNarrow
inputs.description: Become a bottom sheet on a narrow viewport.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The host should re-run the failed load.

outputs.name: itemClick
outputs.description: Emits the id of the clicked item.

outputs.name: itemActionFailed
outputs.description: An `[itemAction]` rejected. The menu stays open and shows the message.

outputs.name: itemSelect
outputs.description: Emits the full clicked item object.

outputs.name: opened
outputs.description: Emitted after the menu opens (by any means, including `[(open)]`).

outputs.name: closed
outputs.description: Emitted after the menu closes (by any means, including `[(open)]`).

outputs.name: openChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `open` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(open)]`.

components.name: Cookie Consent
components.description: A GDPR / ePrivacy cookie banner: a bottom banner, a corner card or a modal dialog, "Reject all" exactly as prominent as "Accept all", per-category native switches with nothing optional pre-ticked, and a consent record — the choices, an ISO timestamp and your policy version — for you to store and hand back.
whenToUse: Any public site that sets non-essential cookies or similar storage (analytics, marketing pixels, embedded players) for visitors covered by the GDPR, the UK GDPR or the ePrivacy Directive.
Gating third-party scripts: load each one only once `(recorded)` or `(restored)` says its category is allowed.
A "Cookie settings" page or footer link, through `openPreferences()` or `[(preferencesOpen)]`.
Not for terms-of-service acceptance or marketing-email opt-ins — those are separate consents with their own records.

examples.title: Your own categories
examples.code:
<sv-cookie-consent
  version="2026-10"
  privacyHref="/privacy"
  [categories]="[
    { id: 'necessary', label: 'Strictly necessary', required: true },
    { id: 'analytics', label: 'Analytics', description: 'Anonymous visit counts.' },
    { id: 'marketing', label: 'Marketing' }
  ]"
  (recorded)="store($event)" />

examples.title: A "Cookie settings" link in the footer
examples.code:
<!-- Withdrawing consent must be as easy as giving it. -->
<sv-cookie-consent #cookies version="2026-10" [record]="saved()" (recorded)="saved.set($event)" />
<footer>
  <button type="button" (click)="cookies.openPreferences()">Cookie settings</button>
</footer>

examples.title: Re-ask when the policy changes
examples.code:
<!-- A stored record with an older version re-opens the banner, says the
     policy changed and starts from the visitor's previous choices. -->
<sv-cookie-consent version="2026-10" [record]="storedRecord" (recorded)="persist($event)" />

examples.title: Let it keep the record (opt-in)
examples.code:
<!-- Versioned envelope in localStorage, read once in the browser after the
     first render — never on the server. Without storageKey it stores nothing. -->
<sv-cookie-consent version="2026-10" storageKey="acme.cookie-consent" (restored)="loadAllowed($event)" />

customization: Three layouts: `banner` (full-width bottom bar), `corner` (compact card, `corner="start" | "end"`) and `modal` (a native dialog up front).
`[inline]="true"` renders the banner or card in normal flow — for previews, docs and settings pages.
With no `categories`, four built-in ones (strictly necessary, functional, analytics, marketing) are worded from the labels and translate with the kit's language packs.
Every string comes from the `cookieConsent` labels — `provideSvLabels(SV_COOKIE_CONSENT_LABELS_DE)` or the per-instance `labels` input.
Buttons and switches paint from the `primary-*` tokens, so a template that remaps primary recolours them.
Persistence is yours by default (`(recorded)`, `[record]`, `[(consent)]`); `storageKey` opts in to a versioned localStorage envelope.
accessibility: The banner is a `role="region"` landmark with an accessible name. It is not a dialog: it never moves focus or blocks the page, so it does not interrupt a keyboard or screen-reader user.
Preferences open in a native `<dialog>` via `showModal()`: the page behind is inert, Escape closes it, focus moves to its heading and returns to the control that opened it.

Each category is a native `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">` with a `<label>` and `aria-describedby` pointing at its description, so Space toggles it and its state is announced as on/off. A required category is checked and disabled, with a visible "Always on" badge.
Recording a choice is announced through a polite `role="status"` region, because the banner it was made in disappears.
Under forced colours the switches fall back to the platform checkbox, so their state stays visible.

inputs.name: categories
inputs.description: The purposes the visitor chooses between. Empty uses four built-in ones — strictly necessary (required), functional, analytics and marketing — worded from the labels, so they translate with the rest. Rows with an empty or duplicate `id` are skipped.

inputs.name: consent
inputs.description: The visitor's choices, category id → allowed. Two-way: bind `[(consent)]` to restore and keep them. Updated only when the visitor decides — toggling a switch changes nothing until "Save choices". Unknown ids are ignored and a missing optional id counts as refused.

inputs.name: record
inputs.description: The visitor's stored record, if any. With the current `version` the banner starts closed and `consent` is restored from it; with an older one the banner re-asks, says the policy changed and starts from the old choices.

inputs.name: version
inputs.description: Your cookie policy's version, stamped into every record. Change it when the policy changes and returning visitors are asked again.

inputs.name: open
inputs.description: Whether the banner (or, for `layout="modal"`, the dialog) is showing. The component closes it when the visitor decides. Two-way: `[(open)]`.

inputs.name: preferencesOpen
inputs.description: Whether the per-category preferences dialog is open. Set it `true` from a "Cookie settings" link so visitors can change their mind later — withdrawing consent must be as easy as giving it. Two-way: `[(preferencesOpen)]`.

inputs.name: layout
inputs.description: `banner` (full-width bottom bar), `corner` (compact card) or `modal` (dialog up front).

inputs.name: corner
inputs.description: Which bottom corner the `corner` card sits in.

inputs.name: inline
inputs.description: Render the banner or card in normal flow instead of fixed to the viewport — for previews, docs and settings pages. The preferences dialog stays modal.

inputs.name: privacyHref
inputs.description: Your privacy or cookie policy URL. Relative paths, `http(s):` and `mailto:` are kept; anything else (`javascript:`, `data:`) drops the link.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Per-instance text, merged over the registry's `cookieConsent` labels.

inputs.name: storageKey
inputs.description: Opt in to keeping the record in `localStorage` under this key, in a versioned envelope. Read once after the first render (never on the server); written on every decision. `null` keeps nothing — persistence is yours through `(recorded)` and `[record]`.

outputs.name: recorded
outputs.description: The visitor accepted, rejected or saved: their choices, an ISO timestamp and the policy version.

outputs.name: restored
outputs.description: A record was read back from `storageKey` — load the scripts it allows.

outputs.name: consentChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `consent` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(consent)]`.

outputs.name: openChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `open` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(open)]`.

outputs.name: preferencesOpenChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `preferencesOpen` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(preferencesOpen)]`.

components.name: Copy to Clipboard
components.description: Copy button in inline, block and icon-only variants with success feedback, the async Clipboard API and an execCommand fallback for older browsers.
whenToUse: Letting users copy a value (code snippet, API key, URL, token) in one click.
You want built-in success feedback and a clipboard fallback for old browsers.
For copying rich/multiple values, build a custom control around the clipboard API.

examples.title: A secret: masked, gated reveal, audited copy
examples.description: The label is masked, revealing asks the host first, the success announcement warns, and every copy emits an SvSensitiveCopyEvent that never carries the value.

examples.title: Why did it fail?
examples.description: copyError emits an SvClipboardError whose reason is denied, insecure-context, unavailable or failed.

examples.title: Drive it from a test (or a native shell)
examples.code: providers: [{ provide: SV_CLIPBOARD, useValue: { writeText: () => Promise.reject(new SvClipboardError('denied')) } }]

customization: Pass the `text` to copy and choose a `variant` (inline, block, icon-only) and `size`.
Customize the `label` and the post-copy `successLabel` / `successDuration`.
Listen to `copied` for success and `copyError` for failures, to trigger toasts or analytics.

Sensitive values (`sensitive`, `sensitiveReveal`, `sensitiveField`, `sensitiveWarning`, `requireAuthorization` / `revealAuthorized` / `revealRequest`, `copyAudited`) follow the kit-wide sensitive-value policy, and `provideSvSensitivePrivacy()` re-masks the label while the screen is shared.
The clipboard sits behind the `SV_CLIPBOARD` injection token (default `svBrowserClipboard`): provide your own to test denied permission or an insecure origin, or to target a native shell.

Variant axes: `variant` and `size` are appearance; `sensitive` + `sensitiveReveal` are a behavioural mode that works with every variant, except that `icon-only` has no label to mask or reveal, so it only warns and audits.

Busy state: a click while a copy is in flight is ignored and the button reports `aria-busy="true"`; the success timer is cleared when the component is destroyed, and a copy that settles after destruction emits nothing. A write that never settles is abandoned after `copyTimeout` (default 10 000 ms, `SV_COPY_TIMEOUT_MS`): `copyError` fires with reason `failed`, busy clears, and a late answer is ignored.

Layout: not applicable — the button and label sit in normal flow; nothing is portalled, measured or scrolled, and no containing block or breakpoint matters. The execCommand fallback appends an off-screen `position: fixed` textarea to `<body>` for the duration of the copy only, and removes it whether the copy succeeded or not.

Browser limits: the async Clipboard API needs a secure context (HTTPS or localhost) and a user gesture, and an iframe needs the `clipboard-write` permission policy. Elsewhere the component falls back to the deprecated `execCommand('copy')`, which iOS Safari only honours inside the tap handler and which browsers may remove. When both fail, `copyError` carries `reason` (`denied`, `insecure-context`, `unavailable`, `failed`) and the live region tells the user to select the text and copy it manually.
accessibility: Renders a labelled button with an accessible name even in icon-only mode.
Success and failure are announced via a polite live region, not colour-only; a failure names its reason and the manual workaround.
Falls back to execCommand when the Clipboard API is unavailable, and emits `copyError` if both fail.
In sensitive mode the reveal toggle is a real button with `aria-pressed`, and the success announcement is the `sensitiveWarning`.
Focus stays on the copy button: the fallback's scratch textarea hands focus back after it copies.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: Text to copy to clipboard.

inputs.name: successLabel
inputs.description: Label shown after successful copy.

inputs.name: successDuration
inputs.description: Duration in ms before reverting to default state.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Display variant.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Component size.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Placeholder shown when no text content is provided via ng-content.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name of the copy button — the only name `icon-only` has. Name WHAT is copied ("Copy API key"), and localise it here. Never derived from `label`, which may be the (sensitive) value itself.

inputs.name: sensitive
inputs.description: Treat the value as a secret — an API key, a recovery code, a token. A copied secret leaves no trace and gets no warning from a generic copy button. On: the `label` is masked, the success announcement becomes `sensitiveWarning`, and every copy emits `copyAudited`. Off by default — the common use is a command or an id, and masking those would break them.

inputs.name: sensitiveReveal
inputs.description: How a `sensitive` label is shown: `masked`, `revealable` (toggle) or `visible`.

inputs.name: sensitiveField
inputs.description: Which field was copied, for the audit event's `field`.

inputs.name: sensitiveWarning
inputs.description: Announced (and shown in the block variant) after a sensitive copy.

inputs.name: requireAuthorization
inputs.description: Whether revealing a `sensitiveReveal="revealable"` value needs the host's authorization first. While on and `revealAuthorized` is off, the toggle emits `revealRequest` instead of revealing — step up, then set `revealAuthorized`.

inputs.name: revealAuthorized
inputs.description: The host has re-authenticated the user; the reveal toggle may reveal.

inputs.name: copyTimeout
inputs.description: How long (ms) a clipboard write may stay pending before it is abandoned as `failed` and `busy` clears. A write that never settles — a permission prompt left open, a native bridge that never answers — would otherwise leave the button busy forever. A late answer after the timeout is ignored. An invalid value (`0`, negative, `NaN`, `Infinity`) uses the default.

outputs.name: copied
outputs.description: Emitted after text is successfully copied.

outputs.name: copyError
outputs.description: Emitted when copying fails (both the Clipboard API and the fallback), or when the write did not settle within `copyTimeout`. The payload is an `SvClipboardError`: `reason` classifies it — `denied`, `insecure-context`, `unavailable` or `failed` (also used for a timeout). When both paths ran and failed, `cause` (and so `message`) is the FALLBACK's error — the last one thrown — while `reason` is derived from the Clipboard API's rejection. Typed `unknown` for compatibility; narrow with `instanceof SvClipboardError`.

outputs.name: copyAudited
outputs.description: A `sensitive` value reached the clipboard. The event says who, which field and when — never the value itself. Log it.

outputs.name: revealRequest
outputs.description: The user asked to reveal while `requireAuthorization` was on and `revealAuthorized` off.

components.name: Credit Card
components.description: A payment-card visual that updates live as the user types: auto-detects the brand from the number, formats the digits (incl. Amex 4-6-5), and flips to the back for the CVC. Display-only — the number and CVC are masked by default, and it never collects or transmits card data. Five gradient themes.
whenToUse: A live preview beside the payment form at checkout.
A saved-cards list in the account, fed from a payment token’s last4 and brand.
You want brand detection and formatting handled for you.

examples.title: Entry preview — explicit opt-out of masking
Privacy mode — take the reveal back for a shared session

customization: Five gradient variants (noir, indigo, sunset, emerald, ocean).
Force a brand (authoritative — use the PSP token’s brand) or auto-detect from the issuer prefix; optional issuer name.
Toggle flippability, CVC visibility, and masking of the number and CVC independently.

privacy overrides both mask opt-outs at runtime, because the opt-out is set at author time while screen sharing is only known during the session — and the face that lost its reveal says so, so dots where digits were requested are not mistaken for a broken render.
Custom placeholder cardholder name.
accessibility: When flippable the card exposes role="button", a descriptive label and Enter / Space activation.
Chip, contactless mark and decorative sheen are hidden from assistive tech.
Number is real, formatted text; the card is always dark-styled with sufficient contrast.
The number and CVC are select-none, so neither can be dragged to the clipboard.
A withheld reveal is announced as real text on the affected face — front for the number, back for the CVC — rather than by the absence of digits alone.
variants: Privacy mode — a session that turned out to be shared

inputs.name: number
inputs.description: Card number (digits; non-digits are ignored). Only the brand and the last four digits are ever rendered unless `maskNumber` is turned off — see the PCI boundary note on the class.

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: Cardholder name.

inputs.name: expiry
inputs.description: Expiry as MM/YY.

inputs.name: cvc
inputs.description: CVC / security code (shown on the back).

inputs.name: brand
inputs.description: The card brand. **Pass the brand your payment provider returned with the token** (Stripe's `card.brand`, Adyen's `brand`, …) whenever you have it — it is authoritative. `'auto'` guesses from the number's issuer prefix (`svDetectCardBrand`), and published BIN ranges change over time, so the guess is a convenience for a live entry form, never the source of truth.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Gradient theme.

inputs.name: issuer
inputs.description: Optional issuing-bank name shown top-left.

inputs.name: flippable
inputs.description: Allow click / keyboard to flip the card.

inputs.name: showCvc
inputs.description: Show the CVC block on the back.

inputs.name: maskNumber
inputs.description: Mask all but the last four entered digits. Masked by default — set false only when the digits on screen are ones you accept appearing in a screenshot or a session recording.

inputs.name: maskCvc
inputs.description: Mask the CVC, so flipping the card cannot expose it. A CVC must never be stored at all, which makes it the value that should never be recoverable from a recording.

inputs.name: privacy
inputs.description: Declare that this session is recorded, screen-shared or replayed. While set, the number and the CVC render masked even where `maskNumber` or `maskCvc` was turned off, and the face that lost its reveal says why. An app-wide `provideSvSensitivePrivacy()` (from `@styloviz/core`) does the same for every card while this is left unset. This is a declaration, not a detection — see the note on the class.

inputs.name: placeholderName
inputs.description: Placeholder cardholder name when empty.

inputs.name: flipped
inputs.description: Whether the back is showing (two-way: `[(flipped)]`).

outputs.name: flippedChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `flipped` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(flipped)]`.

components.name: Cron Builder
components.description: A visual cron / schedule builder: every N minutes, hourly, daily, weekly and monthly modes on a segmented control, or a Custom field for any five-field expression, validated as you type. A plain-language preview ("Every weekday at 09:00") and the next runs in any time zone. The value is the normalised expression; the parse, format, describe and next-runs helpers are exported.
whenToUse: Letting users schedule reports, syncs, backups, reminders or any recurring job in an admin panel or internal tool.
Showing a stored cron expression in words, with its next runs, so nobody has to decode `*/15 9-17 * * 1-5` by eye.
Use `sv-time-picker` instead for a single time of day, and `sv-date-picker` for a single date.

examples.title: Two-way binding
examples.code:
<sv-cron-builder label="Daily digest email" [(value)]="schedule" />

readonly schedule = signal('30 6 * * *'); // "Every day at 06:30"

examples.title: Reactive forms — invalid while the expression is
examples.code:
<sv-cron-builder label="Backup window" [formControl]="schedule" timeZone="Europe/London" />

readonly schedule = new FormControl('0 2 * * 0', { nonNullable: true });
// Typing "0 25 * * *" in Custom: schedule.value stays '0 2 * * 0',
// schedule.errors → { cron: { code: 'range', field: 'hour', token: '25', min: 0, max: 23 } }

examples.title: Next runs in a time zone
The helpers, without the component

customization: Six modes: `minutes` (every 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20 or 30 minutes), `hourly` (a minute past every 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 or 12 hours), `daily`, `weekly` (any weekdays), `monthly` (any days of the month) and `custom`. An expression the visual modes cannot show — `*/7`, a month, both day fields, a list of hours — opens in Custom.

Custom accepts `*`, values, ranges `1-5`, steps `*/15`, `1-30/5`, `a/n`, lists, month and weekday names (`JAN`, `mon`) and `@hourly` / `@daily` / `@weekly` / `@monthly` / `@yearly`; the value is written back normalised.

The preview is `svDescribeCron` in the kit's locale — weekday and month names, times, ordinals and lists come from `Intl` — and `nextRunCount` runs (3 by default, 0 hides them) from `svNextCronRuns`. `showPreview` turns the whole preview off.
Every string comes from the `forms` labels (`cron*` keys, plus `hour` and `minute`) — `provideSvLabels(SV_FORMS_LABELS_DE)` or the per-instance `labels` input.
Mode switch, toggles and focus rings use the `primary-*` tokens and the invalid border the `danger-*` tokens, so a remapped theme recolours the builder.
accessibility: The builder is a `<fieldset>` named by its `label`; the mode switch is the kit's segmented control as a `radiogroup` named "Frequency", operated with the arrow keys.
Intervals, hours and minutes are native `<select>`s with visible labels; weekdays and days of the month are native checkboxes in their own named `<fieldset>`, each target at least 36 px.

An invalid Custom expression sets `aria-invalid` and adds the error to `aria-describedby` beside the format hint; the message names the field and the rejected text, in a `role="alert"`. "Choose at least one day" is described on the day group the same way.
The sentence for the schedule is a polite live region, so a screen reader hears "Every weekday at 09:00" as the controls change; runs are `<time datetime>` elements.
Implements ControlValueAccessor and Validator — `[(ngModel)]`, `[formControl]` and `formControlName` work, and `formControl.disable()` disables every control.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The cron expression (five fields). Two-way: `[(value)]`. Only a valid expression is ever written back, in its normalised numeric form; `''` means no schedule yet.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Visible group label. Null uses the `cronLegend` label ("Schedule").

inputs.name: timeZone
inputs.description: IANA time zone the schedule runs in, for the next-runs preview. Null uses the browser's.

inputs.name: nextRunCount
inputs.description: How many upcoming runs the preview lists, 0–10. 0 hides the list.

inputs.name: showPreview
inputs.description: Show the sentence and next runs under the editor.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP 47 locale for weekday and month names, times and the sentence.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disable every control.

inputs.name: errorMessage
inputs.description: Client-side validation message from the host, shown when the builder has none of its own.

inputs.name: serverError
inputs.description: A rejection reported by the server about this value. Self-expires when the value changes.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Per-instance text, merged over the registry's `forms` labels.

outputs.name: errorChange
outputs.description: The builder's own validation result changed: the parse error (or "choose at least one day") on screen, or `null` once it is valid again. While it is non-null `value` is not updated.

outputs.name: valueChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `value` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(value)]`.

components.name: Data Table
components.description: Sortable, paginated table with row selection, badge cells and a loading skeleton — plus a search toolbar, column filters, inline editing, expandable rows and bulk actions. Pro adds the spreadsheet half: cell ranges with copy, paste and a fill handle, Find, column bands, merged cells, row numbers and a cell context menu — and `svGridAssist`, which asks the table for a view in plain words and shows the answer in the filter builder.
whenToUse: Displaying structured rows that users sort, page, search, or select.
You need selection, bulk actions, density toggles or column visibility.
For unstructured/feed-style content, use List View instead.
Up to ~200 rows: render them unpaged. Every row is in the DOM, so nothing needs configuring.

200 rows to ~10k, held in the browser: `paginated` (or `virtualized` for one continuous scroll). The client pipeline — search, filter, sort and windowing over the whole set — measures 0.5ms at 1k rows and 4.4ms at 10k, so a keystroke still lands inside one frame.

10k to ~25k: `virtualized` keeps rendering flat (the DOM holds `viewportHeight / virtualRowHeight` rows plus a small overscan no matter how large the set is — a 240-row table renders 13 `tr`s), but the pipeline is linear in row count and search is what runs it. Turn `searchable` off, or move to `serverSide`.
Beyond ~25k rows: `serverSide`. The pipeline costs 21ms at 50k rows, so each keystroke drops a frame — and that is before the memory of holding the set client-side.

examples.title: Let a browser agent drive it (WebMCP)
examples.code:
<!-- svWebMcp from @styloviz/core registers orders_describe, orders_… — see /docs/webmcp -->
<sv-data-table-pro svWebMcp="orders" [columns]="columns" [rows]="rows" [searchable]="true" [columnFilters]="true" [selectable]="true" />
<!-- tools: describe, sort, search, filter, clear_filters, select, rows, go_to_page -->

examples.title: Grouped rows (Pro)
examples.description: One collapsible header per distinct value of a column; groupBy replaces client pagination.

examples.title: Transparent — inherit the container background (Pro)
Custom cell templates (svDtCell, Pro)
examples.code:
<sv-data-table-pro [columns]="columns" [rows]="rows" rowKey="id">
  <!-- Render any rich content per column, keyed by the column's `key`. -->
  <ng-template svDtCell="name" let-row let-value="value">
    <sv-avatar [name]="row.name" size="xs" /> {{ value }}
  </ng-template>
  <ng-template svDtCell="status" let-row>
    <sv-badge [label]="row.status" [variant]="statusVariant(row.status)" />
  </ng-template>
</sv-data-table-pro>

examples.title: Cell ranges — copy, paste and fill (Pro)
examples.description: A block of cells copies out as text a spreadsheet reads; a paste or a fill arrives as one validated rangeEdit for the host to apply.

examples.title: Bands, merged cells and Find (Pro)
examples.code:
<!-- columns: { key: 'region', label: 'Region', mergeRepeated: true } -->
<sv-data-table-pro [columns]="columns" [rows]="rows" rowKey="id"
  [columnBands]="[{ label: 'Q1', columns: ['jan', 'feb', 'mar'] }]"
  [findable]="true" />

examples.title: Batch editing — undo, redo and save (Pro)
examples.description: Edits, pastes and fills become a draft; Save sends one batchSave with a requestKey and a rollback().

examples.title: Set filter, filter builder and print (Pro)
examples.code:
<!-- columns: { key: 'stage', label: 'Stage', filterType: 'set', queryType: 'enum', filterOptions: stages } -->
<sv-data-table-pro [columns]="columns" [rows]="rows" rowKey="id"
  [columnFilters]="true" [filterBuilder]="true" [printable]="true"
  [(setFilters)]="setFilters" [(filterQuery)]="query" />

examples.title: Ask the table — svGridAssist (Pro)
examples.description: A question becomes the filter builder's query, a sort and a highlight; the builder opens on it, and Undo puts the view back. The resolver gets the question, fields and columns — never a row.
examples.code:
<sv-data-table-pro [columns]="columns" [rows]="rows" rowKey="id"
  [(filterQuery)]="query" [(highlightQuery)]="highlight">
  <!-- Default resolver: svGridAssistHeuristicResolver(), on the device. -->
  <ng-container svGridAssist [resolver]="askModel"
    [examples]="['Won deals over 20k, biggest first']"
    (assisted)="log($event)" (assistError)="report($event)" />
</sv-data-table-pro>

examples.title: Compare products, transposed (Pro)
examples.code:
<!-- Transposes rows→columns: first column = product name, the rest
     become feature rows; boolean values render as check / cross. -->
<sv-data-table-pro [columns]="columns" [rows]="products" rowKey="id"
  layout="comparison" highlightRowId="pro" />

customization: Pro: set `[transparent]="true"` to remove the table's own surface fill (root, toolbar, body and rows) so it inherits the background of a glass card or coloured panel — hover/selection and `striped` tints are preserved and the card shadow is dropped; pair with `variant="borderless"`.

Pro: project rich cell content per column with the `svDtCell` directive: `<ng-template svDtCell="colKey" let-row let-value="value">…</ng-template>` (context exposes `$implicit` = row, `value`, `column`) — falls back to `col.render` text or a badge cell when no template is provided.
Enable sorting, pagination, selection and bulk actions per table.
Pro adds virtualization, row grouping, resizable and reorderable columns, `svDtCell` cell templates, export, the comparison layout and `transparent`.

Pro: set `resizableColumns` to drag-resize columns (per-column `width` and `resizable` opt-out) and `reorderableColumns` to drag- or keyboard-reorder them; changes emit `columnResize` and `columnOrderChange`.

Pro: set `layout="comparison"` to transpose the table into a Compare-Products grid: the first column supplies each product's name (becoming the column headers) and the remaining columns become feature rows, with boolean values rendered as check / cross icons; `highlightRowId` spotlights the recommended product column.

**Feature compatibility.** `virtualized` and `groupBy` each replace client pagination rather than combining with it: both render the whole sorted set into one scroller and the pager is hidden, so a `pageSize` alongside either is ignored.

**Feature compatibility.** `serverSide` turns the client pipeline off entirely — filtering, sorting and paging all pass `rows` through untouched, because the server already did them. There is no double filtering, and equally no client-side fallback: whatever you do not implement server-side does not happen.
**Feature compatibility.** `serverSide` composes with `groupBy`, but it groups only the page the server sent — a group header reads as a section of this page, not of the dataset.

**Feature compatibility.** `footerFn`, export and selection all operate on rows in hand. Client-side that is the filtered set; in `serverSide` mode it is the current page, so a footer "Total" is a page total and a select-all selects the page.

**Feature compatibility.** `layout="comparison"` is a separate rendering path: toolbar, filters, pagination, selection, virtualization, grouping and the footer row do not apply to it. Use it for a fixed handful of products, not as a table mode to toggle.

Pro: `cellSelection` turns the body into a spreadsheet — a block of cells that follows the cell cursor (two-way `cellRange`, by row key and column key), Ctrl/⌘+C copies it as tab-separated text plus an HTML table, Ctrl/⌘+V pastes a block (one value fills the selection; a block that fits a whole number of times repeats), and the corner handle fills — a series when two or more numbers step evenly, otherwise a repeat. Ctrl+D / Ctrl+R and the menu's Fill down / right / series do the same without a drag.

Pro: a paste or a fill emits ONE `rangeEdit` — `{ source, changes, rejected }`, `changes` in `editComplete`'s shape, each validated by its column — and never writes `rows`. Non-`editable` columns and `validate` refusals land in `rejected` and are announced.

Pro: `findable` adds Find (toolbar button or Ctrl/⌘+F inside the table) — it marks and walks matches across the filtered, sorted set, turning pages, opening groups and scrolling a virtualized window to each; it hides nothing, unlike `searchable`.

Pro: `columnBands` draws headings over runs of columns (bands nest); `mergeRepeated` on a column folds equal neighbours into one cell, and `colSpan(row)` runs a row's cell across the columns after it; `rowNumbers` adds a numbering column (page offsets included).

Pro: `contextMenu` adds a right-click / Shift+F10 menu on cells — Copy, Copy with headers, the fills, Export selection as CSV, pin to the start or end (two-way `columnPins`, saved in the layout state) and Hide (offered only with `showColumnToggle`, so a hidden column can come back). A pinned column moves to its edge, and several pinned columns sit side by side.

**Feature compatibility.** Merged cells (`mergeRepeated`, `colSpan`) need every row of a run rendered, so they are not drawn while `virtualized` or `groupBy` is set. A range, a paste and Ctrl+A cover the rows on screen — the page when paginated.

Pro: `batchEdit` makes every edit — a typed cell, a paste, a fill — a draft the table shows and flags (a corner mark, and "unsaved" for a screen reader) instead of an `editComplete` / `rangeEdit`. Undo / Redo on the batch bar and Ctrl/⌘+Z, Ctrl/⌘+Shift+Z (Ctrl+Y) inside the table step whole edits back and forth; typing a cell back to its saved value stops it being a change; `unsavedChange` reports the count for a leave-page guard.

Pro: Save emits ONE `batchSave` — `{ changes, requestKey, rollback }`, `changes` in `editComplete`'s shape against the rows as the host holds them now. It is the kit's optimistic write (`createOptimisticEdit`): the saved values stay on screen (flagged "saving") until the host binds rows that carry them or lowers `saving`; `rollback()` puts the batch back into the draft, keeping any cell edited again since; a rollback from an older save is refused. `[saving]` locks Save, Discard, Undo and Redo; `[saveError]` shows on the bar.

Pro: `filterType: 'set'` is an Excel-style checkbox filter in the filter row (needs `columnFilters`) — every value of the column (or its `filterOptions`, which a `serverSide` table should declare), a search, Select all and (Blanks), in a body-portaled panel. The state is the two-way `setFilters` (column key → values let through; an empty list lets nothing through), saved as `setFilters` in the layout state, with a chip per column.

Pro: `filterBuilder` adds a toolbar Filter builder — `@styloviz-pro/query-builder` over the columns, `queryType` per column (`'string'` by default, `'number'`, `'date'`, `'enum'` from `filterOptions`, `'boolean'`, or `'none'` to leave it out). The query is the builder's own `SvQueryExpression` in the two-way `filterQuery`: store it with `svSerializeQuery`, read it back with `svParseQuery`. Client-side the table evaluates `svQueryToPredicate`'s result (`svRowMatchesPredicate` is exported); an unfinished rule filters nothing. In `serverSide` mode the table filters nothing itself — read `setFilters` and `filterQuery` in your `queryChange` handler (each change asks again) and translate the query with `svQueryToPredicate`.

Pro: `statusBar` adds a bar under the table — the row count, or for a selected block Count, Sum, Average, Min and Max of its numbers. It reads row values (and drafts), never the formatted text, so a `render` that adds a currency sign does not break the sum.

Pro: `printable` adds a Print button. While the page prints — from the button or Ctrl/⌘+P — the table renders every row that survived the filters and the sort (not the page, not a virtualized window; a `serverSide` table prints the page it holds), hides the toolbar, filter row, pager, checkboxes and row menus, repeats the header on each sheet and keeps each row whole. The controls are hidden by `print:` utilities, so a table without `printable` still prints its page without chrome.

Pro: `svGridAssist` — a content child, the shape of `svSelectSearch` — puts an "Ask the table" bar over the table. A resolver (`SvGridAssistResolver`: the prompt, the builder's fields, the columns and the current view in, `{ filter, sort, highlight, explanation }` out; the default `svGridAssistHeuristicResolver()` reads English on the device) answers with the builder's own `SvQueryExpression`. The table checks it against the fields — unknown columns, an operator the type cannot take, a value outside an enum, an unsortable sort are dropped and reported in `(assisted).skipped` — and writes it through `[(filterQuery)]` (the builder opens on it; `[showQuery]="false"` keeps it closed), `sortChange` and the new two-way `highlightQuery`, so a `serverSide` table hears the usual `queryChange`. One request at a time: asking again or Cancel aborts the one in flight (pass `request.signal` to `fetch`). A failure shows Try again; Undo restores the filter, sort and highlight from before the answer. `[examples]` adds one-click questions; `[maxLength]` caps the prompt (300).
Pro: `highlightQuery` marks the rows a query matches without hiding the rest — a tint and a bar on the leading edge — and works with or without `svGridAssist`; its chip clears it.

**Feature compatibility.** `responsive="cards"` windows on its own `cardRowHeight` under `virtualized`, and deliberately does not group — a collapsible header spanning a card list has no column structure to summarise. Size it to roughly `ceil(visibleColumns / 2) * 46 + 32`px.
accessibility: Keyboard at scale: the free table is paginated by default, so its page size is the ceiling. In every layout the rows are ONE tab stop: ↑/↓, Home/End and PageUp/PageDown move the cursor (in Pro also typeahead over the first column, and under `virtualized` across the whole dataset, scrolling the window to it); Enter or Space activates the row, and keys from a control inside the row keep their own meaning. → steps into the row's cells: ←/→ and Home/End move along it, ↑/↓ keep the column, ← from the first cell returns to the row; Enter or Space on a cell emits `cellClick` (then `rowClick`, as a click does), and F2 on an `editable` cell opens the editor — Enter saves, Escape cancels, and either puts the cursor back on the cell. Documented ceiling: 2,000 rows rendered at once with neither pagination nor `virtualized` — past it a dev-mode warning fires.

Focus after a mutation: if the row holding focus leaves the rendered set — a filter it does not match, a host refresh, a delete — focus moves to the same control in the row now at its index, then the row before it, then the table's scroller, and a polite announcement says the row is not shown.
Native table semantics with scoped headers and an accessible table name from `tableTitle`.
Sortable headers are focusable and operable with Enter/Space, exposing `aria-sort` state.
Resize handles are focusable separators (`role="separator"`) adjustable with ←/→; reorderable columns move from the keyboard with Ctrl/Cmd + ←/→ on a focused header.
Selection, pagination and row actions are keyboard reachable; open menus close on Escape.
Loading regions set `aria-busy`; row-action and export menus are the shared `sv-dropdown-menu`, portaled to the body so no scroll container clips them, with `role="menu"`/`menuitem`.

Pro, `cellSelection`: the table becomes a `role="grid"` with `aria-multiselectable`, and every cell says `aria-selected`. Shift+arrows grow the block (Ctrl adds a jump to the edge), Ctrl+A selects all, Shift+Space a row, Ctrl+Space a column, and each change of size is announced ("3 rows by 2 columns selected"). A paste or fill announces what changed and what was refused. The fill handle and the range outline are decorative; their drag has Ctrl+D / Ctrl+R and the menu's Fill series as keyboard and single-pointer twins (WCAG 2.5.7).

Pro, Find: the field is a labelled `role="search"` region; "4 of 12" is a status line, and stepping announces where the match is ("4 of 12: Customer, Acme Corp"). Escape closes it with focus on the match in view, or back on the Find button.

Pro, `contextMenu`: Shift+F10 or the menu key opens it on the focused cell; it is named for what it acts on ("Actions for Revenue, row 4"), and closing returns focus to the cell. Editors, links and inputs keep the browser's own menu.
Pro, merged cells: a merged cell is one stop for the cell cursor — the arrows step over the positions it covers, and moving onto a covered position lands on the cell that covers it.

Pro, `batchEdit`: a staged cell reads its value then "unsaved" (or "saving"); the flag is a shape in the corner, not only a colour. The batch bar is a named group whose buttons say what they do; undo, redo, save, discard and a failed save that comes back are announced ("Undid the change to 3 cells."). A save error is an alert on the bar.

Pro, set filter: the filter-row button names its column and its state ("Filter Stage by value: 2 of 5"); the panel is a dialog that takes focus, with a labelled search, a tri-state Select all and a checkbox per value, and Escape returns focus to the button.

Pro, `svGridAssist`: the ask bar is a labelled `role="search"` form; Enter asks, Escape cancels a request in flight, and the field is `aria-busy` while it runs. "Working out the view…", the answer's summary ("View updated. Filter: 2 conditions. Sorted by Amount, descending"), Cancelled, View restored and a failure (assertive) are announced; the visible status line is not a second live region. A highlighted row reads "Highlighted" before its first cell, and its mark is a bar as well as a tint — never colour alone.
Pro, status bar: a named group that is deliberately not live — it changes with every cell the cursor crosses, and speaking each would drown the cells themselves.

Under `virtualized`, the table declares `aria-rowcount` and stamps every rendered row with its true `aria-rowindex`, so a screen reader announces "row 140 of 241" rather than the size of the window. Header rows, the column-filter row, group headers, expanded detail rows and the footer row all take their place in that numbering; the spacer rows are `aria-hidden` and unnumbered. Both attributes are omitted whenever every row is already in the DOM, so the browser's own count stands and cannot be contradicted.

A `validate` failure marks the editor `aria-invalid` and points `aria-describedby` at the message, which is also a polite live region — described-by covers arriving at the field, the live region covers an error appearing under a cursor already in it. Enter and blur refuse to commit while it stands; Escape always discards.

inputs.name: virtualized
inputs.description: Windows row rendering to what's scrolled into view, using the same variable-height primitive (`createVariableVirtualizer`, `@styloviz/core`) `list-view` uses — a group header and a data row are different heights, so this table always needs the variable form, never the fixed one. Ignores `paginated`: virtualization and client pagination solve the same problem (a huge row set costing too much DOM), so turning this on reads as opting OUT of pagination rather than stacking both — the same relation `groupBy` has to pagination, and for the same reason.

inputs.name: virtualRowHeight
inputs.description: Approximate pixel height of one data row; the virtualized window is computed from it. Approximate, like `list-view`'s `itemHeight`: measure your own rendered row height for pixel accuracy. A wrong guess still renders every row correctly, with a slightly-off scrollbar length until the next scroll event corrects it.

inputs.name: virtualGroupRowHeight
inputs.description: Pixel height of a collapsible group header row, when `groupBy` is also set.

inputs.name: cardRowHeight
inputs.description: Pixel height of one `responsive="cards"` card; the card list is windowed from it, on the same `virtualized` switch as the table. A card is taller than a row and its height depends on how many columns are visible — a two-column grid of label/value pairs, so roughly `ceil(columns / 2) * 46 + 32`. Approximate for the same reason `virtualRowHeight` is: a wrong guess costs scrollbar accuracy, never correctness.

inputs.name: viewportHeight
inputs.description: Pixel height of the scrolling viewport when `virtualized` is on. A dedicated numeric input rather than reusing `maxHeight` — `maxHeight` accepts any CSS unit (`'50vh'`, `'none'`) that cannot be safely coerced to a pixel count, and the windowing math needs a real number to divide by.

components.name: Date Picker
components.description: Custom calendar picker with month/year navigation, today indicator, min/max constraints and day/month/year views.
whenToUse: Selecting a single calendar date with month/year navigation.
You need min/max constraints and disabled-date handling.
For time-of-day use the Time Picker; for a range, use the Date Range Picker (`sv-date-range-picker`, Pro) or compose two pickers.

examples.title: Accessible name + open/close events
examples.description: ariaLabel names the trigger; opened/closed fire on popover state. Value is a YYYY-MM-DD string.

examples.title: Reactive forms (formControlName)
examples.description: Implements ControlValueAccessor, so it binds to reactive and template-driven forms. The control value is a YYYY-MM-DD string; formControl.disable() disables the trigger.

examples.title: The week starts where the reader expects
examples.description: locale sets the first column and the headings together, from CLDR — en-US Sunday, en-GB Monday, ar-EG Saturday. Omitting it uses the kit's locale (Angular's LOCALE_ID, or provideSvLocale), so the grid matches every other date in the app; locale="" keeps the pre-2.0 Monday-first English grid. weekStart overrides the tag when the host knows better.
examples.code:
<sv-date-picker locale="en-US" [(value)]="start" />

<!-- pinned to a business week regardless of the tag -->
<sv-date-picker locale="ar-EG" [weekStart]="0" [(value)]="start" />

examples.title: A rule for unavailable dates, not a list
examples.description: dateDisabled takes a predicate, so an infinite set (no weekends, nothing inside 48 hours) does not have to be enumerated. It is OR-ed with minDate/maxDate, and it is called once per rendered cell — 42 per month view — so keep it pure and cheap.

customization: **The value is a calendar date, not an instant** — a `YYYY-MM-DD` string, never a `Date`. A birthday is not a moment; it is the same date everywhere on Earth, and a `Date` for "15 June" shifts across midnight for half the world. `@styloviz/core` names the policy: `SvCalendarDate`, `svIsCalendarDate` (which rejects `2026-02-30`, where `new Date()` quietly returns 2 March), `svAddCalendarDays` (UTC arithmetic, so a DST boundary cannot move the day) and `SvDateValueAdapter`, the seam a Temporal or Luxon migration swaps behind.

`timeZone` says whose **today** the calendar means — the one place a calendar date cannot avoid a zone, because for several hours of every day two places on Earth are on different dates. It drives the ringed cell, the Today button, the month the panel opens on and the keyboard’s starting point. Unset means the browser’s zone. It never converts the value: a calendar date has no zone to convert between. To build an instant, compose with `svComposeDateTime`, which reports the DST gaps and ambiguities instead of guessing.
Three views: day grid, month grid and year grid, with a Today / Clear footer.

Opening moves focus into the grid (roving tabindex — a single tab stop); Escape and selection close the popover and return focus to the trigger.

inputs.description: Two-way bindable `YYYY-MM-DD` date string. A calendar date, not an instant: a birthday is not a moment; it is the same date everywhere on Earth. That is why this is a string and not a `Date` — a `Date` is an instant, and storing one for "15 June" means the value shifts across midnight for half the world. Composing this with `sv-time-picker` is not `new Date(d + 'T' + t)`. That composes in the browser's zone, silently, and twice a year it composes something that does not exist: London, 2026-03-29, the clocks go 01:00 → 02:00 and `new Date('2026-03-29T01:30')` returns 02:30 without a word. components.name: Descriptions
components.description: Key–value list for the detail panel of a record — real <dl>/<dt>/<dd> semantics, 1–4 responsive columns with per-item span, horizontal or vertical layouts, and a value that is missing told apart from one that is blank.
whenToUse: The read-only half of a record page — view order, user profile, resource detail, invoice header.
Any place a grid of hand-rolled <span> pairs is standing in for a description list.
For editable fields use a Form; for many records at once use a Data Table.

examples.title: Vertical, with a full-width note
examples.code:
<sv-descriptions
  layout="vertical"
  [columns]="3"
  [items]="[
    { id: 'sku',   label: 'SKU',   value: 'ORD-4182' },
    { id: 'total', label: 'Total', value: '$248.00' },
    { id: 'notes', label: 'Notes', value: 'Leave with the concierge.', span: 3 },
  ]" />

examples.title: An action per row, without breaking the reading model
examples.description: A <dd> is the DEFINITION of its term, and HTML leaves nowhere else to put a control: inside a <dl>'s wrapping <div> only <dt> and <dd> are allowed, so there is no sibling position. The action therefore lives inside the definition, which makes two things compulsory rather than stylistic. It is laid out as its own column, so the value text keeps its alignment instead of being shoved around by a button. And its accessible name must carry the term — "Copy order total", not "Copy" — because a listener who lands on it is inside the definition and has no other way to know which pair they are in. The template gets the item so you can say it; the component cannot enforce it for you.

examples.title: Stacking on a phone
examples.description: A horizontal pair sits side by side above the breakpoint and stacks below it. The rule was always in the class list and never in the API — the layout has been sm:flex since the beginning, so a host had no say and no way to find out. stackAt states it and moves it; 'never' keeps the pair side by side at every width, which only works when the labels are genuinely short. The part that was actually broken: a stacked pair had no vertical spacing at all, so on a phone the label sat directly on its value and read as one wrapped sentence.

customization: Prints cleanly: each term/value pair is `break-inside: avoid` and each term `break-after: avoid`, so a page break falls between pairs and never splits a `<dt>` from its `<dd>` — in every layout and variant.

`svDiffValues()` from `@styloviz/core` turns two records into a list of changed paths, which maps straight onto `DescriptionItem[]` for a before/after view — the same engine Code Block and JSON Viewer use, rather than a fourth one.
Lay out with `layout` (horizontal / vertical), `columns` (1–4, stepping down on narrow viewports) and a per-item `span` that is clamped to the row width.
Choose a surface with `variant` (plain / bordered) and a scale with `size` (sm / md / lg).
Set `emptyValueText` for the missing-value placeholder, and `valueClass` per item (e.g. `font-mono` for an ID).
Full async contract: `loading`, `error`, `emptyText` and a `retry` output.
`<ng-template svDescriptionAction let-item>` adds one action per row, rendered as its own column inside the definition and given the item so the action can name the term it acts on.
`stackAt` (`never` / `sm` / `md` / `lg`) sets where a horizontal pair stops sitting side by side and stacks.
accessibility: Renders a real `<dl>` with one `<dt>`/`<dd>` pair per item, each wrapped in a `<div>` — valid HTML5 that keeps the pairing screen readers announce.
A `title` becomes an `<h3>` and names the list via `aria-labelledby`; ids are instance-scoped, so two lists on one page never collide.
No `aria-labelledby` is emitted without a heading, so the fallback name is never suppressed.
A missing value shows a dimmed placeholder rather than an empty cell that reads as a rendering bug.

A row action is rendered inside its `<dd>` because HTML permits no sibling there, so it becomes part of what the definition reads as — which is why the docs insist its accessible name carries the term. It is laid out as a separate column so the value text keeps its alignment.
A stacked pair gets real vertical spacing, so a label and its value do not read as one wrapped sentence on a narrow screen.

components.name: Diff Viewer
components.description: Compare two versions of a text, or read a unified patch: unified or split view, both line numbers, a visible `+` / `−` on every changed line and an `sr-only` "Added:" / "Removed:" (never colour alone), long unchanged runs folded behind "Show N unchanged lines", the changed words highlighted inside a changed line, CRLF and LF treated alike, a lost final newline shown, and a size cap that says so instead of freezing the tab. `svLineDiff()` is exported; the engine is the kit's shared one in `@styloviz/core`.
whenToUse: Showing what changed in a config, a template, a document or a record's text between two versions.
Reviewing a patch or a pull request diff in an admin or developer tool.
Use `sv-code-block variant="diff"` to let a user accept or reject AI-suggested hunks.

examples.title: A git patch
examples.description: The file name comes from the `---` / `+++` lines and the numbers from the `@@` headers. Lines the patch leaves out are counted, not unfoldable.

examples.title: The comparison on its own

customization: Added and removed tints, markers and word highlights paint from the `accent` and `danger` tokens; notices from `warning` and `info`.
`context`, `wordDiff`, `lineNumbers`, `showViewToggle`, `maxHeight`, `beforeLabel` / `afterLabel` tune the layout.
`svLineDiff`, `svWordDiff`, `svParsePatch`, `svDiffViewItems` and `svDiffSplitSections` are exported for your own renderer.
All visible strings are `codeBlock` labels in 12 language packs; the summary sentence uses the `core` diff labels.
accessibility: The diff is a named region described by a summary sentence ("2 changes, 5 lines added, 3 lines removed."), so its scale is known before it is read.
Changed lines carry a visible `+` / `−` and an `sr-only` "Added:" / "Removed:"; unchanged lines stay silent. Line numbers and markers are `aria-hidden`.
Each scroll pane is focusable and named (the diff, or Before / After in split view), so a keyboard can scroll a long line; split-view padding rows are hidden from screen readers.
The layout switch is two `aria-pressed` buttons in a named group; fold buttons say how many lines they reveal.
Every value renders as text — a patch adding `<script>` shows those characters.

examples.title: Decorative vs semantic
examples.code: Billing

customization: Solid, dashed, dotted and gradient lines.
Inline text or icon label.
Horizontal or vertical.
Optional explicit `width` / `height`, custom `color` and `thickness`.
`semantics`: `semantic` (default — a real thematic break) or `decorative` (a visual flourish, removed from the accessibility tree).

Variant axes: `variant`, `color`, `thickness`, `align`, `spacing`, `width` / `height` are APPEARANCE; `orientation` is LAYOUT; `semantics` is MEANING and is independent of how the rule looks. Known limits: `gradient` ignores `color` and `thickness`; a vertical divider needs a height — a stretched flex-row parent or an explicit `height` — or it collapses to 1rem.
accessibility: `semantics="semantic"` (the default) exposes `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`, named by `label`.

`semantics="decorative"` renders `role="none"`; an unlabelled decorative divider is also `aria-hidden`, so nothing is announced. A decorative divider with a `label` keeps the text readable in reading order ("OR" still means something) but announces no separator.
A divider is not a heading. Screen-reader users navigate sections by headings, and a labelled rule gives them none — see the "Don't" under Best practices.

RTL: `align="start"` / `"end"` are logical — the label sits on the right with `start` under `dir="rtl"` — and the vertical rule draws on the inline-start edge. Nothing in the divider names a physical side.

Icon-only: the icon is decorative (`aria-hidden`) and gives the separator no name, so it must not carry meaning. When the icon says something ("end of results"), set `label` — it becomes the separator's accessible name — or use real text beside it.

Contrast: the line is a decorative graphic, which WCAG 1.4.11 exempts — the default grey and the `gradient` (transparent at both ends) are deliberately quiet. Where the rule is the ONLY boundary between two interactive regions, set `color` to a token with at least 3:1 against the surface (e.g. `var(--color-gray-500)`) and use `solid`; under forced colours every variant already repaints in `CanvasText`.

components.name: Drag-and-Drop List
components.description: Native HTML5 drag-and-drop reorderable list with priority badges, keyboard move alternatives and item removal.
whenToUse: Letting users manually order a short-to-medium list (priorities, steps, playlists).
You want native drag-and-drop with keyboard move alternatives.
For moving items between two lists, use Transfer; for cross-column flow, Kanban.

examples.title: Persisting a reorder
examples.code:
<sv-dnd-list
  [(items)]="items"
  [saving]="saving()"
  [error]="error()"
  (reordered)="onReorder($event)" />

// The list reorders before the server has heard about it, so it hands back the
// only copy of the previous order. Bind [saving] so a second drag cannot start
// while the first is in flight — that is what keeps rollback() unambiguous.
onReorder(event: DndReorderEvent): void {
  this.saving.set(true);
  this.api.saveOrder(event.items.map(i => i.id), event.requestKey).subscribe({
    next:  () => this.saving.set(false),
    error: () => {
      event.rollback();
      this.error.set('Could not save the new order.');
      this.saving.set(false);
    },
  });
}

customization: Native drag-and-drop reordering.
Set `useHandle` to restrict dragging to the grip handle only (rows can't be dragged by their body).
Per-item badges and remove control.
All three writes — `(reordered)`, `(itemRemoved)`, `(itemChanged)` — carry `requestKey` and `rollback()`, because each is applied before the server has heard about it.
`saving` locks dragging and the row controls while a write is in flight; `error` reports the failure above the list.
The `kanban` variant stacks to a single column on phones (`grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-3`) so cards stay readable, then sits three-across from `sm` up.
accessibility: A keyboard-lifted row is scrolled into view (`block: 'nearest'`) at every arrow press, and a mouse drag that hovers near the top or bottom edge of a scrolling panel scrolls it, so a long list can be reordered past what is on screen.

In the default, checklist and compact variants every row has a real grip button (`data-dnd-handle`) for keyboard grab/drop: Space or Enter lifts, the arrow keys move, Space drops (one `reordered` for the whole move) and Escape cancels and restores the original order.

Labelled Move up / Move down buttons in those same variants commit one step at a time — unaffected by `useHandle`. The kanban variant moves cards between columns with named Move left / Move right buttons that are revealed on keyboard focus as well as hover.
After a removal focus moves to the row that took its place (or the previous row, or the list itself when it is empty) instead of falling to <body>.
A polite live region announces the new position after every reorder, removal and complete toggle.
variants: Persisting a Reorder, and Putting It Back

components.name: Dock
components.description: A macOS-style launcher bar on any edge of its container. The item under the pointer and its neighbours grow — by transform only: each control scales from the centre of its edge and the items slide apart by the room they took, so nothing is laid out again and a target never shrinks — and the swell follows keyboard focus too. An APG toolbar with one tab stop and arrow keys along the dock (in the order the eye sees under RTL); items are real links through the link adapter, with aria-current on the current page, or buttons; badges, disabled items, labels on hover and focus, and no magnification under reduced motion.
whenToUse: An app launcher or a set of workspace tools that should stay one move away along an edge of a canvas, desktop-style page or kiosk.
A short set — about four to eight items. Past that the swell and the labels get crowded; use a sidebar or a menu.
Not as the main navigation of a phone app — use Bottom Navigation, whose labels are always visible — and not for a handful of secondary actions on one page, where a Toolbar or Speed Dial fits.

examples.title: Items
examples.code:
readonly apps: SvDockItem[] = [
  { id: 'home', label: 'Overview', icon: 'home', route: '/workspace' },   // a link, through SV_LINK_ADAPTER
  { id: 'mail', label: 'Mail', icon: 'mail', route: '/workspace/mail', badge: 12 },
  { id: 'new', label: 'New document', icon: 'plus' },                   // no route or href: a button
  { id: 'billing', label: 'Billing', icon: 'credit-card', disabled: true },
  { id: 'help', label: 'Help', icon: 'info', href: 'https://example.com/help', external: true },
];

examples.title: A vertical dock on the left edge
Migrating from PrimeNG p-dock
examples.code:
<!-- PrimeNG -->
<p-dock [model]="items" position="bottom" />

<!-- Styloviz: MenuItem { label, icon, routerLink, url, command } → SvDockItem { id, label, icon | image, route, href } -->
<sv-dock [items]="items" position="bottom" (itemSelect)="run($event.item)" />

customization: `position`: `bottom` (default), `top`, `left` or `right` — a physical edge, like a drawer's; it also sets the orientation.
`placement`: `absolute` pins the dock to that edge of the nearest positioned ancestor; `static` leaves it in the flow.
`size`: `sm` 40 px, `md` 48 px, `lg` 56 px items. `magnification` turns the swell off; `magnificationScale` (1–2, default 1.6) sets the peak.

Items take an `icon` (a registered glyph name) or an `image` (only safe URLs load); a `badge` (count or short text); `route` (via `SV_LINK_ADAPTER`) or `href` (with `external` for a new tab); `disabled`. `itemKey` sets identity.
The bar is a tinted surface (`bg-white/85`, `dark:bg-gray-900/85`), items use the `gray-*` tokens, the focus ring and current-page dot `primary-*`, badges `danger-*`.
Strings come from the `layout` labels: `dock` (the toolbar name, overridden by `ariaLabel`) and `dockNewTab`.
The magnification and fitting math is exported as pure functions — `svDockLayout`, `svDockScale`, `svDockPointerIndex`, `svDockFit` — for a custom dock.
accessibility: A `role="toolbar"` named by `ariaLabel` (default "Dock"), with `aria-orientation`. One tab stop (roving tabindex): Tab lands on the current page, else the last item used, and leaves the dock.

Arrow keys along the dock move between items (←/→ for a horizontal dock — mirrored under RTL so the arrows follow what the eye sees; ↑/↓ for a vertical one), Home/End go to the ends, Enter and Space activate. `itemSelect` reports whether the pointer or the keyboard did it.

Every item is a real `<a href>` or `<button>` named by its label, with the badge read after it ("Mail, 12") and "(opens in a new tab)" for an external link. The current route is `aria-current="page"`.

A disabled item stays focusable (APG: discoverable) with `aria-disabled="true"` and never activates. An unsafe `href`/`route` (`javascript:`, `data:`) is never rendered: the item is shown unavailable.
The label shows on hover AND on keyboard focus, stays while the pointer is over it, and Escape hides it (WCAG 1.4.13).

Magnification is `transform` only and only ever enlarges a target (WCAG 2.5.8); it is off for touch and entirely off under `prefers-reduced-motion` — no transform at all. Focus outlines survive forced colors.

It fits its container at any width (WCAG 1.4.10): when the row is longer than the room, the items shrink evenly — never below 32 px, so every target stays above 24 px with a legible glyph — and magnification pauses; when even that does not fit, the dock scrolls along its axis, so no control is cut off.

components.name: Donut Chart
components.description: The Pro pie chart drawn as a ring — `variant="donut"` — with the total (or your own text) in the hole and the hovered slice read out there, plus a gradient ring (`sv-gradient-donut-chart`) with per-slice radial gradients and a staggered entrance.
whenToUse: Showing parts of a whole when there are only a few segments (≤6).
You want a center label/total in the donut hole.
For precise value comparison, a Bar Chart is easier to read than slices.

examples.title: Your own text in the hole, a thinner ring

customization: Solid or per-slice gradient fills. The shading is DECORATIVE — arc length is the whole of the data — and the gradient variant says so under the plot, because every other gradient in dataviz carries a value and a reader arrives trained to look for the second dimension.
`sliceOrder` keeps the host's order (default) or sorts largest first, which is the arrangement a ring is easiest to read in.

`groupBelow` and `maxSlices` fold the unreadable tail into one `Other` slice and disclose how many and what share. Off by default; a single small slice is never folded, since an `Other` of one is that slice with its name taken away.
Center label/total slot.
Configurable thickness and gap.
Handle `sliceSelect` (arc or legend click) for selection.

`valuePolicy` decides what happens to a segment this chart cannot plot — a negative, `NaN` or `Infinity`. A ring divides by the sum of its values, so an unplottable one is not merely undrawable: left in the denominator it changes the angle of every OTHER segment, which is why there is no "leave it alone" option. `omit` (default) drops it and says the percentages are of the remainder; `reject` refuses the dataset. `clamp` is not offered: a clamped segment is a 0° arc, which leaves nothing to mark, so a request for it falls back to `omit` with a dev warning.
accessibility: The ring, the arc labels, the centre readout and the legend all read the SAME resolved list. They did not: the arcs were built from the plotted slices while every label indexed the raw input, so the moment the value policy omitted one, index `i` named a different slice from the one it drew — an arc announcing its neighbour's label, and a legend entry whose hover highlighted the wrong wedge.

The SVG is a `role="group"` with a generated label listing each segment and its share (override via `ariaLabel`) — `group`, not `img`, because a slice can be a tab stop and an `img`'s subtree is pruned.

Arc angle is share and the raw value is nowhere else on the page, so `sv-data-summary-table` publishes segment, value and percentage — on both the solid and the gradient donut. No overview line: the generated name has already read every label with its share before the table begins, and what the table adds is the raw numbers and a structure to compare them in.

When the long tail is folded, the table lists every folded segment in its own row under `Other`, each marked `(in Other)`, which is what the fold notice promises. Because that table is for screen readers and never drawn, the visible notice also names the folded segments itself. `Other` is drawn in a neutral slate rather than the colour of the first segment it folded.
The center label is not a row. `centerLabel` renders as real SVG `<text>` inside the `group`, so it is already in the accessibility tree; repeating it would invent a segment that does not exist.
The legend conveys labels and values as text.

Whatever `valuePolicy` does to the data is stated in the rendered output, under the plot and under the empty state — how many segments were dropped, their real values, and that the shares are of what remains. A `console.warn` is not a disclosure: the person reading the dashboard never sees it.
A ring whose every value is zero shows the empty state rather than a blank circle, and the sentence beneath distinguishes "the data arrived and was all zero" from "the fetch returned nothing".
