components.name: Drawer
components.description: Slide-over panel from any edge with 6 semantic variants, 6 sizes, overlay/push modes, built-in variant-styled footer actions, loading & non-modal states, and ESC/backdrop close.
whenToUse: Showing secondary content or forms alongside the page without full navigation.
Filters, details, settings, carts — anything that slides over and dismisses.
Semantic panels (danger, success, warning) — reach for the matching `variant`.
For a centered, attention-grabbing dialog use a Modal.
components.usage: <sv-drawer [(open)]="isOpen" position="right" variant="primary" title="Filters" subtitle="Refine results" (closed)="isOpen = false">…</sv-drawer>

examples.title: Back closes it, by default
examples.code:
<!-- A drawer is usually a destination — the details panel for the row you
     clicked — so Back means "undo that", and on a phone it is the system
     gesture. Set [backCloses]="false" for a drawer that is part of the
     shell, and call provideSvOverlayRouteClose() so a route change closes
     it too. -->
<sv-drawer [(open)]="showDetails" title="Contact" [backCloses]="true">
  <ng-container slot="body">…</ng-container>
</sv-drawer>

examples.title: Guard an unsaved form
examples.code:
<sv-drawer
  [(open)]="editing"
  title="Edit contact"
  [dirty]="form.dirty"
  unsavedMessage="This contact has unsaved changes."
  (discarded)="log('discarded via ' + $event)">
  <ng-container slot="body">…</ng-container>
</sv-drawer>

examples.title: Danger variant with subtitle
examples.code:
<sv-drawer
  [(open)]="open"
  variant="danger"
  title="Danger zone"
  subtitle="Irreversible account actions"
  (dismissed)="onClose($event)">…</sv-drawer>

examples.title: Modal, but not dimmed
examples.code:
<!-- Traps focus and blocks the page WITHOUT a dim layer:
     a full-height editor panel. -->
<sv-drawer
  [(open)]="open"
  modality="modal"
  [showBackdrop]="false"
  title="Edit invoice">…</sv-drawer>

examples.title: Show / hide header & footer
examples.code:
Custom content only…
 …

customization: Six semantic variants with tinted header/footer, icon badge + accent bar; toggle the badge via `showIcon`.
Open from any edge; six sizes (xs–full). Header and footer are independently optional via `[showHeader]`, `[showHeaderDivider]` and `[showFooter]` (all default `true`).
Built-in variant-styled `primaryAction`/`secondaryAction` footer buttons, or fully custom `[slot=footer]`.
Overlay or push mode (`mode="push"` + `pushTarget`), modal or non-modal (`showBackdrop`), backdrop blur, ESC/backdrop toggles, and a spinner `loading` state.
Body scroll-lock with scrollbar-width compensation; `customClass` on the panel.

Route and history integration: `[closeOnNavigation]` (default on) closes the panel when the app navigates — a drawer is often non-modal, so one left open beside a new page is worse than a stale modal — and `[backCloses]` is default ON here, unlike the Modal, because a drawer is usually a destination rather than a transient question. Wire `provideSvOverlayRouteClose()` for the route half.

A controlled-close policy: `[dirty]` raises the same unsaved-changes prompt the Modal uses — over the panel, focused on Keep editing, closing afterwards with the reason the user actually acted on — and `[canClose]` is your own silent veto. `(discarded)` / `(closeCancelled)` report which way it went. One primitive for both families (`createCloseGuard` in `@styloviz/core`), because a prompt written twice drifts.
Responsive: non-`full` sizes cap to `90vw` (left/right) or `90vh` (top/bottom) so the drawer never exceeds a phone viewport, leaving a sliver of backdrop to tap.

`[sheetOnNarrow]="true"` switches a side (or top) drawer to a bottom sheet at 640px and below: it rises from the bottom edge, sizes to its content up to 85% of the screen, is padded clear of the home indicator and sits above the virtual keyboard. `effectivePosition()` reports the edge actually in use. Off by default.

`[swipeToClose]="true"`: a finger or pen drags the open panel toward its own edge (right, left, up or down — the bottom edge for a sheet) and it follows; release past a third of the panel (at most 96px) or on a flick faster than `swipeVelocity` (0.5 px/ms) and it closes, anything less springs back. Locked to the panel axis after 8px so scrolling inside never drags it; a mouse never swipes. It goes through the normal close path — a dirty drawer still asks, a loading one refuses — and reports `escape`. The gesture is core `svSwipeGesture`, shared with Sidebar Nav. Off by default.
accessibility: `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal` (when backdrop shown), labelled via `aria-labelledby` (title) and `aria-describedby` (subtitle); `aria-busy` while loading.

`modality` decides the contract. A **modal** drawer traps Tab, marks the rest of the page `inert`, locks the page scroll, asserts `aria-modal="true"` and moves focus to `initialFocus` or the first focusable element. An **inline** one does none of those: the page beside it stays usable, so it does not take focus either unless you name an `initialFocus`. Focus is restored on close whichever it is — and if the trigger is gone by then, to the nearest thing that outlived it.

`showBackdrop` controls only the dim layer, and defaults to following the modality — so `[showBackdrop]="false"` on its own gives you an inline drawer; set `modality` when you mean the contract. `modality` and `mode` are different axes: `mode` is overlay-vs-push (layout), `modality` is modal-vs-inline (may the page still be used).
Hiding the header (`[showHeader]="false"`) removes the built-in close button — provide an alternative dismissal (footer action, ESC, or backdrop) so keyboard users can always exit.
`opened`/`closed` fire for every transition; `dismissed` reports the reason (backdrop / escape / close-button / programmatic).
Reduced motion: the slide, the backdrop fade and the push-mode padding glide are all dropped — the panel appears and leaves in place.

inputs.description: Optional title in the default header slot.

inputs.name: subtitle
inputs.description: Optional secondary line beneath the title (also used for aria-describedby).

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible label used when no `title` is provided.

inputs.name: showHeader
inputs.description: Render the built-in header bar.

inputs.name: showHeaderDivider
inputs.description: Bottom dividing line under the header.

inputs.name: showFooter
inputs.description: Render the footer slot.

inputs.name: showIcon
inputs.description: Show the built-in variant icon badge in the header.

inputs.name: showClose
inputs.description: Show the close (×) button.

inputs.name: showBackdrop
inputs.description: Render the dimming backdrop (set false for a non-modal drawer).

inputs.name: modality
inputs.description: Which contract this drawer follows.

inputs.name: backdropBlur
inputs.description: Apply a frosted-glass blur to the backdrop.

inputs.name: closeOnBackdrop
inputs.description: Close when the backdrop is clicked.

inputs.name: closeOnEsc
inputs.description: Close on the ESC key.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: Busy state. While `true` the panel shows a spinner overlay and all close paths (button, backdrop, ESC) are blocked so a running task can finish.

inputs.name: pendingDismissal
inputs.description: May the user dismiss the drawer while `loading` is true? The same answer Modal gives through its own `pendingDismissal` and `loadingCancelled`. `'block'` (the default) refuses every close path while loading. `'abort'` lets every close path through and emits `loadingCancelled` first, so the host can abort the work it started — the drawer does not own the request.

inputs.name: closeOnNavigation
inputs.description: Does a navigation close this drawer? Without it a route change leaves the drawer open over a page it has nothing to do with — and a drawer is worse than a modal here, because it is often non-modal: the user can carry on with the new page while a panel from the old one sits beside it. Takes effect once the app calls `provideSvOverlayRouteClose()` from `@styloviz/layout`; without that provider nothing changes.

inputs.name: backCloses
inputs.description: Does the browser Back button close this drawer? On by default here, unlike the modal — and the asymmetry is the point. A drawer is usually a DESTINATION: a details panel for the row you clicked, a filter sheet you opened on purpose. Back is the gesture for "undo that", and on a phone it is the system gesture. A modal is more often a transient question, where Back should belong to the page. The mechanism is a marked `history` entry, not a route: the URL is untouched.

inputs.name: dirty
inputs.description: Is there unsaved work in this drawer? A drawer is the kit's preferred home for a long edit form — that is what the size and the scroll are for — and it is dismissed by a click anywhere in the large dim area beside it, so one missed click would discard the lot. Set this and the drawer asks first. The prompt is the same as the Modal's, from the same primitive (`createCloseGuard`), so the two behave identically.

inputs.name: canClose
inputs.description: The host's own veto, consulted before anything else. Return `false` to refuse a close, or nothing to have no opinion. A veto is silent — it does NOT raise the unsaved-changes prompt, because the host refused for its own reasons and owns its own messaging.

inputs.name: unsavedTitle
inputs.description: Heading of the unsaved-changes prompt.

inputs.name: unsavedMessage
inputs.default: 'This panel has changes that have not been saved.'
inputs.description: Body of the unsaved-changes prompt.

inputs.name: discardLabel
inputs.description: Label of the button that closes and loses the changes.

inputs.name: keepEditingLabel
inputs.description: Label of the button that returns to the panel.

inputs.name: loadingText
inputs.description: Accessible label announced while `loading` is true.

inputs.name: initialFocus
inputs.description: CSS selector for the element to focus first when the drawer opens (e.g. `'#search'`). Falls back to the first focusable element.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Content relationship. `overlay` (default) floats above the page; `push` squeezes `pushTarget` aside so the panel and content sit side by side.

inputs.name: pushTarget
inputs.description: CSS selector for the element pushed aside in `mode="push"` (e.g. `'#app-content-area'`). No-op when empty or in overlay mode.

inputs.name: primaryAction
inputs.description: Built-in primary footer action label. Empty hides the button.

inputs.name: secondaryAction
inputs.description: Built-in secondary footer action label. Empty hides the button.

inputs.name: customClass
inputs.description: Extra CSS classes merged onto the panel.

outputs.name: loadingCancelled
outputs.description: The drawer was dismissed while `loading` — by a close path under `pendingDismissal="abort"`, or by a navigation (which `loading` cannot hold back). Emitted BEFORE `closed`, so the host can stop the work.

outputs.name: opened
outputs.description: Emits when the drawer opens by any means.

outputs.name: closed
outputs.description: Emits when the drawer closes by any means.

outputs.name: dismissed
outputs.description: Emitted alongside `closed`, describing what triggered the close. A close caused by a navigation or a Back press reports `'programmatic'` here — the published union cannot grow — and its exact reason on `dismissedBy`.

outputs.name: dismissedBy
outputs.description: Emitted alongside `dismissed` with the exact reason, including `'route'` (the app navigated) and `'history'` (the Back button).

outputs.name: discarded
outputs.description: The user discarded unsaved changes; the close follows.

outputs.name: closeCancelled
outputs.description: The user backed out of a close and returned to the panel.

outputs.name: primaryClick
outputs.description: Emitted when the built-in primary footer action is clicked.

outputs.name: secondaryClick
outputs.description: Emitted when the built-in secondary footer action is clicked.

outputs.name: openChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `open` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(open)]`.

components.name: Dropdown Menu
components.description: Action menu with checkbox/radio items, 2 themes, 3 sizes, groups, descriptions, badges, header/footer slots, type-ahead keyboard nav and auto-flipping placement.
whenToUse: Offering a list of actions or links from a trigger (kebab/overflow menus).
Toggling options (checkbox items) or picking one of several (radio items).
You want grouped items, icons, descriptions, shortcuts, badges and danger actions.
For a single form choice, use a Select; for global search, a Command Palette.

examples.title: Checkbox items (stay open)
examples.code:
<sv-dropdown-menu [items]="columnItems()" (itemClick)="toggleColumn($event)" />
// item: { id, label, type: 'checkbox', checked: visible[id], keepOpen: true }

examples.title: Radio items (single select)
examples.code:
<sv-dropdown-menu [groups]="sortGroups()" (itemClick)="setSort($event)" />
// group: { label: 'Sort by', items } — the label is what the radio set announces
// item:  { id, label, type: 'radio', checked: sort === id }

examples.title: Async item — [itemAction]
examples.code:
<!-- The menu runs the work: it stays open with a spinner on the row, a
     second click on it is refused, and a rejection is shown in the menu
     with Try again (only when retrying could plausibly succeed). -->
<sv-dropdown-menu
  [items]="rowItems"
  [itemAction]="runRowAction"
  (itemActionFailed)="log($event)" />

examples.title: The item action itself

customization: Two themes (default · dark) and three density sizes (sm · md · lg).
Action, checkbox and radio item types; per-item icon, description, shortcut, badge, danger, divider, keepOpen and link (`href`).
Flat `items` or `groups` with section labels; optional `[slot=header]` / `[slot=footer]` (auto-hide when empty).
Portaled to `document.body`, re-anchored on scroll of any ancestor, auto-flips + clamps to the viewport; `closeOnSelect`, `offset`, `minWidth`, `customClass`.

Placement arithmetic is shared with Popover and Tooltip: `start`/`end` mirror for RTL text, coordinates are corrected for a transformed ancestor that has become the containing block, and a trigger that is removed or collapses while the menu is open closes it instead of leaving a menu of actions for a row that is gone.
Responsive: the menu caps its width and height to the viewport and a long list scrolls internally, so it never overflows a phone or short landscape screen.
`triggerMode="contextmenu"` and the public `openAt(x, y)` method turn this into a right-click context menu — see the dedicated Context Menu entry.

`[itemAction]` hands an item's async work to the menu: the row shows a spinner and goes `aria-busy`, every row refuses input while one is working, a rejection renders inside the menu with a Try again button when the failure is retryable, and closing the menu aborts the request. One async contract, shared with the rest of the kit — `createAsyncAction` in `@styloviz/core`.

Cascading submenus: give an item `children` and it opens a submenu instead of running — beside its parent, flipped at the viewport edge, to the LEFT in RTL. Hover opens it after `submenuOpenDelay` (120 ms); while the pointer crosses other items inside the safe corridor toward an open submenu the switch waits `submenuCloseDelay` (300 ms). Nest as deep as you need; ids must be unique across the whole tree. With `sheetOnNarrow`, each level is a bottom sheet with a "Back to …" row.
accessibility: Trigger exposes `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`; the menu uses `menu` + `menuitem`/`menuitemcheckbox`/`menuitemradio` roles with `aria-checked` and `aria-activedescendant` tracking the highlighted item — correct across groups and disabled items.
Keyboard: ↑/↓ navigate (skipping disabled), Home/End jump to ends, type-ahead jumps to a matching label, Enter selects, Esc closes.

Submenus follow the APG submenu pattern: the parent item carries `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded` and (while open) `aria-controls`; each level is its own `role="menu"` named by its parent. ArrowRight, Enter or Space opens one on its first enabled child; ArrowLeft and Escape close one level and return to the parent — mirrored in RTL. DOM focus stays on the trigger at every depth and `aria-activedescendant` follows the highlight, held by item id so a refreshed list cannot move it.

Type-ahead is locale-aware: labels and keystrokes are folded the same way — accents stripped (`e` reaches "Édition"), case lowered by the kit locale (`provideSvLocale('tr')` lowers `I` to `ı`), full-width and ligature forms normalised — so a letter the user can see is a letter that matches. The Menubar uses the same rule.
variants: Accessibility — a closed menu is really closed
Context Menu — One shared menu across many rows
Context Menu — Checkable, disabled & destructive items

inputs.name: open
inputs.description: Controls menu visibility. Use `[(open)]` for two-way binding.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the menu's contents are being fetched — a permissions-aware or workspace-scoped menu is a list the server owns.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Load failure. Use `toSvDataError()` from `@styloviz/core` to normalize an `HttpErrorResponse`.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: Flat list of menu items, rendered as a single ungrouped section; ignored when `groups` is non-empty.

inputs.name: groups
inputs.description: Grouped menu items. Takes precedence over `items`.

inputs.name: placement
inputs.description: Where the menu opens relative to its anchor. Same flip/clamp resolution applies whether the anchor is the trigger's bounding rect (click mode) or a point (`openAt()` / right-click) — for a point, `bottom-start` means "top-left corner of the panel at the cursor," which is the conventional context-menu placement.

inputs.name: itemAction
inputs.description: The work an item performs, run by the menu. `(itemClick)` alone is a notification: the menu emits the id and closes in the same tick, so a slow action shows nothing to say the click registered. Give the menu the work and the menu stays open, the row shows a spinner and goes `aria-busy`, a second click on it is refused rather than queued (first click wins), and a rejection is rendered in the menu. `(itemClick)` and `(itemSelect)` also emit for every accepted click. Wiring both this and a click handler does the work twice.

inputs.name: triggerMode
inputs.description: How the menu opens — left-click toggle, or right-click at the cursor. See DropdownMenuTriggerMode.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Panel theme.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Density preset.

inputs.name: offset
inputs.description: Gap between the trigger and the panel (px).

inputs.name: flip
inputs.description: Flip to the opposite side when there's no room; always clamps to viewport.

inputs.name: closeOnSelect
inputs.description: Close the menu after selecting an item (per-item `keepOpen` overrides).

inputs.name: submenuOpenDelay
inputs.description: Hover time before an item with `children` opens its submenu, in ms. Long enough that a pointer sweeping down the list does not flash every submenu it crosses.

inputs.name: submenuCloseDelay
inputs.description: Grace before an open submenu closes once the pointer moves to another item, in ms — applied while the pointer is inside the safe corridor toward the submenu (`svInSafeCorridor`), so a diagonal path to it does not close it on the way. Outside the corridor the submenu switches after `submenuOpenDelay`.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Prevent the menu from opening.

inputs.name: minWidth
inputs.description: Minimum width of the menu panel (px).

inputs.name: triggerRole
inputs.description: ARIA role for the trigger WRAPPER, or `null` to leave it generic. The wrapper is a layout `<div>` that provides the bounding rect to anchor against. That is invisible to a host — until the host is a composite whose own role requires the trigger to be one of its owned children: a `role="menubar"` must own `role="menuitem"`s, and a roleless div in between breaks that ownership. Passing `'none'` takes the wrapper out of the accessibility tree so the composite owns the button directly. `'none'` also stops the menu writing `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-owns` and `aria-activedescendant` at all, so the composite is the single writer: `panelId` and `activeDescendantId` are public for exactly that, and `sv-menubar` binds all five itself. In the default case the menu writes its state on the projected trigger — the element that takes focus — not on this wrapper.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible label for the menu (role="menu").

inputs.name: targetLabel
inputs.description: What these actions act ON — a row, a file, a record.

inputs.name: nativeMenuSelector
inputs.description: Right-clicks inside an element matching this selector keep the BROWSER's context menu.

inputs.name: customClass
inputs.description: Extra CSS classes merged onto the menu panel.

inputs.name: sheetOnNarrow
inputs.description: Become a bottom sheet on a narrow viewport.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The host should re-run the failed load.

outputs.name: itemClick
outputs.description: Emits the id of the clicked item.

outputs.name: itemActionFailed
outputs.description: An `[itemAction]` rejected. The menu stays open and shows the message.

outputs.name: itemSelect
outputs.description: Emits the full clicked item object.

outputs.name: opened
outputs.description: Emitted after the menu opens (by any means, including `[(open)]`).

outputs.name: closed
outputs.description: Emitted after the menu closes (by any means, including `[(open)]`).

outputs.name: openChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `open` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(open)]`.

components.name: Embedding Map
components.description: A 2D projection of an embedding space with clusters and lasso selection, drawn without inviting the false reading every t-SNE plot invites. 3 variants: scatter, clusters and selection.
whenToUse: Exploring an embedding space that has already been projected to two dimensions by UMAP, t-SNE or PCA.
Checking whether a clustering actually separated anything, rather than whether it looks like it did.
Lassoing a region of interest out of a corpus for labelling or review.
customization: `points` must already carry projected `x` / `y`; the component does no dimensionality reduction. `clusters` supplies labels and optional colours.

`[projection]` carries how the points were made — `{ method, params, model, modelVersion }` (`EmbeddingProjection`) — and renders as a caption under the plot ("Projection: UMAP. Parameters: n_neighbors 15, min_dist 0.1. Embeddings: text-embedding-3-small, version 2024-01."), folded into the plot’s `role="img"` name too. Two maps of one corpus are comparable only when these match, so with no `[projection]` the caption says the method is not recorded rather than saying nothing. `svProjectionMetaLabel()` builds the same sentence outside the component; `DEMO_PROJECTION` is the showcase’s.
Three layouts via `variant`: `scatter`, `clusters` (per-cluster separation plus the entangled pairs) and `selection` (lasso).
Both axes share ONE scale. Stretching them independently to fill the box destroys local shape, which is the only property these layouts preserve.
Separation is measured as k-NN label agreement: for each point, the share of its `neighbours` (default 10) nearest neighbours in the projection that carry the same cluster.

`[knnMaxPoints]` (1200, from the still-exported `SV_KNN_MAX_POINTS`; set it to `SV_CANVAS_MIN`, 2000, to measure every map drawn as SVG exactly) is the point past which the statistics are computed on a deterministic even sample — labelled as sampled, never silently. It is a performance budget, not a statistical one: the grid-indexed k-NN is roughly linear but synchronous (about 65 ms at 2,000 points and 300 ms at 10,000 for both statistics), so it belongs to whoever knows what machine this runs on, and the purity figure and the tangle table always use the SAME cap so two statistics about one picture cannot disagree.

`[lowPurity]` (0.6, from `SV_LOW_PURITY`) is the share of same-cluster neighbours below which separation is called weak. Sixty per cent is weak for four well-defined topics and rather good for forty fine-grained intents that genuinely overlap. It is a share, so 0–1; a figure above 1 would call every projection weak — a permanent warning, which is the same as none — and is refused with a dev warning.
The lasso is point-in-polygon on screen coordinates, with the half-open vertex rule, so a point level with a corner is not randomly missed. It closes on release, not on every move.
Emits `selectionChange` with the caught points and `pointSelect` for a single dot; `selectedIds` is two-way.

`[maxKeyboardPoints]` (200, from `SV_KEYBOARD_POINT_CEILING`) is how many points one cluster offers to a keyboard walk. It is a budget for a person, not a renderer: two hundred rows is a long walk and two thousand is a list nobody finishes — so raise it for forty points per cluster and lower it for a million. Whatever it is, the list says what it left out.

`navCluster` is two-way: the cluster the keyboard walk is inside, `null` at the top level. A reader four hundred rows into one cluster who follows a link and comes back can be put back where they were, which a private signal could not do.

`[renderer]` (`'auto'`) picks the drawing surface: SVG below `SV_CANVAS_MIN` (2,000 points) and a canvas above it. Neither answer is right at both ends — real nodes mean real hover and a `<title>` per dot, and 100,000 of them is a layout the browser does not finish. `'svg'` and `'canvas'` force it.

The canvas has no per-point nodes, so the dots are not focusable and carry no `<title>`. That is stated on the chart and the keyboard route is the browse list, which renders under both renderers — the list is not a nicety here, it is the only reading a keyboard gets.

`[devicePixelRatio]` pins the backing store for a screenshot or a test; unset reads the browser's, clamped to 3. A canvas sized in CSS pixels on a 2× display is blurry, and a blurry scatter is one whose dots have a different apparent size — the exact property the caveat tells the reader not to interpret.

The neighbourhood statistics run on a uniform grid rather than a full scan: 40,000 points take about 0.6s where the scan takes about 10 minutes, and a full k=10 pass over 100,000 points takes under 3s. The grid is exact, not approximate — it returns the same neighbours the scan does, including the tie-breaks, which the specs assert point by point on a uniform cloud, a cloud flat in one axis and a lattice where every distance is a tie. `[knnMaxPoints]` is still yours to set; what changed is what it costs you.

Hit-testing and the lasso go through the same index. A click resolves to the NEAREST point rather than the first one in range, and the lasso tests only the cells its bounding box touches — 100,000 ray casts on pointer-up is a freeze at the moment the reader expects their selection.
Not offered: zoom and pan. The statistics are computed once per data change rather than per frame, so the figures above are a load-time cost and not a per-interaction one.
accessibility: The plot is `role="img"` with an accessible name carrying the point count, the separation finding and how the map was made (method, parameters, model — or that it is not recorded), so the conclusion does not depend on seeing the picture.

A dot carrying a `<title>` is not an accessibility story: an SVG `<circle>` is not focusable, so nothing in the plot answers an arrow key. The route in is a two-level list in a `<details>` beside the chart — clusters, then the points inside one — with one tab stop per level, arrow keys inside it, Enter to drill in and Escape to come back.

`tabindex` is deliberately NOT on the dots. It satisfies the same audit rule and produces one tab stop per point, in whatever order the host's array happened to be, with no way out but Tab — which is worse than the bug, because it looks solved.

A point row reads its name, its cluster, its position in the list and what is AROUND it — the share of its nearest points that carry the same label. Not its coordinates: those are layout units, and comparing them is the false reading the caveat refuses.

The point list is capped at `[maxKeyboardPoints]` and says how many of the cluster it did not reach, naming the cluster figures as what covers the rest. A list that claims to be the alternative to the plot and silently holds 200 of 5,000 is worse than no list.
Points with no cluster label get a row of their own, or they would be reachable by pointer and by nothing else.
In the selection variant, activating a row toggles that point — a lasso is a pointer gesture and cannot be anything else, so without it the variant has no keyboard story at all.
The caveat about distances is rendered on the chart as text, not as a tooltip.

Switching to the canvas renderer takes the per-point nodes away and nothing else: the plot keeps its `role="img"` summary label, the caveat and the separation finding stay, the browse list still walks the clusters and points, and a line on the chart says the dots are not individually focusable and where to go instead.
variants: Scatter — With the Caveat on the Chart
Clusters — The Numbers Disagree With the Picture

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the projected points are being fetched; shows a chart skeleton in place of the plot.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Load failure, shown as an error panel in place of the content. Use `toSvDataError()` from `@styloviz/core` to normalize an `HttpErrorResponse`.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Presentation: the scatter, the cluster report, or lasso selection.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP 47 locale for dates and numbers.

inputs.name: points
inputs.description: The projected points.

inputs.name: clusters
inputs.description: Cluster metadata — labels and optional colours.

inputs.name: projection
inputs.description: How the points were made — `{ method, params, model, modelVersion }`. Rendered as a caption under the plot and folded into its `role="img"` name, so two maps can be compared; unset, the caption says the method is not recorded.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Plot box, in px.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Plot box height in px — the SVG viewBox height the points are projected into.

inputs.name: neighbours
inputs.description: Neighbours used for the separation statistics.

inputs.name: selectedIds
inputs.description: Ids of the currently selected points.

inputs.name: lowPurity
inputs.description: Share of same-cluster neighbours below which separation is called weak. A judgement about one kind of data. Sixty per cent is weak separation for four well-defined topics and rather good for forty fine-grained intents that genuinely overlap — the same figure calls one projection broken and flatters the other. A share, so `0`–`1`.

inputs.name: knnMaxPoints
inputs.description: Points above which the neighbourhood statistics use a deterministic sample. A performance budget, not a statistical one. The k-NN reads a grid index, so it is roughly linear — but it runs twice (purity and cluster tangle), synchronously, whenever `points` or `neighbours` change: about 65 ms at 2,000 points and 300 ms at 10,000 on a laptop. Set it to `SV_CANVAS_MIN` (2,000) to measure every SVG-drawn map exactly, or higher if your machines can take the longer freeze for an exact figure. The result is still LABELLED as sampled whatever the cap is.

inputs.name: renderer
inputs.description: How the plot is drawn. `'auto'` because neither answer is right at both ends. Below a couple of thousand points the SVG is better and not merely adequate — real nodes mean real hover, a `<title>` per dot and a selection the browser paints for you. Above it the DOM is the ceiling: 100,000 elements is a layout the browser does not finish. `'svg'` and `'canvas'` force it, for a host that knows something this component does not.

inputs.name: devicePixelRatio
inputs.description: Device pixel ratio for the canvas backing store. An input so a test and a screenshot can pin it; unset reads the browser's, clamped — see `SV_MAX_DPR`.

inputs.name: maxKeyboardPoints
inputs.description: Points a keyboard reader can walk inside one cluster. A budget for a person, not a renderer — see `SV_KEYBOARD_POINT_CEILING`. Whatever it is set to, the list says what it left out.

inputs.name: navCluster
inputs.description: The cluster whose points the keyboard walk is inside; `null` at the top. A `model()` rather than private state. A reader four hundred rows into `billing` who follows a link and comes back lands at the top of the cluster list with no way to say where they were — unless the host can read this back and restore it, which it cannot do with a private signal.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: Emitted when the user presses the error panel's "Try again" button (retryable errors only); the host should re-run the failed load.

outputs.name: selectionChange
outputs.description: The reader finished a lasso.

outputs.name: pointSelect
outputs.description: The reader activated a single point.

outputs.name: selectedIdsChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `selectedIds` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(selectedIds)]`.

outputs.name: navClusterChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `navCluster` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(navCluster)]`.

components.name: Empty State
components.description: Full-page or inline empty states with icons or illustrations, titles and action buttons — dashed, ghost-preview and glow variants, five sizes, an onboarding checklist, a search echo with suggestions, and a reason (no data, no results, error, no access) that picks the right copy.
whenToUse: Communicating that a list, search or section has no content — and what to do next.
First-run states, empty searches, cleared inboxes.
For load failures specifically, use the Result component (error status).

Not sure this is the right outcome surface? Compare toast, banner, result, empty state, notification center and modal by severity, persistence and whether the user can correct it in the “Choosing a feedback pattern” guide under Guides.

examples.title: With actions
examples.code:
<!-- The FIRST action is primary and the rest are secondary unless they
     say otherwise. Three primary buttons side by side is no hierarchy:
     the user reads all three to find the one the page expects. -->
<sv-empty-state
  icon="folder"
  title="No projects yet"
  message="Create your first project to get started."
  [actions]="emptyActions"
  (actionClick)="create()" />

examples.title: A filtered zero, which is a different fact
examples.code:
<!-- "Nothing here yet" when the user has filtered is a lie that reads
     as a bug: it tells a customer with 4,000 orders they have none
     because they mistyped a search term - and the cheerful inbox glyph
     agrees with it.

     Pass the filters and the copy becomes "No matching results", the
     glyph becomes a search, and the filters themselves are echoed with
     one button to drop them. The reason is inferred from them, so the
     mistake of echoing filters under "Nothing here yet" is impossible. -->
<sv-empty-state
  [activeFilters]="activeFilterLabels()"
  (clearFilters)="resetFilters()"
  [actions]="emptyActions"
  (actionClick)="create()" />

examples.title: The other two reasons
examples.code:
<!-- An error and a permission wall are not empty containers either;
     each gets its own copy and glyph. -->
<sv-empty-state reason="error" />
<sv-empty-state reason="no-access" />

customization: Inline or full-page layout; five sizes (`xs` is a one-line table row, `xl` a full-page hero), `layout` (`vertical` · `horizontal`) and `align` (`center` · `start`).
Icon, title, description and actions.

`variant`: `default`, `dashed` (with exactly one action the whole card is that action — "Create your first project"), `ghost` (your `[svGhost]` content faintly behind, a preview of the filled screen) or `glow` (a soft tinted glow behind the icon).
A built-in `illustration` (`auto` follows `reason`), or your own `[svIllustration]` art or `[svMedia]` content in its place.

Extras, each off until set: an onboarding `steps` checklist (`(stepClick)`), the `query` that found nothing with a Clear search button and "did you mean" `suggestions`, `errorDetails` behind a disclosure, `requestAccessLabel` for `no-access`, a quiet `secondaryLink`, an `avatars` stack (`maxAvatars`), and a `shortcut` drawn as keys with its `shortcutHint`.

`reason` (`no-data` · `no-results` · `error` · `no-access`) picks the copy AND the glyph when you do not state them — a cheerful inbox over "no matching results" says "you have nothing" when the truth is "your filters match nothing". Passing `[activeFilters]` infers `no-results` by itself.

`[activeFilters]` echoes the filters narrowing the list, as chips, with a `(clearFilters)` button beside them: "No matching results" is unanswerable on its own, and the filter hiding everything is usually one the user set three screens ago. Strings rather than a filter model, because only the host can render a date range as words a person recognises.
Action hierarchy by position: the first action is primary, the rest secondary, unless an action states its own `style`.
`[offline]` takes precedence over `reason`, and `retryLabel` with `(retry)` offers a second attempt for `reason="error"` and for offline — the two causes one can fix.
12 built-in icon presets, or `icon="custom"` with `customIcon` naming any icon-library glyph. An unstated icon follows `reason`.
accessibility: Clear heading hierarchy.
Decorative icon hidden from assistive tech.
Actions are labelled buttons/links.

Long localized text wraps: the title is capped at `max-w-xl` and both title and description use `hyphens-auto` plus `wrap-anywhere`, so a German or Finnish compound breaks (at a syllable where the browser knows the page `lang`) instead of pushing the centred layout off a 320px screen — WCAG 1.4.10 reflow.

components.name: Eval Scorecard
components.description: Two eval runs compared honestly: pass rates with their intervals, the cases that actually flipped, and a delta that stays grey when the sample cannot support it. 3 variants: summary, compare and cases.
whenToUse: Judging whether a prompt or model change actually regressed anything, rather than reading a headline pass rate.
An eval board people are expected to act on — where a false regression costs more than a missed one.
For per-run token cost and latency, use the AI Token Dashboard; this is about correctness.
customization: `run`, `baseline` and `history` are inputs and all default to empty/null; import `DEMO_RUN` / `DEMO_BASELINE` for a demo.
Three layouts via `variant`: `summary` (per-suite rates, worst first), `compare` (the verdict plus a case-by-case list) and `cases` (this run’s cases, failures first).
Pass rates carry a 95 % Wilson interval — the Wilson form because eval suites are small and rates sit near 0 or 1, where the textbook normal interval returns bounds outside 0–100.

The compare verdict **names its method in the UI**: a change is called beyond chance only when the two runs’ 95 % Wilson intervals do not overlap, and the line under the verdict says that this is "a conservative heuristic, not a significance test" — and that overlapping intervals do not prove nothing changed. The verdict never says "a real improvement". The coloured headline delta carries the same sentence as its title in every variant (`verdictMethod` label).

`error` and `skipped` cases are excluded from the denominator and surfaced as an "ungraded" count: an error is the harness falling over, and counting it as a failure blames the model for the infrastructure.
The delta is only coloured when the two rates’ intervals do not overlap. Everything else stays grey, because a red arrow on noise is what teaches a team to stop reading its own eval board.
The case list sorts broken → fixed → added → removed → stable, and `caseSelect` emits the delta the reader activated.

A scale ceiling: `[maxCases]` (300) bounds both case tables. The window is taken AFTER the worst-first sort, which is what makes it tolerable — the failures are at the top and the rows dropped are the passes; slicing first would keep an arbitrary subset and then arrange it beautifully with the failures left outside. The pass rate is still computed over the whole suite. `0` turns it off.

`provenance` on a run — judge model, judge version, rubric version, seed, trial count, dataset hash and dataset size — is rendered as only the fields the run declared. An eval you cannot reproduce is an anecdote, and a missing seed does not mean 'unseeded': the gaps are named in a **Not reproducible** badge rather than defaulted into something that looks fine.

The compare view checks that the two runs are comparable: if they used a different judge, judge version, rubric, trial count or dataset, the delta is **a measurement of the judge**, and the component says so above the verdict. A different *seed* is deliberately not flagged — two runs at different seeds are the same experiment sampled twice, which is what you want to compare — and a field only one run declared is a gap, not a mismatch.

Export: the **Cases (CSV)** button downloads the case list and emits it through `(exportRequested)`, so a host can upload it instead. The provenance rides along in the comment header, because a case list with no judge and no rubric is the anecdote this component exists to stop producing.
accessibility: Each case row carries an accessible name stating what changed, its before/after outcomes, and the flakiness caveat in words.
Suite bars state their counts and rate as text, not only as a bar width.
The changed-only filter reports `aria-pressed`.
variants: Compare — The Headline Barely Moved and Two Things Happened
Significance — Why the Arrow Is Grey

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the eval run is being fetched; shows a skeleton in place of the scorecard.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Load failure, shown as an error panel in place of the content. Use `toSvDataError()` from `@styloviz/core` to normalize an `HttpErrorResponse`.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Presentation: suite summary, run comparison, or the case list.

inputs.name: run
inputs.description: The run being judged.

inputs.name: baseline
inputs.description: The run to judge it against. Without one the component reports rates and refuses to report movement, rather than comparing a run with itself and printing a confident `0.0 pts`.

inputs.name: history
inputs.description: Earlier runs, for spotting cases that flip in both directions. Three or more, or nothing is claimed: two runs can only show a change, and calling that flaky would suppress every real regression the moment it appeared.

inputs.name: maxCases
inputs.description: How many case rows either table renders at once. `0` = no ceiling. An eval suite is the one list-shaped surface here that is supposed to grow. A team that takes evals seriously adds cases every week and never removes them, so a mature suite is thousands of rows — and both tables here are already sorted worst-first, which is what makes a ceiling tolerable: the rows that matter are at the top, and the ones dropped are the passes. Which is also the trap. The sort is the reason the window is safe, so the window has to be taken AFTER it — slicing first and sorting second would keep an arbitrary subset and then arrange it beautifully, with the failures that matter left outside.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: Emitted when the user presses the error panel's "Try again" button (retryable errors only); the host should re-run the failed load.

outputs.name: caseSelect
outputs.description: The reader activated a case.

outputs.name: exportRequested
outputs.description: The reader asked for the case list. Emitted as well as downloaded.

components.name: Calendar / Scheduler
components.description: Month, week, day, agenda and year views (plus a planner week time-grid) with color-coded event chips, keyboard navigation, a today highlight and opt-in drag-to-create. Recurring series are expanded by the calendar itself from an RFC 5545 RRULE, with EXDATE and moved occurrences; an event dialog edits one occurrence, the rest of a series or all of it; a calendar `timeZone` converts each event from its own; `.ics` files import and export. Emits the visible date range so you fetch only what is on screen, and `view` / `focusedDate` are two-way bindable for deep links. `sv-scheduler`, in the same package, shows the same events against resources.
whenToUse: Showing scheduled events across month, week, day or agenda views.
You want color-coded categories and click-to-create/inspect.
For activity history (not scheduling), use the Timeline.

examples.title: Let a browser agent drive it (WebMCP)
examples.code:
<!-- svWebMcp from @styloviz/core registers calendar_describe, calendar_… — see /docs/webmcp -->
<sv-event-calendar svWebMcp="calendar" [events]="events" variant="planner" [creatable]="true" />
<!-- tools: describe, list_events, create_event, move_event, set_view, go_to_date -->

examples.title: Wired to an API — fetch only what is on screen
examples.code:
<sv-event-calendar
  [events]="events()"
  [loading]="loading()"
  [error]="error()"
  [(view)]="view"
  [(focusedDate)]="focusedDate"
  (rangeChange)="load($event)"
  (retry)="load(range())" />

// The calendar asks for the range it is about to show — on first render and on
// every navigation, never twice for the same range. In month view the range
// covers the WHOLE grid, including the greyed days from the neighbouring
// months, so those cells are not left looking empty.
load({ start, end }: CalendarRange): void {
  this.range.set({ start, end });
  this.loading.set(true);
  this.api.events(start, end).subscribe({
    next: (events) => { this.events.set(events); this.loading.set(false); },
    error: (e) => { this.error.set(toSvDataError(e)); this.loading.set(false); },
  });
}

// `view` and `focusedDate` are models: bind them two-way to keep the month
// the user navigated to in the URL. `(viewChange)` also fires.

examples.title: Planner with drag-to-create
examples.code:
<sv-event-calendar
  variant="planner"
  [events]="events"
  [creatable]="true"
  (rangeSelect)="addEvent($event)" />
// $event = { date, startTime, endTime } — add it to your own event store

examples.title: A recurring series, edited in scope
A calendar zone, and events that carry their own
examples.code:
<sv-event-calendar [events]="events" timeZone="Europe/Berlin" />

// { title: 'Customer call', date: '2026-11-03', startTime: '11:00', endTime: '12:00', timeZone: 'America/New_York' }
// is drawn at 17:00 and named "… 11:00 to 12:00 in New York". All-day events never move.

examples.title: Import and export .ics

customization: `rrule` (RFC 5545: DAILY / WEEKLY / MONTHLY / YEARLY with INTERVAL, COUNT, UNTIL, BYDAY with ordinals, BYMONTHDAY, BYMONTH, BYSETPOS, WKST) and `exdates` make an event a series the calendar expands. A rule part it does not support is refused out loud — the event is drawn once and the notice above the grid names it.
`views` lists the switcher's views; add `'day'` and `'year'` to offer them. The year view shades each day by how busy it is and opens it in the day view.

`eventDialog` opens the details dialog on an event (the rule in words, a moved occurrence's original day, the zone it was written in); `editable` adds date and time fields, Delete, and the three scopes — the calendar emits `eventChange` / `eventRemove` and never writes.
`readOnly: true` on an event keeps its dialog read-only and refuses `requestEventChange` (and, in `sv-scheduler`, a drag or a keyboard move) with the reason.
`timeZone` (an IANA name) converts every timed event that carries its own `timeZone`; `null` keeps the wall-clock grid.
`maxEventsPerDay` (default 3) caps the chips a month-view day draws; the rest collapse into a "+N more" button that opens the day in the week view, where every event of the day is listed.

Overlapping events are laid out in side-by-side lanes rather than stacked, sized per cluster — two meetings at 9am and two at 4pm need two lanes, not four. Touching is not overlapping, so a day of back-to-back meetings stays full width.
`weekStart` takes any weekday, 0 Sunday to 6 Saturday — Saturday is the working-week start across much of the Middle East and North Africa.
`endDate` for multi-day events, and `recurrence` for a repeat disclosure.
Switch month / week / day / agenda views, plus default / compact / timeline / planner variants.
Color-coded event categories.
In the planner, set `creatable` to drag out a new time range (15-min snap, live preview) — `rangeSelect` emits `{ date, startTime, endTime }` for your store.
Today indicator and custom event templates.
accessibility: A recurring occurrence says its rule in words in its accessible name ("Every week on Monday, Wednesday and Friday"), and a moved one adds "Moved from Wednesday, November 11, 2026"; a converted event adds the time it was written in ("09:00 to 10:00 in New York").

The event dialog is a native modal `<dialog>`: focus moves to its heading, the page behind is inert, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the event. The three scopes are a native radio group; a refusal is a `role="alert"` sentence naming the reason.

The year view is one tab stop for 365 days: arrows move by day and week, Page Up / Page Down by month, Home / End to the ends of the week; every day is named with its date and event count, and today carries `aria-current="date"`.

A month cell never drops an event silently: past `maxEventsPerDay` it shows a "+N more" `<button>` named with the count and the date ("Show 2 more events on Wednesday, June 10, 2026"), and activating it opens the week view with focus on that day.
Concurrent events are given lanes so none is hidden behind another. Two events at the same hour sit side by side, so a double-booked morning never looks free.

A recurring event carries its rule in WORDS in its accessible name, not only as a repeat glyph: moving next Tuesday's stand-up and moving every Tuesday's are different actions, and the glyph says nothing to a screen reader.

The month view is a true ARIA `grid` (rows of day `gridcell`s) with roving-tabindex day buttons: arrow keys move between days, Home/End jump to week ends, Enter/Space select; each day is labelled with its full date, event count and today state.
Prev/next controls are labelled per view, the period heading is a polite live region, and the view switcher exposes `aria-pressed`.
Today is marked with `aria-current="date"`; events activate on Enter/Space and expose their title to assistive tech.
variants: Resources — day columns, working hours and blocked time
Drag, resize and keyboard moves — a refused drop
Time zones — per calendar and per event
Wired to an API — loading, error and empty

inputs.name: events
inputs.description: Calendar events for the currently visible range. Fetch them from `rangeChange` rather than loading a year at a time.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP 47 locale for dates and numbers.

inputs.name: timeZone
inputs.description: The IANA zone the calendar shows times in — `'Europe/Berlin'`. When set, an event carrying its own `timeZone` is converted into it and says where it came from ("09:00 to 10:00 in New York"). When `null`, nothing is converted: the grid draws every date and time as given.

inputs.name: views
inputs.description: The views the switcher offers, in order. Add `'day'` and `'year'` to offer them; a `view` that is not listed still renders.

inputs.name: eventDialog
inputs.description: Open the event details dialog when an event is activated: its time, the repeat rule in words, a moved occurrence's original day, the zone it was written in. `eventClick` still fires.

inputs.name: editable
inputs.description: Let the dialog change an event's date and times and delete it — with "this event / this and following / all events" for a recurring one. The calendar never writes: apply `eventChange` / `eventRemove` with `svApplyEventChange` / `svApplyEventRemoval` and send the events back.

inputs.name: view
inputs.description: Active view. Two-way bindable — `[(view)]` keeps it in the URL so a shared link reopens the week the sender was looking at. Still emits `viewChange`.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Visual variant.

inputs.name: weekStart
inputs.description: Which weekday a week begins on, `0` Sunday to `6` Saturday. Any day, not only Sunday or Monday: Saturday is the working-week start across much of the Middle East and North Africa.

inputs.name: maxEventsPerDay
inputs.description: The most event chips a month-view day cell draws. The rest collapse into a "+N more" button, named with the count and the date, that opens the day in the week view where every event is listed. Values below 1 count as 1. No event is hidden without a count on screen and in the accessibility tree.

inputs.name: focusedDate
inputs.description: The date the calendar is centred on, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Two-way bindable, so the month the user navigated to survives a reload or a deep link. Defaults to today.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the visible range is being fetched. Replaces the grid with a placeholder on first load.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Load failure for the visible range. Use `toSvDataError()` from `@styloviz/core` to normalize an `HttpErrorResponse`.

inputs.name: showZonePolicy
inputs.description: Show the one-line zone policy under the calendar — whether times are shown as given or converted into `timeZone` — so the reader knows which. Hide it only when the host states the policy itself.

inputs.name: creatable
inputs.description: Enable drag-to-create in the planner (week time-grid).

inputs.name: notes
inputs.description: Day notes keyed by ISO date (two-way: `[(notes)]`).

outputs.name: dateClick

outputs.name: rangeChange

This is what makes the calendar usable against a real backend: without it a host has to load every event that exists, because it cannot know what the component is about to show. ```ts onRangeChange({ start, end }: CalendarRange): void { this.loading.set(true); this.api.events(start, end).subscribe((events) => { this.events.set(events); this.loading.set(false); }); } ```

components.name: Expand / Collapse
components.description: Animated height expand/collapse container using pure JS measurement (no @angular/animations) with lazy content rendering and accessible aria-hidden handling.
whenToUse: Animating arbitrary content open/closed by height — show-more panels, inline detail.
You want a smooth transition without pulling in @angular/animations.
For truncating long text specifically, use Line Clamp; for grouped sections, Accordion.

examples.title: Full disclosure wiring (aria-controls)
examples.description: Give the panel a panelId and point your trigger's aria-controls / aria-expanded at it. Pass ariaLabelledby so the panel is exposed as a labelled region.

customization: Drive open state with the two-way `[(expanded)]` model.
Tune the `duration` and `easing` of the height transition.
Defer rendering of heavy content with `lazy`.
Wire the ARIA disclosure relationship with `panelId` (for a trigger's `aria-controls`) and `ariaLabelledby` / `ariaLabel` (exposes the panel as a labelled `region`).

Variant axes: `duration` and `easing` are appearance; `expanded`, `lazy` and `returnFocusTo` are behavioural modes; `panelId` / `ariaLabelledby` / `ariaLabel` are semantics. All combine freely. Limits: height (vertical) only; a `duration` of 0 still settles through the fallback timer, one tick later.

Server rendering: the initial state is a template binding, so a panel that starts collapsed is serialised with `display: none` — hidden in the prerendered HTML — and the client's first render binds the same value, so hydration shows no flash of open content. Nothing is emitted for the initial state (`expandedChange` reports transitions only). A collapsed non-lazy panel's content is in the server HTML (hidden, `inert`, `aria-hidden`); a collapsed `lazy` one ships no content until it is first opened.
accessibility: Collapsed content is `aria-hidden` and `inert` — out of the tab order from the moment the collapse starts, not only once it has finished.

Focus after collapse: if focus is inside the panel when it collapses, it moves to `returnFocusTo`, else the element named by `ariaLabelledby`, else a control whose `aria-controls` names `panelId`, else the `sv-expand` host (made focusable with `tabindex="-1"` for that move) — never `<body>`. Focus outside the panel is left alone.
Optional `panelId` lets a trigger reference the panel via `aria-controls`; `ariaLabelledby` / `ariaLabel` expose it as a named `role="region"`.
Height animates without layout-shift surprises.
Honours reduced-motion preferences.

inputs.name: expanded
inputs.description: Controls open/closed state.

inputs.name: duration
inputs.description: Animation duration in ms. Ignored under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, where the panel opens and closes without a height transition.

inputs.name: easing
inputs.description: CSS easing function.

inputs.name: lazy
inputs.description: Only attach content after first open. Content is RETAINED after that — a collapse hides it, it never destroys it. Projected components are still instantiated by the host up front; wrap them in your own `@if` / `@defer` to defer creation.

inputs.name: panelId
inputs.description: Optional id for the collapsible panel. Point your trigger's `aria-controls` at this id to complete the ARIA disclosure relationship.

inputs.name: ariaLabelledby
inputs.description: Id of the element that labels this panel (usually the trigger button).

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Explicit accessible name for the panel (used when `ariaLabelledby` is unset).

inputs.name: returnFocusTo
inputs.description: Where focus goes when the panel collapses while focus is inside it — an element, or the id of one (normally the trigger). A collapse must never strand focus. The content is about to be hidden and made `inert`; a focused control inside it would drop focus to `<body>`, and the next Tab restarts at the top of the page. When this is unset (or cannot take focus) the fallbacks are, in order: the element named by `ariaLabelledby`, any element whose `aria-controls` names `panelId`, and finally the `sv-expand` host itself (made focusable with `tabindex="-1"` for that one move).

outputs.name: expandedChange
outputs.description: Emitted after the animation completes — once, for the final state of a burst of toggles.

components.name: File Display
components.description: File attachment item with a MIME-type-aware icon badge, formatted size, upload progress, success/error status and download/remove actions — in card, row or compact layouts.
whenToUse: Listing uploaded or attached files with type, size and per-item actions.
You want a built-in upload progress bar and success/error states.
For the upload dropzone itself, use the File Upload component.

examples.title: Deleting a file
The download is not a safety claim
examples.description: scan defaults to 'unscanned', which is not a synonym for 'clean'. An unlabelled one-click download on every file asserts, on your behalf, that the file is safe to open — the one claim a file viewer must never make by omission. 'pending' withholds the download until the check finishes; 'flagged' withholds it outright and says why, unless allowUnsafeDownload puts the bytes behind an explicit confirmation for the people who genuinely need them.

examples.title: Retrying — or resuming — a failed upload
examples.description: A failed upload shows the reason and a way to try again, so the user does not have to remove the row and pick the file a second time. The retry control states which of the two acts it performs, because a "Retry" that silently re-sends 900 MB over a metered connection is a different offer from resuming.
examples.code:
<sv-file-display
  [fileName]="file.name"
  [fileSize]="file.size"
  [status]="file.status"
  [uploadError]="file.error"
  [resumable]="true"
  [uploadedBytes]="file.sent"
  (retryUpload)="resume($event)"
  (cancelUpload)="abort($event.fileName)" />

// resumeFrom is 0 unless you said BOTH that the upload is resumable and how
// far it got — either half missing means the bytes have to go again.
resume(e: FileRetryEvent) {
  this.api.upload(e.fileName, { offset: e.resumeFrom, key: e.requestKey });
}

customization: Sizes are written in the kit locale with `Intl` unit formatting ("1.5 kB", "1,5 ko", "512 bytes"); the same function is exported as `svFormatBytes(size, locale)` for your own lists.
Three layouts via `variant`: card, row, compact.
Toggle the `removable` and `downloadable` actions independently.
Drive the progress bar and status chip with `status` + `progress`.
`confirmRemove` (on by default) asks inline before emitting `(remove)`. Set it to `false` when the host runs its own confirmation dialog, and the × emits straight through.
`removing` locks the × and the confirm button while the delete is in flight; `removeError` reports a failed delete under the row, which is still there because the host never took it out.
`(remove)` carries `{ fileName, requestKey }`. There is deliberately no `rollback()`: one file cannot put itself back into a list it does not own.

`scan` (`unscanned` / `pending` / `clean` / `flagged`) drives both the disclosure and whether a download is offered at all; `scanNote` supplies your own wording and `allowUnsafeDownload` puts a flagged file behind a confirmation instead of withholding it.

`status="error"` renders `uploadError` and a retry control. `resumable` + `uploadedBytes` turn it into "Resume from 412 MB" and put the offset in `(retryUpload)`; `(cancelUpload)` abandons one that is still running.
accessibility: A long name truncates only its stem — the extension (".pdf") always stays on screen — and the full name is disclosed in a tooltip; assistive tech reads it whole from the group name.
Each item is a labelled `group` named by its file; download/remove buttons include the file name so they are unambiguous in a list.

The × keeps its place while the confirmation is open rather than being swapped out, so the focus that pressed it still has somewhere to be. It exposes `aria-expanded`, and its label becomes "Cancel removing <file>".
The confirmation is a labelled `group` whose text says the delete cannot be undone — not colour alone. A failed delete renders as `role="alert"`.
The progress bar is a labelled `progressbar` exposing its current value; success/error indicators are exposed as labelled images.
Image previews require `alt` (derived from the file name).

The scan state is written in words, not conveyed by a colour or a glyph alone — "Not checked for threats" and "Checked — no threats found" must not look like each other. In the compact layout, where there is no room for the sentence, the glyph carries it as its accessible name.
A withheld download is absent rather than disabled, and the reason is stated beside it: a greyed control answers nothing and invites a harder press.
The download button keeps its place while the unsafe-download confirmation is open, exposes `aria-expanded`, and the strip that follows it is the next tab stop.

components.name: File Upload
components.description: Button-style file uploader with type/size constraints and progress; the drag-and-drop dropzone and compact variants are in the Pro package.
whenToUse: Letting users attach files via drag-and-drop or a button trigger.
You need type/size constraints and per-file progress out of the box.
Use the dropzone variant (Pro) for media-heavy flows, the button variant in tight toolbars.

examples.title: Validation events
examples.description: accept and maxSizeMb are enforced whenever a file is added; rejected files surface through uploadError. The dropzone/compact variants shown here also enforce it on drag-and-drop, but they ship in the Pro package — the free tier's button variant enforces the same picker-side validation.

examples.title: Chunked and resumable uploads (Pro)
examples.description: A factory that builds an uploader, because resumability is a property of the transport. Chunk planning, resume from a server-reported offset, retryable-status policy and full-jitter backoff are exported separately for hosts with their own transport.

examples.title: Paste to upload
examples.description: Off by default. `page` listens document-wide and ignores any paste aimed at an input, textarea or contenteditable — that is how an upload zone avoids stealing a paste meant for the comment box beside it. `zone` only counts a paste made with focus inside the dropzone. A paste carrying only text is never touched.
examples.code:
<sv-file-upload-pro pasteToUpload="page" accept="image/*" />

// Every pasted screenshot arrives named image.png, so three pastes would
// collide on the server. They are renamed from the clock and their ordinal:
//   pasted-2026-08-17-101530.png
//   pasted-2026-08-17-101530-2.png

examples.title: Folder upload
examples.description: `directory` sets webkitdirectory on the picker. Dropped folders are expanded whichever way it is set, because dataTransfer.files reports a directory as a zero-byte File — reading it would queue the folder itself as a broken upload.
examples.code:
<sv-file-upload-pro
  [directory]="true"
  accept="image/*"
  [maxScannedFiles]="20000"
  (intakeSkipped)="notice.set($event)" />

// Each file keeps the path it had inside the folder, so three folders each
// holding an IMG_0001.jpg stay distinguishable.
files()[0].path;   // 'trip/day1/IMG_0001.jpg'

// intakeSkipped reports what was left behind — .DS_Store, the accept filter,
// or the scan limit. A folder drop that quietly loses files is
// indistinguishable from a broken component.

examples.title: Inline crop
examples.description: `cropImages` holds croppable images instead of sending them. It is a distinct **status**, not a flag on a pending file — `uploadAll()` sends everything pending, so the flag version uploads the un-cropped original while the crop dialog is still open. file-upload takes no dependency on image-editor: bind `<sv-image-cropper>` to `cropQueue()` and hand the blob back with `applyCrop()`. The result is re-validated, because a lossless PNG re-encode of a lossy JPEG routinely doubles the file — the crop that removed pixels is what pushes it past the size limit.
examples.code: @let held = upload.cropQueue()[0]; @if (held && held.preview) { } // A template statement cannot await, so the crop runs in the component: async crop(upload: SvFileUploadProComponent, id: string, cropper: SvImageCropperComponent) { const blob = await cropper.cropImage(); if (blob) upload.applyCrop(id, blob); } // canvas.toBlob falls back to image/png when it cannot write the type it was // handed — silently, with no error and no flag. The blob's own type therefore // wins over the request, or photo.webp ends up full of PNG bytes. svCropReplacement(original, pngBlob, { type: 'image/webp' }).name; // 'photo.png' // HEIC, TIFF and SVG are never offered a cropper: an pointed at an HEIC // outside Safari never fires load, so the cropper sits blank forever with no // error to react to. They upload untouched. svIsCroppableImage({ type: 'image/heic' }); // false

examples.title: Reactive forms (formControlName)
examples.description: Opt-in ControlValueAccessor: the control value is the native File[], so the field binds to reactive and template-driven forms while keeping its event API. formControl.disable() disables the dropzone and row actions.

examples.title: Resume across a page reload (Pro)
examples.description: svChunkedUploader resumes from whatever offset the probe reports; svLocalResumeStore remembers WHICH upload session a file belongs to, so the probe still has something to ask about after a reload. Scope it to the account — an upload URL is a capability — and check svCanResume before trusting a record.

customization: Choose `variant` (dropzone · compact · button) and `size`; the free tier ships the button variant.
Constrain with `accept`, `maxSizeMb`, `maxFiles` and `multiple`; wire a real backend with the `uploader` function (progress, cancel via AbortSignal, retry, concurrency limit).
React to `filesChange`, `fileAdded`, `fileRemoved`, `uploadComplete` and `uploadError`, or bind the `File[]` value with a reactive control (CVA).

Chunked and resumable uploads (Pro) via `svChunkedUploader`. `svPlanChunks`, `svResumePlan`, `svIsRetryableStatus`, `svRetryDelay`, `svChunkProgress` and `svUploadKey` are exported for hosts with their own transport.

Paste-to-upload (Pro) via `pasteToUpload` (`off` · `zone` · `page`), and folder upload via `directory` and `maxScannedFiles`, with `intakeSkipped` reporting what an intake left behind. `svExpandDrop`, `svReadDirectory`, `svNamePastedFiles` and `svFilterIntake` are exported.

Both tiers: `initialFiles` shows files already stored (an edit form), `labels` rewords every string, `validator` is your own check per file (it may be async; the file waits at "Checking…"), `required`, `minFiles`, `minSizeMb` and `maxTotalSizeMb` join the validation, and `actions` (`auto` · `show` · `hide`) controls the Upload all / Cancel all / Retry failed row.

Pro: `listType="grid"` for picture cards, `reorderable` (drag or arrow keys, `(reordered)`), `rowActions` (preview in a dialog, download), `pausable` rows, `transferDetails` (bytes, speed, time left), `minImageSize` / `maxImageSize` read from the decoded image, `metadataFields` per file (`(metaChange)`), `beforeRemove` to confirm a removal (`(removeRefused)`), `dropOnPage` for a full-screen drop target, `addFrom` (`device` · `url` · `camera`) and a `resumeStore` that offers interrupted uploads back on the next visit.
accessibility: Focus after a mutation: removing a file moves focus to the Remove button of the file that took its place, then the one before it, then the control that adds files; Clear all goes to that control. A host calling `removeFile()` programmatically does not move focus.
Keyboard-accessible `role="button"` dropzone (Pro; Enter/Space opens the dialog) with a visible focus ring; disabled removes it from the tab order and disables the row actions.
File add/remove/upload status is announced through a visually-hidden `aria-live="polite"` region; progress bars expose `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`/`min`/`max`.
The `accept` filter is enforced on drag-and-drop (Pro) as well as the picker — non-matching files are flagged as errors rather than accepted.

Paste-to-upload never swallows a text paste and never calls preventDefault on one, so copying a URL and pressing Ctrl+V on a page that happens to contain an upload zone keeps working. In `page` mode a paste aimed at an editable element is ignored outright.
Each file row exposes labelled retry/remove controls.
Implements ControlValueAccessor — the value is `File[]`; works with `[(ngModel)]`, `[formControl]` and `formControlName`, and `formControl.disable()` disables the field.

inputs.name: size

inputs.name: accept
inputs.description: Accepted file types — which files the picker offers and the queue keeps — `"image/*,.pdf"`. This is a convenience filter. It is not a security check. It matches an extension out of a filename the user chose, or a `File.type` the browser derived from that same extension — so `payload.exe` renamed `photo.png` passes `accept=".png"` and reports `image/png`, because it is called `.png`. Nothing here reads the bytes. And the file need not come through this component at all. Your upload endpoint accepts requests; `curl` is not running this filter. Every check here runs in a browser belonging to a user who is not the attacker in the case that matters. What it is genuinely for: keeping the OS picker tidy and keeping junk out of the queue. Both are about the honest user's experience, which is the whole job. **Validate the type on the server, from the bytes, at the point of storage** — with a size limit the client cannot raise and a malware scan. `markScanned` is how the verdict gets back here.

inputs.name: maxFiles
