inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name for the slider itself.

inputs.name: allowMismatch
inputs.description: Suppress the aspect-ratio warning. Provided because a caller who has deliberately letterboxed both images to a common frame is telling the truth and the warning would be noise. It is NOT a way to silence a real mismatch, and the docs say so.

inputs.name: landmarks
inputs.description: Draw a fixed alignment reference over both images.

inputs.name: position
inputs.description: Wipe position, 0–1. Two-way.

outputs.name: mismatch
outputs.description: Emitted once when the two images turn out not to be comparable.

outputs.name: loadError
outputs.description: An image failed to load — `'before'` or `'after'`. The wipe is replaced by the reason.

outputs.name: positionChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `position` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(position)]`.

components.name: Image Cropper
components.description: Crop, with the parts that silently corrupt the result handled: EXIF orientation, the browser's canvas ceiling, and a quality setting PNG ignores. An image cropper fails by producing a picture rather than an error, so it reports what the crop will actually produce rather than what was selected.
whenToUse: Letting a user choose the part of an image you will store — an avatar, a cover, a thumbnail.
You need the crop in the image's own pixels, not the ones on screen.
For a before/after wipe rather than a selection, use Image Compare.

examples.title: What the crop will actually produce
examples.description: The plan is exposed rather than applied silently: a crop past what a browser will render is downscaled, and past that ceiling a canvas is not an error — it is blank, and toBlob succeeds. The warnings are the only thing standing between the user and a transparent file.

examples.title: A photograph that is not stored the way it is shown
examples.description: A phone photograph is stored sideways with a tag saying which way is up. The component cannot read that tag — it lives in the file's bytes and an does not expose it — so a host that decoded the file passes it in. Leave it at 1 for an image the browser has already auto-oriented.
examples.code:
<sv-image-cropper [src]="photo()" [orientation]="6" />

// 4032 x 3024 stored, 3024 x 4032 upright. Reading the stored size and
// letting the user drag over the upright rendering mixes two coordinate
// systems 90 degrees apart, and the crop lands on a region that is not in
// the picture.

examples.title: The geometry on its own
examples.description: Exported so a host with its own surface — an inline crop inside an uploader, a canvas editor — gets the same arithmetic rather than a second copy that drifts.

customization: Lock the shape with `aspect`, bound it with `minSize`, and pick the encoding with `outputType` and `quality`; `maxDimension` and `maxPixels` override the conservative canvas ceilings.

`shape="round"` for an avatar mask, `showGrid` for the rule-of-thirds guides, `aspectPresets` for an aspect switch, `minOutput` for the smallest crop the exported file may have, and `outputSize` to export at exactly 256 × 256 whatever the crop's resolution.

Editing, all two-way: `zoomable` turns on `[(zoom)]` (wheel, pinch, ±) within `minZoom` / `maxZoom`; `[(rotation)]` in quarter turns, `[(flipX)]` / `[(flipY)]`, a free-angle `[(straighten)]` (−45° to 45°) and `[(filters)]` (brightness, contrast, saturation), all baked into the export. `dragMode="move"` keeps the box still and moves the picture under it.

`toolbar` shows zoom, turn, flip, the aspect switch, reset, undo and redo (`straightenControl`, `adjustControls` add the sliders; `labels` words it); `<sv-crop-preview [cropper]="cropper">` shows a live preview of the export.

`flattenTo` (default `'#ffffff'`) is the colour a JPEG export is filled with before the draw — JPEG has no alpha, so a transparent ground would otherwise come out black. PNG and WebP keep their transparency and are never filled.
Read the selection with `cropChange` (source pixels) or `sourceCrop()`, the rendering with `plan()` and `outputLabel()`, and produce the image with `cropImage()`.
`svDefaultCrop`, `svResizeCrop`, `svMoveCrop`, `svClampCrop`, `svCropToSource`, `svOrientedSize`, `svOrientationTransform` and `svOutputPlan` are exported for a host building its own surface.
accessibility: The crop box is a focusable `role="group"` whose label reports what the crop will produce, and the eight handles are labelled buttons sharing one roving tab stop (Page Up / Page Down and Home / End move between them, each described by a hint) — "drag a box" has no non-pointer equivalent unless one is built, so arrows nudge by a pixel, Shift by ten, `+` / `-` on the box zoom when `zoomable`, and Escape resets.
Only the keys it handles are swallowed: Tab and everything else pass through, so the crop box cannot become a focus trap.
The dimming mask is `pointer-events-none` and `aria-hidden`, so it neither swallows a drag aimed at a handle nor appears in the accessibility tree.
What the crop will produce — including any downscale and its reason — is a `role="status"` caption rather than something the user has to infer from the file they get later.
variants: The Failures That Produce a Picture Instead of an Error

inputs.name: src
inputs.description: Image URL. Anything an `` accepts, including a blob: or data: URL.

inputs.name: alt
inputs.description: Alt text for the image being cropped.

inputs.name: crossOrigin
inputs.description: CORS mode for the image request — `'anonymous'` for a CDN that sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, `'use-credentials'` when it needs cookies. A cross-origin image loaded without it taints the canvas. It displays fine and crops fine on screen; only the export fails, as a `cropFailed` with a security error and no hint why. Leave `null` for same-origin, blob: and data: sources.

inputs.name: aspect
inputs.description: width ÷ height. 0 leaves the crop free. Two-way: the aspect switch (`aspectPresets`) writes it, and a new value starts a new crop.

inputs.name: aspectPresets
inputs.description: The aspect switch shown in the toolbar — `SV_ASPECT_PRESETS` is a ready set. Empty shows none.

inputs.name: minSize
inputs.description: Smallest crop, in displayed pixels.

inputs.name: minOutput
inputs.description: Smallest crop in SOURCE pixels — what the exported file must have at least, however far the user zooms in. 0 sets no floor.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: The image's EXIF orientation, when the host knows it. The component cannot read this itself, and pretending otherwise would be the lie. The tag lives in the file's bytes; an `` element does not expose it. A host that decoded the file already has it, and one that did not should leave this at 1 — which is correct for every image a browser has already auto-oriented, and that is most of them today.

inputs.name: outputType
inputs.description: Format of the exported image: `'image/png'`, `'image/jpeg'` or `'image/webp'`.

inputs.name: strictFormat
inputs.description: Refuse an export in a format other than `outputType`. A browser that cannot encode a type does not say so. `toBlob` falls back to PNG — Safari before 16.4 did this for every WebP export — so a host that asked for a 90 KB WebP gets a 1.2 MB PNG under a `.webp` name. The fallback is always detected (`formatFallback` fires and a dev warning names it); with `strictFormat` it is also refused: `cropFailed` instead of `cropped`, so the host can retry as JPEG.

inputs.name: quality
inputs.description: Encoder quality from 0 to 1 for JPEG and WebP exports; PNG ignores it. Unset uses 0.92 — and only a quality the host actually SET earns the "PNG ignores the quality setting" warning.

inputs.name: flattenTo
inputs.description: The colour transparency is flattened onto for a format with no alpha. Only JPEG needs it, and only JPEG gets it. A canvas starts transparent and JPEG has no alpha channel, so without a fill a logo on a transparent ground exports as artwork on BLACK — a valid file, no error, and the classic silent corruption. White is the default because it is what printing does and what a user expects.

inputs.name: maxDimension
inputs.description: Longest side the export may have, in px; a larger crop is scaled down. Unset uses the browser canvas limit (16,384).

inputs.name: maxPixels
inputs.description: Total pixel budget for the export; a larger crop is scaled down to fit. Unset uses the browser canvas limit (16,777,216).

inputs.name: outputSize
inputs.description: Export at exactly this size, whatever the crop's resolution — an avatar at 256 × 256, a cover at 1500 × 500. Pair it with a matching `aspect`; a mismatch stretches and the plan says so.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Locks the crop box and its resize handles against pointer and keyboard edits.

inputs.name: shape
inputs.description: `'round'` crops the ellipse inside the box — a circle at 1:1 — and exports it with transparent corners (PNG or WebP; JPEG flattens them onto `flattenTo`).

inputs.name: showGrid
inputs.description: Rule-of-thirds guides inside the box.

inputs.name: zoomable
inputs.description: Turn on zoom: the mouse wheel, a two-finger pinch and the toolbar's ± buttons, bounded by `minZoom` / `maxZoom`. Off by default so a page that scrolls past a cropper keeps scrolling.

inputs.name: zoom
inputs.description: The zoom, as a factor of the fitted picture (1 shows all of it). Two-way; applies only when `zoomable`.

inputs.name: minZoom
inputs.description: The furthest out `zoom` may go; never below 1, the fitted picture.

inputs.name: maxZoom
inputs.description: The furthest in `zoom` may go.

inputs.name: rotation
inputs.description: Clockwise quarter turns applied to the picture: 0, 90, 180 or 270. Two-way.

inputs.name: flipX
inputs.description: Mirror the picture left to right, as the user sees it. Two-way.

inputs.name: flipY
inputs.description: Mirror the picture top to bottom, as the user sees it. Two-way.

inputs.name: straighten
inputs.description: A free-angle straighten, −45° to 45° clockwise, on top of the quarter turns. The picture grows just enough to keep filling the frame, so no crop reaches an empty corner. Two-way.

inputs.name: filters
inputs.description: Brightness, contrast and saturation in percent (100 = unchanged), shown live and baked into the export. Two-way.

inputs.name: straightenControl
inputs.description: With `toolbar`, show the straighten slider.

inputs.name: adjustControls
inputs.description: With `toolbar`, show the brightness / contrast / saturation sliders.

inputs.name: dragMode
inputs.description: What a drag inside the box does. `'crop'` moves the box (and dragging the dimmed area pans a zoomed picture); `'move'` keeps the box still and moves the picture under it, the way a phone's avatar picker does.

inputs.name: toolbar
inputs.description: Show the toolbar: zoom, turn, flip, the aspect switch, reset, undo and redo.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: The cropper's words for this instance, merged over the app's `provideSvLabels({ imageEditorPro })` and `SV_IMAGE_CROPPER_LABELS`.

inputs.name: initialCrop
inputs.description: Where the crop starts, in SOURCE pixels, the first time the image loads — the crop a user saved last time. Unset centres the largest crop of `aspect`.

outputs.name: cropChange
outputs.description: The crop, in SOURCE pixels, whenever it changes.

outputs.name: cropped
outputs.description: The rendered image, once `crop()` resolves.

outputs.name: cropFailed
outputs.description: An export that could not be produced, with the reason.

outputs.name: formatFallback
outputs.description: The browser encoded the export in a different format than `outputType` asked for (a codec it does not have). Fires before `cropped` — or before `cropFailed` under `strictFormat`.

outputs.name: aspectChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `aspect` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(aspect)]`.

outputs.name: zoomChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `zoom` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(zoom)]`.

outputs.name: rotationChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `rotation` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(rotation)]`.

outputs.name: flipXChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `flipX` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(flipX)]`.

outputs.name: flipYChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `flipY` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(flipY)]`.

outputs.name: straightenChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `straighten` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(straighten)]`.

outputs.name: filtersChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `filters` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(filters)]`.

components.name: Image Gallery
components.description: Grid, masonry, strip and product-viewer layouts with a lightbox viewer, keyboard navigation and selectable mode.
whenToUse: Displaying a collection of images users browse and open full-screen.
You want grid/masonry/strip layouts plus a keyboard-friendly lightbox.
For a single rotating banner, use the Carousel.

examples.title: A selection that survives pagination
examples.description: `selected` is a `model`, so the HOST owns the set — which is what makes it persist across a page turn or a route change, and is the only place it can persist. The component deliberately never prunes ids for images it cannot see: a gallery that "tidied up" the selection to match the images currently bound would silently delete the user's choices on every page turn, which is the persistence itself, destroyed by the tidying. What comes with keeping them is the duty to show them — select twelve on page one, turn to page two, and none of them is ticked while "Delete selected" still acts on all twelve. The strip says so, and "Clear selection" clears the hidden part too.
examples.code:
<sv-image-gallery
  [images]="page()"
  [selectable]="true"
  [(selected)]="chosen" />

// chosen lives in the HOST, so it survives the page change:
readonly chosen = signal<Set<string>>(new Set());

customization: Grid, masonry, strip or product-viewer layouts (2–5 columns).
Lightbox with keyboard navigation.
Optional selectable mode.
Product-viewer layout: a large main image with hover-zoom (zoomLevel) and a thumbnail strip to switch images.
accessibility: The lightbox's previous/next buttons sit beside the frame on a wide screen and over the picture's edges on a phone — their offset is the free space beside the frame less an 8px margin, so they are never pushed off-screen below ~480px.

Focus after a mutation: closing the lightbox returns focus to the control that opened it — or, if the reader paged to another image, to THAT image's thumbnail (the viewer layout also makes it the active image). If neither survives, focus goes into the gallery, never `<body>`.

Every layout is a `<ul role="list">`, so a listener is told the images are one set of a known size — "list, 12 items" — which was the only fact the grid conveyed visually and nothing carried. A table of alt texts would be the alt texts again in a worse container, so there is no companion summary here.
The `role="list"` is not redundant: Tailwind's preflight strips `list-style`, and that alone is enough for Safari/VoiceOver to stop treating the `<ul>` as a list.
Name the gallery with `ariaLabel` when a page has more than one.
The lightbox is a modal `dialog` with a focus trap; focus returns to the originating thumbnail on close, and ←/→/Esc navigate.
Built with safe DOM APIs (no HTML injection), so image-supplied alt/title/author cannot inject markup.
View and select controls are labelled buttons reachable by keyboard in every layout; images require descriptive alt text.

A selection that outlives the page it was made on is disclosed in a `role="status"` strip — "12 selected — 9 not on this page" — because the component deliberately never prunes ids for images it cannot see, and a reader who cannot tell would believe the selection is only what is ticked in front of them.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the images are being fetched.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Load failure. Use `toSvDataError()` from `@styloviz/core` to normalize an `HttpErrorResponse`.

inputs.name: emptyMessage
inputs.description: Copy for the no-data state.

inputs.name: filtered
inputs.description: True when the emptiness is caused by a filter rather than an empty set.

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: Images to display (src, alt, optional caption).

inputs.name: layout
inputs.description: Layout: grid, masonry or strip.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: What this gallery is, e.g. `'Product photos'` — names the list of images. Two galleries on one product page (the shots and the customer uploads) both announce as an unnamed list of N items without this. Left unset, no name is invented: `<ul role="list">` already gives a listener the count and the boundaries.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Number of columns (2–5).

inputs.name: lightbox
inputs.description: Open images in a full-screen lightbox on click.

inputs.name: captions
inputs.description: Show captions under images.

inputs.name: selectable
inputs.description: Enable multi-select mode.

inputs.name: zoom
inputs.description: Product-viewer: enable hover-zoom on the main image.

inputs.name: zoomLevel
inputs.description: Product-viewer: magnification factor for the hover-zoom.

inputs.name: viewerSize
inputs.description: Width of the `viewer` layout. `compact` caps it at 28rem.

inputs.name: viewerAspect
inputs.description: Frame of the `viewer` layout's main image.

inputs.name: selected
inputs.description: Which images are selected (two-way). Bind it to preselect a saved set or clear the selection after acting on it; `(selectedChange)` emits on every change.

inputs.name: activeIndex
inputs.description: Optional externally-controlled active image (viewer layout). Clamps to range; resets on image change.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The host should re-run the failed load.

outputs.name: imageClick
outputs.description: Emitted with the clicked image.

outputs.name: selectedChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `selected` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(selected)]`.

components.name: Import Wizard
components.description: A CSV import in four steps — upload or paste, match columns to your fields, review every row, import the valid ones. The file is read and checked in slices, so 10,000 rows never freeze the page; each bad cell is marked with an icon and its message, an error summary jumps to it, and the rows that failed download as a CSV. The save is yours, through a promise or a resolve / reject request.
whenToUse: Letting customers bring contacts, products, users or transactions from a spreadsheet into your app.
Bulk onboarding where you need typed rows and a list of what failed, row by row, before anything is saved.
Any CSV whose columns may be named differently from your fields — the mapping step is where that is settled.

examples.title: Fields, and a save that reports progress
examples.description: Each field is a column in YOUR data: a key, a label, a type that checks and converts the cell, and `aliases` for the header names your customers use. `commitAction` receives only the valid rows, already typed.

examples.title: Your own rule, with the rest of the row
examples.description: `validate` runs after the type check passes, with the other converted values beside it. Return a message to reject the cell, `null` to accept it.

examples.title: Without commitAction: resolve or reject the request
examples.code:
<sv-import-wizard [fields]="fields" (importRequest)="onImport($event)" />

onImport(req: SvImportRequest): void {
  this.api.bulkInsert(req.records, req.signal).subscribe({
    next: (saved) => req.resolve({ imported: saved.count }),
    error: (e) => req.reject(e),   // shown in an alert, with Try again
  });
}

examples.title: The same checks on a server
examples.description: The pipeline is exported, so a script or a server can reach the verdict the user saw.

customization: `fields` with `type` `string` / `number` / `date` (ISO) / `email` / `enum` (case-insensitive by value or label), `required`, `aliases` and `validate`.
`maxSizeMb`, `previewRows` (grid rows and summary entries, up to 500), `headerRow` (`auto`, or force it), `delimiter` (`auto`, `,` `;` or tab), `allowPaste`, `headingLevel`.
Every visible string is a label in the `formsPro` namespace, in 12 language packs; override per instance with `[labels]`.

Outputs: `importRequest` (when no `commitAction`), `imported` with `{ fileName, imported, skipped, rejected }`, `stepChange`. Method `reset()` starts over; `errorRowsCsv()` returns the error file as text.
accessibility: The four steps are the kit stepper; each step change moves focus to the step heading, so a screen reader hears where it landed.

Column mapping uses the kit’s select combobox (APG select-only combobox, listbox portalled). Pressing Next with a required field unmapped names the field in an alert and focuses its combobox, which reports `aria-invalid`.

The preview is a `role="grid"` table with one tab stop: arrows move between cells, Home/End to the row ends, Ctrl+Home/End to the corners, PageUp/PageDown by ten rows. `aria-rowcount` / `aria-rowindex` give the position in the full list.
A bad cell carries `aria-invalid` and shows an icon and its message as text — never colour alone. The error summary is the kit’s `sv-form-error-summary`; each entry moves focus into the grid cell.
Reading, checking and saving progress are `role="progressbar"` with values; failures are `role="alert"`. Buttons and checkboxes are at least 24px targets.

Engine: the ADR-aria row asks for `@angular/aria` combobox and grid. The package is not a dependency of the kit yet (it is adopted from 2.1, ADR rule 1), so this ships on the kit’s own select combobox and an APG grid built on `svCollectionTarget`; moving to Aria later changes no input or output.
variants: Async Commit — A Save That Fails

inputs.name: fields
inputs.description: The fields to fill: `{ key, label, required?, type?, options?, aliases?, validate? }`. Rows with an empty or repeated `key` are ignored.

inputs.name: maxSizeMb
inputs.description: Largest file accepted, in MB.

inputs.name: previewRows
inputs.description: Rows shown in the review grid (and entries in the error summary), 1–500.

inputs.name: headerRow
inputs.description: Whether the file's first row holds column names; `'auto'` detects it. The user can switch it on the mapping step.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: The field separator, or `'auto'` to detect `,` `;` or tab.

inputs.name: allowPaste
inputs.description: Offer a text area to paste CSV as well as the file picker.

inputs.name: commitAction
inputs.description: Save the rows: called with an SvImportRequest; return a promise (or call `request.resolve()` / `reject()`). The wizard tracks it — one save at a time, cancel aborts `request.signal`, a rejection offers Try again. Without it the wizard emits `importRequest` instead.

inputs.name: headingLevel
inputs.description: Level of each step's heading, so the wizard sits correctly in the page outline.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Per-instance text, merged over the registry's `formsPro` labels.

outputs.name: importRequest
outputs.description: The user pressed Import and no `commitAction` is bound: save `records`, then call `resolve()` — or `reject(error)` to show the failure and offer Try again.

outputs.name: imported
outputs.description: The save resolved: `{ fileName, imported, skipped, rejected }`.

outputs.name: stepChange
outputs.description: The wizard moved to another step.

components.name: Inplace Edit
components.description: Edit one field where it is displayed — a value that reads as text until you click it, then becomes an input, then goes back. Text, textarea and select modes, with a save lifecycle that keeps the draft when the write fails.
whenToUse: A read-mostly field the user occasionally corrects — a display name, a note, a status cell.
You want the page to stay a page rather than becoming a form with a Save button at the bottom.
For a screenful of fields being filled in together, use a real form; inline editing is for changing one thing.

examples.title: Autosizing textarea editor
examples.description: With `mode="textarea"`, `autosize` grows the editor with the draft; `rows` is the minimum and `maxRows` the cap.

examples.title: Host-owned save, with the failure handed back
examples.description: One-way `[value]` plus `(save)` is the pessimistic wiring: the host writes the value only once the server agrees. A non-null `error` re-opens the editor with the draft intact, so a 500 costs a retry rather than the typing.

examples.title: Multi-line note — Enter adds a line, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter commits
Two people, one field
examples.description: Two people editing one field is the normal case in any collaborative app, and the two usual answers are both wrong: last-write-wins destroys someone's work and tells nobody, while refusing the save leaves the user holding text with nowhere to put it — so they paste it over the top anyway, having now lost the other version as well. Setting `conflict` shows both and lets the person who is actually there decide. `(conflictResolved)` reports which won, and the winning value is already written through.
examples.code:
<sv-inplace-edit
  label="Project name"
  [(value)]="name"
  [conflict]="conflict()"
  (saveRequest)="save($event)"
  (conflictResolved)="resolve($event)" />

save(e: InplaceEditSave): void {
  this.api.rename(e.value, e.requestKey).subscribe({
    error: (err) => {
      // A 409 is not a failure to report — it is a question to ask.
      if (err.status === 409) { this.conflict.set({ theirs: err.error.current, by: err.error.by }); return; }
      e.rollback();
      this.error.set('Could not save that.');
    },
  });
}

examples.title: A field the user may not edit
examples.description: The alternative is worse than a disabled field: letting them type and failing on save costs them the edit as well as the answer. `lockReason` renders the value as text with the reason beside it, linked by `aria-describedby`, and offers no way in. Named to match `sv-toggle-switch`'s input of the same name — the same question deserves the same API.
examples.code:
<sv-inplace-edit
  label="Workspace ID"
  value="ws_8f21c4"
  lockReason="Only an administrator can change this" />

examples.title: A write, with a key and a way back
examples.description: `(saveRequest)` is the additive sibling of `(save)`: the same commit, carrying an idempotency key so a retried request cannot write twice, and a `rollback()` that refuses if the user has edited again since. `(save)` still fires for a field that writes only to local state.

customization: Pick the editor with `mode` (text · textarea · select), size it with `size` and `rows`, and constrain it with `maxlength` and `required` / `requiredMessage`.

Choose how the read view offers itself with `trigger`: `auto` (default) shows a pencil on hover or focus and always on a touch screen; `click` is the value alone with a hover underline, right for a dense table but with no affordance at all on a phone; `button` shows the pencil everywhere. Word the blank state with `emptyText`.

Drive the save lifecycle with `saving` and `error`, and handle `(saveRequest)` for a `{ value, previous, requestKey, rollback }` payload when a server has to agree; two-way bind `[(editing)]` to open the editor from a row action of your own.
`conflict` turns the editor into a two-value choice when someone else changed the field; `lockReason` renders it as text with an explanation and no way in.
`commitOnBlur` decides whether an outside click saves or discards.
accessibility: The read view is a real `<button>`, named `Edit <label>` so the announcement says what pressing it does — not just the value it happens to contain.
Enter commits and Escape reverts; in `textarea` mode Enter inserts a newline and Ctrl/Cmd+Enter commits, so a multi-line field can hold multiple lines.
Escape stops propagating, so an inline edit inside a dialog or menu cancels the edit rather than closing what surrounds it.
Leaving edit mode returns focus to the trigger when the editor still had it — and leaves focus alone when the user clicked another field, so it is never yanked back.
A refused `required` commit renders a `role="alert"` message that the editor points at via `aria-describedby`, with `aria-invalid` set.

The default `trigger="auto"` renders its pencil ALWAYS on a coarse pointer. Tailwind compiles `hover:` to `@media (hover: hover)`, so a hover-only affordance does not render faintly on a phone — it does not render at all, and the field is indistinguishable from plain text. The pencil is `aria-hidden`: the value button beside it already carries the name and offers the same action, and two tab stops onto one field is worse than none.

A conflict is a labelled `role="group"` with a `role="alert"` sentence naming who changed it and when, then both values as text with a button each. Nothing is auto-selected — the whole point is that only the person present can decide.
A `lockReason` is linked to the value with `aria-describedby`, so the explanation is announced with the field rather than found by accident.
variants: Conflict, permission, and the write itself
Pencil Trigger, and the Empty State
Required, and Discard on Outside Click

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The field's value. Two-way bindable. `[(value)]` is the optimistic wiring: the component writes the new value through on commit and the host persists in the background. `[value]` one-way plus `(save)` is the pessimistic wiring: the host writes it only once the server has agreed, and pushes the old value back if it has not.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Accessible name of the field, e.g. `Display name`. Not decoration. The read view is a button whose text is the VALUE, so without this a screen reader announces "Ada Lovelace, button" and never says what pressing it edits.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: What the editor is.

inputs.name: options
inputs.description: Choices for `select` mode. Ignored in the other modes.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Type scale and padding.

inputs.name: trigger
inputs.description: How the read view offers itself. - `auto` (default) — a pencil button that is **always visible on a touch screen** and appears on hover or focus on a mouse-driven one. - `click` — the value alone, with a hover underline. **On touch this has no affordance at all**: Tailwind compiles `hover:` to `@media (hover: hover)`, so the underline never renders on a phone and nothing indicates the text can be edited. Kept because it is the right density inside a table of many fields, but choose it deliberately. - `button` — the pencil, always visible everywhere.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Placeholder inside the editor.

inputs.name: emptyText
inputs.description: Read-view text when the value is empty. It has to be SOMETHING. An empty value renders an empty button, and a zero-width target cannot be clicked or seen — the field silently becomes uneditable exactly when it most needs editing.

inputs.name: rows
inputs.description: Rows for `textarea` mode.

inputs.name: autosize
inputs.description: With `mode="textarea"`: grow the editor with its text instead of scrolling `rows` lines — `field-sizing: content` where supported, measured elsewhere; `rows` stays the minimum and `maxRows` caps the growth.

inputs.name: maxRows
inputs.description: With `autosize`: the most rows before the editor scrolls; `0` is no cap.

inputs.name: maxlength
inputs.description: Native `maxlength` on the editor. 0 leaves it off.

inputs.name: required
inputs.description: Refuse to commit an empty value, and say why.

inputs.name: requiredMessage
inputs.description: Message shown when a `required` field is committed empty.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Not editable — the read view renders as plain text.

inputs.name: showActions
inputs.description: Show the save / cancel buttons. Never shown in `select` mode.

inputs.name: commitOnBlur
inputs.description: Commit when the editor loses focus. `false` makes an outside click discard the edit — safer for a destructive field, and surprising everywhere else, which is why it defaults on.

inputs.name: customClass
inputs.description: Extra classes on the root element.

inputs.name: saving
inputs.description: The host is persisting the value — the editor stays open and goes busy.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: The save failed. Re-opens the editor with the draft intact. Accepts an `SvDataError` or a plain string, so an `HttpErrorResponse` normalized with `toSvDataError()` can be bound without unwrapping it.

inputs.name: lockReason
inputs.description: Why this field cannot be edited — a permission, a plan, a workflow state. Non-empty renders the value as static text with the reason beside it, and no way in. Distinct from `disabled`, deliberately, and named to match `sv-toggle-switch`'s input of the same name: a disabled field tells the user "not you, not now" and leaves them to guess, and the guess they most often make is that the page is broken. The alternative it replaces is worse — letting them type, then failing on save, which costs them the edit as well as the answer.

inputs.name: conflict
inputs.description: Someone else changed this field while it was open. Setting it puts the editor into a two-value choice: their text, the user's text, and a button each. Clear it (back to `null`) when the choice has been made — `(conflictResolved)` tells you which one won and has already written it through to `value`.

inputs.name: editing
inputs.description: Whether the editor is open. Two-way bindable, so a host can open it.

outputs.name: save
outputs.description: A new value was committed. Not emitted when the value did not change.

outputs.name: saveRequest
outputs.description: The same commit, carrying what a server write needs: an idempotency key and a guarded way back. Additive, not a replacement — `save` still fires, and a field that writes only to local state has no use for either of these. Both are emitted for one commit, in this order.

outputs.name: conflictResolved
outputs.description: The user chose which side of a conflict to keep. The winning value has already been written through to `value`; persist it, and clear `conflict`.

outputs.name: cancel
outputs.description: The user backed out — Escape, or the Cancel button.

outputs.name: valueChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `value` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(value)]`.

outputs.name: editingChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `editing` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(editing)]`.

components.name: Input Mask
components.description: 8 built-in mask presets (phone, credit card, date, time, SSN, ZIP, IP) plus custom patterns, with 3 visual variants.
whenToUse: Enforcing a fixed input format: phone, credit card, date, SSN, ZIP, IP.
You want the display formatted while still capturing the raw value.
For validation without rigid formatting, a Text Field with `state` is enough.

examples.title: Date and time in the locale
examples.description: The `date` preset's order and separator come from `Intl` for `locale` (default: the kit locale) — DD.MM.YYYY in German, YYYY/MM/DD in Japanese — and the calendar check follows the order. `time` takes the locale's separator. `phone-us`, `ssn` and `zip` are US formats and are labelled so.

examples.title: Custom pattern
examples.description: Use customMask for formats outside the presets.

customization: `inputmode`, `autocomplete` and `inputDir` override the preset's keyboard, autofill token and text direction — e.g. a digits-only `custom` mask wants `inputmode="numeric"`; a sensitive field stays `autocomplete="off"` whatever is passed.
Eight presets or a fully custom pattern; three visual variants and a leading `icon`.
Mask tokens: `#` a digit (any script — `\p{Nd}`, not `[0-9]`), `A` a letter, `*` either. Everything else in the pattern is a literal the user may type or skip.
`hasRejected()`, `rejectedChars()` and `maskComplete()` report what the mask could and could not hold, without deciding whether the value is right — that stays with the host.

Pasting is handled as a paste rather than as very fast typing: a marked country code (`+1 …`, `00 1 …`) is dropped when the mask is exactly full without it, so a number copied from a contact list arrives intact instead of shifted a place.
Emits both the raw (`rawChanged`) and formatted (`changed`) value; `error` shows a validation message.
Two-way bind `[(value)]` or a reactive control (CVA).
`locale` drives the `date` (field order + separator) and `time` (separator) presets; the value is the masked string in that order, so bind a locale-aware parser if you store an ISO date.
accessibility: The `label` is associated with the input via `for`/`id`; `inputmode` adapts the on-screen keyboard (tel/numeric) to the preset.
When `error` is set the input gets `aria-invalid` and is linked to the message via `aria-describedby` (the message uses `role="alert"`).

Characters the mask could not hold are reported in a `role="status"` line linked by `aria-describedby` — a count, not "invalid input", because the field is showing a complete and plausible value that is not what was entered. It is not `aria-invalid`: a partial fit may be exactly what the host expects.
Implements ControlValueAccessor — works with `[(ngModel)]`, `[formControl]` and `formControlName`.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP 47 locale for the `date` and `time` presets: the date's field order and separator — `MM/DD/YYYY` in en-US, `DD.MM.YYYY` in German, `YYYY/MM/DD` in Japanese — and the time separator come from `Intl`, and the placeholder letters from the labels. `phone-us`, `ssn` and `zip` are US formats whatever the locale, and say so in their default labels.

inputs.name: preset
inputs.description: Built-in mask preset (phone, credit card, date, SSN, ZIP, IP…).

inputs.name: customMask
inputs.description: Custom mask pattern, used when `preset` is `custom`. Tokens: `#` a digit, `A` a letter, `*` either; every other character is a literal that is typed in for the user (e.g. '###-##' or 'AA-####'). A mask with no token in it can never accept input.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Formatted value (two-way).

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Field size: sm, md or lg.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Visual variant.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disable the field.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Visible field label rendered above the input.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name applied via `aria-label` on the actual `<input>` while `label` is hidden. Use when a parent component owns the visible label and only needs the input to announce its purpose (e.g. `sv-phone-input`, which renders a single shared label for the country button + number field).

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Error message shown below the field.

inputs.name: icon
inputs.description: Name of an icon in `@styloviz/icons`, e.g. `'credit-card'`. A name, not a raw `<path d="…">` string: the library supplies the sizing, stroke and dark-mode handling.

inputs.name: sensitivity
inputs.description: Whether this field carries a regulated or personally identifying value.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Placeholder override. Empty uses the mask's own underscores.

inputs.name: required
inputs.description: Mark the field required (native `required` + `aria-required`).

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: The `name` the input submits under in a native form.

inputs.name: inputmode
inputs.description: Virtual-keyboard override. `null` keeps the preset's choice (`tel` for the phone presets, `numeric` for the digit presets, `text` for `custom`) — a `custom` mask that only takes digits wants `'tel'` or `'numeric'` here, or a phone shows the full QWERTY keyboard.

inputs.name: autocomplete
inputs.description: `autocomplete` token override, e.g. `'tel-national'`. Empty keeps the preset's token. Ignored on a sensitive field, which is always `off`.

inputs.name: inputDir
inputs.description: Text direction of the input itself. `'ltr'` keeps a number's digits and separators in reading order inside a right-to-left page, where `(555) 010` would otherwise be laid out around its punctuation. `null` inherits.

inputs.name: errorMessage
inputs.description: Client-side validation message.

inputs.name: serverError
inputs.description: A rejection reported by the server about this value. Self-expiring.

outputs.name: changed
outputs.description: Emitted with the masked/formatted value.

outputs.name: rawChanged
outputs.description: Emitted with the raw (unformatted) value.

outputs.name: valueChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `value` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(value)]`.

components.name: Items With More
components.description: Renders N items then collapses the overflow into a "+N more" badge, chip or text indicator — with an optional dropdown listing the hidden items and automatic width-based overflow.
whenToUse: Showing a few items inline and collapsing the rest into a "+N more" affordance.
Avatar stacks, tag rows, attendee lists where space is limited.
For a full expandable text block, use Line Clamp instead.

examples.title: Keeping the one that matters
examples.description: Overflow collapses by position, which assumes the list is ordered by importance. It usually is not — an "Overdue" chip appended to eight labels is the one the reader needed, and it is the first thing a narrow container hides. A pinned item is taken out of that race; if more are pinned than fit, every one is still shown and the row wraps, because a flag that means "unless it is inconvenient" is worse than no flag at all.

examples.title: maxVisible is the split before measurement
examples.description: A server has no layout, so autoOverflow cannot measure during a prerender. maxVisible is the split until a measurement exists, so the first client frame does not jump, because it is a number the server has too: both renders agree and hydration changes nothing.

customization: Cap visible items with `maxVisible` or let `autoOverflow` measure available width — `maxVisible` is also the split used until a measurement exists, which is every server render.
Pick the indicator style with `moreVariant` (badge, chip, text) and `moreLabel`.
Enable `moreDropdown` to reveal hidden items inline, or handle `moreClick` yourself.
Mark an item `pinned: true` and it is never collapsed into the overflow, wherever it sits in the list. `svSplitOverflow(items, max)` is exported if you need the same split elsewhere.
accessibility: The "+N more" indicator is a labelled, focusable button that exposes `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` when it opens a dropdown.

Its accessible name **names the hidden items**, not just how many: "+3 more" says three things are hidden and nothing about whether the one you came for is among them — and with `moreDropdown` off, which is the default, there is no panel to open to find out. Past five names it goes back to counting, because a label that reads out forty tags is one nobody listens to the end of.
Opening the dropdown moves focus into the panel; Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger — or to the component itself if the trigger has since been removed by a resize.

If the container widens so that everything fits, the "+N more" control is destroyed. When it held focus, focus lands on the component rather than falling to the top of the page, and the change is announced politely.
The panel is a labelled list ("N more items"); the item count is conveyed to assistive tech.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: Items to display. Strings or objects with a `label` field.

inputs.name: maxVisible
inputs.description: How many items to show before collapsing (inline variant).

inputs.name: moreLabel
inputs.description: Template for the overflow indicator. Use `{n}` as placeholder.

inputs.name: moreVariant
inputs.description: Style variant for the overflow indicator.

inputs.name: moreDropdown
inputs.description: Show overflow items in a dropdown when clicking the indicator.

inputs.name: autoOverflow
inputs.description: Auto-detect overflow: measure how many items fit on a single line and collapse the rest. Responds to container width changes via ResizeObserver. `maxVisible` still applies when this is on: it is the split used until the first measurement, so a server render and the first frame are not a single unbounded line. See `_effectiveMax`.

outputs.name: moreClick
outputs.description: Emitted when the "+N more" button is clicked. Payload = overflow items.

components.name: JSON Viewer
components.description: Expandable tree over any value — the panel a webhook inspector, an admin tool or a debug drawer needs. Tells NaN from null, a Map from an empty object and a cycle from a shared reference. Masks secrets in the value as well as on screen, lists accessors without invoking them, discloses the own properties `Object.entries` silently drops, holds a total row ceiling rather than only a per-container one, and carries a full tree keyboard model with copy-path and copy-value.
whenToUse: Showing a raw API response, webhook payload, event body, config blob or reducer state.
Any admin or support screen where the question is "what did we actually receive?".
Anywhere the panel could end up in a screenshot, a screen recording or a support ticket — pass `redact` and the secrets never reach the DOM or the clipboard.
Inspecting live objects rather than parsed JSON: class instances, things with accessors, values you have no reason to trust enough to execute.
For source code with syntax highlighting, use Code Block. For a hierarchy of app entities, use Tree View.

examples.title: A webhook payload, opened two levels
A very large array, capped
examples.code:
<sv-json-viewer [value]="rows()" [maxChildren]="50" />
<!-- The cap is counted and shown as "… N more" rather than silently dropping rows. -->

examples.title: Masking secrets before the screenshot
A redactor of your own
Reading accessors, on request
examples.code:
<sv-json-viewer [value]="session()" [evaluateGetters]="true" />
<!-- Off by default: opening a panel to look at an object is not consent to run
     its getters. On, each is read in its own try/catch. -->

examples.title: A ceiling that nesting cannot get past
examples.code:
<sv-json-viewer [value]="config()" [expandDepth]="3" [maxRows]="500" />
<!-- 40 containers of 40 children is 1,640 rows, all inside maxChildren: 100. -->

examples.title: Driven from the host
examples.code:
@ViewChild(SvJsonViewerComponent) viewer!: SvJsonViewerComponent;
// viewer.expandAll() / viewer.collapseAll() — or press * on the focused row.

customization: `svDiffValues()` from `@styloviz/core` compares two JSON values leaf by leaf and returns `{ path, kind, before, after }` — the shared diff engine, so a JSON diff is not a private half-implementation of one. Its `ignore` predicate takes the PATH rather than the key, so `meta.updatedAt` can be excluded while a top-level `updatedAt` is not.

Control the initial shape with `expandDepth`, the per-container width with `maxChildren` and the total size with `maxRows`; `expandAll()` / `collapseAll()` are public, and `*` on a focused row expands everything.
`size` (sm / md), `sortKeys` for alphabetical object keys, `quoteStrings` to render strings as JSON would, and `showCopy` for the per-row copy actions.

`redact` takes any `(context) => boolean` over `{ path, key, kind, value }`, and `redactedLabel` sets what the masked row shows. There is no default redactor — a component cannot know which of your fields is a secret, and one that guessed would hide data the reader came to read.

`evaluateGetters` switches accessors from listed-unread to read-in-a-try/catch; a getter that throws shows its message rather than taking the panel down. Only own accessors are listed — a `get` in a class body lives on the prototype, and the prototype is named rather than walked.
`nodeClick` reports `{ path, key, value }`; `copied` reports `{ path, what, text, redacted }`. On a masked row both carry the mask, not the secret.

Bytes are one leaf: an `ArrayBuffer`, `SharedArrayBuffer`, typed array, `DataView` or `Blob` renders as its type and byte length ("Uint8Array · 1,024 bytes") instead of one row per byte or an empty `{}`, and "Copy value" copies that summary, never the bytes. `BigInt` prints with its `n` suffix.
accessibility: A real `role="tree"` of `role="treeitem"` rows with `aria-level` and `aria-expanded` — flattened rather than nested, so depth is announced without a DOM nest that cannot be traversed.
One tab stop for the whole tree; Up/Down move, Right opens then descends, Left closes then climbs to the parent, Home/End jump to the ends and `*` expands everything.
Type is carried by more than colour — every value renders its own text (`null`, `undefined`, `NaN`, `Map(2)`, `[Circular]`), so nothing depends on being able to tell green from blue.

A masked row says `[redacted]` in words. There is no icon-only or tint-only version: "this field was hidden from you" is not conveyable in colour, and the label is what a screen reader and a translator both need.
An unread accessor reads as `(getter — not read)` and one that threw reads as its message, so neither looks like a value that happens to be missing.

Skipped own properties are counted out loud under their container ("+ 1 non-enumerable, 1 symbol-keyed own properties not shown") rather than leaving a container whose count is a claim the tree cannot support.

The truncation, ceiling and omission notices are `

` elements rather than tree items, so they do not appear in the node count assistive technology reads out.
A masked row is not expandable, so the keyboard cannot open a subtree that has nothing behind it.
variants: Cycles, and What Is Not One
What It Refuses to Run, and What It Admits It Skipped
maxChildren Is a Width Limit, Not a Ceiling

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The value to show. Anything at all — this is not restricted to parsed JSON.

inputs.name: rootLabel
inputs.description: Name of the root node.

inputs.name: expandDepth
inputs.description: Auto-expand to this depth on load. 1, not 0 and not Infinity. A collapsed root shows nothing and reads as broken; a fully expanded 4 MB response locks the tab.

inputs.name: maxChildren
inputs.description: Maximum children rendered per container before a "… N more" row. A 50,000-element array is not a rendering problem to solve with patience: it is a row per element, and the browser stops responding. The cap is visible and counted rather than silent — a viewer that quietly drops rows is worse than one that shows fewer.

inputs.name: maxRows
inputs.description: Maximum rows rendered in total, across the whole tree. `maxChildren` is not a ceiling, it is a width limit. A hundred children each with a hundred children is ten thousand rows, and every one of them passed the per-container cap. Nesting multiplies, and `expandAll()` / `*` reaches all of it at once — which is how a debug panel becomes the reason the tab stopped responding. This is the actual ceiling, and the walk stops *at* it rather than building the rest and slicing: the cost of a payload nobody can read is paid in the traversal, not just in the DOM. Reaching it prints a row saying so, because a tree that silently ends is a tree the reader believes they finished.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Type scale and row density.

inputs.name: sortKeys
inputs.description: Sort object keys alphabetically instead of insertion order.

inputs.name: quoteStrings
inputs.description: Render strings with quotes and escapes, as JSON would.

inputs.name: showCopy
inputs.description: Show the copy-path / copy-value action on the focused row.

inputs.name: redact
inputs.description: Masks matching nodes before they are rendered. A JSON viewer is where an API key ends up in a screenshot. Bearer tokens, card numbers and session cookies all arrive inside perfectly ordinary payloads, and the person who pastes one into a debug drawer is not thinking about the screen recording. Return `true` from the predicate and the row prints `redactedLabel` instead of the value, stops being expandable, and — the part that matters — carries the MASK as its value, so "Copy value" and `nodeClick` cannot hand the secret out either. Redaction that only changed the pixels would be redaction the clipboard walks straight past. Redacting a container masks the entire subtree: the walk does not descend, so nothing underneath is rendered, counted or copyable. There is no default. A component cannot know which of your fields is a secret, and one that guessed would hide data the reader needed. Pass the exported `secretKeyRedactor` for the usual suspects.

inputs.name: redactedLabel
inputs.description: What a masked row shows in place of its value.

inputs.name: evaluateGetters
inputs.description: Read accessor properties instead of listing them unevaluated. Off, because looking at an object is not consent to run its code. A getter can hit the network, mutate state, throw, or be an intentionally expensive lazy field; `Object.entries` calls every one of them just to enumerate. Off, each accessor gets a row that says it is a getter and was not read. On, each is called inside a `try` and a thrower renders its message rather than taking the panel down.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name for the tree.

inputs.name: customClass
inputs.description: Extra classes on the root element.

outputs.name: nodeClick
outputs.description: A row was activated (click or Enter).

outputs.name: copied
outputs.description: Something reached the clipboard. Reports the path, which button was pressed and whether the row was masked, so a host can keep an audit trail without logging a second copy of the value it just tried to protect.

outputs.name: copyAudited
outputs.description: Something reached the clipboard — the audit-safe twin of `copied`. Carries the source, the path, whether the copied text contained a mask and when, and never the text itself, so it can be logged as-is.

components.name: Jump Menu
components.description: Compact navigation as a single native select: grouped destinations, the current one shown, and the platform picker on touch. The small form of a tab strip or an anchor rail.
whenToUse: A row of destinations does not fit — on a phone, in a toolbar, or in a narrow sidebar.
You want one control that shows where you are and moves you somewhere else.
For a persistent row of peers with room to breathe, use Tabs; for in-page sections with room, use Anchor. This is what either becomes when the room runs out.

examples.title: The small form of a tab strip
examples.code:
<!-- Below the breakpoint, swap the strip for the menu. Both read the
     same state, so nothing is duplicated. -->
@if (narrow()) {
  <sv-jump-menu [items]="asDestinations()" [(value)]="activeTab" />
} @else {
  <sv-tabs [tabs]="tabs" [(activeId)]="activeTab" />
}

customization: Three sizes: sm, md, lg.
Grouped destinations via `optgroup` — consecutive items sharing a `group`.
A placeholder while `value` names nothing, or none at all.
Navigates through `SvLinkAdapter` when a destination carries an `href`; otherwise the host handles `jump`.

`scrollTarget` (`id`, or a scroll container) scrolls to the destination with the item's id itself, leaving `scrollOffset` px for a sticky header, and emits `(jumped)` once the scroll starts. `activeId` lets a scroll-spy drive the select, so scrolling the content moves the control.
`goButton` adds a Go button (WCAG 3.2.2): choosing only marks a destination, and nothing happens until Go or Enter — for menus whose destinations are new pages. `goLabel` words it.

`surfaceId` names this instance in the shared navigation-analytics stream (`provideSvNavTelemetry()`): every destination taken is `jump` (with its position). Consent and retention are the sink's; under `retention: 'none'` keys and labels are stripped.
accessibility: A native `<select>`, so keyboard, screen-reader and platform-picker behaviour are the browser's rather than the kit's.
The label is a real `<label for>`, kept for assistive technology even when visually hidden.
Groups are real `<optgroup>` elements, announced as groups.
A disabled destination is a disabled `<option>`, skipped by keyboard and refused by the component.
variants: Replaces a tab strip under 640 px

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: Destinations, in display order.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Id of the current destination. Use `[(value)]` for two-way binding.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Visible label above the control. Not optional in practice: a bare `<select>` in a navigation bar reads as *"combo box, Overview"* and nothing tells a screen-reader user it moves them.

inputs.name: labelHidden
inputs.description: Hide the label visually, keeping it for assistive technology.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Control size.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Prevents any destination from being chosen.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Text for the placeholder option shown while `value` matches no destination. Empty string removes the placeholder entirely.

inputs.name: customClass
inputs.description: Additional CSS classes on the root wrapper.

inputs.name: scrollTarget
inputs.description: Scroll to the chosen destination, by id. `'none'` leaves it to the host's `(jump)`; `'id'` scrolls the page to the element with the item's id; an element scrolls THAT container to the matching id inside it. Emits `jumped` once the scroll has started.

inputs.name: scrollOffset
inputs.description: Pixels left above the destination — a sticky header's height.

inputs.name: activeId
inputs.description: The destination something else says is current — typically a scroll-spy's `activeId()`. When set, the select follows it, so scrolling the content moves the control. `null` leaves `value` alone.

inputs.name: goButton
inputs.description: Choosing marks a destination; nothing happens until the Go button (or Enter on the select) — WCAG 3.2.2 for menus whose destinations are new pages.

inputs.name: goLabel
inputs.description: The Go button's label.

inputs.name: surfaceId
inputs.description: Names this menu in the shared navigation-analytics stream when a page has more than one — a static name, never a record id. Ignored unless `provideSvNavTelemetry()` is wired up.

outputs.name: jump
outputs.description: Emitted whenever a destination is chosen — always, because a `<select>` is not a link and the browser does not navigate from it. Fires on every `change`, which on Windows includes each arrow key pressed on the closed control (WCAG 3.2.2); set `[goButton]="true"` to emit only on Go or Enter.

outputs.name: jumped
outputs.description: Emitted after `scrollTarget` scrolled to a destination, with the element.

outputs.name: valueChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `value` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(value)]`.

components.name: Kanban Board
components.description: 8 variants: sprint board, CRM pipeline, helpdesk, compact, swimlanes, collapsible columns, rich headers and fixed-header scrolling.
whenToUse: Visualizing work moving through stages: sprint, pipeline, helpdesk, intake.
You want drag-and-drop between columns with optional WIP limits.
For date-driven schedules use the Gantt Chart instead.

The board is NOT virtualized — every card in every expanded column is in the DOM, measured at ~26 DOM nodes per card on the default variant. Around 300 rendered cards is the practical ceiling; past that, page the columns with `hasMore` + `(columnLoadMore)` rather than passing the whole backlog, which is what those inputs exist for. Virtualizing is the wrong fix here: a column is a drop target and a scroll container at once, and a recycled row cannot be the thing a finger is holding.
Where a stage genuinely holds thousands of cards, that stage is a queue rather than a board column — show a count and a filtered Data Table for it.

examples.title: Let a browser agent drive it (WebMCP)
examples.code:
<!-- svWebMcp from @styloviz/core registers roadmap_describe, roadmap_… — see /docs/webmcp -->
<sv-kanban-board svWebMcp="roadmap" [columns]="columns" [transitionRules]="rules" />
<!-- tools: describe, list_cards, move_card, move_cards, select_cards -->

examples.title: A WIP limit that actually holds
examples.code:
<sv-kanban-board
  [columns]="columns()"
  wipLimitMode="strict"
  (cardMoved)="persist($event)"
  (wipLimitBlocked)="onBlocked($event)" />

// 'soft' is the default: the badge warns and the move still goes through,
// because a WIP limit is a team agreement before it is a permission. Use
// 'strict' where the limit IS the rule — a deploy gate, a regulated review step.
//
// The refusal fires INSTEAD of cardMoved, so the board never changed and there
// is no rollback() on the payload. Say what happened: a drop that silently does
// nothing reads as a broken board.
onBlocked(event: KanbanWipLimitEvent): void {
  this.toast.warn(
    `${event.card.title} stayed put — ${event.columnTitle} is at its limit of ${event.limit}.`,
  );
}

examples.title: Who may move what — canMove
examples.code:
<sv-kanban-board
  [columns]="columns()"
  [canMove]="canMove"
  (cardMoved)="persist($event)"
  (moveRefused)="onRefused($event)" />

// Called on EVERY route — mouse drag, touch drag, the Move panel and the
// keyboard grab — and for reorders too (from === to). Returning false refuses
// the move the way a strict WIP limit does: the board is untouched, the
// refusal is announced, and moveRefused fires instead of cardMoved.
readonly canMove: KanbanCanMove = (card, from, to) =>
  this.user().canApprove || to !== 'approved';

onRefused(event: KanbanMoveRefusedEvent): void {
  this.toast.warn(`You cannot move ${event.card.title} there.`);
}

examples.title: Persisting a move
examples.code:
<sv-kanban-board
  [columns]="columns()"
  [draggable]="true"
  [pendingCardIds]="pending()"
  (cardMoved)="onCardMoved($event)" />

// The card lands where it was dropped before the server has heard about it — a
// card that snaps back for 300ms on every drag feels broken. Bind
// [pendingCardIds] so it cannot be dragged again while its write is in flight.
onCardMoved(event: KanbanCardMoveEvent): void {
  this.pending.update(s => new Set(s).add(event.card.id));

  // Two people dragging the same card is the normal case on a board, so the
  // requestKey matters: a retry of a request that actually succeeded would
  // otherwise move the card again, past wherever the other person put it.
  this.api.move({
    cardId: event.card.id,
    toColumnId: event.toColumnId,
    newIndex: event.newIndex,
    requestKey: event.requestKey,
  }).subscribe({
    error: () => { event.rollback(); this.toast.error('Could not move that card.'); },
    complete: () => this.pending.update(s => { const n = new Set(s); n.delete(event.card.id); return n; }),
  });
}

customization: `transitionRules` sets which column may follow which (`allow`, `deny`, `*`, `backward: false`) and what a card needs before it may enter a column (`svKanbanRequires.assignee`, `.field`, `.subtasksDone`). `moveRefused` reports the `reason` and what is `missing`.
`multiSelect` with two-way `selectedCardIds`: drag any selected card and the whole selection moves as one `cardsMoved`, with one `rollback()`.

Companions: `sv-kanban-quick-edit` (a draft editor for a card, opened from `cardClicked`), `svKanbanCardPreview` (a rich preview on hover and focus) and `sv-kanban-view-bar` with `svKanbanApplyView` (a remembered search and sort).
Native HTML5 drag-and-drop plus a built-in keyboard move mode (`keyboardMove`).

Touch drag is its own gesture: press and hold a card for ~220ms to pick it up, drag to a column, lift to drop. Moving before it lifts is a scroll, so a column stays scrollable; holding near a board edge scrolls it sideways so a column that started off-screen is reachable. HTML5 drag-and-drop does not fire on touch at all, so without this the board could not move a card on a phone.

`wipLimitMode` — `'soft'` (default) warns and allows; `'strict'` refuses the move before applying it and emits `(wipLimitBlocked)` instead of `(cardMoved)`. Strict holds on the drag, the arrow key AND the inline "+", because a limit that only blocks the drag is a locked front door beside an open window. A reorder inside a column is never refused, even one already over its limit — the count does not change, and freezing a full column would trap the work the limit exists to finish.
Swimlanes, SLA tracking and deal-value bars.
Inline card creation per column.
`(cardMoved)` carries `requestKey` and `rollback()` — the drag is applied before the server confirms it, so the payload is also the way back.
`pendingCardIds` marks the cards whose writes are in flight and stops them being dragged again.
No virtualization by design — see When to use for the measured ceiling and what to do past it.
accessibility: With `multiSelect`, a card's selected state is `aria-pressed` as well as an outline. Ctrl/⌘+Space toggles it from the keyboard, and Shift+Space extends the selection.
A rule refusal is announced with what the card still needs ("… can't move to Review yet — it needs: an assignee.").
The card preview is a `role="tooltip"` the card points to with `aria-describedby` while it shows. It opens on focus as well as hover, and closes on Escape.

Keyboard at scale: each card list is ONE tab stop (the card last focused in it). Without a grabbed card ↑/↓/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown move focus within the column, ←/→ move to the neighbouring column at the same position, and typing moves to the next card whose title starts with it; a grabbed card's arrows still move the card. Documented ceiling: 2,000 cards on a board, past which a dev-mode warning fires.

Focus after a mutation: a moved card keeps focus; if it is off screen after the move, focus goes to the card now at its position in that column, then the one before it, then the column — never `<body>`.

A card's COLUMN is its status, and a column is a position on screen — so the board publishes a table of cards with a Column cell each. Read as a flat list of cards, the one fact a board exists to show is the fact that is missing. The table gains a Swimlane column when lanes are on, and Value / Win probability or Ticket / SLA when those variants are.

It mirrors the board rather than the data: collapsed columns and hidden lanes drop out, and a one-line overview gives the card count, how many columns are collapsed, how many cards are overdue and which columns are over their WIP limit — the at-a-glance facts the layout conveys with colour and position.
Set `boardLabel` on any dashboard with more than one board. Without it both summaries are captioned identically and a listener landing in one cannot tell which board they are in.
Cards are focusable `role="button"`s; Enter opens a card and, with `keyboardMove`, Space picks it up.
Full keyboard drag alternative: Space to grab, ←/→ to change column, ↑/↓ to reorder, Space/Enter to drop, Escape to cancel — moves are announced via a live region.
Column collapse/expand and swimlane toggles are labelled and keyboard operable (`aria-expanded`); inline add-card supports Enter/Escape.

The WIP badge is worded, not just numeric. "5/5" read aloud is two numbers with nothing to say the second is a ceiling, and the amber that carried that meaning is invisible to a reader who cannot separate it from the grey — so the badge carries `aria-label="2 of 2 cards, at the limit"`, and "over the limit" once it is passed.

A strict refusal is announced, on all three routes in: "Payments service v4.2 was not moved. Deploying is at its limit of 1 card." A drop that just fails to happen is indistinguishable from a board that does not work.
An arrow-key move into a COLLAPSED column expands it. A collapsed column renders no cards, so without that the card would seem to vanish — from the board and from the summary table that mirrors it.
Touch drag is announced on pick-up, and on a cancel or a release that never reached a column, so a gesture with no cursor and no drag image still says what it did.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Column definitions with initial card data.

inputs.name: collapsedColumnIds
inputs.description: Which columns are collapsed (two-way). Seeded once from `col.collapsed` on the first non-empty `columns()`, after which the user owns it — a `model`, so a host restoring a board or persisting a per-user layout can both write it and see it change. It was an internal signal, which put the one piece of board state a user actually rearranges out of reach of the app that has to remember it.

inputs.name: collapsedSwimlaneIds
inputs.description: Which swimlane rows are collapsed (two-way). Same reasoning as collapsedColumnIds.

inputs.name: boardLabel
inputs.description: What this board is, e.g. `'Sprint 24'`. Names the board's tabular summary, which is what a screen-reader user reads instead of the layout. Set it on any dashboard showing more than one board: without it both summaries are captioned identically, and a listener landing in one cannot tell which. Default: `''`.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Card rendering style and board layout. Default: 'project'.

inputs.name: draggable
inputs.description: Enable HTML5 drag-and-drop between columns. Default: true.

inputs.name: collapsible
inputs.description: Allow columns to be collapsed (regular variants). Default: false.

inputs.name: showAddCard
inputs.description: Show per-column "Add card" button. Default: true.

inputs.name: currency
inputs.description: Currency symbol used in CRM variant totals. Default: '$'.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP 47 locale for dates and numbers.

inputs.name: maxCardsHeight
inputs.description: Maximum height of the scrollable card body in the `fixed-header` variant. Accepts any valid CSS length: `'520px'`, `'60vh'`, `'calc(100vh - 200px)'`. Default: `'520px'`.

inputs.name: fillHeight
inputs.description: Fill the height the host gives the board, and scroll each column's cards inside it (project, crm, helpdesk, compact and toggle-columns variants). Give the host a definite height — `class="block h-full"` inside a flex column, say — and the columns stretch to it, their headers stay put and only the cards scroll. With an auto-height host nothing changes: the columns keep their natural height, so a phone layout can scroll the page. Default: false.

inputs.name: keyboardMove
inputs.description: Enable the keyboard drag-and-drop alternative. With a card focused, press Space to pick it up, arrow keys to move it (←/→ between columns, ↑/↓ within a column), Space/Enter to drop, and Escape to cancel. Requires `draggable`. Default: true.

inputs.name: wipLimitMode
inputs.description: What a column's `limit` does when a move would exceed it — see KanbanWipLimitMode. `'soft'` warns and allows; `'strict'` refuses the move and emits wipLimitBlocked instead of cardMoved. Default: `'soft'`.

inputs.name: canMove
inputs.description: Who may move what — see KanbanCanMove. `(card, fromColumnId, toColumnId) => boolean`; `false` refuses the move exactly as a strict WIP limit does: the board is untouched, the refusal is announced, the drop target paints as blocked during a drag, and moveRefused fires instead of cardMoved. Honoured by mouse drag, touch drag, the Move panel and the keyboard grab. `null` allows every move.

inputs.name: transitionRules
inputs.description: Workflow rules — which column may follow which, what a card needs before it may enter a column. Checked with `canMove` on every path a move can take; a refusal says why in moveRefused (`reason`, `missing`).

inputs.name: multiSelect
inputs.description: Let cards be selected together: Ctrl/⌘+click or Ctrl/⌘+Space toggles, Shift extends; dragging one moves them all.

inputs.name: selectedCardIds
inputs.description: The selected card ids. Two-way.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the board's first load is in flight. Replaces the board with a skeleton. For a *background* refresh of one column, set `loading` on that `KanbanColumn` instead — blanking a board the user is reading is worse than showing slightly stale cards.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Load failure. Replaces the board with a retry prompt. A bare string is accepted; use `toSvDataError()` from `@styloviz/core` to normalize an `HttpErrorResponse` and get sensible retry behaviour.

inputs.name: pendingCardIds
inputs.description: Ids of cards with a write in flight. Those cards dim, stop responding to pointer events and cannot be dragged or picked up by keyboard — so a second move cannot race the first, and `rollback()` can never be ambiguous.

inputs.name: doneColumnIds
inputs.description: Ids of finished columns (Done, Won, Lost). A due date there is history: never overdue, no due chip, not counted as overdue.

inputs.name: emptyMessage
inputs.description: Message shown when the board has no columns at all. Leave empty for the default copy.

inputs.name: loadMoreLabel
inputs.description: Label of the per-column "Load more" control.

outputs.description: Emitted after a successful drag-drop move.

outputs.name: cardClicked
outputs.description: Emitted when a card is clicked.

outputs.name: addCardClicked

outputs.name: retry

outputs.name: columnLoadMore

outputs.name: wipLimitBlocked
outputs.description: A move `wipLimitMode="strict"` refused. Emitted *instead of* `cardMoved`, so the board is unchanged and there is nothing to roll back.

outputs.name: moveRefused
outputs.description: A move the host's `canMove` or `transitionRules` refused. Emitted *instead of* `cardMoved`, so the board is unchanged and there is nothing to roll back.

outputs.name: cardsMoved
outputs.description: Several selected cards dropped together — emitted instead of `cardMoved` (`multiSelect`).
