inputs.description: Container style: plain border, tinted `soft` surface, or a heavier `outlined` border.

inputs.name: density
inputs.description: Row padding: `compact`, `comfortable` or `spacious`.

inputs.name: selectionMode
inputs.description: Row selection: `single` replaces the selection on click, `multiple` toggles each clicked row. Selection lives in `selectedIds`.

inputs.name: checkable
inputs.description: Show a checkbox on every row plus a "Select all" box; checked rows live in `checkedIds`. Also on in `checklist` mode.

inputs.name: nested
inputs.description: Render `items` as an expandable tree using each item's `children`. Same as `mode="nested"`; takes precedence over grouping and windowing.

inputs.name: virtualized
inputs.description: Render only the rows in view (windowing) inside a `viewportHeight` scroller. Flat lists only; ignored when nested or grouped.

inputs.name: grouped
inputs.description: Split rows into sections by each item's `group` (missing groups fall under "Ungrouped"). Same as `mode="grouped"`.

inputs.name: searchable
inputs.description: Show the search box that filters rows by their text. Always shown in `scrolling` and `virtualization` modes.

inputs.name: stickyGroupHeaders
inputs.description: Keep each section header pinned to the top while its rows scroll, in grouped mode.

inputs.name: infiniteScroll
inputs.description: Emit `loadMore` when the list is scrolled near its end, and show the paging footer.

inputs.name: hasMore
inputs.description: Whether more pages exist. While false `loadMore` is not emitted and the footer shows the end-of-list marker.

inputs.name: loadingMore
inputs.description: True while the next page is being fetched. Shows a "Loading more" footer and holds back further `loadMore` events.

inputs.name: viewportHeight
inputs.description: Height in pixels of a flat list's scroll area: fixed when virtualized or in `scrolling` mode, a maximum otherwise. Also sets the PageUp/PageDown step.

inputs.name: itemHeight
inputs.description: Height of a **single-line** row, in pixels — the base every windowed row is measured from. Windowing has to know where row 4,000 starts without rendering rows 0–3,999, so a row's height is computed rather than measured: this base, plus a line for a `subtitle`/`description` and a strip for `tags` on the rows that carry them. See `rowHeightOf`. The estimate is what the row is then sized to, so the scrollbar and the rows agree exactly.

inputs.name: overscan
inputs.description: Extra rows rendered above and below the visible window when virtualized, to avoid blank flashes while scrolling.

inputs.name: searchPlaceholder
inputs.description: Placeholder and accessible label of the search box.

inputs.name: emptyMessage
inputs.description: Message in the empty state when there are no rows and no search term is active.

inputs.name: customClass
inputs.description: Extra CSS classes added to the list container.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name of the list region.

inputs.name: announceActions
inputs.description: Announce selection, check, action and paging changes to screen readers through a polite live region.

inputs.name: showQuickActions
inputs.description: Show the `quickActions` buttons on every row.

inputs.name: quickActions
inputs.description: Per-row action buttons, shown when `showQuickActions` is true. Clicks emit `quickActionClick`.

inputs.name: bulkActions
inputs.description: Actions in the bar that appears while rows are checked (or selected, when not checkable). Clicks emit `bulkActionClick`.

inputs.name: enableBulkHotkeys
inputs.description: Let single keys trigger bulk actions while rows are selected. Keys map via `bulkHotkeys`, falling back to Delete/Backspace, A and R.

inputs.name: bulkHotkeys
inputs.description: Map of lowercase key to bulk action `id`, used when `enableBulkHotkeys` is on. Overrides the built-in `delete`, `archive` and `mark-read` keys.

inputs.name: enableRovingFocus
inputs.description: Make the list a single tab stop: arrow, Home/End and PageUp/PageDown keys plus typeahead move between rows.

inputs.name: swipeStartActions
inputs.description: Actions behind each row's START edge, revealed by swiping the row toward its end — right in a left-to-right page, left in a right-to-left one. The first sits at the edge and is the one a full swipe runs. Every action is also in the row's Actions button, for a mouse, a keyboard and a screen reader. Flat and grouped rows, windowed or not; nested rows do not swipe.

inputs.name: swipeEndActions
inputs.description: Actions behind each row's END edge, revealed by swiping toward the start. The first is the full-swipe action.

inputs.name: fullSwipe
inputs.description: A swipe past 60% of the row's width runs that side's first action without a tap.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the first page is being fetched. Replaces the list with a placeholder. For the *next* page use `loadingMore`, which keeps the rows already on screen.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Load failure. Use `toSvDataError()` from `@styloviz/core` to normalize an `HttpErrorResponse`.

inputs.name: serverSide
inputs.description: Search on the server instead of in the component. The supplied `items` are rendered as given — filtering them again would hide rows the server deliberately returned, and client-side search can only ever look at the page already downloaded.

inputs.name: debounceMs
inputs.description: Delay before `searched` fires, in milliseconds. `0` emits immediately.

inputs.name: selectedIds
inputs.description: Ids of the selected rows (two-way). Used when `selectionMode` is not `none`.

inputs.name: checkedIds
inputs.description: Ids of the checked rows (two-way). Used when the list is checkable.

inputs.name: expandedIds
inputs.description: Which nested items are expanded (two-way). A `model` alongside `selectedIds` and `checkedIds` because it is the same kind of fact and the host has the same reasons to reach it: open the branch a deep link names, restore the tree after a route change, persist what the user had open. Held in a private signal it could be neither set nor observed — the one piece of this component's item state that was unreachable.

inputs.name: activeItemId
inputs.description: The row the keyboard cursor is on (two-way) — the roving tab stop. An id, not an element, because a windowed list renders twenty rows of five hundred: the cursor moves to the end of the list, not the edge of the window, and keeps its place when the focused row scrolls out of the DOM. Two-way because it is the same kind of fact as `selectedIds`: a host can put the cursor on the row a deep link names, and read where the user left it.

inputs.name: scrollOffset
inputs.description: Scroll position of the list viewport, in pixels (two-way). Written on every scroll, applied to the viewport whenever it changes from the outside — bind it and the position survives what destroys the component: a route change, a tab switch, a `@defer` block re-entering, an infinite-scroll page arriving. Without it, restoring a list meant restoring its rows and landing the user back at the top of them.

inputs.name: query
inputs.description: The search term. Two-way bindable, so it can be restored from a URL and kept in step with a server-side query.

outputs.name: itemClick
outputs.description: A row was activated by click or keyboard. Not emitted for disabled rows.

outputs.name: selectionChange
outputs.description: The user changed the selection. Carries the new set of selected ids.

outputs.name: checkChange
outputs.description: A single row's checkbox was toggled. Carries the item and its new checked state; "Select all" and section checkboxes do not emit it.

outputs.name: loadMore
outputs.description: The list was scrolled near its end with `infiniteScroll` on, `hasMore` true and no page loading. Carries rendered and total row counts.

outputs.name: quickActionClick
outputs.description: A row's quick action was clicked. Carries the item and the action.

outputs.name: bulkActionClick
outputs.description: A bulk action was triggered by its button or hotkey. Carries the action and a copy of the checked (or selected) ids.

outputs.name: swipeAction
outputs.description: A swipe action ran — from a revealed button, a full swipe or the row's Actions menu. The list removes nothing itself.

outputs.name: searched
outputs.description: The debounced search term — fetch matching rows. Debounced by `debounceMs` and never emitted twice for the same term. Pair with `serverSide`. Named `searched` rather than `queryChange`, and that is load-bearing: `query` below is a `model()`, which already owns an output of that name and emits it on every keystroke. Declaring it here as well claimed the same binding twice — Angular reports "Output 'queryChange' is bound to both 'query' and 'queryChange'", the component's metadata stops resolving, and every component importing it then fails with "Component imports must be standalone components…". It also made the debounce contract above a lie, since the model's undebounced emission went out under the same name. `sv-search-bar` has the identical shape and solves it the same way: `value = model()` for the two-way text, `searched = output()` for the debounced notification. Enforced by `model-output-collision` in scripts/check-ui-invariants.mjs.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The host should re-run the failed load.

outputs.name: selectedIdsChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `selectedIds` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(selectedIds)]`.

outputs.name: checkedIdsChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `checkedIds` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(checkedIds)]`.

outputs.name: expandedIdsChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `expandedIds` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(expandedIds)]`.

outputs.name: activeItemIdChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `activeItemId` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(activeItemId)]`.

outputs.name: scrollOffsetChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `scrollOffset` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(scrollOffset)]`.

outputs.name: queryChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `query` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(query)]`.

components.name: Markdown Editor
components.description: A Markdown source editor on a native textarea — undo, IME, spellcheck and phone keyboards intact — with a toolbar that wraps and unwraps (heading, bold, italic, strikethrough, code, link, quote, bulleted / numbered / task lists, code block, table), Ctrl/Cmd+B/I/K, list-aware Enter and Tab, write / preview / split views with synced scroll, paste-to-link and HTML-to-Markdown paste. The preview is the kit’s safe renderer, so nothing typed can become markup.
whenToUse: You store Markdown — docs pages, READMEs, release notes, knowledge-base articles, canned replies — and authors should see and own the syntax.
A comment or reply box where a few marks (bold, code, a link, a list) are enough and HTML would be a liability.
For formatted HTML with fonts, colours and merged cells, use the Rich Text Editor instead.

examples.title: Split view for a docs page
examples.description: Source and rendered page side by side, scrolled together; stacks under 640px (`stackBelow`). `view` and `splitAt` are models, so a host can remember both.

examples.title: A comment box
examples.description: A short toolbar, Write and Preview only, a limit, and Ctrl/Cmd+Enter to send.

examples.title: Reactive forms (CVA + validator)
examples.description: Binds with formControl / formControlName / ngModel; reports `required` and `maxlength` in Angular’s error shapes. `[formField]` (Signal Forms) works through the same accessor.

examples.title: Insert at the caret
examples.description: `insertText()` replaces the selection with text as one undo step — a snippet, a template, a canned reply. A preview switches back to write first.

examples.title: Your own toolbar
examples.description: The edits are pure functions of (text, selection) — each returns the range to replace and where the selection lands.

customization: `value`, `view` (`write` / `preview` / `split`) and `splitAt` are two-way models; `toolbar` takes tool ids in order (`SV_MARKDOWN_TOOLS` is all twelve), `views` the views the switch offers.

`height`, `placeholder`, `maxLength` (native `maxlength` + counter, amber from 90%), `required`, `invalid`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `spellcheck`, `showCount`, `syncScroll`, `stackBelow`, `headingOffset` (preview), `pasteHtml` (`markdown` or `text`).
Outputs: `submitted` (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter), `pasteConverted` (`{ markdown, lost }` from `svHtmlToMarkdown`), `linkClick` (a preview link). Methods `insertText()`, `format(tool)`, `focus()`.
Every visible string is a label in the `richEditorPro` namespace (the `md…` keys), in 12 language packs.
Print shows the rendered document, never the source.
accessibility: The source is a native `<textarea>` — screen readers, dictation, IME composition, spellcheck and undo work as they do anywhere else. It carries `aria-required`, `aria-invalid`, `maxlength`, and an `aria-describedby` keyboard hint joined to the host’s own ids.

The toolbar is `role="toolbar"` with one tab stop: ←/→ move between buttons (mirrored under RTL), Home/End go to the ends. Tools that cannot act (read-only, preview) stay focusable with `aria-disabled`; view buttons expose `aria-pressed`; shortcuts are in `aria-keyshortcuts` and the tooltip.

Tab and Shift+Tab change a list item’s indent and nothing else: outside a list, or Shift+Tab at the margin, they move focus. Escape, then Tab, always leaves the editor — announced through a polite status region, so focus is never trapped.

The preview is a focusable, named `role="region"` so it can be scrolled from the keyboard; the split divider is the kit splitter’s `role="separator"` with arrow keys and step buttons. A refused edit (character limit) and a converted paste are announced, not silent.

Engine: the ADR-aria row asks for the `@angular/aria` toolbar. The package is not a dependency of the kit yet (adopted from 2.1, ADR rule 1), so the toolbar is an in-house WAI-ARIA toolbar on core’s `svRovingTarget`; moving to Aria later changes no input or output.
variants: Docs Page — Split View with Synced Scroll
Comment Box — Write / Preview, Ctrl+Enter to Post
Reactive Forms — Required, with a Character Limit
Paste, Lists & Snippets — the Keys That Do the Work

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The Markdown source. Two-way bindable with `[(value)]`; also a form control.

inputs.name: view
inputs.description: What is shown: `'write'` (source), `'preview'` (rendered) or `'split'` (both). Two-way bindable.

inputs.name: splitAt
inputs.description: Share of the width (or height, stacked) the source takes in split view, in %. Two-way bindable.

inputs.name: toolbar
inputs.description: The formatting tools to show, in toolbar order (as `sv-rich-text-editor`'s `toolbar` takes tool ids). `[]` leaves only the view switch. Shortcuts follow the list: Ctrl/Cmd+B does nothing when `bold` is not in it.

inputs.name: views
inputs.description: The views the switch offers, in order. One view hides the switch.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Placeholder for an empty source. Not an accessible name — set `ariaLabel` or a `<label for>`.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name of the source textarea. Falls back to "Markdown source".

inputs.name: ariaDescribedBy
inputs.description: Ids of elements that describe the field (a hint, an error), joined to the editor's own keyboard hint.

inputs.name: inputId
inputs.description: Id for the textarea, so an external `<label for>` can name it. Generated when empty.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Height of the editing area, as a CSS length.

inputs.name: maxLength
inputs.description: Maximum characters (the native `maxlength`, and a counter). `0` is unlimited.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disable the editor: no editing, no toolbar. A form control's `disable()` does the same.

inputs.name: readonly
inputs.description: Read-only: the source can be selected, copied and previewed, not changed.

inputs.name: required
inputs.description: Mark the field required (`aria-required`, and a `required` error when bound to a form).

inputs.name: invalid
inputs.description: Show the field as invalid (`aria-invalid`, danger border) — bind your form's state.

inputs.name: spellcheck
inputs.description: The browser's spellcheck on the source.

inputs.name: showCount
inputs.description: Show the word and character count under the editor.

inputs.name: syncScroll
inputs.description: In split view, scroll the preview with the source and the source with the preview.

inputs.name: stackBelow
inputs.description: Below this width (px) the split view stacks the preview under the source instead of beside it.

inputs.name: pasteHtml
inputs.description: What an HTML paste becomes: `'markdown'` converts a pasted web page or document through `svHtmlToMarkdown` and reports what Markdown could not carry; `'text'` keeps the browser's plain-text paste. Code copied from an editor (`<pre>`, `white-space: pre`) always pastes as text.

inputs.name: headingOffset
inputs.description: Added to every heading level in the preview, so `#` becomes `<h3>` at 2.

outputs.name: linkClick
outputs.description: A link in the preview was activated.

outputs.name: pasteConverted
outputs.description: An HTML paste was converted to Markdown — `lost` lists what Markdown could not carry.

outputs.name: submitted
outputs.description: Ctrl/Cmd+Enter in the source — the "send" chord of a comment box. Carries the value.

outputs.name: valueChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `value` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(value)]`.

outputs.name: viewChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `view` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(view)]`.

outputs.name: splitAtChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `splitAt` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(splitAt)]`.

components.name: MCP Tool Registry
components.description: Registry for the tools and MCP servers an agent is connected to. Connection lifecycle and health, credential expiry, per-tool parameter schemas, usage and error rates, a scope permission matrix and a recent call log. Four variants — grid, table, permissions and detail.
whenToUse: Building the integrations page for an agent product — what is connected, what is healthy, what expires soon.
Letting an operator narrow what an agent may do, per tool, without editing a config file.
Diagnosing why a tool call keeps failing, with the declared schema and the recent call log side by side.
Giving a compliance reviewer a read-only view of every connection and granted scope.

examples.title: Scope matrix
examples.description: Scopes are ordered, so a policy is a threshold rather than a set.

examples.title: Audit the transition, not just the result
examples.description: Every scope change reports the value it replaced.

examples.title: Diagnose a failing connection
examples.description: The schema says what the tool expects; the call log says what happened.

examples.title: Read-only audit view
examples.description: Keeps the information, removes every control.

customization: Redaction, from the pack-wide policy: the credential LABEL, the server URL, the server error and every call-log error are masked per `provideSvAiPrivacy({ patterns })`. A URL carries a credential without looking like one (`https://user:pass@…`, `…?token=…`) and a failing client echoes it into its error; `SV_AI_COMMON_PATTERNS` includes `url-credentials` and `url-secret-param` for exactly this.

Role-gated reveal: with `provideSvAiPrivacy({ reveal: true })` — provided only for the roles allowed to see secrets — each server with something masked on screen gets a Reveal / Hide control, and `(revealChanged)` reports `{ server, revealed }` so you can log who looked. `reveal` is false by default, and it never switches masking off: values stay masked until a viewer asks.
`variant` chooses the shape: `grid` for a landing page, `table` when there are more servers than fit, `permissions` for the scope matrix, `detail` for one connection in full.

Health freshness: every status shows its as-of time from `McpServer.lastCheckedAt` ("checked 4 min. ago", locale-formatted through `[locale]`, the absolute time in its tooltip and `datetime`). Past `[healthStaleAfter]` (5 minutes, the exported `SV_MCP_HEALTH_STALE_MS`) it reads "stale — checked 2 hr. ago" in warning colour and the header counts it; a server with no `lastCheckedAt` says "check time unknown" instead of looking current. Set the window a few polls above your health check's interval; `0` turns the stale mark off. The age keeps moving on its own (re-read every 30 s in the browser), and `svMcpHealthFreshness` / `svMcpHealthAge` are exported for your own roll-ups.
`editable` false turns the whole component into an audit view — switches, radios and actions all disappear.
`showHealth` and `showUsage` drop the roll-up counts and the per-tool metrics independently.
`logLimit` is the call-log page size: a longer log says how many calls are hidden and offers "Show N more". `0` hides the log. `selectedId` drives which server the single-server variants show.

`maxParamsPerTool` (8) bounds a tool's parameter table: a generated schema can carry a hundred parameters, so the table stops at the ceiling, says what it hid, and "Show all N parameters" expands it for the one tool being inspected. `0` turns it off.
The `SCOPE_ORDER`, `scopeAtLeast`, `registryHealth` and `credentialExpiry` helpers are exported, so a policy layer can threshold scopes and compute its own roll-ups.

Scale ceilings: `[maxServers]` (100) bounds the catalogue and `[maxToolsPerServer]` (50) bounds one server's tool list — the second is the one that bites, because a single server exposing a generated API can carry several hundred tools, each with a parameter table. Both disclose what they left out, and the tool count beside a server name stays the SERVER's count, so the warning does not vanish exactly when it is earned. `0` turns either off.
accessibility: The permission matrix is a real table: scope columns are `th[scope="col"]`, each tool row is `th[scope="row"]`, and a visually-hidden `caption` names the server.
Each radio carries an explicit label ("merge_pull_request: write"), so the cell is meaningful without reading the row and column headers separately.
The connected count is `role="status"`, so a connection dropping while the operator is elsewhere is announced.
Table rows use proper `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls` disclosures pointing at the revealed tool list.
Status is never colour-only — each state carries a text label beside its dot, and a connecting server animates rather than relying on hue alone.
Every switch has an explicit `aria-label` naming what it enables, since the visible text belongs to the row rather than the control.
The Reveal control is a toggle button with `aria-pressed` and a label naming the server; the parameter "Show all" control carries `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls` pointing at the parameter list.
variants: Permissions — What the Agent May Actually Do
Detail — Schemas and the Call Log

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the data is being fetched.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Load failure. Use `toSvDataError()` from `@styloviz/core` to normalize an `HttpErrorResponse`.

inputs.name: servers
inputs.description: The connected servers.

inputs.name: selectedId
inputs.description: Which server the `detail` and `permissions` variants show. Defaults to the first.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Presentation preset.

inputs.name: showHealth
inputs.description: Show the roll-up counts above the list.

inputs.name: showUsage
inputs.description: Show per-tool call counts, error rate and latency.

inputs.name: editable
inputs.description: Let the reader flip servers and tools on and off.

inputs.name: logLimit
inputs.description: How many call-log entries the `detail` variant shows per page. `0` hides the log. When the log is longer, a notice says how many are hidden and a "Show more" control reveals the next page.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible label for the registry.

inputs.name: now
inputs.description: Clock used for credential expiry, injectable so a test is not at the mercy of the wall clock.

inputs.name: healthStaleAfter
inputs.description: How old a server's health check may be, in milliseconds, before its status is marked stale. Every status shows its age ("checked 4 min. ago", from `McpServer.lastCheckedAt`); past this window it reads "stale — checked 2 hr. ago" and the header counts it, because a status nobody has re-checked is a claim about the past. Set it a few polls above your health check's interval; `0` turns the stale mark off (the age still shows). The age keeps moving between inputs: it advances `now` by the time elapsed since `now` was last set, re-read every 30 seconds in the browser.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale for the health age ("4 min. ago").

inputs.name: expandedIds
inputs.description: Server ids whose tool list the viewer expanded (two-way). A `model` so a host can restore or persist which servers were open.

inputs.name: maxServers
inputs.description: How many servers the registry lists at once. `0` = no ceiling. A registry is a catalogue, and catalogues grow monotonically. Nobody removes an MCP server; a platform team's registry passes a hundred entries in its first year and nothing in this component was bounded.

inputs.name: maxToolsPerServer
inputs.description: How many of one server's tools are listed when it is expanded. `0` = none. This is the ceiling that actually bites, and it is per SERVER rather than per page. One server exposing a generated API can carry several hundred tools, each with a parameter table — so a registry of six servers renders thousands of rows the moment somebody expands the wrong one, and the count beside the name gave no warning because it is the number the ceiling hides.

inputs.name: maxParamsPerTool
inputs.description: How many of one tool's schema parameters are listed before "Show all". `0` = no ceiling. A generated schema can carry a hundred parameters, and the tool ceiling alone does not bound the page: fifty tools × a hundred rows is still five thousand. The table stops at the ceiling, says how many are hidden, and expands on demand for the one tool being inspected.

inputs.name: paramsExpandedKeys
inputs.description: `server::tool` keys whose full parameter table the viewer expanded (two-way). A `model` so a host can restore or persist it.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The host should re-run the failed load.

outputs.name: serverToggled
outputs.description: A server's master switch was flipped.

outputs.name: toolToggled
outputs.description: A single tool was enabled or disabled.

outputs.name: scopeChanged
outputs.description: A tool's granted scope changed, with the value it replaced.

outputs.name: reconnect
outputs.description: The reader asked to reconnect a server.

outputs.name: credentialAction
outputs.description: A credential needs re-authorising or revoking — the host does the work.

outputs.name: serverSelected
outputs.description: A server row or card was activated.

outputs.name: revealChanged
outputs.description: A viewer revealed or re-hid a server's masked values. Only fires when the privacy policy allows reveal (`provideSvAiPrivacy({ reveal: true })`) — log it to keep an audit trail of who looked at what.

outputs.name: expandedIdsChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `expandedIds` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(expandedIds)]`.

outputs.name: paramsExpandedKeysChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `paramsExpandedKeys` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(paramsExpandedKeys)]`.

components.name: Media Player
components.description: Kit chrome around a native `<video>` or `<audio>`: play / pause, a seek slider that speaks the time, volume and mute, playback speed, WebVTT captions and subtitles, full screen and picture in picture where the browser has them, and a playlist with previous / next that moves on when an item ends. One ARIA toolbar with a single tab stop, shortcuts scoped to the player, safe source URLs, a playback-error state with Try again, and the loading / error / empty states for the playlist. It never starts with sound.
whenToUse: Lesson videos in a course platform, product tours and recorded webinars in a SaaS app, or a podcast / voice-note player.
Anywhere the browser's own controls look out of place, or you need events to save progress, count views or move to the next item.
Use the Carousel for a set of still images, and a third-party player for adaptive streaming (HLS / DASH) or DRM — this one plays what a native element can.

examples.title: One video with captions and a poster
examples.description: A single item is a playlist of one: no list, no previous / next. `sources` offers several encodings (best first); `tracks` are WebVTT files, and `captionLanguage` picks the one shown (null is off).
examples.code:
<sv-media-player
  [items]="[{
    id: 'intro', title: 'Product tour', poster: '/media/tour.jpg',
    sources: [{ src: '/media/tour.webm', type: 'video/webm' }, { src: '/media/tour.mp4', type: 'video/mp4' }],
    tracks: [{ src: '/media/tour.en.vtt', srclang: 'en', label: 'English' }]
  }]"
  captionLanguage="en" />

examples.title: Resume where the viewer stopped
examples.description: `startTime` on an item seeks there when it loads, without emitting `seekComplete`. Save the place from `timeUpdate` (at most once per `timeUpdateInterval`, never mid-seek) and `paused`.
examples.code:
item = { id: lesson.id, title: lesson.title, src: lesson.url, startTime: bookmark() };

<sv-media-player [items]="[item]" (timeUpdate)="bookmark.set($event.currentTime)" (paused)="save($event)" />

examples.title: A podcast
examples.description: `kind="audio"` drives a hidden `<audio>` and draws the artwork, title and subtitle; the active caption cue is shown as text.

examples.title: A voice note
examples.description: `layout="compact"` draws an audio clip as one row — play, seek, length / position and speed — for a voicemail, a dictated message or a call recording. `sinkId` (e.g. from `sv-audio-device-select`) routes it to a chosen speaker where `setSinkId` exists.

examples.title: Demo media without files
examples.description: `svDemoVideo`, `svDemoAudio` and `svDemoCaptions` make a WebM clip of any length, a WAV chime and a WebVTT file in the browser — for prototypes and tests. Create the object URLs after render and revoke them.

customization: Surfaces use the `gray` and `primary` tokens with `dark:` pairs; the picture area is always black. `playlistPosition="end"` puts the playlist beside the player when the player is wide enough (a container query), otherwise below.

`playbackRates`, `seekStep`, `preload`, `crossOrigin`, `autoAdvance`, `showPlaylist`, `shortcuts` and `timeUpdateInterval` tune behaviour; `play()`, `pause()`, `togglePlay()`, `seek(seconds)`, `next()`, `previous()` and `select(index)` drive it from code.
Every string comes from the `display` labels (`media*` keys) in 12 language packs — `provideSvLabels(SV_DISPLAY_LABELS_DE)` or the per-instance `labels` input.

`layout="compact"` is the one-row voice-note shape for `kind="audio"` (video keeps the full player); `sinkId` picks the output device through `HTMLMediaElement.setSinkId`, feature-detected, and a refusal is reported through `sinkError` while playback carries on through the default device.
Sources, tracks and posters pass `svIsSafeMediaUrl` / `svIsSafeUrl`: http(s), relative, `blob:` and media `data:` URIs play; `javascript:` and friends are never requested.
accessibility: The controls are one `role="toolbar"` with a roving tab stop: Tab enters it once, ←/→ / Home / End move between controls, and on the volume slider ↑/↓ change the volume — so no control traps focus. This follows the WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern, built on the kit's own `svRovingTarget` rather than `@angular/aria`, which the kit does not depend on in 2.0.
The seek slider is a native range with its own tab stop, an accessible name and `aria-valuetext` such as "1:02 of 3:00"; its arrow keys skip `seekStep` seconds and Page Up / Page Down a tenth.

Shortcuts work only inside the player and never with Ctrl, Alt or Meta: Space or K play / pause (Space is left to a focused button), ←/→ on the picture skip, M mutes, F full screen, C cycles captions, < and > change the speed. They are described to screen readers and named in `aria-keyshortcuts`.

Toggles say their state (`aria-pressed` on mute and captions; the full-screen and picture-in-picture buttons change their names); a caption or speed change is announced politely. The current playlist item has `aria-current` and "Now playing".
A playback failure is a `role="alert"` with the reason in words and a Try again button; buttons are at least 40 px, with visible focus rings in both themes.
variants: States — Loading, Error, Empty & Playback Failure

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: What to play — one item for a single clip, several for a playlist.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The item playing, as an index into `items` (two-way). Out-of-range values are clamped.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: `video` draws the picture; `audio` draws the artwork and title, and shows captions as text.

inputs.name: layout
inputs.description: `compact` draws an audio clip as one row — play, seek, time, speed — for a voice note or a call recording. No artwork, volume slider or playlist (the M key still mutes). Ignored for `kind="video"`.

inputs.name: sinkId
inputs.description: The output device (`MediaDeviceInfo.deviceId`, e.g. from `sv-audio-device-select`'s `outputDeviceId`) the sound plays through. Applied with `setSinkId` where the browser has it, and ignored where it does not; null leaves the system default.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the host is still fetching the playlist.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: The playlist failed to load (a string or an `SvDataError`). Playback errors are not this — they show inside the player and emit `mediaError`.

inputs.name: itemKey
inputs.description: Identity of an item, a property name or a function.

inputs.name: captionLanguage
inputs.description: The caption / subtitle track shown, by `srclang`; null is off (two-way).

inputs.name: volume
inputs.description: Volume from 0 to 1 (two-way).

inputs.name: muted
inputs.description: Sound off (two-way).

inputs.name: playbackRate
inputs.description: Playback speed (two-way).

inputs.name: playbackRates
inputs.description: The speeds the speed button steps through.

inputs.name: autoplay
inputs.description: Start playing as soon as the first item can play — always muted (a viewer turns the sound on), and never when the viewer prefers reduced motion.

inputs.name: autoAdvance
inputs.description: When an item ends, go on to the next one.

inputs.name: seekStep
inputs.description: Seconds the arrow keys skip.

inputs.name: preload
inputs.description: How much to fetch before play: `none`, `metadata` (length and first frame) or `auto`.

inputs.name: crossOrigin
inputs.description: CORS mode for the media and its tracks — set it when the `.vtt` files live on another origin.

inputs.name: shortcuts
inputs.description: Keyboard shortcuts inside the player (Space/K, ←/→, M, F, C, `<`/`>`).

inputs.name: showPlaylist
inputs.description: Show the playlist when there is more than one item.

inputs.name: playlistPosition
inputs.description: `bottom` stacks the playlist under the player; `end` puts it beside the player when there is room.

inputs.name: timeUpdateInterval
inputs.description: Least time between two `timeUpdate` emissions, in milliseconds.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: The player's accessible name. Null derives "<title> — media player".

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP-47 locale for the speed figures.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Per-instance text, merged over the registry's `display` labels.

outputs.name: played
outputs.description: Playback started or resumed.

outputs.name: paused
outputs.description: Playback paused — by the viewer, by `pause()`, or at the end.

outputs.name: finished
outputs.description: The item played to its end (before any `autoAdvance`).

outputs.name: timeUpdate
outputs.description: The playhead moved while playing — at most once per `timeUpdateInterval`, never during a seek.

outputs.name: seekComplete
outputs.description: The viewer (or `seek()`) moved the playhead — `from` is where it was. Not emitted for an item's `startTime`.

outputs.name: trackChange
outputs.description: The playlist moved to another item. `index` changes with it.

outputs.name: mediaError
outputs.description: The current item could not be played. The player shows the reason and a Try again button.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The host should re-run the failed playlist request (`error`).

outputs.name: sinkError
outputs.description: `sinkId` could not be applied — the device was unplugged, or the page is not allowed to choose one. Playback carries on through the default device.

outputs.name: indexChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `index` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(index)]`.

outputs.name: captionLanguageChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `captionLanguage` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(captionLanguage)]`.

outputs.name: volumeChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `volume` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(volume)]`.

outputs.name: mutedChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `muted` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(muted)]`.

outputs.name: playbackRateChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `playbackRate` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(playbackRate)]`.

components.name: Mega Menu
components.description: Multi-column dropdown header navigation. Top-level items link directly or open a mega panel: columns of links (headings, descriptions, badges, icons), a tabbed panel, a two-pane cascade or an icon grid, with featured cards, a footer bar and in-panel search. Opens on hover or click, with a hover corridor, animated panel and keyboard support.
whenToUse: Job: destination links — renders real `<a href>` links to global destinations across the site (compare all seven in the “Choosing a navigation pattern” guide under Guides).
A storefront / marketing header where a section fans out into many links across columns.
You want a featured promo (image + CTA) alongside the link columns.
For a simple single-column menu, use a Dropdown Menu instead; for in-page section switching, use Tabs.

examples.title: Let the browser navigate (the default)
examples.code:
<!-- Items carry real hrefs and the browser follows them.
     The outputs stay quiet, because nothing was cancelled. -->
<sv-mega-menu [items]="items" />

customization: Hover or click trigger, with a configurable close delay.
Swaps to a Drawer below `mobileBreakpoint` — there is no small version of a multi-column panel, so it becomes a different control rather than a squeezed one.
Columns with optional headings; per-link description, badge and leading icon.
Optional featured promo panel with image, copy and CTA — or several `featuredCards` (`promo` · `stats` · `testimonial`) placed by `featuredLayout` (`side` · `top` · `bottom`).

Per-item `layout`: `columns` (the default), `cascade` (categories on the left, their links on the right) or `icon-grid` (`gridColumns` 2 or 3); `tabs` turns a panel into a vertical tab list, each tab with its own columns, featured card and footer.
A tinted `footer` strip of links and a call to action; `searchable` puts a filter box at the top of a panel, and `recent` shows the menu's `recent` links as a column of their own.

`width` (`anchored` · `full`) for a full-width bar, `panelTone` (`auto` · `light` · `dark` · `glass`), `hoverIntent` (`corridor` · `delay` · `none`), and `activeHref` to mark the active trail from the current URL.

In the mobile drawer, `mobileLayout` opens a panel item as an `accordion` (the default) or as `stacked-pages`, one level at a time with a Back button; `panelTone="glass"` is for a sticky or fixed header only.
Three sizes and active-item highlighting via `activeId`.

`surfaceId` names this instance in the shared navigation-analytics stream (`provideSvNavTelemetry()`): a panel opened is `explore`, a link, top-level item or featured card followed is `jump`, Escape is `escape`. Consent and retention are the sink's; under `retention: 'none'` keys and labels are stripped.
accessibility: Triggers expose `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded`; Escape closes the open panel.
Panel links are real anchors and are only in the tab order while their panel is open.

Left / Right move along the top-level bar (Home / End to the ends) and across the panel's columns; under `dir="rtl"` — read from the host, so a `dir="rtl"` ancestor counts — both mirror, so the arrow always points where focus goes.
Chevron rotation and the featured image are decorative (aria-hidden); focus states are visible in light and dark mode.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: Top-level navigation items.

inputs.name: trigger
inputs.description: How panels open.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Nav item size.

inputs.name: activeId
inputs.description: Id of the active item — highlights the matching trigger.

inputs.name: closeDelay
inputs.description: Delay (ms) before a hovered panel closes on mouse-leave.

inputs.name: openDelay
inputs.description: Delay (ms) before hovering an item opens its panel, when no panel is open yet. Switching between items while one is already open is always immediate. Set to `0` to open on the first pointer enter.

inputs.name: mobileBreakpoint
inputs.description: Viewport width below which the menu becomes a drawer instead of hover panels. Set to `0` to keep the desktop form at every size.

inputs.name: surfaceId
inputs.description: Names this menu in the shared navigation-analytics stream when a page has more than one — a static name such as `'primary-nav'`, never a record id. Ignored unless `provideSvNavTelemetry()` is wired up.

inputs.name: mobileMenuLabel
inputs.description: Accessible label for the button that opens the mobile drawer.

inputs.name: navigation
inputs.description: Who navigates when an entry has an `href` — the browser (`'link'`) or your router, via the outputs (`'emit'`). An entry with no `href` always emits.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: How wide an open panel is: sized to its content beside the trigger (`'anchored'`), or spanning this menu's whole `<nav>` with the content in a centred container (`'full'`).

inputs.name: hoverIntent
inputs.description: How hover opens and keeps a panel: `'corridor'` (the delays plus the safe corridor), `'delay'` (the delays only), or `'none'` (opens on the first pointer enter; `closeDelay` still bridges the gap to the panel).

inputs.name: corridorTolerance
inputs.description: How far behind the point where the pointer left a trigger the corridor's apex sits, in px. More forgives a bigger backwards wobble as the hand sets off; the far edge is always the panel's near side.

inputs.name: activeHref
inputs.description: The `href` of the page the reader is on. Its top-level item is highlighted, the link gets `aria-current="page"`, and its tab or category is the one a panel opens on.

inputs.name: panelTone
inputs.description: The panel's surface: follow the page's theme (`'auto'`), always light, always dark, or frosted glass — for a menu in a sticky or fixed header, where the page scrolls underneath it.

inputs.name: recent
inputs.description: Recently viewed links, shown as a column in every panel whose item sets `recent: true`. Supply them from your own history or `svNavRecorder`.

inputs.name: mobileLayout
inputs.description: What the mobile drawer does with a panel item: expand its links in place (`'accordion'`), or push in a page of its own with a Back button (`'stacked-pages'`).

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Every string the menu renders itself. Merged over the `megaMenuPro` labels (`provideSvLabels`).

outputs.name: linkSelect
outputs.description: Emitted when a panel link is activated.

outputs.name: itemSelect
outputs.description: Emitted when a top-level (link) item is activated.

outputs.name: featuredSelect
outputs.description: Emitted when the featured promo card is activated and this component cancelled the browser's navigation — same rule as the other two. It exists because the card had **no output at all**: a featured promo with no `href` swallowed the click and closed the menu, which is a dead control in the most prominent slot of the panel.

outputs.name: intentChange
outputs.description: The safe corridor while the pointer travels from a trigger to its open panel, on every move — and `null` when the approach ends. For drawing it; the menu needs nothing from the listener. Fires only under `hoverIntent="corridor"`.

components.name: Mention Input
components.description: Contenteditable input with @mention autocomplete — a cursor-anchored suggestion dropdown, keyboard navigation and styled mention chips. Supports single- or multi-line entry and multi-trigger mode (@ people, # topics, / commands).
whenToUse: Letting users reference people or entities inline (comments, chat, task notes).
You want @-style autocomplete that anchors to the caret.
For a standalone tag field (not inline in prose), use Tag Input.

examples.title: Character limit
examples.description: `maxLength` counts plain text with each mention chip atomic: typing stops at the limit, a paste is cut to fit, a mention that would not fit is not inserted (announced), a counter shows `count / max`, and the control reports `{ maxlength }` to a form.

examples.title: Multi-trigger — @ people, # topics, / commands (Pro)
examples.description: Pass a triggers array; each entry has its own char, suggestion set and optional chip colour. triggerSelected tells you which trigger fired.
examples.code:
<sv-mention
  [triggers]="[
    { char: '@', suggestions: people },
    { char: '#', suggestions: topics, chipClass: 'mention-chip ... bg-emerald-50 text-emerald-700' },
    { char: '/', suggestions: commands, chipClass: 'mention-chip ... bg-amber-50 text-amber-700' }
  ]"
  [multiLine]="true"
  (triggerSelected)="onPick($event)" />

customization: Provide `suggestions` (`MentionSuggestion[]`) and change the `triggerChar` (e.g. `@`, `#`, `/`).
For several inline autocompletes in one field, pass `triggers` (`MentionTrigger[]`) — each has its own `char`, `suggestions`, optional `chipClass` and `label`; the nearest trigger to the caret wins.
Toggle `multiLine` for a textarea-style field and cap results with `maxSuggestions`.
Listen to `mentionSelected` for the chosen entity, `triggerSelected` for the `{ trigger, suggestion }` pair, and `valueChange` for the raw text.
Bind the plain-text content with `[(value)]`, or use `[formControl]` / `[(ngModel)]` — the editor implements `ControlValueAccessor` and hydrates programmatic values when not focused.
Responsive: the suggestion popup is anchored to the caret and its width is capped to the viewport, so it stays fully on-screen on narrow devices.
`maxLength` (plain-text length, mention chips atomic) with a counter and a `{ maxlength }` form error; Signal Forms' `maxLength` metadata flows into it.
accessibility: The editor is `role="textbox"` with `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant` tracking the highlighted suggestion (ids are generated per instance, so multiple fields never collide).
Arrow keys move, Enter/Tab insert, Esc closes without losing the text; the suggestion popup is a `role="listbox"` of `role="option"` rows.
Inserted mentions render as styled chips kept in the text flow for screen readers.
variants: Token Integrity — an edited chip is not a mention of anybody

inputs.name: suggestions
inputs.description: List of mention candidates.

inputs.name: triggerChar
inputs.description: Character that triggers the dropdown (single-trigger mode).

inputs.name: triggers
inputs.description: Multi-trigger configuration (Pro). When non-empty, this takes precedence over `triggerChar`/`suggestions`: each entry defines a trigger character, its own suggestion set, and optional chip styling.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Placeholder text.

inputs.name: multiLine
inputs.description: Multi-line mode (expand with content).

inputs.name: maxSuggestions
inputs.description: Maximum items shown in the dropdown.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disabled state.

inputs.name: maxLength
inputs.description: The most characters the composer holds, counted on its PLAIN TEXT — a mention chip counts as the text it shows (`@Ada Lovelace`) and is never cut in half: a mention that would not fit is not inserted. Typing and pasting stop at the limit (a paste is cut to the room left), a counter shows `count / max`, and the control reports `{ maxlength }` to a form. `0` is no limit. Accepts Signal Forms' `maxLength` metadata.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Plain-text content. Two-way bindable with `[(value)]`.

inputs.name: serverSide
inputs.description: Let the server do the matching. The supplied `suggestions` are shown exactly as given.

inputs.name: debounceMs
inputs.description: Delay before `queryChange` fires, in ms. `0` emits immediately.

inputs.name: minChars
inputs.description: Characters after the trigger before a lookup is sent. `0` looks up as soon as the trigger is typed, which is what most directories want.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while suggestions are being fetched.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Failure loading suggestions, rendered inside the panel.

inputs.name: noResultsText
inputs.description: Copy when the lookup returned nothing.

inputs.name: errorMessage
inputs.description: Client-side validation message.

inputs.name: serverError
inputs.description: A rejection reported by the server about this value. Self-expiring.

outputs.name: mentionSelected
outputs.description: Emitted when a mention is selected.

outputs.name: triggerSelected
outputs.description: Emitted alongside `mentionSelected`, carrying the trigger character that produced the mention — useful in multi-trigger mode to tell `@`, `#` and `/` selections apart.

outputs.name: valueChange
outputs.description: Emitted when the text content changes (pairs with `value` for `[(value)]`).

outputs.name: queryChange
outputs.description: The text typed after the trigger changed — fetch matching people. Carries the trigger character too, because a component with several triggers (`@` for people, `#` for channels) queries different endpoints. Debounced by `debounceMs` and never emitted twice for the same pair.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The host should re-run the failed lookup.

outputs.name: mentionsChange
outputs.description: The mentions actually in the field, and the ones whose text has changed since they were inserted, so they do not say what they mean. An output rather than only a method, because this component's value carries no ids. `value` is plain text; the ids live only in the DOM. A host binding `[(value)]` and `(mentionSelected)` therefore keeps its recipient list BESIDE the document — and that list is wrong the moment somebody deletes a chip, pastes over one, or edits its text. There is no reconciling it from the value, so the component has to volunteer the truth. `sv-rich-text-editor` exposes methods instead and can afford to: its value is the markup, so the ids are in the thing the host already persists. Emitted only when the state CHANGES, not per keystroke. A mention field fires `input` on every character, and a host that re-runs a permission check each time would be doing it thousands of times per message.

components.name: Menubar
components.description: The application menu bar — File · Edit · View. One tab stop with a roving tabindex, Left/Right between menus that carries the open menu along, hover that switches only once something is open, and first-letter type-ahead. The panels are Dropdown Menu, so portalling, flipping and the in-panel keyboard model are shared rather than copied.
whenToUse: An application shell that needs File / Edit / View — an editor, an IDE-like tool, a design surface.
A dense toolbar where the same commands need keyboard access and a discoverable home.
For a single button that drops a list of actions, use Dropdown Menu. For right-click, use Context Menu.

examples.title: The menus
Checkbox items that keep the menu open
examples.code: { id: 'grid', label: 'Show grid', type: 'checkbox', checked: grid(), keepOpen: true }

examples.title: Opened from your own shortcut
examples.code:
<sv-menubar [menus]="MENUS" [(openMenuId)]="openMenu" />
// openMenu.set('file') from an Alt+F handler; set null to close everything.

examples.title: Letting the bar own its shortcuts
examples.code:
<!-- Off by default: an app with a menubar has almost certainly bound its
     own File/Edit keys already, and turning this on for it would fire
     both. With it on, every item's `keys` is registered through the
     shared registry - so a second component claiming the same binding is
     refused and reported rather than firing alongside it. -->
<sv-menubar
  [menus]="MENUS"
  [registerShortcuts]="true"
  (itemClick)="run($event.itemId)"
  (shortcutConflicts)="reportClashes($event)" />

customization: Feed `menus` with either flat `items` or `groups` per menu — the same item shape Dropdown Menu takes, including icons, shortcuts, badges, dividers, checkbox/radio types and `danger`.
`size` sets the bar's own density; `menuSize` is passed through to the panels.
Two-way bind `[(openMenuId)]` to open a menu from a shortcut of your own or close everything on navigation.
`disabled` on the bar or on a single menu; disabled menus are skipped by the arrow keys rather than focused and refused.

Shortcuts it actually owns: an item's `keys` (`'mod+n'`) renders itself for the running platform, and `[registerShortcuts]` binds it through the shared registry, where `[shortcutScope]` decides whether an overlay's binding outranks it. Duplicates are reported through `(shortcutConflicts)` whether or not anything is bound. Off by default, because an app with a menubar has usually bound these keys already.

Menus can cascade: any item with `children` opens a submenu (the Dropdown Menu contract). ArrowRight on such an item opens it and ArrowLeft inside it closes it — the bar only moves between menus when the open menu has nothing to do with the key. Submenu items with `keys` register and collide like any other item.

Narrow widths: the bar never pushes the page wider — it scrolls sideways inside itself (`max-w-full overflow-x-auto`; the panels are portalled, so nothing is clipped). `[collapseBelow]="640"` goes further: at or below that viewport width the bar becomes ONE "Menu" button whose menu lists every top-level menu as a submenu, each a bottom sheet with a Back row on a phone — everything opens by tap, nothing needs hover. Picks still arrive through `(itemClick)` with their `menuId`. `collapsed()` reports the state.
accessibility: A real `role="menubar"` owning `role="menuitem"` buttons — the Dropdown Menu trigger wrapper is made presentational so the ownership assistive technology walks is not broken by a layout div.

ONE tab stop for the whole bar via a roving tabindex; Left/Right move between menus (wrapping, skipping disabled), Home/End jump to the ends, Down/Enter/Space open, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
With a menu open, moving along the bar carries the open menu with it — and the keys the open panel owns (Up/Down, Enter, type-ahead over items) are left to the panel rather than handled twice.
The panel keeps DOM focus on the trigger and moves a virtual cursor, so `aria-activedescendant` and `aria-owns` are published from the trigger button — the element that actually has focus.

inputs.name: menus
inputs.description: The top-level menus, left to right.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Type scale and density.

inputs.name: menuSize
inputs.description: Panel size passed through to each `sv-dropdown-menu`.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name of the bar itself, e.g. `Editor`. A page with more than one menubar — an app bar plus a per-panel one — is two unnamed "menu bar"s in the landmark list without this.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Nothing in the bar opens.

inputs.name: customClass
inputs.description: Extra classes on the bar.

inputs.name: collapseBelow
inputs.description: Viewport width, in px, at or below which the bar collapses into ONE "Menu" button whose menu lists every top-level menu as a submenu. `null` keeps the bar at every width.

inputs.name: registerShortcuts
inputs.description: Register every item's `keys` so pressing one fires `(itemClick)`.

inputs.name: shortcutScope
inputs.description: Which band the item bindings register in.

inputs.name: openMenuId
inputs.description: The open menu, or `null`. Two-way bindable, so a host can open one from a shortcut of its own (`Alt+F`) or close everything on route change. ONE id rather than a flag per menu: two menus open at once is not a state this widget has, and modelling it as a set would make it representable.

outputs.name: itemClick
outputs.description: An item was chosen, with the menu it came from.

outputs.name: opened
outputs.description: The bar opened a menu (any means).

outputs.name: closed
outputs.description: Everything closed.

outputs.name: shortcutConflicts
outputs.description: Two or more items declare the same binding. Reported whether or not `registerShortcuts` is on: two File-menu items both claiming ⌘N is a bug in the menu definition either way, and only one of them could ever run from it.

outputs.name: openMenuIdChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `openMenuId` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(openMenuId)]`.

components.name: Message Actions
components.description: The row of actions under a chat message — copy that confirms only once the clipboard write lands, thumbs up / down and regenerate — with a slot for a timestamp or token count.
whenToUse: Under every finished assistant reply in a chat or an answer panel.
Anywhere a block of generated text needs a reliable copy button and a quality signal.
customization: `[actions]` picks the built-ins and their order: `copy`, `like`, `dislike`, `regenerate`.

Copy has three states: idle, copied (after the write resolves, for `copyResetMs`) and failed, which shows a hint naming the platform’s copy shortcut and emits `copyFailed`. `copy()` is public and resolves `true` only when the text actually reached the clipboard.
`[(feedback)]` is `'up' | 'down' | null`; the thumbs are mutually exclusive and a second press clears.
Text comes from the `ai` labels, or per instance through `[labels]` — `sv-ai-chat` passes its own copy-failure wording that way, because it also selects the message for the reader.
Free tier: uses only free icons.
accessibility: A named group of real buttons; each thumb reports `aria-pressed`.
The copy button’s accessible name changes with its state, and the failure hint is a polite status message.
Buttons are 24×24 with visible focus rings.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text the copy action writes to the clipboard.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.description: Which built-in actions to show, in this order.

inputs.name: feedback
inputs.description: The reader's verdict. Two-way: the thumbs are mutually exclusive, and pressing the active one again clears it.

inputs.name: copyResetMs
inputs.description: How long the "Copied" confirmation stays, in milliseconds.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: The group's accessible name; `null` uses the `messageActions` label.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Per-instance text, merged over the registry's `ai` labels.

outputs.name: copied
outputs.description: The text reached the clipboard. The payload is that text.

outputs.name: copyFailed
outputs.description: The clipboard refused. The button shows its failed state and the hint names the shortcut; offer the text another way if you can.

outputs.name: regenerate
outputs.description: The user asked for another answer.

outputs.name: feedbackChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `feedback` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(feedback)]`.

components.name: Modal
components.description: Dialog overlay with 6 semantic variants, 7 sizes, bottom-sheet & loading states, slot-based projection, focus trap and ESC/backdrop close.
whenToUse: Interrupting the flow for a focused task or message that needs attention.
Forms, details or confirmations that benefit from a focus trap.
Semantic confirmations (delete, warning, success) — reach for the matching `variant`.
For a yes/no decision specifically, the Confirm Dialog is more concise.
components.usage: Body content…

<!-- The backdrop is the whole screen around the panel and Escape is one

     Confirm Dialog use, so the three behave identically. A programmatic
     close() still closes: your own code has already decided. -->
<sv-modal
  [(isOpen)]="open"
  title="Edit profile"

  unsavedMessage="Your profile changes have not been saved."

Let Back close a dialog that is a destination
examples.code:
<!-- Off by default: Back closing a transient question eats a press the
     user meant for the page. Turn it on when the dialog is somewhere the
     user navigated TO — a details panel, a wizard step — and on a phone
     the system back gesture does the right thing too. The URL is
     untouched; this is a marked history entry, not a route. -->

examples.title: Veto a close for your own reasons
A loading state the user can get out of
examples.code:
<!-- Every close path is blocked while loading, which is right for a
     two-second save and wrong for a request that has hung. These say so
     explicitly: the overlay explains itself after 10s, offers a way out
     at 30s, and pendingDismissal="abort" lets the user leave — the modal
     emits (loadingCancelled) first, because the host started the work and
     is the only one who can stop it. -->
<sv-modal
  [(isOpen)]="open"
  [loading]="saving()"
  loadingText="Saving…"
  pendingDismissal="abort"
  [slowAfterMs]="10000"
  [stalledAfterMs]="30000"
  cancelLoadingLabel="Stop saving"
  (loadingCancelled)="abortSave()"
  title="Edit profile">
  <ng-container slot="body">…</ng-container>
</sv-modal>

customization: Six semantic variants with icon badge + accent bar; toggle the badge via `showIcon`.
Seven sizes (xs–2xl, full) and three positions (center, top, bottom-sheet).
Backdrop blur, ESC/backdrop close toggles, and a spinner `loading` state.
Rendered into `document.body` via a portal, so it always covers the full viewport and is never clipped by a parent `overflow` or `transform`.
Scroll-locking with scrollbar-width compensation; `customClass` on the panel.

Route and history integration: `[closeOnNavigation]` (default on) closes the dialog when the app navigates, once `provideSvOverlayRouteClose()` is wired; `[backCloses]` (default off) pushes a marked history entry so the browser Back button — and the phone back gesture — closes it, and pops that entry again on any other close so the history does not grow junk. Both compose with the unsaved-changes prompt: a navigation still asks before discarding.

A controlled-close policy: `[dirty]` raises one shared unsaved-changes prompt (over the panel, focused on Keep editing) instead of discarding; `[canClose]` is your own veto, consulted before anything else and silent by design; `(discarded)` and `(closeCancelled)` report which way it went, and the eventual `(dismissed)` carries the reason the USER acted on rather than `programmatic`. Shared with Drawer and Confirm Dialog — `createCloseGuard` in `@styloviz/core`.

A loading state with a way out: `pendingDismissal` (`block` · `abort`) decides whether the user may leave mid-flight, `[slowAfterMs]` / `[stalledAfterMs]` escalate the overlay from "taking longer than usual" to "seems to be stuck" (both timed from the moment `loading` goes true, not from when the modal opened), `cancelLoadingLabel` adds an in-overlay cancel once stuck, and `(loadingCancelled)` / `(loadingEscalated)` report it. Shared with the Spinner and Skeleton Loader — `createWaitEscalation` in `@styloviz/core`.

`[sheetOnNarrow]="true"` turns the dialog into a bottom sheet at 640px and below — full-width whatever `size` says, rounded at the top only, padded clear of the home indicator (`env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`; add `viewport-fit=cover` to your viewport meta) and lifted above the virtual keyboard so a field near the bottom is not covered by the keyboard it raised. The same `createSheetMode` contract Dropdown Menu, Drawer and Popover use. Off by default.
accessibility: `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal` live on the panel, labelled via `aria-labelledby` (title) and `aria-describedby` (subtitle).

Focus is trapped while open and moved to `initialFocus` (or the first focusable element), then restored to the trigger on close — or, if the trigger is gone by then, to the nearest part of the page that outlived it. An `initialFocus` selector that matches nothing falls back to the first focusable element and warns in dev mode: the fallback looks like success, so nothing else would tell you the selector was never used.
`opened`/`closed` fire for every transition; `dismissed` reports the reason (backdrop / escape / close-button / programmatic). `aria-busy` is set while loading.

An escalation message is announced from the loading overlay's own `role="status"` region, which already exists when the text appears — one wait, one voice. Escape is not consumed while dismissal is refused: the modal has nothing to do with the keystroke, so it does not take it.
variants: Open a Dialog and Await a Typed Result

inputs.name: closeOnNavigation
inputs.description: Does a navigation close this dialog? A modal that outlives its route floats over an unrelated page — a common overlay bug, and the mechanism is simple: a link inside the dialog, a redirect from a guard, a host that navigates on success — after which the panel is still up, still modal, still describing a page that has gone from underneath it. It only takes effect if the app asks: `provideSvOverlayRouteClose()` from `@styloviz/layout` is what tells the overlay layer a navigation happened, and an app that wires nothing sees no change. Set this false for a dialog that belongs to the shell rather than to the page.

inputs.name: backCloses
inputs.description: Does the browser Back button close this dialog? Back is the gesture users reach for to undo "I opened this", and on a phone it is the system gesture — a dialog that ignores it sends the user off the page instead, losing whatever they were doing. Off by default, and that is the opposite decision from the one above. Back closing a dialog is right when the dialog is a destination the user navigated TO — a details panel, a wizard step — and wrong when it is a transient question, where it eats a Back press meant for the page. Only the host knows which this is. The mechanism is a marked `history` entry, not a route: the URL is untouched and the host's own state is preserved. Giving a dialog its own URL is a routing decision, and leaves that to the host.

inputs.name: dirty
inputs.description: Is there unsaved work in this dialog? A form in a modal can be thrown away by a missed click. The backdrop is the whole screen around the panel, Escape is one key, and both discard everything the user typed with no warning and no undo. It is the single most-reported overlay complaint in any dashboard, and the reason "are you sure?" exists. Set this and the dialog asks instead of closing — once, in one place, from `createCloseGuard`, so Modal, Drawer and Confirm Dialog answer it identically. A prompt written four times behaves four ways. A programmatic `close()` still closes. The prompt is for accidental dismissal; your own code calling `close()` has already decided, and a component that second-guesses its own API is unusable. See `createCloseGuard`'s `alwaysAllow`.

inputs.name: canClose
inputs.description: The host's own veto, consulted before anything else. Return `false` to refuse a close; return nothing to have no opinion, so a guard that only cares about the backdrop needs one `if`. A veto is silent: it does NOT raise the unsaved-changes prompt, because the host refused for its own reasons and owns its own messaging. ```html <sv-modal [canClose]="notWhileUploading" /> ``` ```ts protected readonly notWhileUploading = (reason: ModalCloseReason) => reason === 'backdrop' ? !this.uploading(): undefined; ```

inputs.name: unsavedMessage

inputs.name: pendingDismissal
inputs.description: May the user dismiss the modal while `loading` is true? `'block'` (the default) blocks every close path — the × button, the backdrop, Escape — while `loading`. That is right for a two-second save and wrong for a request that has hung, where the modal would simply stop responding. `'abort'` lets the close through and emits `loadingCancelled` first, so the host can abort the work it started. The modal does not own the request — `loading` is an input — so the host does the aborting.

components.name: Notification Center
components.description: 6 variants: dropdown, drawer, inline, activity feed, compact and grouped — with mark-as-read, dismiss, search, tab filtering and inline actions.
whenToUse: Aggregating app notifications in a bell dropdown, drawer or inline feed.
You need unread counts, mark-as-read, search and tab filtering.
For one-off transient messages, use Toast instead.

Not sure this is the right outcome surface? Compare toast, banner, result, empty state, notification center and modal by severity, persistence and whether the user can correct it in the “Choosing a feedback pattern” guide under Guides.

examples.title: Optimistic writes that can fail
examples.code:
<!-- pendingIds dims the row and stops it responding while a write is in
     flight. itemErrors is its counterpart: the row whose write FAILED says
     so, in place, with a Try again — otherwise a dismissal that was rolled
     back looks like a click that never landed, and the user clicks again
     against an endpoint that is refusing. -->
<sv-notification-center
  variant="dropdown"
  [notifications]="notifications()"
  [pendingIds]="inFlight()"
  [itemErrors]="failures()"
  (dismiss)="onDismiss($event)"
  (retryItem)="onDismiss({ notification: $event })" />

examples.title: Merging a realtime stream
A "View all" link to a full notifications page
examples.code:
<!-- Off by default: a control that promises a page and does nothing
     is worse than no control, because the user concludes the page
     is broken rather than absent. Opt in once you have somewhere
     to send them. -->
<sv-notification-center
  variant="dropdown"
  [notifications]="notifications"
  [showViewAll]="true"
  (viewAll)="router.navigateByUrl('/notifications')" />

customization: Dropdown, drawer, inline or feed presentations.
Mark-as-read, dismiss and search.
Priority indicators and inline actions.
Opt-in "View all" footer via [showViewAll] + (viewAll).

A realtime identity contract: `version` (a monotonic revision — a lower one is stale), `seq` (position in the stream, used for ordering only when every row has one) and `dedupeKey` (two rows that are one event). Merge your stream with `svMergeRecords` from `@styloviz/core`, which answers identity, staleness, deduplication and order in one pass and reports what it did. The panel applies the same rules to whatever is in its input, so a duplicate id renders one row instead of throwing.

Per-row async state: `[pendingIds]` dims a row and stops it responding while its write is in flight, `[itemErrors]` (a record or a Map of id → message) renders that row's failure in place with a Try again wired to `(retryItem)`. Both work in all six variants.

Paging an unbounded feed: `(loadMore)` carries `cursor` — `{ id, timestamp }` of the last notification in hand — beside the `loaded` offset. Page with the cursor (`?before=<timestamp>&after_id=<id>`): an offset skips a row whenever a newer notification is inserted at the top between pages, a cursor does not. `null` before anything has loaded. Both tiers.
accessibility: Trigger exposes `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`; the panel closes on Escape and outside click.
Notification rows are keyboard-operable `role="button"` elements (Tab to reach, Enter/Space to open); inline actions and dismiss are labelled buttons.

A pending row carries `aria-busy`, so the dim is not the only signal that the click landed. A failed write is a `role="alert"` scoped to its row — something the user asked for did not happen, and it happened because of their click.

outputs.name: retryItem
