components.name: Number Input
components.description: Numeric input with increment/decrement controls, prefix/suffix, min/max clamping and decimal precision.
whenToUse: Entering a precise number with optional min/max bounds and stepping.
Quantities, prices, durations — anything where the exact value matters.
For approximate values across a range, a Slider is friendlier.

examples.title: Wheel policy
examples.description: A wheel over the focused field scrolls the page and leaves the value alone — Chromium otherwise steps a focused `type="number"` silently on every notch. `wheelSteps` restores the native behaviour.

examples.title: Required + reactive forms
examples.description: Implements ControlValueAccessor; required sets aria-required and errorMessage sets aria-invalid (linked via aria-describedby).

examples.title: Quantity stepper (PDP / cart)
examples.description: The quantity preset is a compact stepper with large +/– buttons for product pages and cart rows.

examples.title: A reason rendered by the parent
examples.description: When a composed control prints the explanation itself, point at it instead of passing it in as errorMessage — otherwise the message renders twice, or the field is a number with no stated reason it will not go higher.
examples.code: Only 3 left — your cart has 5

customization: Add `prefix`/`suffix` adornments, or use a `variant` preset (currency → $, percentage → %); set `size`.
Clamp with `min` / `max`, control decimal places with `decimals`, and the increment with `step`.
Add `label`, `hint`, `errorMessage`, `required`, `placeholder`, `name`; two-way bind `[(value)]` or use a reactive control; listen to `(changed)`.
Use `preset="quantity"` for a compact stepper with large +/– buttons, ideal for product pages and cart rows.
`wheelSteps` (default off): the mouse wheel over a focused field scrolls the page (nearest scrollable ancestor) instead of stepping the value.
accessibility: Built on the native `<input type="number">` — implicit spinbutton role with full keyboard support (Arrow Up/Down and direct typing); the +/– buttons have descriptive `aria-label`s.
A unique id is generated automatically so the `<label for>` association works without `inputId`; use `ariaLabel` when there is no visible label.
`prefix`/`suffix` are announced via `aria-valuetext` (e.g. "$12.00"); `hint` and `errorMessage` are linked with `aria-describedby`, and `errorMessage` sets `aria-invalid`.
The +/– buttons are named after the field (`label`, else `ariaLabel`), so several steppers on one page are told apart.

`ariaDescribedby` appends ids owned by a parent to the field's own description, and `invalid` marks the value wrong when the parent renders the reason. The border follows `aria-invalid` either way, so the visual and the announced state never disagree.
Implements ControlValueAccessor — works with `[(ngModel)]` and reactive forms; `formControl.disable()` disables the input and buttons.
variants: Clamp Timing — the field stops fighting the keyboard

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Current numeric value. Use `[(value)]` for two-way binding.

inputs.name: min
inputs.description: Minimum allowed value.

inputs.name: max
inputs.description: Maximum allowed value.

inputs.name: step
inputs.description: Step amount for increment/decrement.

inputs.name: decimals
inputs.description: Number of decimal places.

inputs.name: clampOn
inputs.description: When the typed value is forced into `[min, max]` and rounded to `decimals`. `'blur'` (the default) lets the field hold what was typed while it is being typed, and clamps and rounds it when focus leaves. Clamping every keystroke fights the person typing: with `min = 10`, typing `50` into a selected field would give `5` → `10` → `100`, and with `decimals = 0` the `.` of `1.5` would round away before the `5` arrives. The value can be out of range in between — see `outOfRange`, which is why the control says so. `'input'` clamps and rounds on every keystroke, for hosts that depend on the value never leaving range, even transiently.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Label text above the input.

inputs.name: hint
inputs.description: Hint text below the input (hidden when `errorMessage` is set).

inputs.name: errorMessage
inputs.description: Error message shown below the input; sets `aria-invalid` and red styling.

inputs.name: serverError
inputs.description: A validation failure reported by the **server** — the 422 that comes back after submit, not something the client could have known. It is a separate input from `errorMessage` because it has a different lifetime, not because it needs a second way to show a string. A server error is a statement about *the value that was submitted*: the moment the user edits the field it stops being true, and this input expires itself rather than sitting there telling someone their new email is already taken. `errorMessage` has no such expiry — it is the host's to clear. While live it outranks `errorMessage`: it is the more specific fact, and it is the one the user has not seen yet. Typed structurally rather than as `SvDataError` so this stays dependency free — an `SvDataError` satisfies it unchanged.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Placeholder text.

inputs.name: prefix
inputs.description: Text/symbol shown to the left of the value (e.g. '$').

inputs.name: suffix
inputs.description: Text/symbol shown to the right of the value (e.g. '%').

inputs.name: inputId
inputs.description: Explicit id for the input. Auto-generated when omitted.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: `aria-label` for the input when there is no visible `label`.

inputs.name: ariaDescribedby
inputs.description: Ids of description text rendered **outside** this component, appended to whatever `hint`/`errorMessage` already contribute. A composed control — a cart row that prints "Only 3 left" beside the title rather than under the stepper — otherwise has no way to associate the two. Passing the message in as `errorMessage` would render it twice; leaving it unassociated means a screen-reader user hears the quantity and none of the reason it is capped. Same rationale as `ariaLabel`: the visible thing lives in the parent, so the parent has to be able to point at it.

inputs.name: invalid
inputs.description: Mark the value invalid when the message explaining why is rendered by the parent (paired with `ariaDescribedby`). `errorMessage`/`serverError` already imply this; use it when the text is not ours to show.

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: `name` for native form submission.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Size variant.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Format preset. Provides default `prefix`/`suffix` when you don't set them: `percentage` → `'%'` suffix; `currency` → see `currency` below.

inputs.name: currency
inputs.description: ISO 4217 code — `'USD'`, `'EUR'`, `'JPY'`.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP-47 tag for the currency symbol's placement and the announced value.

inputs.name: preset
inputs.description: Layout preset. `quantity` renders a compact stepper with large +/– buttons, sized for comfortable tapping on product pages and cart rows.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disable the input and buttons.

inputs.name: readonly
inputs.description: Make the input read-only (buttons still disabled).

inputs.name: required
inputs.description: Mark the field as required (native `required` + `aria-required`).

inputs.name: autofocus
inputs.description: Autofocus the input on render.

inputs.name: wheelSteps
inputs.description: Let the mouse wheel step the value while the field has focus — the native `type="number"` behaviour. Off by default: a user scrolling the page with the pointer over a focused field changed the number without looking at it, and nothing announced it. Off, the wheel scrolls the page instead and the value stays put.

outputs.name: changed
outputs.description: Emits the new value after each change.

outputs.name: valueChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `value` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(value)]`.

components.name: Number Ticker
components.description: Animated count-up display with easing functions, IntersectionObserver start-on-view, prefix/suffix, thousands separator, decimal precision, auto-fit (scales down so large values never overflow) and reduced-motion support. Variants: `count`, `odometer` (rolling reels) and `scramble`; `format="currency"` formats through Intl.
whenToUse: Drawing attention to a metric with an animated count-up (stats, hero numbers, results).
Landing pages and dashboards where a headline figure should count up on first view.
For a value that changes many times a second, set `updatePolicy="snap"` or bind plain text.

examples.title: Locale grouping and compact notation
examples.code: {{ row.users | svTickerNumber: { notation: 'compact' } }}

examples.title: Auto-fit a large value
The same format in a table cell — no animation
examples.description: The ticker formats through svFormatTickerDisplay; the pipe is that function, for cells that must not animate.
examples.code: import { SvTickerNumberPipe } from '@styloviz-pro/layout'; {{ row.revenue | svTickerNumber: { format: 'currency', decimals: 2 } }}

examples.title: A live metric that updates every few hundred ms
examples.code:
<!-- retarget (default) counts from what is on screen and never past the
     end of an animation already running; snap skips animation entirely -->
<sv-number-ticker [value]="activeUsers()" updatePolicy="snap" announce="off" />

customization: Animate to `value` from `from` over a `duration` with a chosen `easing`.

Formatting is a separate pure API: `svFormatTickerDisplay(value, options)`, `svFormatTickerNumber` and the `svTickerNumber` pipe (`SvTickerNumberPipe`) take the same options as the component's inputs, and the component formats through them.

Updates: `updatePolicy` — `retarget` (default) animates from the displayed value and never beyond the end of an animation already in flight, so a burst of updates settles on the latest value on schedule; `snap` shows updates immediately; `restart` counts from `from` every time, which never settles under frequent updates.

Invalid numbers: `NaN`, `±Infinity` and `null` render `invalidPlaceholder` (default en dash) with no prefix or suffix, and are announced as `invalidLabel` (default "No value") — never "NaN" or a fake 0.

Measurement: automatic — auto-fit observes the parent through the core `svElementSize` primitive (one reading per frame, disconnected on destroy, nothing on the server) and re-fits whenever it resizes; where there is no `ResizeObserver` it falls back to viewport resizes. There is no manual measure call; a ticker inside a container that is hidden at init measures 0 and fits the moment the container is laid out.

Layout: not applicable — the ticker is inline content in normal flow; nothing is portalled, no scroll root is listened to (start-on-view uses an IntersectionObserver against the viewport), and no containing block or breakpoint matters. Auto-fit sizes against the parent's content box, so keep `min-w-0` on a grid or flex parent that must be able to shrink below the number.
`delay` applies to the first count; a new `value` arriving while it is still pending does not skip it — the pending start counts to the latest value when the delay elapses.
`value` accepts `null` but reads as a `number`: `null` is mapped to `NaN`, which renders the invalid placeholder.

Variant axes: `variant` (count, odometer, scramble) and `format` (plain, currency) are appearance; `startOnView`, `fit`, `updatePolicy` and `announce` are behavioural modes that combine with every variant.

Browser limits: without IntersectionObserver (SSR, very old engines) the count runs immediately; without requestAnimationFrame it snaps to the value; `format="currency"` depends on the runtime's Intl data and falls back to plain digits for an unknown currency or locale.
Pick a `variant`: `count` (default), `odometer` rolling reels, or `scramble`.
Format with `prefix`, `suffix`, `decimals` and `separator`, or set `format="currency"` with `currency` + `locale`.

Locale: the plain format follows `locale` (default: the kit locale, `provideSvLocale`) for grouping AND the decimal mark — `1,234.5` in en-US, `1.234,5` in de-DE, `12,34,567` in hi-IN — through `Intl.NumberFormat`, which also prints very large numbers as digits (not `1e+21`) and rounds half away from zero. `separator` is an override of the GROUP separator only (`''` turns grouping off); the decimal mark stays the locale's. An unknown locale falls back to `,` and `.`. 2.0 changed the default from `','`-whatever-the-locale — see the CHANGELOG migration. A locale whose digits are not 0–9 (`ar-EG`) prints its own digits; the odometer reels and the scramble animate 0–9 only, so those characters do not roll.

Compact notation: `notation="compact"` renders `1.2M`, `12.3K`, `1,2 Mio.` in the locale's words, for both formats (`$1.2M`); `decimals` becomes a maximum, and `0` means up to one. The pipe and `svFormatTickerNumber` take the same `notation`. Changing `locale`, `notation` or any other formatting input re-renders the settled figure in place — no recount.
Start on scroll into view with `startOnView` and a `delay`.
Auto-fit is on by default so big values never overflow — it sizes against the container content box (parent padding is subtracted), bound it with `minFontScale` or disable via `[fit]="false"`.
accessibility: Final value is real text in the `aria-label`, readable by assistive tech (uses the formatted value).

One announcement per value: the animating digits are `aria-hidden`, and the live region carries only the SETTLED value, updated when an animation lands — never per frame. `announce="off"` silences it while keeping the value readable.
Animation is skipped and the value snaps when reduced-motion is requested — including the odometer reels.
Emits `animationStart` and `animationComplete` around the count.
variants: Format Reference — prefix · suffix · decimals · separator

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the figure is being fetched.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Target value to animate to. `NaN`, `±Infinity` and `null` are not numbers and render `invalidPlaceholder` rather than `"NaN"` or a fake `0`. Accepts `null`, but READS as `number`: `null` is mapped to `NaN` (already the invalid state), so host code calling `ticker.value()` keeps a `number`.

inputs.name: invalidPlaceholder
inputs.description: Shown in place of a value that is not a finite number.

inputs.name: invalidLabel
inputs.description: Read to assistive tech in place of a value that is not a finite number.

inputs.name: announce
inputs.description: Whether the settled value is announced (`polite`) or not (`off`). The animating digits are never announced, whatever this says.

inputs.name: updatePolicy
inputs.description: What a new `value` does after the first one has been shown. `restart` RESTARTS FOREVER. A metric updated every 200 ms with a 1500 ms count restarts from `from` on every update and never displays a stable number. `retarget` (the default) animates from what is on screen and never beyond the end of an animation already running, so a burst of updates lands on the latest value on schedule; `snap` skips the animation.

inputs.name: from
inputs.description: Starting value.

inputs.name: duration
inputs.description: Animation duration in milliseconds.

inputs.name: easing
inputs.description: Easing function.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Visual style of the animation.

inputs.name: format
inputs.description: Number formatting mode.

inputs.name: currency
inputs.description: ISO 4217 currency code (used when `format='currency'`).

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP-47 locale for both formats — grouping, decimal mark, currency and compact words.

inputs.name: prefix
inputs.description: String prepended to the number (e.g. '$').

inputs.name: suffix
inputs.description: String appended to the number (e.g. '%', 'K').

inputs.name: decimals
inputs.description: Number of decimal places.

inputs.name: separator
inputs.description: Grouping separator for `format='plain'`, as an override. `null` (the default) takes grouping and the decimal mark from `locale`; a string replaces only the locale's group separator (`''` turns grouping off). Before 2.0 the default was `','`, whatever the locale.

inputs.name: notation
inputs.description: `standard` digits, or `compact` notation in the locale's words — `1.2M`, `1,2 Mio.`, `123.5万`. With `compact`, `decimals` is a maximum (`0` → up to one).

inputs.name: startOnView
inputs.description: Start animation only when element scrolls into view.

inputs.name: delay
inputs.description: Delay before the first animation starts (ms). A new `value` arriving while the delay is still pending does NOT skip it: the pending start simply counts to the latest value once the delay elapses (a non-number still shows the placeholder at once). Later updates follow `updatePolicy`; `restart` waits for the delay again.

inputs.name: fit
inputs.description: Auto-fit the digits to the available width so a large value never overflows its wrapper (or the viewport). Measures the widest value against the container's real content box — the parent's horizontal padding and border are subtracted from the budget — and scales the font down (keeping a small margin) only when it would otherwise clip.

inputs.name: minFontScale
inputs.description: Lower bound for auto-fit scaling (fraction of the base font size).

outputs.name: animationStart
outputs.description: Emitted when the count-up animation starts.

outputs.name: animationComplete
outputs.description: Emitted when the count-up animation completes.

components.name: Onboarding Checklist
components.description: A setup checklist for a new account or workspace: a progress ring and "3 of 5 done", a native checkbox and a link or button per step, optional steps that say they do not count toward completion, and a `completed` event when the last required step is done. The steps — and whether each is done — stay yours.
whenToUse: The first screens of a SaaS product, admin panel or store: the handful of things a new account must do before it is useful.
A "Get set up" card on a dashboard that goes away once setup is done or dismissed.
Anywhere progress is a short list of discrete tasks rather than a percentage — use `sv-progress-bar` for a single running job and `sv-stepper` for a linear form.

examples.title: Apply a toggle
examples.code:
<!-- The checklist never flips done itself: it emits, you update. -->
<sv-onboarding-checklist [steps]="steps()" (stepToggle)="mark($event)" />

mark({ step, done }: SvOnboardingStepToggle): void {
  this.steps.update((list) => list.map((s) => (s.id === step.id ? { ...s, done } : s)));
}

examples.title: Links, buttons and optional steps
examples.code:
<sv-onboarding-checklist
  [steps]="[
    { id: 'invite', title: 'Invite your team', href: '/settings/team', actionLabel: 'Invite' },
    { id: 'data', title: 'Connect a data source', actionLabel: 'Connect' },
    { id: 'theme', title: 'Pick a theme', optional: true }
  ]"
  (stepAction)="open($event.id)" />

customization: Two variants: `card` (bordered panel with a 64 px ring) and `inline` (no chrome, a 48 px ring) for a panel or sidebar that already frames it.
The ring is the kit's own `sv-progress-ring`, painted from the `primary-*` tokens, so a template that remaps primary recolours it.

Each step takes an `href` (rendered as a link; unsafe schemes such as `javascript:` are dropped) or just an `actionLabel` (rendered as a button that emits `stepAction`). The action hides once the step is done.
`headingLevel` (2–4) fits the title into your page outline; `title` and `description` replace the default heading.
Every string comes from the `overlays` labels (`onboarding*` keys) — `provideSvLabels(SV_OVERLAYS_LABELS_DE)` or the per-instance `labels` input.
Loading, error with retry and empty states from `@styloviz/core`, so it wires to a real endpoint like every data component.
accessibility: A `<section>` named by its heading; the steps are an ordered list.

Each step is a native `<input type="checkbox">` with a `<label>` and `aria-describedby` pointing at its description, so Space toggles it and the state is announced. Read-only steps read "done" or "not done yet" after the title.
A step's action is a real link or button, described by the step title, so "Start" is never announced without context.
The ring is a `role="progressbar"` whose value text is the same "3 of 5 done" shown beside it.
Completion is announced through a polite `role="status"` region. The collapse toggle carries `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the dismiss button has an accessible name.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: The steps, in order. Each one's `done` is yours: tick a box and the checklist emits `stepToggle`; it shows the change once you hand back steps with `done` updated. Rows with an empty or duplicate `id` are skipped.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the host is fetching the steps — shows a skeleton in place of the list.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: The fetch failed — shows the error with a Try again button that emits `retry`.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: The heading. Null uses the `onboardingTitle` label ("Get set up").

inputs.name: description
inputs.description: A line under the heading.

inputs.name: headingLevel
inputs.description: Heading level for the title — match the page outline.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Per-instance text, merged over the registry's `overlays` labels.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: `card` (bordered panel) or `inline` (no chrome, smaller ring).

inputs.name: checkable
inputs.description: Render a native checkbox per step so the user can tick it. `false` shows read-only state — for steps your app detects as done by itself.

inputs.name: dismissible
inputs.description: Show a dismiss button that closes the checklist and emits `dismissed`.

inputs.name: collapsible
inputs.description: Show a toggle that hides the steps and keeps the heading and progress.

inputs.name: collapsed
inputs.description: Whether the steps are hidden. Two-way: `[(collapsed)]`, so you can remember it.

inputs.name: open
inputs.description: Whether the checklist renders at all. Dismissing sets it `false`. Two-way: `[(open)]`, so a dismissal can be stored and restored.

outputs.name: stepToggle
outputs.description: The user ticked or unticked a step: the step and the state they asked for. Update `done` to apply it.

outputs.name: stepAction
outputs.description: The user activated a step's action — its link (which also navigates) or its button.

outputs.name: dismissed
outputs.description: The user dismissed the checklist.

outputs.name: completed
outputs.description: Every required step became done. Fires on the change, once — not on a checklist that arrives already complete, and not again until it is incomplete and completed again.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The host should re-run the failed fetch of the steps.

outputs.name: collapsedChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `collapsed` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(collapsed)]`.

outputs.name: openChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `open` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(open)]`.

components.name: Order Summary
components.description: Cart / checkout totals panel that renders the server quote verbatim and badges any locally-derived total as an estimate. Shipping / tax / discount rows, inclusive-tax mode, arbitrary extra lines, and content slots for a coupon field and checkout button. All arithmetic runs on integer minor units, so the visible rows always add up to the visible total.
whenToUse: The totals panel on cart, every checkout step and the order confirmation.
You have an authoritative total from a pricing or checkout API and want it rendered verbatim beside the rows that explain it.
You only have client-side figures and want them honestly labelled as an estimate.
You need to drop a coupon field or checkout button beside the totals.
components.usage:
<!-- [quote] is the total your pricing API returned; it is rendered verbatim.
     Omit it and the total is derived from the rows and badged "Estimate". -->
<sv-order-summary [subtotal]="129.97" [itemCount]="3" [shipping]="0" [tax]="10.4" [discount]="15" [quote]="quote()" />

examples.title: Server quote (authoritative)
examples.description: Rendered verbatim. A disagreement with the rows is shown, not hidden.

examples.title: Re-pricing in flight
examples.description: Marks the figure stale so nobody pays against a superseded total.

examples.title: Inclusive tax (VAT / GST)
examples.description: The subtotal already contains the tax, so the tax line is shown but not added.

examples.title: Pending shipping/tax
examples.description: Null values read "Calculated at checkout".

examples.title: Itemized adjustments, one line per label
examples.description: A `tax` line follows `taxMode` — added when exclusive, shown and marked "(included)" when the subtotal already contains it. Repeated labels are expected: itemizing per item or per shipment is what produces them.
examples.code:
readonly lines: readonly OrderSummaryLine[] = [
  { label: 'VAT · Germany 19%', amount: 15.97, kind: 'tax' },
  { label: 'VAT · shipping 7%',  amount: 0.59,  kind: 'tax' },
  { label: 'Gift wrap', amount: 4 },
  { label: 'Gift wrap', amount: 4 },
  { label: 'Carbon-neutral delivery', amount: 1.2, kind: 'muted' },
  { label: 'Newsletter voucher', amount: 8, kind: 'discount' },
];

examples.title: Acting on the gap between the two figures
examples.description: The panel always says how far apart they are and in which direction. `reconciliationDelta` is that number, signed and positive when the server charges more, so a host can hold the pay button rather than only show a notice.

customization: Discrete subtotal / shipping / tax / discount rows plus arbitrary extra lines, each with its own label, optional note and one of four kinds (`charge`, `discount`, `tax`, `muted`).

Free-shipping, pending, estimate, updating and reconciliation-notice labels are all configurable — including the two direction words the repriced notice reads with (`repricedHigherLabel` / `repricedLowerLabel`) and the still-calculating notice (`linesIncompleteLabel`).
Exclusive or inclusive tax mode, honoured by itemized `tax` lines as well as the built-in row.
Content slots: `[svSummaryTop]` and `[svSummaryFooter]`.
Any ISO currency + locale, with minor-unit support and the correct exponent per currency (JPY has none, KWD has three).
accessibility: Rendered as a definition list with a labelled region, and the heading id is per-instance so a cart drawer and a checkout panel on one page are never announced with each other's name.
Totals are tabular-nums text, not images.
The estimate / updating badges are text, not colour alone.
Reconciliation notices sit in a `role="status"` region so they reach a screen reader without a focus change — including the size and direction of any gap between the rows and the authoritative total.
An inclusive tax line carries its "(included)" marker as text on the label, so a row that is deliberately not added never reads as an arithmetic error.
Discount and free-shipping colours meet contrast in light and dark mode.

inputs.name: heading
inputs.description: Panel heading.

inputs.name: subtotal
inputs.description: Items subtotal.

inputs.name: itemCount
inputs.description: Number of items (shown next to the subtotal label).

inputs.name: shipping
inputs.description: Shipping cost. `null` shows the pending label; 0 shows the free label.

inputs.name: tax
inputs.description: Tax amount. `null` shows the pending label.

inputs.name: taxMode
inputs.description: Whether `tax` is added to the subtotal or already inside it. An `inclusive` tax is informational and is *not* added to the total.

inputs.name: discount
inputs.description: Discount as a positive number (subtracted from the total).

inputs.name: discountLabel
inputs.description: Label for the discount line.

inputs.name: lines
inputs.description: Extra lines (fees, gift wrap, credit, …) inserted before the total.

inputs.name: quote
inputs.description: The authoritative total from the server. When set, it is rendered verbatim and the panel's own arithmetic is used only to detect a divergence. See the note on the class.

inputs.name: quotePending
inputs.description: A fresh quote is in flight, so the figure on screen is already stale. Set this while re-pricing (an address change, a coupon being applied) so nobody confirms payment against a superseded total.

inputs.name: currency
inputs.description: ISO 4217 currency code.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP-47 locale for amounts.

inputs.name: minorUnits
inputs.description: Treat all amounts as minor units.

inputs.name: freeShippingLabel
inputs.description: Label used when shipping is 0.

inputs.name: pendingLabel
inputs.description: Text shown for a null shipping / tax value.

inputs.name: inclusiveTaxLabel
inputs.description: Marks the tax row when `taxMode` is 'inclusive'.

inputs.name: estimateLabel
inputs.description: Badge on the Total row when the figure is derived locally.

inputs.name: updatingLabel
inputs.description: Badge on the Total row while `quotePending`.

inputs.name: repricedLabel
inputs.default: 'This total was confirmed by the server and differs from the lines above.'
inputs.description: Notice when the server total differs from what the lines add up to.

components.name: Pagination
components.description: Smart page-window with ellipsis, a page-size selector, jump-to-page, a load-more variant, server-driven loading, 4 variants and 3 sizes.
whenToUse: Job: result-set position — renders buttons and emits `pageChange`; it owns no data and no URL (compare all seven in the “Choosing a navigation pattern” guide under Guides).
Splitting a large result set into navigable pages.
Tables and lists where loading everything at once is impractical.
For continuous feeds, infinite scroll (List View) can feel more fluid.

examples.title: Load more
examples.code:
<!-- the host appends each page; the button goes once all are shown -->
<sv-pagination variant="load-more" [totalItems]="total()" [pageSize]="20"
  [(currentPage)]="page" [loading]="loading()" (pageChange)="append($event)" />

examples.title: Server-driven
examples.code:
<!-- pageAction owns the load: busy, one request at a time, failure + retry -->
<sv-pagination [totalItems]="total()" [(currentPage)]="page"
  [pageAction]="loadPage" retryLabel="Try again" />

customization: Ellipsis page window.
Optional page-size selector.
Variants: `default`, `simple`, `compact` (the phone shape) and `load-more` (one button and a "Showing 40 of 95" count; the host appends each page); three sizes.
`jumpToPage` adds a "Go to page" box when the total is known; an entry past either end goes to the first or last page.
`pageAction` hands the load to the paginator (busy state, one request at a time, failure with `retryLabel`); `mode="cursor"` pages by keyset cursor.
accessibility: Controls are labelled buttons inside a labelled nav landmark (`ariaLabel`).
Current page exposed via aria-current.
The "Go to page" field has a visible label; after a jump, focus stays on the field or Go button you used.
Load more keeps focus on its button between pages and, once everything is shown and the button goes, on the navigation landmark rather than the top of the page.

inputs.name: totalItems
inputs.description: Total number of items across all pages, or `null` when the backend cannot report one. `null` hides the numbered pages and the count summary — see `mode`.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: `'offset'` for `?page=`-style APIs (numbered pages, needs a total), `'cursor'` for keyset APIs (Previous/Next and an ordinal, needs neither).

inputs.name: nextCursor
inputs.description: `mode="cursor"` only: the cursor the server returned for the page *after* the one on screen. `null` means this is the last page, so Next disables.

inputs.name: hasMore
inputs.description: Override "is there a page after this one?" — for an offset API that reports no total but does know whether more rows exist (`LIMIT n + 1`). `null` lets the component infer it from the total, or from `nextCursor` in cursor mode.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the host is loading a page. Every control disables, the nav is `aria-busy`, and a second press is refused rather than queued. Bind this when the host owns the fetch; bind `pageAction` instead and the component tracks it for you.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: A failed page load, normalized with `toSvDataError()`. Rendered as a `role="alert"` beside the controls. Unnecessary when `pageAction` is bound.

inputs.name: retryLabel
inputs.description: Label for the Try-again button. Non-null is what RENDERS it: an output cannot be asked whether anyone is listening, and a retry button that does nothing is worse than none.

inputs.name: pageAction
inputs.description: Hand the component the page load itself. It then owns the sequencing: a second press while one is in flight is refused (not queued, not superseded), and a response that arrives after a cancel is discarded. Pass `request.signal` to your transport.

inputs.name: pageSizeChangePolicy
inputs.description: Where the user lands when the page size changes.

inputs.name: pageSize
inputs.description: Number of items per page. Use `[(pageSize)]` for two-way binding.

inputs.name: currentPage
inputs.description: 1-based current page index. Use `[(currentPage)]` for two-way binding.

inputs.name: pageSizeOptions
inputs.description: Options shown in the page-size `<select>`. Empty array hides the selector entirely.

inputs.name: urlKey
inputs.description: Put the page number in the URL under this key, so a page can be shared, refreshed and reached with the back button. Needs `provideSvNavLocation()` at the app root; give a second paginator on the same page a different key.

inputs.name: surfaceId
inputs.description: Names this paginator in the shared navigation-analytics stream, when a page has more than one. Ignored unless `provideSvNavTelemetry()` is wired up.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Visual variant. `load-more` is one button that asks for the next page — the host appends it to what is already shown — and a "Showing 40 of 95" count; it disappears once there is nothing more.

inputs.name: jumpToPage
inputs.description: A "Go to page" box beside the page buttons. Needs a known total; an entry past either end goes to the first or the last page.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Control size.

inputs.name: showSummary
inputs.description: Show total-item count summary (e.g. "Showing 1–10 of 234").

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible label for the navigation landmark.

inputs.name: customClass
inputs.description: Additional CSS classes on the root wrapper.

inputs.name: scrollToTop
inputs.description: Scroll back to the top of the results after a page change. Leave it off when the paginator is inside a card or a scroll container of its own.

inputs.name: scrollTarget
inputs.description: With `scrollToTop`, the element to bring into view — usually the top of the results list. `null` scrolls the paginator itself into view.

outputs.name: pageChange
outputs.description: Emitted when the user navigates to a different page.

outputs.name: unresolved
outputs.description: Emitted when `currentPage` names a page that does not exist. Carries what was asked for, what is shown instead, why, and whether `currentPage` was corrected.

outputs.name: cursorChange
outputs.description: `mode="cursor"` only: the cursor of the page now on screen (`null` for the first page). Fetch with this; hand the response's next cursor back through `[nextCursor]`.

outputs.name: retryRequested
outputs.description: The Try-again button was pressed and no `pageAction` is bound, so the host owns the retry. Only fires when `retryLabel` is set.

outputs.name: loadFailed
outputs.description: A `pageAction` rejected. Already normalized; also readable as `activeError()`.

outputs.name: pageSizeChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `pageSize` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(pageSize)]`.

outputs.name: currentPageChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `currentPage` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(currentPage)]`.

components.name: Password Strength
components.description: A dependency-free password guidance meter that pairs alongside any text input — a segmented bar, a strength band, and up to three suggestions. Length carries three of the four points and character variety adds the fourth, so a passphrase outranks a short password stuffed with symbols. It advises and never blocks: a heuristic run in the browser cannot measure how guessable a password is, so the only real evidence — a breach lookup — comes in as an input the host owns.
whenToUse: Sign-up, invite-acceptance and password-change forms where you want to explain what would make a password harder to guess.
Anywhere you want live client-side advice without shipping a large dictionary-backed scoring library.
To surface a breach-list result you already have — pass it in as `breach` and let the component word it, including the outage case.
Not a security boundary and not a gate. Enforce your policy in the field validator and on the server; this component explains.

examples.title: Your own policy minimum
examples.code:
<!-- Length is counted from here; variety only pays out once it is met. -->
<sv-password-strength [value]="password()" [minLength]="14" />

examples.title: A breach result the host looked up
examples.code:
<!-- breach is an input, never a request from the component. Check on blur or
     on submit — never per keystroke, which sends every prefix of someone's
     password to a third party. Map both a non-OK response and a thrown error
     onto 'unavailable': an outage is not a clean bill of health. -->
<sv-password-strength
  [value]="password()"
  [breach]="breach()"
  (guidanceChange)="guidance.set($event)" />

customization: Two densities: `md` (default) and `sm`.
`showSuggestions` toggles the suggestion list independently of the bar and band label.
`announceDelay` (default 700ms) is the quiet period before a band change is announced; every keystroke restarts it.

The headless `evaluatePassword(password, options, labels)` function and the `PASSWORD_STRENGTH_LABELS` map are exported separately from `@styloviz/password-strength` for custom UI or server-side reuse of the same heuristic — pass `SV_PASSWORD_STRENGTH_LABELS` for the English guidance, or your translated labels.
accessibility: The visible band label is plain text, deliberately not a live region — as `role="status"` it would re-announce on every keystroke and interrupt screen-reader users mid-word.
A separate `sr-only` `aria-live="polite"` region carries the same words, and speaks only when the band actually changes and only after typing has paused for `announceDelay`.
The segmented bar is `aria-hidden` — the band label carries the same information in words, so the bar never needs its own name.
A breach notice is polite text, never an alert, and an in-flight check is marked `aria-busy` rather than reporting an answer it does not have.
Suggestions render as a real list (`<ul>`/`<li>`), readable by assistive tech in document order.
variants: A Breach Check the Component Does Not Make
Announcements That Wait for a Pause

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The password to advise on — bind it to the same signal driving your text input.

inputs.name: minLength
inputs.description: Your own minimum length, which the advice is measured against. Defaults to 12 rather than 8: length is the lever that actually matters, and a component that calls eight characters "enough" is teaching the wrong thing.

inputs.name: breach
inputs.description: What your breach check knows. An input, never a network call from here — the component has no business choosing your provider, sending a hash of a password to a third party, or firing a request per keystroke. `unavailable` exists so an outage can be reported as an outage. Whatever the status, nothing here blocks anything.

inputs.name: showSuggestions
inputs.description: Show the improvement-suggestion list below the meter.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Density preset.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Accessible group label; it also opens the announcement.

inputs.name: announceDelay
inputs.description: Quiet period before an announcement, in milliseconds. Announcements wait for typing to stop and fire only when the band changed, so a screen-reader user is not interrupted mid-word. Set 0 in tests.

outputs.name: guidanceChange
outputs.description: The guidance changed. It emits advice, not a score to threshold on.

components.name: Permission Matrix
components.description: Roles × capabilities, each cell Allow, Deny or Inherit. A role can extend another, and a grant on a capability group covers what is inside it, so an Inherit cell shows the value it ends up with and where from ("via Viewer", "via Billing") — dashed rather than solid, and said in words. Group rows roll up All / None / "2 of 4" through the kit's tri-state ancestry and toggle everything inside them, never a locked cell; locks on a role, a capability or one cell carry their reason. It is a WAI-ARIA treegrid (a grid when no capability nests) with one tab stop, a sticky header row and first column in a named scroll region, row and column bulk actions, search, and a draft: changed cells are marked, a summary lists each change with Revert, and Save / Discard hand the decision to the host, which owns persistence.
whenToUse: A roles & permissions settings page: which role may do what, with roles that build on each other.
Reviewing access before an audit, read-only, with the reason every locked cell is locked.
Use the Tree View checkbox variant for one set of choices, and Data Table for a list of records with per-row actions.

examples.title: Roles that extend roles
examples.description: An Inherit cell takes, in order: a grant on an enclosing group on the same role, then the role it `inherits`, all the way up, then `defaultEffect` (deny). A cycle stops at the first repeat.

examples.title: Saving the draft
examples.description: `save` carries the `changes` (role, capability, before → after, the effect each way) and the `grants` they produce. Persist either, then pass the saved grants back: the draft clears itself. A refused save keeps it — show the reason with `saveError`.

examples.title: Locks with reasons
examples.description: A role lock covers its column, a capability lock (on the row or in `locks`) covers the row and everything inside it, and a lock naming both covers one cell. `readonly` locks everything.
examples.code:
<sv-permission-matrix [roles]="roles" [capabilities]="capabilities" [grants]="grants"
  [locks]="[{ role: 'guest', capability: 'billing', reason: 'Guests never see billing' }]" />

examples.title: The rules without the component
examples.description: The resolver, the group roll-up and the change list are exported — for a server that enforces the same rules, a test, or a digest e-mail.

customization: Values: `allow` / `deny` in `grants`, absent = inherit; `defaultEffect` decides what an unset chain comes to.

Colours: allow paints `accent`, deny `danger`, mixed groups and unsaved cells `warning` — always with a shape (check, ban, minus, dashed outline, pencil) and a word, so the theme can remap them freely.

`maxHeight` sets where the grid starts to scroll under its sticky header row (`'none'` grows with the rows); the first column sticks on horizontal scroll. Logical properties throughout, so it mirrors in RTL.
`showSearch` hides the search box and the "Changed only" filter; `headingLevel` fits the page outline.
Every string comes from the `displayPro` labels (`perm*` keys) in 12 language packs, or the per-instance `labels` input.
`svResolvePermission`, `svResolvePermissionTable`, `svPermissionGroupStates`, `svPermissionGroupToggle`, `svPermissionChanges` and `svPermissionSearch` are exported.
accessibility: A WAI-ARIA grid built on the kit's own primitives (`@angular/aria` is not a dependency in 2.0, as with the import wizard): `role="treegrid"` when capabilities nest — group rows carry `aria-level` and `aria-expanded`, which ARIA allows only on treegrid rows — and `role="grid"` when the list is flat, with `aria-rowcount` / `aria-colcount`, a `columnheader` per role and a `rowheader` per capability, so every cell is announced with both. One tab stop; arrows, Home / End, Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End and PageUp / PageDown (through the shared `svCollectionTarget`) move it, mirrored in RTL.

Space or Enter cycles a cell (Inherit → Allow → Deny); A, D and I set it and Delete resets it. On a group row Space allows or denies everything reachable inside it; on a row header it expands or collapses the group (`aria-expanded` on the row). The keys are described to the grid with `aria-describedby`.

Each cell says what it is in words — "Editor, View projects: allowed. Inherited from Viewer." — and the strip under the grid repeats it for the active cell, visibly. Inherited cells are dashed and carry "via …" text; locked cells are `aria-readonly` with a lock glyph and their reason; unsaved cells have a pencil. Never colour alone.

The grid scrolls inside a named, focusable region; sticky headers are marked `data-sv-sticky` and the region uses `svRevealFocus`, so a focused cell is never hidden under them (WCAG 2.4.11). Targets are at least 32px tall.

Bulk actions are buttons whose names say exactly what they do ("Allow Delete projects for every role"); a bulk change is announced in a polite status. A failed save is a `role="alert"`. Loading, error and both empties use the kit's shells.
Prints the whole grid without its controls: the scroll region grows, the sticky headers become static, and the cells keep their words.
variants: A Refused Save — The Draft Survives

inputs.name: capabilities
inputs.description: The rows: capabilities, grouped by nesting `children`. Rows without a `label` are skipped.

inputs.name: roles
inputs.description: The columns, in order. A role may `inherits` another by id.

inputs.name: grants
inputs.description: The saved grants, `grants[roleId][capabilityId]` = `'allow'` | `'deny'`; a missing cell inherits. A grant on a group id applies to every capability inside it that inherits. Edits are kept as a draft on top of this until the host saves and passes the new value back.

inputs.name: itemKey
inputs.description: Identity of a capability, a property name or a function — the key used in `grants`.

inputs.name: locks
inputs.description: Read-only rules: a role, a capability (with everything inside it), or one cell, each with its reason.

inputs.name: readonly
inputs.description: Make every cell read-only — e.g. for a viewer without the right to change roles.

inputs.name: defaultEffect
inputs.description: What a cell comes to when nothing in its chain sets it.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the first request is in flight — keep it false on a background refresh.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: The load failed. A string or an `SvDataError`; a non-retryable error hides the retry button.

inputs.name: filtered
inputs.description: Something outside this component narrowed `capabilities`, so an empty matrix says "No matching capabilities".

inputs.name: saving
inputs.description: The host is persisting a `save`: the buttons wait and cells stay put.

inputs.name: saveError
inputs.description: The last save failed — shown as an alert above the changes, which stay so the user can try again.

inputs.name: query
inputs.description: The capability search text. Two-way bindable, so a host can restore it.

inputs.name: collapsedIds
inputs.description: Keys of the collapsed groups. Two-way bindable. A search shows every match regardless.

inputs.name: heading
inputs.description: The title. `''` uses the "Permissions" label.

inputs.name: headingLevel
inputs.description: Heading level of the title — match your page outline.

inputs.name: maxHeight
inputs.description: Tallest the grid grows before it scrolls under its sticky header row (any CSS length; `'none'` to grow with the rows).

inputs.name: showSearch
inputs.description: Show the search box and the "changed only" filter.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP-47 locale for counts and plurals.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Per-instance text, merged over the registry's `displayPro` labels.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The error state's retry button was pressed — re-run the request.

outputs.name: save
outputs.description: Save was pressed. Persist `changes` (or `grants`), then pass the saved grants back in.

outputs.name: discard
outputs.description: Discard was pressed: the draft is gone and the saved grants show again.

outputs.name: draftChange
outputs.description: The draft changed — every unsaved edit, e.g. for a "leave without saving?" guard.

outputs.name: queryChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `query` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(query)]`.

outputs.name: collapsedIdsChange

components.name: Phone Input
components.description: A phone number field with a country selector (local flag assets, no remote images) that masks the NATIONAL number against a per-country numbering plan — the country code stays in the picker, where it is already shown. The bundled plans are a best effort rather than an authority: numbering plans change more often than a release cycle, so the length check is a hint and `plans` lets a host supply its own.
whenToUse: Sign-up, checkout and profile forms that collect a phone number and benefit from an explicit country + matching mask.
International products where a plain `tel` input leaves users guessing at the expected format.
Domestic-only forms — `countries` set to one entry hides the picker (no chevron, just a static flag and dial code) while keeping the country-specific mask.

examples.title: Numbering plans change; a bundled table does not
examples.description: The mask covers the national number only, from a per-country plan — the picker already shows the dial code, so a UK, German or Japanese number gets its own length and grouping rather than a US shape with a plus in front. The bundled plans are a best effort: pass `plans` to replace them with data you keep current (generated from libphonenumber, fetched, whatever), and the component stops pretending to own knowledge it cannot maintain.
examples.code:
<sv-phone-input [(value)]="phone" [(country)]="country" [plans]="myPlans()" />

// PhoneCountry: { code, name, dialCode, nationalDigits, groups?, nationalMask? }
// nationalDigits is a number or [min, max]; groups is cosmetic.

examples.title: A length hint, not a validity claim
examples.description: When the digits fall outside the plan, the field says what it expected — "United Kingdom numbers are usually 9–10 digits; this has 6" — and leaves the judgement alone. That is deliberate: the plan may be out of date, which is the premise of the whole design, so a number the table calls short may be perfectly dialable. The one hard rule is E.164's ceiling of 15 digits including the country code, because that is the format's own definition and cannot go stale. For real validation, use a library that ships its own updates.

customization: Wraps `@styloviz/forms`' `sv-input-mask`, so `size` (sm · md · lg), `disabled`, `error`, `hint`, `placeholder` (empty shows the plan's own shape), `required`, `name` and `variant` (`default` · `filled` · `ghost`) all pass through unchanged.
`(rawChanged)` reports the raw, unformatted digits, next to `(e164Changed)` for the stored form.
`countries` accepts an array of ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes to narrow the picker; omit it for the full bundled set.
Switching country re-groups the digits and updates the dial code shown in the picker, keeping the typed number — the country code was never among the digits.

`plans` replaces the bundled numbering data outright; each entry carries `nationalDigits` (a number or `[min, max]`), an optional cosmetic `groups`, and an optional `nationalMask` for punctuation a group list cannot express.
`svNationalMask()`, `svLengthHint()`, `svGroupNational()` and `SV_E164_MAX_DIGITS` are exported for building the same checks elsewhere.
`showExtension` adds a separate digits-only extension field, two-way bound through `[(extension)]`. It is kept OUT of `e164Changed` — E.164 has no extension — so store it in its own column.

A leading country code is only stripped when the value says it is there — it opens with `+` or `00`, or has more digits than the plan allows — so an Indian mobile such as 91987 65432 keeps its leading 91.
accessibility: The number field asks for the phone keypad (`inputmode="tel"`) and national-number autofill (`autocomplete="tel-national"`, since the country code is the picker's), and is `dir="ltr"` so the digits and separators stay in reading order on a right-to-left page. A pasted number with spaces, dashes or brackets is reshaped to the plan.
With `label` cleared, the field's accessible name falls back to the label pack's "Phone number", translated like every other string.

The country picker is a labelled button (`aria-haspopup="listbox"`) opening a keyboard-navigable listbox — arrow keys move, Enter selects, Escape closes, and typing a letter jumps to the first country with that name (repeat it to cycle).
Each flag is decorative (`aria-hidden`); the accessible name for each option is the country name, not the flag.
The underlying `sv-input-mask` keeps its own label/error association, so the field remains a single accessible text input.
variants: International preset with a starting country

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Formatted phone value (two-way), forwarded straight from `sv-input-mask`.

inputs.name: country
inputs.description: Selected country, by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (two-way).

inputs.name: countries
inputs.description: Restrict the picker to a subset of the bundled countries. `null`/empty = show all.

inputs.name: plans
inputs.description: Replace the bundled numbering data outright. The answer to the part a bigger table cannot fix. Numbering plans change more often than a release cycle — new mobile prefixes, new area codes, whole plans renumbered — so a table compiled into a component is stale the day it ships. The bundled list is a best effort for eight countries; a host that needs the other two hundred, or needs today's data, passes its own in (generated from libphonenumber, fetched, whatever it keeps current) and the component stops pretending to own knowledge it cannot maintain.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Field size, forwarded to `sv-input-mask`.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disable the whole control.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Field label.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Error message, forwarded to `sv-input-mask`.

inputs.name: hint
inputs.description: Helper text under the control, linked to it with `aria-describedby`.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Placeholder for the number field. Empty shows the plan's own shape.

inputs.name: required
inputs.description: Mark the number required.

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: The `name` the number submits under in a native form.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Field style, forwarded to `sv-input-mask`.

inputs.name: extension
inputs.description: The extension, kept in its own field and OUT of the number. An extension is not part of a phone number. E.164 has no room for one — it is a country code plus a subscriber number and nothing else — so an extension typed into the main field corrupts the value that gets dialled and stored. Users type them anyway, because there is nowhere else to put them, which is exactly why the field has to exist.

inputs.name: showExtension

components.name: Pie Chart
components.description: 5 variants: the default pie, plus four in Pro — donut (`variant="donut"`), variable radius, custom legend template and smart labels. Optional largest-first ordering and long-tail grouping into a single Other slice. Pure SVG with entrance animations and hover effects.
whenToUse: Showing simple proportions of a single total with few segments.
You want smart labels with connector lines.
When comparison precision matters, prefer a Bar Chart.
customization: Fixed or variable-radius slices. The radius is EMPHASIS ONLY — the angle carries the value — and the chart says so under the plot whenever a radius is actually varied, with the area cost named: a sector's area grows with the square of its radius, so a slice pulled in to 0.7 covers about half the area its share would occupy at full radius.

`sliceOrder`: keep the host's order (default) or sort largest first, which is the arrangement a pie is easiest to read in — the eye compares neighbouring arcs rather than arcs on opposite sides of the circle.

`groupBelow` and `maxSlices` fold the unreadable tail into one `Other` slice and disclose how many and what share. Off by default, because folding a host's categories is a decision about their data; a single small slice is never folded, since an `Other` of one is that slice with its name taken away.
Smart auto-positioned labels with connectors.
Custom legend templates.
Handle `sliceSelect` (arc or legend click) for selection.

`valuePolicy` decides what happens to a slice this chart cannot plot — a negative, `NaN` or `Infinity`. A pie divides by the sum of its values, so an unplottable one is not merely undrawable: left in the denominator it changes the angle of every OTHER slice, which is why there is no "leave it alone" option. `omit` (default) drops it and says the percentages are of the remainder; `reject` refuses the dataset. `clamp` is not offered: a clamped slice is a 0° arc, which leaves nothing to mark, so a request for it falls back to `omit` with a dev warning. All four pie treatments take it.
accessibility: The SVG is a `role="group"` with a generated label listing each segment and its share (override via `ariaLabel`) — `group`, not `img`, so that focusable slices are not pruned out of the accessibility tree with the rest of an `img`'s subtree.

Arc angle is share and the raw value is nowhere else on the page, so `sv-data-summary-table` publishes segment, value and percentage — on all four pie treatments (default, smart labels, radius, legend template). No overview line: the generated name has already read every label with its share, so a summary sentence there is that sentence again.
Slice labels and values are real text; the hover state has a non-color cue.

Whatever `valuePolicy` does to the data is stated in the rendered output, under the plot and under the empty state — how many slices were dropped, their real values, and that the shares are of what remains. A `console.warn` is not a disclosure: the person reading the dashboard never sees it.
A pie whose every value is zero shows the empty state rather than a blank circle, and the sentence beneath distinguishes "the data arrived and was all zero" from "the fetch returned nothing".

Grouping is disclosed in the rendered output — how many slices were folded, which ones, and what share they came to — and the summary table lists each folded slice in its own row under `Other`, marked `(in Other)`, so the aggregate never hides the detail from a reader using the table. `Other` is drawn in a neutral slate, not the colour of the first slice it folded, and on the radius pie at the value-weighted radius of its members rather than full emphasis.
variants: What the Radius Does Not Mean

components.name: Pin Map
components.description: Points of interest on a projected map, over an optional base layer of shapes. Markers that would overlap merge into one pin that states its own count, so the map never shows fewer things than it has. Shares the choropleth's projections and fitting. Pure SVG.
whenToUse: WHAT and WHERE — the listings, stores, incidents or sites themselves.
A companion map beside a result list, with hover and selection synced both ways.
For one number per administrative region, use the Choropleth Map: colour per shape answers "how much", not "which one".

examples.title: Planar coordinates (a floor plan, a fictional city)
Price labels and a selected pin
Dots instead of labels on a dense map
Theme the pins (SVG fill cannot read a CSS token)

customization: Four projections, including identity for pre-projected or invented coordinates.
Labelled price bubbles or plain dots, with a per-tone colour palette.
Optional base shapes with haloed labels, drawn behind the pins and out of the tab order.
Cluster radius, or 0 to disable merging entirely.
accessibility: The SVG is a `role="group"` whose generated summary states the point count and says outright when pins were merged because they overlap.

A pin's position IS the datum, and position is the one thing that does not survive into text — so `sv-data-summary-table` publishes one row per MARKER, not per pin, with its label, detail, status and which merged pin it sits inside. A merged pin draws one thing where there are five; the table is where the other four are.

One roving tab stop for the whole map: Tab enters and leaves, arrow keys and Home/End move between pins in reading order, Enter/Space activates. Each pin carries an aria-label; a merged pin names its count and every member it stands for.
The selected pin exposes `aria-pressed`.
variants: Figures the Map Is Less Sure About
Pin Map — Sites on a World Base Layer
Pin Map — Clustering On and Off
Pin Map — Tones, Highlights and a Custom Palette
Pin Map — Loading, Error, Empty and Filtered-Empty

components.name: Pivot Table
components.description: Cross-tab summarization with a field configurator reachable by drag OR by keyboard — dimensions, six aggregators, expand/collapse subtotals, sort-by-measure, top-N filter, a cardinality guard, Excel/PDF export that matches the grid cell for cell, and server-side aggregation.
whenToUse: Summarizing a flat dataset by one or more dimensions, with grand totals and subtotals.
You want the end user to reconfigure what's being summarized (drag fields, not a form).
For row grouping without cross-tab columns or aggregators, the Data Table's grouping is lighter weight.

examples.title: Nested rows, sorted, top-N, with export
Guarding a high-cardinality field
examples.code:
<sv-pivot-table
  [fields]="fields"
  [data]="orders"
  [(config)]="config"
  [maxAxisGroups]="500" />

// A pivot's cost is per GROUP, not per row: drop `orderId` into Rows and you
// have asked for one <tr> per record. Past the limit the grid is replaced by a
// notice naming the widest field, with the configurator still on screen and a
// "Render it anyway" escape hatch. Set 0 to switch the guard off.

examples.title: The headless engine, outside Angular

customization: Six aggregators (sum, average, count, min, max, distinct count) and five number formats (general, integer, decimal, currency, percent). Every subtotal is the aggregator applied to that group's own source rows, so an average is a true average and a distinct count is a true distinct count — never a roll-up of the numbers on the rows beneath.
Sort any row level by a measure, ascending or descending.
Top-N filters the outermost row groups by a measure's total.

Excel/PDF export serializes exactly what's on screen — collapsed groups stay collapsed, the label column and Grand Total row are always present because the grid always draws them, and each measure's format carries across. XLSX keeps true numeric cells (with the format as a real Excel number format, so host formulas still work) while PDF takes the formatted strings, because a picture of the grid that reads `0.42` where the screen reads `42.0%` is the wrong picture.

`maxAxisGroups` (default 1000) caps how many groups either axis may render. Past it the grid is replaced by a notice naming the axis, its group count and the widest field responsible, with a "Render it anyway" waiver that is re-armed as soon as the axes change again. `0` switches the guard off; `serverSide` skips it, since the host is already deciding what to aggregate.
accessibility: The grid IS a `<table>`, so it gets no second off-screen copy — a companion summary here would read every figure twice. What it gets instead is its own semantics: an `sr-only` `<caption>` naming the fields in play rather than counting them, `scope="col"`/`scope="row"` on both header axes, and a Grand Total row that is a row header, not a stray cell.
The row hierarchy is in the accessible name, not the indent: each row header carries its branch, so "West" and "West → Seattle" announce differently.
The scroll container is a labelled `role="region"` with `tabindex="0"`. A scrollable box is a keyboard tab stop whether or not you name it, and an unnamed stop announces as nothing at all.
Expand/collapse buttons expose `aria-expanded` and a computed label ("Expand West" / "Collapse West").

Drag is one path, not the path. Native HTML5 drag is reachable by pointer only — not keyboard, not switch access, not voice control — so every field carries a zone menu naming where it sits (Unused / Rows / Columns / Values) and every placed field carries move buttons for its position. Order is not decoration here: `rows` order IS the nesting order, so a configurator without reorder could only express the arrangement the fields happened to be dropped in. Focus follows the field across the re-render, because a zone change destroys the control that triggered it.

Every value cell carries a `title` naming the measure, the row path and the column it came from, and marks a subtotal as one — the sighted answer to "is this a subtotal, and of what", which a grid of bare numbers cannot give. It is deliberately not an `aria-label`: on a `<td>` that REPLACES the cell's own content, and the `scope` headers already carry the association.

Loading, error and empty states follow the kit-wide async contract (`data-sv-state`). A pivot blocked by `maxAxisGroups` is not one of them — it has too much data, not none, so it gets a `role="status"` notice that keeps the configurator on screen rather than an empty shell that would hide the only way out.
variants: Nested groups, sorted, top-N, with export

inputs.name: fields
inputs.description: Every field available to drag into Rows / Columns / Values. This is also the field-permission seam. A field that is not in this list cannot be dragged, aggregated, filtered or restored from a saved view, so a user who may not see `salary` gets a `fields` array without it. Filter `data` server-side as well — the rows are still in memory, and an export is not the only way to read memory.

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: Source rows. Ignored (and may be left unbound) in `serverSide` mode. Numeric fields must carry numbers. A string that `Number()` reads (`"1234.5"`) is accepted; one it does not (`"1.234,50"`, `"$12"`) counts as 0 and a dev-mode warning names the field once. The engine never guesses a locale — `"1,234"` is a thousand in en-US and one-point-two in de-DE — so parse with the locale your data came from before binding.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Rows/columns/measures/sort/topN — two-way, so a host can persist the layout.

inputs.name: result
inputs.description: Pre-aggregated result from the server. Required (and used verbatim) when `serverSide` is true.

inputs.name: serverSide
inputs.description: When true, the component renders `[result]` instead of computing one from `[data]` — aggregation happened on the server. `config` still updates from drag-and-drop / the toolbar, so its `(configChange)` is what to key a refetch off.

inputs.name: maxAxisGroups
inputs.description: How many distinct groups one axis may render before the pivot stops and warns instead of building. `0` disables the guard. The cost of a pivot is per group, not per row. Dropping a field like `orderId` or `email` into Rows asks for one group — one `<tr>`, one aggregated array per column leaf — per source row, so a 100,000-row dataset becomes 100,000 rendered rows and the tab stops responding before anything reaches the screen. The limit is per-axis rather than a cell budget precisely so the warning can name the field responsible; "too many cells" leaves a user with five dimensions guessing. Client-side only: in `serverSide` mode the component never sees `data`, so the host is the only party that can count anything.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: Show a skeleton placeholder in place of the pivot while data loads.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Load failure, shown as an error banner with a Retry button above the pivot (a stale `result` stays visible below it).

inputs.name: emptyMessage
inputs.default: 'Drag a field into Rows or Columns to build a summary.'
inputs.description: Text shown in place of the pivot when there is no result to display.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Title shown in the toolbar.

inputs.name: exportable
inputs.description: Show export buttons in the toolbar, one per format in `exportFormats`.

inputs.name: exportFormats
inputs.description: Formats offered as export buttons when `exportable`: 'xlsx' (Excel) and/or 'pdf'.

inputs.name: exportFileName
inputs.description: Base filename, without extension.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP 47 locale for dates and numbers.

inputs.name: collapsedIds
inputs.description: Row-node ids that are collapsed (two-way). Absent from this set = expanded — a fresh pivot starts fully open. A `model` because it is the same kind of fact as a Kanban's collapsed columns or a Gantt's folded rows: something the host has reason to restore after a route change, deep-link to, or persist per user. Held in a private signal it could be neither set nor observed.

components.name: Polar Area Chart
components.description: Nightingale rose / polar area chart with area-proportional (√) or linear radius scaling, padded wedges, labelled grid rings and a configurable start angle. Pure SVG.
whenToUse: Cyclical categories where the wrap-around matters — weekdays, months, compass bearings.
Comparing magnitudes across equal-width categories with a shared origin.
For non-cyclical categories, a bar chart is easier to read; for multi-series profiles, use the Radar chart.
customization: The shape of the rose depends on the order of the sectors, and the chart says so under the plot: every sector gets the same angular slice, so the silhouette is decided by which values sit next to each other. Under `linear` scaling it also states that area is not the value — a wedge's area grows with the square of its radius, so a doubled value covers four times the ink. `sqrt`, the default, is what keeps area proportional.
√ or linear radius scaling.
Grid ring count and value labels.
Pad angle between wedges and a custom start angle.
Per-sector colours.

`valuePolicy` decides what happens to a sector this chart cannot draw — a negative, `NaN` or `Infinity`. Radius is the encoding and there is no radius below the centre. `omit` (default) drops it and keeps it out of the share denominator; `reject` refuses the dataset. `clamp` is not offered: a wedge at the centre has no area to mark, and its table row would read as a genuine `0`, so a request for it falls back to `omit` with a dev warning.
accessibility: Every wedge is a keyboard-focusable `role="button"` named with its value and share of the total.
The plot is a labelled `role="group"`; Enter/Space emits `sectorSelect` and focus emits `sectorHover`.

Under the default √ scale wedge AREA is the value, which no reader can invert by eye. `sv-data-summary-table` publishes each sector's value and share of the total, in the cycle order the wedges are drawn in — the order is part of the data on a polar chart.

Whatever `valuePolicy` did is stated under the plot, not only in `console.warn`. An all-zero week is disclosed rather than replaced by the empty state: unlike a pie this chart still has its grid, its scale and every rim label, so all-zero is a legible picture of a real answer.
variants: Polar Area — Linear Radius, Padded Wedges

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the sectors are being fetched.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Load failure. Use `toSvDataError()` from `@styloviz/core` to normalize an `HttpErrorResponse`.

inputs.name: emptyMessage
inputs.description: Copy for the no-data state.

inputs.name: filtered
inputs.description: True when the emptiness is caused by a filter rather than an empty set.

inputs.name: sectors
inputs.description: Wedges to plot, drawn clockwise from `startAngle`.

inputs.name: valuePolicy
inputs.description: What to do with a sector this chart cannot plot — a negative value, `NaN`, `Infinity`. Radius is the encoding here, and there is no radius below the centre, so a negative has no honest wedge. It also reaches the share the tooltip and the data table quote, so leaving it in the sum would misstate every OTHER sector's percentage. - `omit` (default) — drop the wedge, and disclose the count. The remaining wedges each widen, since the slice is `360 / count`. - `reject` — refuse the dataset and show the error state. `clamp` is not supported: a wedge at radius zero has no area to mark, and the table would print a flat `0` indistinguishable from a real zero. It falls back to `omit` with a dev warning. `render` likewise.

inputs.description: Scale maximum. `0` (the default) rounds one out of the data.

inputs.description: How a value becomes a radius.

inputs.description: Chart diameter in pixels.

inputs.description: Number of concentric grid rings.

inputs.description: Angular gap between wedges, in degrees.

inputs.description: Where the first wedge starts, in degrees clockwise from twelve o'clock.

inputs.description: Show the labels around the rim.

components.name: Popover
components.description: Anchored panel with 7 variants, 8 auto-flipping placements, an optional pointer arrow, click/hover/manual triggers, and header/subtitle/close.
whenToUse: Showing rich, possibly interactive content anchored to a trigger.
Detail cards, mini-forms or menus that exceed what a Tooltip can hold.
Semantic confirmations or status callouts — reach for the matching `variant`.
For plain hint text, a Tooltip is lighter; for a list of actions, a Dropdown Menu.

examples.title: Semantic variant with arrow
examples.code: Are you sure?

examples.title: Passive callout vs interactive mini form
examples.code:
<!-- Passive: role="tooltip", the trigger is aria-describedby the panel,
     focus never moves. For a read-only note. -->
<sv-popover trigger="hover" [interactive]="false" title="Billing cycle">…</sv-popover>

<!-- Interactive: role="dialog", focus moves to the first field on open,
     and Tab cycles inside the panel instead of walking out of it. -->
<sv-popover [interactive]="true" title="Rename">
  <button slot="trigger">Rename…</button>
  <input aria-label="Name" /> <button>Save</button>
</sv-popover>

examples.title: The Popout preset
examples.code:
<!-- What 1.x sv-popout was (removed in 2.0):
     the same position + align spelling, the same engine, the same pixel, and
     padding="none" so your content owns the whole panel. -->
<sv-popover trigger="click" [interactive]="true" [autoFocus]="true" padding="none"
            position="right" align="start" ariaLabel="Account">
  <button slot="trigger">Account</button>
  …
</sv-popover>
// Or in code: import { SV_POPOUT_PRESET } from '@styloviz-pro/overlays';

customization: Seven variants (default · dark · primary · success · warning · danger · info) with tinted header, icon badge and accent bar.

Eight placements with automatic flip + viewport clamping; optional pointer arrow via `[showArrow]`. `align` (`start` · `center` · `end`) folds into the side of `position`, which adds the four side-aligned placements (`left-start` … `right-end`) — `SV_POPOUT_PRESET` reproduces 1.x `sv-popout`, removed in 2.0.
Portaled to `document.body` and re-anchored to its trigger on scroll of any ancestor container (capture-phase) and on resize — never drifts or leaves the viewport.

Click / hover / manual triggers, configurable `offset`, hover delays, and min/max width. A hover popover also keeps itself open while the pointer travels across the gap towards the panel (a safe corridor, not a longer timer), so reaching for it does not dismiss it — and turning away from the panel mid-way starts the close again rather than leaving it stuck open.

Placement arithmetic is shared with Dropdown Menu and Tooltip: twelve placements, conditional flip, viewport clamp, `start`/`end` mirrored for RTL text, and correction for a transformed ancestor that has become the containing block.

If the trigger is removed or collapses to nothing while the popover is open — the row it sits in is deleted, its `<details>` closes — the popover closes rather than floating over unrelated content. The trigger is size-watched while open, so this happens at the collapse, not at the next scroll.
Header (title + subtitle + optional close button), content and footer slots; `closeOnOutsideClick` / `closeOnEsc` / `closeOnContentClick` toggles; `customClass` on the surface.
Responsive: the panel width is capped to the viewport (`max-w-[calc(100vw-1rem)]`) on top of flip + clamp, so wide content can never overflow a small screen.

`[sheetOnNarrow]="true"` turns the panel into a bottom sheet at 640px and below, where there is no room beside the trigger: anchored coordinates and the arrow are dropped, it scrolls inside 70vh, clears the home indicator and rides above the virtual keyboard. Applies to the Popout preset too. Off by default.

Long content scrolls inside the panel, which is capped at the viewport height (`max-h-[calc(100vh-1rem)]`) and `overscroll-contain`: scrolling past its end does not chain to the page and drag the anchor (and the panel) away.
accessibility: Trigger exposes `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the panel is `role="dialog"` labelled via `aria-labelledby`/`aria-label` and described via `aria-describedby` (subtitle).

With `[autoFocus]` focus moves into the panel on click/manual open; on close focus returns to the trigger unless the user has already put it somewhere else (an outside click on another control keeps its focus). Closes on Esc and outside click (both configurable).

`[interactive]="false"` makes the panel `role="tooltip"` and references it from the trigger's `aria-describedby` while open, with no `aria-haspopup` — it never takes focus, and it renders no Close button even with `[showClose]`, because a tooltip must not hold controls (dev mode warns if you project a focusable element into one). `[interactive]="true"` keeps `role="dialog"`, moves focus to the first focusable element (or the panel, `tabindex="-1"`) on a click/manual open, and keeps Tab / Shift+Tab inside the panel.

inputs.description: Controls popover visibility.

inputs.name: position
