inputs.name: batchEdit
inputs.description: Edits, pastes and fills become an undoable draft (Ctrl/⌘+Z, Ctrl/⌘+Shift+Z) the table shows and marks, saved in one `batchSave` — instead of `editComplete` / `rangeEdit` per change.

inputs.name: saving
inputs.description: A `batchSave` is in flight: Save, Discard, Undo and Redo wait for it.

inputs.name: saveError
inputs.description: The last `batchSave` failed — shown on the batch bar. Call that save's `rollback()` too.

inputs.name: setFilters
inputs.description: `filterType: 'set'` filters (two-way): column key → the values let through. Saved with the layout.

inputs.name: filterBuilder
inputs.description: A toolbar Filter builder — `@styloviz-pro/query-builder` over the columns (`queryType` per column).

inputs.name: filterQuery
inputs.description: The builder's AND/OR query (two-way) — store it with `svSerializeQuery`. `null` filters nothing.

inputs.name: highlightQuery
inputs.description: Rows to mark without hiding the rest (two-way), in the builder's query shape — `svGridAssist` sets it from "highlight …". `null` marks nothing.

inputs.name: statusBar
inputs.description: A bar under the table: the row count, or count / sum / average / min / max of the selected cells.

inputs.name: printable
inputs.description: A toolbar Print button; printing then shows every filtered row and none of the table's controls.

inputs.name: emptyMessage
inputs.description: Text shown when there are no rows to display.

inputs.name: customClass
inputs.description: Extra CSS classes appended to the root element.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Load failure. Use `toSvDataError()` from `@styloviz/core` to normalize an `HttpErrorResponse`. Rendered in place of the rows, above the toolbar so the user can still change the filter that caused it.

inputs.name: debounceMs
inputs.description: Milliseconds typing in the search box or a text column filter waits before `queryChange` asks the server again (`serverSide` only). The rows on screen still filter on every keystroke; sorting, paging and clearing ask at once. `0` asks on every keystroke.

inputs.name: hiddenColumnKeys
inputs.description: Which columns the user has hidden (two-way). Bind it to restore a saved set of hidden columns, and read `(hiddenColumnKeysChange)` to store what the user changes.

inputs.name: revealedColumnKeys
inputs.description: Columns declared `hidden: true` that the user has since shown from the Columns menu. A `hidden` column starts hidden and stays in the Columns menu, so the user can show it. Two-way, like `hiddenColumnKeys`: together the two ARE the column-visibility view, and a host that persists one without the other restores a table whose revealed columns have vanished again.

outputs.name: sortChange
outputs.description: Emitted with the full list of active sorts (empty when cleared) whenever the user changes the sort.

outputs.name: selectionChange
outputs.description: Emitted with the new set of selected row ids whenever the user changes the selection.

outputs.name: rowClick
outputs.description: Emitted with the row when the user clicks a row or one of its cells, or activates it with Enter.

outputs.name: cellClick
outputs.description: Emitted with the row, column and displayed value when the user clicks a cell; `rowClick` fires as well.

outputs.name: editComplete
outputs.description: Emitted with the row, column, old and new value when an inline cell edit is committed with a valid, changed value, so the host can persist it.

outputs.name: rangeEdit
outputs.description: Many cells at once — a paste or a fill (`cellSelection`): every changed cell, validated, in one event to apply in one go.

outputs.name: batchSave
outputs.description: `batchEdit`: the draft, saved. Apply `changes`, send `requestKey`, call `rollback()` if it fails.

outputs.name: unsavedChange
outputs.description: `batchEdit`: how many cells are unsaved, whenever that changes — for a leave-page guard.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The host should re-run the failed load.

outputs.name: queryChange
outputs.description: Everything the user is asking to see, in the kit's shared shape. This is the output to wire in `serverSide` mode: one handler regardless of whether they paged, sorted, filtered or searched, and the same `SvDataQuery` every other component in the kit emits — so `@styloviz/data` and a hand-rolled fetch both take it without a translation layer.

outputs.name: rowExpand
outputs.description: Emitted with the row when the user expands or collapses its detail panel.

outputs.name: bulkActionClick
outputs.description: Emitted with the bulk action and a snapshot of the selected row ids when the user runs a bulk action.

outputs.name: columnResize
outputs.description: A column finished resizing (pointer drag or ←/→ on a focused handle) — emits the column key and its new pixel width, so a host can persist the layout.

outputs.name: columnOrderChange
outputs.description: Columns were reordered by drag — emits the full column-key order, left to right.

outputs.name: exportFailed
outputs.description: An export failed. PDF loads `jspdf` / `html2canvas` at click time, so a host that has not installed them learns about it here rather than through an unhandled rejection and a button that appears to do nothing.

outputs.name: groupToggle
outputs.description: A group was expanded or collapsed by the user, with its new state.

outputs.name: layoutStateChange
outputs.description: Fires whenever anything `TableLayoutState` describes changes — column order/width/visibility, sort, column filters, page size, or which groups are collapsed — so a host knows there is something new to save. Store `serializeLayoutState()` rather than this payload: the payload is the live shape, while the serialized form carries a kind and a schema version, and `restoreLayoutState()` can then say why it ignored a blob instead of applying one whose shape does not fit the current table. Does not fire for the state the table mounted with, only for a real change after that, so a host writing straight through to storage does not immediately re-save what it just loaded via `applyLayoutState`.

outputs.name: selectedIdsChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `selectedIds` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(selectedIds)]`.

outputs.name: expandedRowIdsChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `expandedRowIds` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(expandedRowIds)]`.

outputs.name: pageSizeChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `pageSize` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(pageSize)]`.

outputs.name: recordExpandedIdsChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `recordExpandedIds` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(recordExpandedIds)]`.

outputs.name: cellRangeChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `cellRange` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(cellRange)]`.

outputs.name: columnPinsChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `columnPins` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(columnPins)]`.

outputs.name: setFiltersChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `setFilters` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(setFilters)]`.

outputs.name: filterQueryChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `filterQuery` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(filterQuery)]`.

outputs.name: highlightQueryChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `highlightQuery` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(highlightQuery)]`.

outputs.name: hiddenColumnKeysChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `hiddenColumnKeys` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(hiddenColumnKeys)]`.

outputs.name: revealedColumnKeysChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `revealedColumnKeys` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(revealedColumnKeys)]`.

components.name: Relationship Graph
components.description: A network of nodes and links in two layouts — a deterministic force layout and a chord diagram — with neighbour highlighting, one-tab-stop keyboard roving and a link table. In-house layouts, no dependencies. Pure SVG.
whenToUse: Who connects to whom: service dependencies, team collaboration, referral networks.
Chord: the volume between a handful of groups, in both directions.
For flow through ordered stages (budget → department → line), use a Sankey.
customization: `layout`: `force` (default) or `chord`.
Node size from `value` (square-root scale); link width from `value` (a missing value counts as 1).
`width` / `height` of the drawing.
Links to unknown nodes, self-links and NaN, negative or zero values are left out and named in a notice under the plot.
accessibility: One tab stop; arrow keys move between nodes in label order, Home/End to the ends, Enter or Space emits `nodeSelect`, Escape clears the highlight. A hidden hint says so.
Each node is named with its group and its connections: “Chen, Engineering: 3 connections — Ana, Dev, Eli”.
Hover or focus dims everything but the node, its links and its neighbours — opacity only, no motion under reduced-motion.
The data table lists every drawn link (“Source → Target”, value, relationship), and the chart a11y module can put it on screen.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: True while the graph is being fetched.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: Load failure. Use `toSvDataError()` from `@styloviz/core` to normalize an `HttpErrorResponse`.

inputs.name: emptyMessage
inputs.description: Copy for the no-data state.

inputs.name: filtered
inputs.description: True when the emptiness is caused by a filter rather than an empty set.

inputs.name: nodes
inputs.description: Nodes: `{ id, label, group?, value? }`.

inputs.name: links
inputs.description: Relationships: `{ source, target, value?, label? }`. A missing value means 1.

inputs.name: layout
inputs.description: `'force'` (deterministic force-directed) or `'chord'` (arcs and ribbons).

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Drawing width in SVG units; the SVG scales to its container.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Drawing height in pixels.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Chart title rendered above the drawing.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name override. Falls back to a generated summary.

inputs.name: customClass
inputs.description: Extra CSS classes applied to the root wrapper.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP 47 locale for numbers and plural forms.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The host should re-run the failed load.

outputs.name: nodeSelect
outputs.description: Emitted when a node is clicked or activated with Enter/Space: the node and its neighbours.

components.name: Result Page
components.description: Success / error / warning / info / empty result pages with semantic SVG icons, a title, description and content/action projection slots.
whenToUse: Showing the outcome of a flow on its own screen: success, error, warning, info.
Post-checkout, post-submit, 404/500 pages, access-denied screens.
For an empty list within a page, use the Empty State instead.
components.usage:
<sv-result
  status="success"
  title="Payment complete"
  description="Your order is on its way.">
  <sv-button label="Back to dashboard" />
</sv-result>

examples.title: Error result
examples.code:
<sv-result status="error" title="Something went wrong" description="We couldn't load this page. Try again.">
  <sv-button label="Retry" (clicked)="reload()" />
</sv-result>

examples.title: An error a support desk can act on
examples.code:
<!-- Bind the error and the page shows its correlation id with a copy
     button. "It said something went wrong" is an unanswerable ticket;
     the same sentence with a reference is one log query, and the id was
     already on the error - toSvDataError() reads it out of the body or
     the x-request-id header.

     focusHeading moves focus to the title on arrival: a routed error
     page otherwise leaves focus on whatever the user clicked, often an
     element that has been removed.

     showDetails adds a collapsed Status/Code block - for an internal
     tool or a staging build. The error's "cause" is never rendered
     anywhere: it is a raw thrown value, and this is a screen people
     photograph. -->
<sv-result
  status="error"
  title="Could not load the report"
  [description]="error()!.message"
  [error]="error()"
  [focusHeading]="true"
  [showDetails]="isInternalUser()"
  retryLabel="Try again"
  [retryAction]="reload" />

examples.title: A retry that can fail again
examples.code:
<!-- A slotted button is right for "go home" — a link cannot fail. The
     retry is the one action that can, repeatedly, so it is first-class:
     [retryAction] makes the component own it, which means a second press
     is refused, the button shows a spinner, and a second failure is
     rendered instead of vanishing. Without the action, (retry) is emitted
     and the pending state is yours. -->
<sv-result
  status="error"
  title="Could not load the report"
  retryLabel="Try again"
  [retryAction]="reloadReport"
  (retryFailed)="logFailure()">
  <sv-button label="Back to dashboard" svResultActions />
</sv-result>

customization: Pick a `status` (success, error, warning, info, empty) for the semantic icon and color.

Diagnostics from the error itself: bind `[error]` and the server's correlation id renders with a copy button — "it said something went wrong" is an unanswerable ticket, and the same sentence with a reference is one log query. `[showDetails]` adds a collapsed status/code block for internal surfaces. `cause` is never rendered: it is a raw thrown value, and an error page is a screen people photograph.

`[focusHeading]` moves focus to the title when the page appears, which is what a routed error page owes a keyboard or screen-reader user — the SPA swapped the view and left focus on an element that has been removed. Opt-in, because `sv-result` is also used inline, where stealing focus interrupts something else.
Override the glyph with `icon` (an icon-library name) and choose a `size`.
Project body content and action buttons into the result slots.

A first-class retry: `retryLabel` renders the button, `[retryAction]` hands the work to the component (first-wins, so repeated presses are refused; a spinner and `retryPendingLabel` while it runs; the rejection rendered under the button), and `(retry)` / `(retryFailed)` report what happened. Built on `createAsyncAction` in `@styloviz/core`.
accessibility: Status icons are decorative; the title carries the meaning as a heading.

`[focusHeading]="true"` gives the title `tabindex="-1"` and focuses it once on arrival — `-1` so it does not become a permanent tab stop. Without it a routed error page leaves focus wherever the user clicked, often on an element that has been removed, so the next Tab starts at the top of the page and a screen reader announces nothing.
The copy confirmation is announced as well as shown: a sighted user sees the label change to "Copied", and an `aria-live="polite"` region says so for everyone else.
Action buttons are labelled and keyboard reachable.
Adequate contrast across statuses in light and dark.
The retry button carries `aria-busy` and is disabled while its action runs, so a screen-reader user is not told to press a button that is already working.

inputs.name: status
inputs.description: Semantic status that drives icon, colour palette and `role`.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Primary headline.

inputs.name: description
inputs.description: Supporting description.

inputs.name: icon
inputs.description: Icon-library NAME overriding the status default. Was `iconPath`.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Component size.

inputs.name: retryLabel
inputs.description: Label for a built-in retry button. `null` renders none. A slotted retry is a host `<button>` with a `(click)`: it has no state, so it can be pressed repeatedly, with no feedback, firing the failed request again and again. The built-in one pairs with `retryAction` for a pending state and a rendered failure. Slotted actions still work and are still right for "go home" or "contact support". This is for the one action whose whole point is that it might fail again.

inputs.name: retryAction
inputs.description: The work the retry performs, run by the component. With it: repeated presses are refused (`createAsyncAction` is first-wins), the button shows a spinner while the work is in flight, and a rejection is rendered under it rather than disappearing. Without it, `(retry)` is emitted and the pending state is the host's problem.

inputs.name: retryPendingLabel
inputs.description: Label while the retry is in flight.

inputs.name: retryPending
inputs.description: The host's own retry is in flight — for a host that listens to `(retry)` instead of passing `[retryAction]`.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: The error being reported, for its diagnostics. An error page with no diagnostics is an unsupportable ticket. "It said something went wrong" is unanswerable: nobody can find the request. The status, the code and above all the server's correlation id are already on `SvDataError` — this input is what puts them on screen, where the user can read them out or copy them. The `cause` is never rendered, and that is not an oversight. It is a raw thrown value — a stack trace, a response body, sometimes a token in a URL — and an error page is a screen users photograph and paste into chat. `message`, `status`, `code` and `reference` are the four fields that are safe to show and sufficient to find the request in a log.

inputs.name: copyLabel
inputs.description: Label for the copy button beside the reference. `null` renders none.

inputs.name: copiedLabel
inputs.description: Confirmation shown in place of `copyLabel` after a copy.

inputs.name: detailsLabel
inputs.description: Heading for the collapsed technical block.

inputs.name: showDetails
inputs.description: Show the status/code block.

inputs.name: focusHeading
inputs.description: Move focus to the heading when this page appears.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The retry button was pressed. Always emitted, action or not.

outputs.name: retryFailed
outputs.description: The `[retryAction]` rejected. The message is rendered under the button.

components.name: Rich Text Editor
components.description: Full-featured contenteditable editor with a configurable 35-tool toolbar — fonts, colors, alignment, lists and checklists, link/table/code, emoji, undo/redo, export, source view, fullscreen and word count.
whenToUse: Authoring formatted content: comments, descriptions, articles, email bodies.
You need bold/lists/links/tables without pulling in a heavy third-party editor.
For plain short text, a multiline Text Field is lighter.

examples.title: A comment box
examples.description: toolbar="comment" — bold, italic, strike, link, code block and blockquote. Presets: full (default), basic, minimal, comment, none.

examples.title: Exactly these tools
examples.description: An id list shows only those tools; hiddenTools then takes tools away from whatever toolbar resolved to.

examples.title: Accessible labelling
examples.description: Give the editor a meaningful accessible name with ariaLabel; the built-in role="textbox" + aria-multiline and aria-pressed toolbar toggles do the rest.

examples.title: Reactive forms (CVA)
examples.description: Implements ControlValueAccessor, so it binds with formControlName / ngModel; formControl.disable() disables the toolbar and editor.

examples.title: Paste cleaning
examples.description: On by default. Clipboard markup is parsed inertly and rebuilt from an allowlist before it reaches the document — the browser paste is cancelled first, so nothing from the clipboard ever touches a live node.
examples.code:
<sv-rich-text-editor
  [(value)]="content"
  [cleanPaste]="true"
  (pasteCleaned)="onCleaned($event)" />

// what was removed, so you can tell the author rather than
// silently eating half of what they pasted
onCleaned(r: SvPasteResult): void {
  this.notice.set(svPasteSummary(r));   // 'Cleaned on paste: removed 2 unsupported elements and 5 attributes.'
}

examples.title: Mentions
examples.description: The trigger scan is shared with sv-mention, so the rule that stops an email address opening a people-search is one rule. The inserted chip is atomic to the caret.
examples.code:
<sv-rich-text-editor
  [(value)]="content"
  [mentionTriggers]="['@']"
  [mentionSuggestions]="candidates()"
  (mentionQuery)="lookUp($event)"
  (mentionInserted)="onMentioned($event)" />

// The host filters; the component displays. Async lookup is just a signal
// that arrives later.
lookUp({ query }: SvTriggerMatch): void {
  this.candidates.set(this.directory().filter(p => p.label.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase())));
}

// Read the mentions back off the DOCUMENT, never off a list kept beside it —
// a list drifts the moment somebody deletes a chip or undoes.
editor.mentions();        // → [{ id: 'u-1', label: 'Priya Sharma', trigger: '@' }]
editor.plainText();       // → 'cc @Priya Sharma please'

examples.title: Mentions that were edited after insertion
examples.description: contenteditable="false" makes a chip atomic to the caret; it does not make it immutable. A chip reading "@Priya Sharm" still carries Priya's user id.

examples.title: Merged table cells
examples.description: Select across cells and merge. The grid model is the HTML spec's slot map, because once a cell has a span the DOM stops telling you which column a cell is in.

examples.title: The grid model, on its own
examples.description: Exported, because "which column is this cell in" has no answer in DOM terms once a span exists — and any host doing its own table work needs the same map the editor uses.

examples.title: Markdown mode
examples.description: A round trip through Markdown is lossy — Markdown has no colour, no underline and no merged cells — so the conversion returns what it dropped instead of pretending it dropped nothing. The notice is shown on the way in, while the HTML that carried the formatting still exists.
examples.code:
@if (editor.markdownNotice()) {

{{ editor.markdownNotice() }}

}

examples.title: Markdown without the mode toggle
examples.description: Read and write Markdown directly. While the mode is open, markdown() returns the live textarea rather than a stale conversion of the HTML behind it — an autosave wired to the other choice saves the wrong text, and only for authors who happened to be in Markdown mode when it fired.

examples.title: Clean markup outside the editor
examples.description: The sanitiser is exported, so the same rules can be applied to content arriving from anywhere else — an import, a webhook, a migration.
examples.code:
import { svCleanPastedHtml } from '@styloviz-pro/rich-editor';

const { html, droppedElements } = svCleanPastedHtml(incoming);

customization: Set `height`, `placeholder`, `ariaLabel` and the `toolbarLine` overflow mode (wrap or scroll).

Every one of the 35 tools is a switch: `toolbar` takes a preset (`full` — the default — `basic`, `minimal`, `comment`, `none`) or a list of tool ids, and `hiddenTools` takes any tool id away from whatever that resolved to. `SV_RTE_TOOL_GROUPS` exports the 11 groups, so a host can build "everything in `insert` except `image`".
Switch between rich and source (HTML) views, fullscreen, and toggle the word / character counters.
Two-way bind with `[(value)]` or bind a reactive control (ControlValueAccessor); react to `contentChange`, `editorFocus` and `editorBlur`.

Paste cleaning via `cleanPaste` (on by default), `pastePlainText` and `allowPastedDataImages`, with a `pasteCleaned` output naming what was removed. `svCleanPastedHtml`, `svPlainTextFromHtml` and `svIsSafeUrl` are exported for use outside the editor.

Merged table cells via `mergeTableCells()`, `splitTableCell()`, `tableMergeRefusal()` and `caretInMergedCell()`. The slot map (`svTableGrid`, `svSelectionRect`, `svMergePlan`, `svSplitCell`) is exported for hosts doing their own table work.

Markdown mode via `toggleMarkdownMode()`, `markdown()`, `setMarkdown()`, `markdownNotice()` and the `markdownChanged` output. `svHtmlToMarkdown` returns `{ markdown, lost }`; `svMarkdownToHtml`, `svEscapeMarkdown` and `svMarkdownLossLabel` are exported too.

Mentions via `mentionTriggers` (any number of characters — `@` people, `#` topics, `/` commands), `mentionSuggestions`, `mentionQuery` and `mentionInserted`. `mentions()`, `mentionRepairs()` and `plainText()` read the document back. The scan is `svScanTrigger` from `@styloviz/core`, shared with `sv-mention`.
Slash commands via `slashCommands` (`true` for the built-ins, or your own `SvRteSlashCommand[]`) and the `slashCommand` output; `checklist` and `emoji` are toolbar tools like any other.

Track changes with the `svRteSuggest` directive (`[svRteSuggest]`, `suggestAuthor`, `#s="svRteSuggest"` → `suggestions()`, `accept`, `reject`, `acceptAll`, `rejectAll`, `resolved`); comments, find & replace and the outline are siblings — `sv-rte-comments`, `sv-rte-find-replace`, `sv-rte-outline` — that take the editor as `[editor]`.

Revision compare with `svDiffHtml(before, after)`, Word import with `svDocxToHtml(file)`, and real-time collaboration with the `svRteCollab` directive over any `SvEditorCollabAdapter` (`svCreateMemoryCollabHub()` is the in-memory fake peer; a Yjs adapter is in the gallery).

Building your own sibling: `surface()` is the editing element, `commitEdit()` records a change you made to it as one undo step, `setFindHandler()` claims Ctrl/Cmd+F and `applyRemoteHtml()` replaces the document keeping the caret.
accessibility: The editing surface is `role="textbox"` with `aria-multiline`; `ariaLabel` sets a meaningful accessible name (falling back to the placeholder).
The `role="toolbar"` holds labelled buttons, and formatting toggles (bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, super/subscript, ordered/unordered list, source, fullscreen) expose `aria-pressed`.
The word / character count is an `aria-live="polite"` status region; common shortcuts (Ctrl/Cmd+B/I/U, undo/redo) are supported.
Merging keeps the content of every absorbed cell rather than only the top-left one — silently destroying three of four values is not something an author can see happen, and undo is the only way back.

The mention panel is a `role="listbox"` that never takes focus: the editor keeps it and announces the active option through `aria-activedescendant`, because moving focus out of the contenteditable loses the caret the insertion needs. Arrows move, Enter and Tab insert, Escape closes — and those keys are only claimed while the panel is open, so Enter still makes a paragraph the rest of the time.

The Markdown loss notice is `role="status"`, not an alert: it reports a consequence of the button the author just pressed, and an alert would interrupt a screen reader mid-sentence to announce something they asked for. The Markdown textarea carries its own label, and the rich surface goes `aria-readonly` while the mode is open so it is not announced as two editable regions.

Pasting is cleaned rather than blocked: the content the author meant survives (an unknown wrapper is unwrapped, not deleted), and what was removed is reported instead of vanishing — a silent sanitiser is indistinguishable from a broken paste for somebody who cannot see the result.
Track changes are `<ins>`/`<del>` — announced as insertions and deletions by screen readers that support them, and shown with an underline or strike as well as colour.
The slash menu is the mention panel's pattern: a `role="listbox"` announced through `aria-activedescendant` while the caret stays in the text.
The emoji grid is one tab stop with arrow-key movement, and each emoji is named by the screen reader in the user's language rather than by an English label.
Checklist boxes are real checkboxes named "Done"; Ctrl/Cmd+Enter ticks the item at the caret, so a keyboard user never has to reach for the box.
variants: Paste Cleaning — the Half Nobody Writes the Feature For
Mentions — the Chip That Cannot Be Half-Deleted
Merged Cells — Where Every Hand-Rolled Table Editor Breaks
Markdown Mode — the Conversion That Admits What It Lost

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: HTML content. Use `[(value)]` for two-way binding.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Placeholder shown when empty.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name for the editor (announced by screen readers). Falls back to the placeholder.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Editor height (CSS length).

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disable editing.

inputs.name: readonly
inputs.description: Read-only mode — content visible but not editable.

inputs.name: maxLength
inputs.description: Max character count (0 = unlimited).

inputs.name: showWordCount
inputs.description: Show the word counter.

inputs.name: showCharCount
inputs.description: Show the character counter.

inputs.name: autoFocus
inputs.description: Focus the editor on init.

inputs.name: toolbarLine
inputs.description: Toolbar overflow behaviour: wrap to multiple rows or scroll.

inputs.name: documentTitle
inputs.description: Title for a printed or exported document. It becomes the exported document's `<title>`, which is what a browser offers as the default filename in its print dialog — "Document Export" for every document in the product is a folder of indistinguishable PDFs.

inputs.name: toolbar
inputs.description: Which tools the toolbar shows: a preset (`'full'` | `'basic'` | `'minimal'` | `'comment'` | `'none'`), or the exact tool ids to show. `hiddenTools` is then taken away from whatever this resolved to.

inputs.name: hiddenTools
inputs.description: Tools to hide, from whatever `toolbar` resolved to. Any SvRteToolId — the original four (SvRichTextEditorTool) keep working unchanged. See SvRichTextEditorTool for why a host would want this.

inputs.name: htmlSanitizer
inputs.description: Replaces the sanitiser applied to HTML that ENTERS the editing surface from outside — `[value]`, `writeValue` (formControl) and leaving source view — and to the HTML handed to print/PDF/image export. The default is on, and `null` means "the default", not "none": a stored `` in a saved document is removed before it reaches a live node. The default is `svSanitizeEditorHtml` from `@styloviz/core`, whose allowlist matches what this editor writes (tables, images, fonts, mentions) so a saved document round-trips unchanged. Pass your own function to use a different policy (e.g. DOMPurify with your configuration). Returning the input unchanged switches sanitising off; only do that for HTML you have already sanitised on the server. components.name: Sankey / Flow Diagram
components.description: Flow diagram with reproducible column layout, cubic-bezier flow paths, width-proportional links and hover tooltip. Cyclic graphs are ranked rather than collapsed, and any flow it cannot draw is named under the diagram. Pure SVG.
whenToUse: Visualizing flow and proportion between stages: budgets, traffic, conversions, energy.
You want link widths proportional to magnitude.
The process loops — returns, refunds, recycled material. A backwards flow is drawn dashed and does not disturb the column order.
For simple stage counts, a Funnel chart is lighter.

examples.title: Validate a graph before it reaches the chart
examples.code:

if (diagnostics.feedbackLinks) console.info(svSankeyNotice(diagnostics, SV_CHARTS_PRO_LABELS));

customization: Reproducible column layout: longest-path ranking, with `nodeOrder` choosing input order or heaviest-first within a column.
Width-proportional links.
Per-node and per-link colors.
Backwards flows drawn dashed and excluded from ranking.
accessibility: The SVG is a `role="group"` with a generated summary (override via `ariaLabel`) — `group`, not `img`, because the ribbons and nodes are tab stops.

`sv-data-summary-table` publishes one row per flow, named "Source to Destination", with its value and its share of BOTH ends. Ribbon width is the value, and the two shares are what the picture makes obvious and a bare list of numbers does not: 60 out of a 600 source is a trickle, 60 into a 60 destination is everything that destination gets.

A backwards flow is marked "(backwards)" in its row and in its accessible name, not only by the dash. The dash is the one part of the drawing a screen reader cannot report and a colour-blind reader can miss.
The table lists what is actually on screen. A flow the chart refused is absent from it and named in the note instead, so the rows and the ribbons never disagree.
Ribbons and nodes are keyboard-focusable `role="button"` elements with `aria-label`s; hover/focus shows the tooltip and Enter/Space emits `linkSelect`/`nodeSelect`. Labels carry meaning beyond color.

components.name: Resource Scheduler
components.description: Resources against time: rooms, people or equipment in rows (timeline day, week and month) or columns (resource day), grouped into collapsible trees. Bookings sit in lanes so a double booking is never hidden; working hours are shaded and blocked time hatched; `overlapRule` warns about or prevents double bookings. Drag, tap or press Enter on free time to book it — the booking rules answer first, by name. With `editable`, a booking drags to another time, day or resource and its end edge drags to resize, or moves from the keyboard (Space, arrows, Space); every drop asks the same rules as the edit dialog, then the host's `canMoveEvent`, and is refused out loud when either says no. Every booking is at least a 24 px target, however short. Same `CalendarEvent`s as `sv-event-calendar`, recurring series and zones included.
whenToUse: Booking shared things — rooms, vehicles, equipment — or rota-ing people, where WHO or WHAT matters as much as when.
For one person's calendar, use `sv-event-calendar`; for task dependencies over weeks, use the Gantt chart.

examples.title: Let a browser agent drive it (WebMCP)
examples.code:
<!-- svWebMcp from @styloviz/core registers rooms_describe, rooms_… — see /docs/webmcp -->
<sv-scheduler svWebMcp="rooms" [resources]="rooms" [events]="bookings" />
<!-- tools: describe, list_events, create_event, move_event, set_view, go_to_date -->

examples.title: Booking rules
examples.code:
<sv-scheduler
  [resources]="rooms"
  [events]="bookings()"
  view="resource-day"
  [blocked]="[{ id: 'lunch', label: 'Lunch', start: '12:00', end: '13:00', daysOfWeek: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] }]"
  overlapRule="prevent"
  [creatable]="true"
  (slotSelect)="book($event)" />
// $event = { resourceId, date, startTime, endTime, check } — only slots the rules allow arrive here

examples.title: Drag, resize and keyboard moves
examples.code:
<sv-scheduler
  [resources]="rooms"
  [events]="bookings()"
  view="resource-day"
  overlapRule="prevent"
  [editable]="true"
  [canMoveEvent]="canMove"
  (eventChange)="bookings.set(svApplyEventChange(bookings(), $event))"
  (eventMoveRefused)="say($event.message)" />
// $event.source: 'dialog' | 'drag' | 'keyboard' | 'api' — one handler for all of them.
// canMove = (change) => true | false | 'Spree is cleaned from 16:00.'
// A booking with readOnly: true is drawn and opened, never moved. [eventDrag]="false" keeps editing to the dialog.

customization: Four views: `resource-day`, `timeline-day`, `timeline-week`, `timeline-month`; `views` picks which the switcher offers.

Moving: with `editable`, drag a booking to move it (by `slotMinutes`, or by whole days in the week and month timelines) and across resources; drag its end edge to resize it in the single-day views. `eventDrag` turns drag and keyboard moves off; `canMoveEvent` refuses a move with a reason; `readOnly` on an event locks it. A recurring booking moves one occurrence, as the dialog does by default; open it to move the series.
`dayStart` / `dayEnd` set the hours drawn (08:00–18:00 by default) and `slotMinutes` the slot size (30). A booking outside the hours is pinned to the edge with a marker, never dropped.
Resources nest through `parentId`; `collapsed` is a two-way model of the folded groups, so a host can persist it.
A resource's own `workingHours` wins over the scheduler's.
accessibility: The free slots are one tab stop, roving like a grid: arrow keys along and across, Home / End to the ends; Enter or Space books the focused slot. Each slot is named with its resource, date and time, and a blocked one says so with `aria-disabled`. Time under a booking is not a slot: the tab stop lands on the first free one and the arrows step over bookings, so no focus ring is ever hidden behind one.
Every booking is at least 24 × 24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8), however short — the box is padded and the lanes are laid out on the padded boxes, so a short booking never covers its neighbour.

Every move has a keyboard path (WCAG 2.5.7): focus a booking, Space picks it up, the arrows move it along time and across resources, Shift and an arrow change its end, Space or Enter drops, Escape cancels. Each step is said in a live region; a refused drop is said there and in the status line, in words. Touch lifts a booking on a long press, so a finger still pans the grid.
Every booking is a button named with its title, time, rule, zone and what it books; each resource's bookings are a list named "Bookings for …".
A refused or warned booking is said in a polite live region, in words — "Lunch — nothing can be booked then.", "It would overlap Design review, …".
Groups collapse through a real button with `aria-expanded`. Touch never starts a drag-to-book, so a finger can pan the grid; a tap books one slot (WCAG 2.5.7).

Drag, resize and keyboard moves — a refused drop

Wired to an API — loading, error and empty

components.name: Scroll Area
components.description: A styled scrollbar drawn over a genuinely scrolling element — never in place of one. Minimum grabbable thumb with the track arithmetic corrected for it, click-to-page on the track, and edge fades that are the only affordance a hidden scrollbar leaves.
whenToUse: A bounded region — a panel, a dropdown, a log — that needs a scrollbar matching the rest of the design.
You want the native scrollbar hidden without losing anything the native scrollbar gave you.
For scrolling the page itself, do not use this: style the document scrollbar or leave it alone.

examples.title: Horizontal, RTL-safe
examples.description: The thumb, the fades and track paging follow the inline start, so the same markup works under dir="rtl".

customization: Four thumb policies: `auto` (on hover, focus and scroll), `always`, `hover` (lingers for `hideDelay`), `hidden`.
Any CSS length as `maxHeight`, or `fill` to take the height the parent gives it (`flex-1` in a flex column).
The thumb's look: `scrollbars` (`overlay` over the content, or `inset` with a reserved gutter), `thumbStyle` (`pill` · `square` · `track`) and `size` (sm · md · lg).
Fades: `fadeStyle` (`gradient` · `shadow`) and `fadeColor` (or `--sv-sa-fade`) so a fade over a coloured card matches the card.
A sticky header projected with `[svScrollAreaHeader]`, a `backToTop` button after `showAfter` px, and a `progress` bar along the start edge.

`snap` (`mandatory` · `proximity`) with `(snapChange)` and `scrollToSnap(i)`; `scrollTo`, `scrollBy`, `scrollToStart` and `scrollToEnd`; `(reachedEnd)` / `(reachedStart)` fire `threshold` px early for infinite scroll; `contentHeight` gives a virtual list its full scroll length.
Tune the smallest grabbable thumb with `minThumb` (24px by default).
Edge fades on or off via `edgeFade`.
`orientation="horizontal"` draws the thumb, fades and track paging along the x axis, normalised for RTL; `orientation="both"` draws a thumb on each axis with a corner where they meet.
`tabStop`: `auto` (a tab stop only while scrollable — the default), `always`, or `never` (for content that is itself focusable).
`observeContent` (default on) re-measures on content or viewport resize; turn it off to call `measure()` yourself.

Variant axes: `variant`, `minThumb` and `edgeFade` are appearance; `orientation` and `maxHeight` are layout; `observeContent` and `tabStop` are behavioural modes. All combine. In `vertical` or `horizontal` mode the other axis still scrolls natively but has no drawn thumb — use `both` for a wide table in a short card.
accessibility: The element genuinely scrolls, so Page Up/Down, Home/End, arrow keys, spacebar, trackpad momentum, `scrollIntoView`, find-in-page auto-scroll and every screen reader's virtual cursor keep working.

`role="region"` with `tabindex="0"` while it can scroll, because a scrollable region must be reachable by keyboard — and no tab stop when everything fits, where it would be a stop that does nothing. `tabStop` overrides it.
In RTL the vertical thumb sits on the left like a native scrollbar, and a horizontal thumb and its track paging run from the inline start.
A visually-hidden read-out reports the scroll position and how much of the content is visible — the cue a hidden scrollbar removes, and one a screen reader user never had.
Clicking the track pages by one viewport, as every native scrollbar on every platform does, rather than jumping the thumb to the pointer.

Edge Fades — The Only Affordance Left
Horizontal — The Same Thumb in RTL

components.name: Scroll to Top
components.description: Fixed scroll-progress ring overlay with circle/rounded/pill shapes, four appearances (solid, glass, gradient, outline) and a configurable show threshold.
whenToUse: Helping users return to the top of long, scroll-heavy pages.
Articles, feeds, documentation and dashboards with deep content.
Inside a scrollable panel, drawer or card via `contained` + `scrollTarget`.
For short pages it adds clutter — skip it.

examples.title: Move focus to the page heading
examples.description: Scroll AND move keyboard focus, so the next Tab starts at the top instead of from a button that just hid itself.

examples.title: Sharing a corner with a FAB
examples.description: Both join the shared floating layer: the dial keeps the corner, the button stacks above it.

customization: Circle, rounded or pill shapes.
Four appearances: solid, glass, gradient, outline — composable with any shape.
Progress ring recolours itself to match the appearance.
Viewport-fixed or `contained` inside a scrollable panel/drawer.
Configurable show threshold.
Shows live scroll progress.
Customisable button name via `ariaLabel`.

Floating layer: in the viewport-fixed mode the button joins the shared floating layer while it is shown (`floatingOrder`, default 20 — above a Speed Dial at 10), so it stacks clear of a FAB, affixed blocks and any region the host registers (chat, cookie banner, bottom nav), plus the device safe-area inset. Hidden, contained and demo buttons register nothing.
`scrollBehavior`: `smooth` (default) or `auto`. Smooth is downgraded to an instant jump under `prefers-reduced-motion`, read at click time.

`focusTarget`: `true` focuses `main h1`, else the first `h1`, else the first heading, inside the scroll root; a string is a CSS selector. A non-focusable target gets `tabindex="-1"`; focus moves with `preventScroll` so the scroll is not cut short. An invalid selector warns in dev mode and leaves focus alone. Unset, focus moves only when the button itself holds it (see Accessibility).

Variant axes: `variant` (circle, rounded, pill) and `appearance` (solid, glass, gradient, outline) are appearance; `showProgress`, `contained`, `scrollBehavior` and `focusTarget` are behavioural modes. The progress ring draws only on circle and rounded — pill has no room for it. Every appearance survives forced colors with a ButtonText edge; glass and gradient lose their surface there by design.

Scroll roots and containing blocks: `scrollTarget` wins, else the nearest scrollable ancestor, else the window. The floating layer is viewport-level, so `contained` buttons do not register. The fixed button is not portalled: an ancestor with `transform`, `filter`, `perspective`, `backdrop-filter`, `contain` or `container-type` becomes its containing block, so it pins to that ancestor instead of the viewport — keep it outside animated or filtered wrappers.

Browser limits: safe-area insets only apply with `viewport-fit=cover`; smooth scrolling is ignored by browsers without `scroll-behavior` support (the jump is instant); iOS's virtual keyboard can cover a fixed button.
accessibility: Labelled button (`ariaLabel`) that scrolls the page to the top.
Disabled, aria-hidden and removed from the tab order until it becomes visible.

Focus after scrolling: with `focusTarget` unset, focus that is elsewhere is left alone (a mouse click in Safari never focuses the button). But if the button itself holds focus when it is activated or hides, focus is never stranded on a control that just became `aria-hidden`: it moves to the page's main heading (as `focusTarget: true`), else to `main` / `[role="main"]`, made `tabindex="-1"`, else it is released to the document. A `demo` button never hides, so it keeps focus. An explicit `focusTarget` always wins.
Forced colors: the focus ring is a box shadow, which forced colors removes, so every shape and appearance also draws a system-coloured focus outline in that mode.
Reduced motion: no smooth scroll, and the show/hide and ring transitions are stilled.
The progress ring is decorative (`aria-hidden`) and has no text equivalent — it is not a reading-progress indicator for assistive tech.

examples.title: Composed: features as children, options from an adapter
examples.description: Features are content children that render nothing and register through a token; where the options come from is one adapter, svSelectSource from @styloviz/core, which owns search, paging and the loading / stale / error states. Each setting resolves as source, then feature child, then the select's built-in default.
examples.code:
<sv-select-dropdown [source]="people" [selectedOption]="current()" [(value)]="personId">
  <ng-container svSelectSearch searchPlaceholder="Search people…" />
</sv-select-dropdown>

<!-- Pro adds windowing and bulk selection the same way: -->
<sv-select-dropdown-pro [options]="rows()" [multiple]="true" [maxSelected]="10" [(value)]="ids">
  <ng-container svSelectSearch />
  <ng-container svSelectVirtual [optionHeight]="52" />
  <ng-container svSelectBulk selectAllLabel="Add everyone" />
</sv-select-dropdown-pro>

<!-- people = svSelectSource<SelectOption>({
       search: (term, signal, { offset, limit }) => api.people(term, offset, limit, signal),
       pageSize: 50,   // rows per "Load more"; 0 = whole answer per term
       minChars: 2,
     }); -->

customization: Pass `options` (and `groups`) for grouped lists; each option supports `icon` (an icon-library name), `avatarUrl`, `sublabel`, `badge` / `badgeColor` and `disabled`.
Toggle `multiple` and `clearable`; cap multi-select with `maxSelected` and size/style via `size` and `variant` (default · filled · flushed · floating).

Search is a content child: `<ng-container svSelectSearch />` turns it on, and it carries `searchPlaceholder`, `noResultsText`, `loadingText`, `minChars`, `debounceMs`, `serverSide` and `(searchChange)`. A member it leaves unbound keeps the select's default.

Pro: long flat lists window themselves above 150 rows; `<ng-container svSelectVirtual />` overrides `virtualThreshold`, `optionHeight` and `virtualViewportHeight`. Grouped lists are never windowed — headers and options are two different index spaces, and half-doing it would navigate wrongly.

Pro: `<ng-container svSelectBulk />` adds a tri-state "select all" to a multi-select (`selectAllLabel` for the wording). It acts on the VISIBLE, ENABLED options — not the whole array — deselects only what is on screen, and refuses (rather than filling up to) a `maxSelected` cap.

A server list is `[source]="svSelectSource({ search, pageSize, minChars, debounceMs })"` from `@styloviz/core`: it fetches on open, searches as the user types, pages on "Load more", retries a failure itself and owns the loading / stale / error states. A list it fetched is never filtered again. Closing aborts what is in flight but keeps what is on screen, so a live selection does not read as "Unavailable" the moment the panel shuts. Pass `selectedOption` for a value its list may not contain.
`loading` is the host's own switch for the trigger: set it while you resolve the selected entity, and the trigger spins, reports `aria-busy` and does not open.

Drive validation with `required`, `errorMessage`, `serverError` and `hint`; react to `selectionChange` and `dropdownOpen` / `dropdownClose`. Free ships only `svSelectSearch`; the Pro directives share its token and are ignored by the free select.
accessibility: Full ARIA combobox: `role="combobox"` with `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant`; the popup is a `role="listbox"` of `role="option"` rows with stable ids.
Keyboard: arrows, Home/End to move, Enter to select, Esc/Tab to close — the active option is scrolled into view and announced to screen readers.

Pro, windowed lists: the active option is always kept mounted. `aria-activedescendant` names it by DOM id, and a window that unmounted it would leave that id dangling — the screen reader then announces nothing at all as the user arrows. The spacer rows are `aria-hidden` so a windowed listbox does not report two unreachable phantom items.
A unique id is generated automatically so the `<label>` association, `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` (hint/error) always resolve, even without `inputId`.
Closes on outside click and returns focus to the trigger; programmatic `formControl.disable()` disables the native trigger.

inputs.name: serverError
inputs.description: A validation failure reported by the **server** — the 422 that comes back after submit, not something the client could have known. It is a separate input from `errorMessage` because it has a different lifetime, not because it needs a second way to show a string. A server error is a statement about *the value that was submitted*: the moment the user edits the field it stops being true, and this input expires itself rather than sitting there telling someone their new email is already taken. `errorMessage` has no such expiry — it is the host's to clear. While live it outranks `errorMessage`: it is the more specific fact, and it is the one the user has not seen yet. components.description: A floating row of actions over text the reader selects — quote it, ask about it, explain it — with a keyboard path for read-only text.

Any read-only text the user acts on a phrase at a time.
For rewriting text the user is editing, use the AI Writing Assistant.

examples.title: Quote into the composer

<sv-selection-toolbar class="block" [actions]="[{ id: 'quote', label: 'Quote', icon: 'quote' }, { id: 'explain', label: 'Explain' }]"
                      (action)="onAction($event)">

The host is an inline element: give it `block`, or `contents` to stay out of a flex or grid layout.

In `sv-ai-chat`, bind `[selectionActions]`; an action with id `quote` also quotes the selection into the composer.

Focus follows the keyboard into the toolbar, and only the keyboard — a mouse selection keeps the caret where it was.
Touch needs nothing extra: a long-press selection opens it the same way.

components.name: Sentiment Analysis Widget
components.description: 5 variants: summary (semicircle gauge + breakdown + KPIs), topics (stacked sentiment bars), timeline (SVG area + volume), feed (filter pills + source badges + score bars) and aspects (sentiment per subject — what is loved and what is hated).
whenToUse: Visualizing sentiment from reviews, support tickets, social or survey text.
You want summary gauges, per-topic breakdowns, trends and a source feed.
For raw numeric metrics, the Charts components are more general.
customization: Every content set is an input that starts EMPTY — `overallScore`, `topics`, `feedItems` and `timeline` — so an unwired widget shows no invented scores; demos pass the exported `DEMO_SCORE`, `DEMO_TOPICS`, `DEMO_FEED` and `DEMO_TIMELINE_BY_RANGE`.

`timeline` is shown exactly as given — `null` renders the empty state and never substitutes sample data — and `timeRangeChange` reports the range the user picked for you to refetch (a demo can bind `DEMO_TIMELINE_BY_RANGE[range]`).
Summary, topics, timeline, feed and aspects views.
Source badges and score bars.
Emits `timeRangeChange` when the analysis range changes.

`[classifier]` — model, version, languages, when it was last calibrated and its agreement with human labels — renders above every variant. A sentiment number without a classifier identity cannot be defended when somebody disputes it, and two figures from either side of a model swap are **not comparable at all**: the change measures the classifier, not the customers. With no classifier the widget says so — in every variant that has figures on screen, not only the summary — rather than rendering figures that cannot answer for themselves. Undeclared fields are named as gaps (‘Not recorded: Version, Calibrated’), and a dev build warns once when scores render without a model and its languages.

Calibration is not training. A model can be years old and calibrated last week, or new and never checked against this dataset — and the second is the one that quietly reports everything as mildly positive. An out-of-range `agreement` is **dropped rather than clamped**: 85 is a host that meant 0.85, and rendering '8500%' as if it were meant is worse than saying nothing.

`languages` is the field most often left out, and its absence is a silent failure that looks like data: an English-only classifier scores German reviews as **neutral** because it cannot read them, and neutral is indistinguishable from 'no strong feelings' on every chart here. `svClassifierReads()` matches on the primary subtag, so `de` covers `de-AT`, and an undeclared list means unknown rather than none. Set `FeedItem.language` and the feed marks each item the classifier cannot read as unclassified, not neutral.

`mixed` and `unknown` are first-class `SentimentLabel`s. “Love the camera, hate the battery” is two strong opinions, not a neutral one, and text the classifier could not read has no sentiment at all — folding either into `neutral` reports “no strong feelings” about text nobody measured. `SentimentBreakdown.mixed` / `.unknown` add rows to the summary breakdown and segments to the topic bars when present; an `unknown` feed item shows “Not scored” instead of a score; aspect means leave unknown mentions out. An item labelled `neutral` in a language the declared `classifier` does not read is shown as `unknown`, beside the note that says why.

`[aspectMinMentions]` (default `SV_ASPECT_MIN_MENTIONS`, 5, still exported) is the mention floor before an aspect is ranked worst/best or called divided. It is domain-sensitive — lower it for a B2B tool with forty reviews a month, raise it for a consumer app — and the “unranked” notice quotes the floor actually applied.
accessibility: Scores and breakdowns rendered as text.
Time-range and sentiment filters report aria-pressed; show-more toggles expose aria-expanded.
Filters are labelled, keyboard-operable controls.

Two figures from either side of a model swap are not comparable at all — the change measures the classifier, not the customers.

components.name: Sidebar Nav
components.description: The reusable half of a dashboard sidebar: grouped items, click-to-expand sub-navigation with an active trail, a collapsed rail and a mobile drawer — with no router dependency and no brand welded in. Bring your own header and footer. Pro adds rail flyouts, search, pinning, tones, floating and inset appearances and a resizable width.
whenToUse: The primary navigation of a dashboard, admin panel or internal tool.
You want the rail and the mobile drawer without writing route-sync three times.
Your app does not route the way Angular's router does — a hybrid shell, a micro-frontend, a widget embedded in somebody else's page.
For a horizontal header, use Mega Menu; for in-page sections, use Anchor. This is the persistent side rail.
Part of the App Shell family — Sidebar (shell) · Sidebar Nav (tree): `sv-sidebar` (in `@styloviz/layout`) is the collapsible container of a dashboard shell, and this is the tree you put inside it.

examples.title: Wiring it to the Angular router

customization: Expanded, collapsed rail and mobile drawer out of one model. The model and its route matcher (`svSidebarActiveItem`, `svSidebarRouteActive`) are exported, so your own navigation surfaces can reuse them rather than re-implementing route sync.
Badges per item, with four tints; sub-navigation groups per item.
`childKey` names the URL parameter that tracks the open sub-item, read through `SvNavLocation`; `activeChildId` pins it from host state instead.
`showHeader` / `showFooter` remove the chrome boxes entirely for a bare rail.

Items with children expand on click (chevron + `aria-expanded`), the active item's parents open by themselves, and `expandMode` (`multiple` · `single`) with `[(expandedIds)]` and `[(collapsedGroups)]` holds the state.

`activeStyle` (`fill` · `bar`), `badgeVariant` (`pill` · `count` · `dot`), `density` (`comfortable` · `compact`), `scrollFade` (`gradient` · `shadow` · `none`) and translatable `labels`; the mobile drawer has `drawerMode` (`overlay` · `push`), `swipeToClose` and `edgeSwipe`.

Pro (`sv-sidebar-nav-pro`, in `@styloviz-pro/layout`): rail `flyouts`, a `searchable` filter with `[(query)]`, `pinnable` items with `[(pinned)]`, `tone` (`auto` · `light` · `dark` · `dual`), `appearance` (`docked` · `floating` · `inset`), `glass`, and a `resizable` `[(width)]` between `minWidth` and `maxWidth`.
accessibility: Every destination is a real `<a href>`, so middle-click, ⌘-click and "copy link address" work — which they cannot when a router directive owns the element.
The current item carries `aria-current="page"`, as does the open sub-item.
The collapse control is a real `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and a label that says which way it will go.
A modified click is never intercepted: that gesture means "open this somewhere else".
The `<nav>` landmark takes its accessible name from `ariaLabel`.

Sidebar Nav — Accordion Groups with Active Trail
Sidebar Nav — Mobile Drawer — Overlay or Push, with Swipe
Sidebar Nav — Icon Rail with Flyouts
Sidebar Nav — Search, Pins, Workspace — Floating, Dark and Resizable

components.name: Signature Pad
components.description: Sign with a finger, a pen or a mouse. The signature is held as STROKES rather than pixels, so it survives a resize, undo removes a mark rather than a point, and export refuses to hand back a blank image from a pad nobody signed.
whenToUse: Consent, delivery confirmation, a contract, a waiver — anywhere a person signs.
You need the mark itself, not a typed name.
For a typed acknowledgement use a Checkbox with the terms beside it; a drawn signature that nobody checks is not stronger evidence.

examples.title: Gate a submit on a real signature
Export — and handle the empty case
Replay a stored signature at any size
examples.code: pad.setValue(saved);  // rescaled into the current box from saved.width/height

customization: **Not a `ControlValueAccessor`, and it cannot be one.** A CVA moves ONE value in and out of a form control; `SignatureValue` carries the stroke geometry, the typed name, and — once `attest()` has run — the consent wording, its digest, the timestamp and the signer metadata. Collapsed into a `formControlName` the host gets back a picture, which is the failure the attestation work exists to fix: E-SIGN, UETA and eIDAS care about intent, attribution and association with the record signed.

The contract instead: read `(signatureChange)` for a live draft, and call **`await signedValue()`** — not `value()` — for anything stored or sent. `attest()` returns `null` when the field is unsigned or no `consentText` was given, and a null is not an error to swallow: it means this signature is not a record. Validation is the host's; there is no `required` a form group can see, so use `(emptyChange)` or `isEmpty()`. `setValue()` restores a draft and keeps any attestation already on it — `value()` and `signedValue()` return the record as stored until a stroke, undo, clear or typed-name edit changes it — because re-attesting on load would date the record to the moment it was opened.

Size the drawing area with `size` (sm / md / lg); ink with `penColor` and `penWidth`; `pressureSensitive` varies the stroke where the device reports pressure (a mouse always reports 0.5, so it is off by default).
`showActions` toggles the Undo / Clear toolbar, `showBaseline` the signing rule, `hint` the helper text under the pad.
Public methods: `undo()`, `clear()`, `value()`, `setValue()`, `toDataUrl()`, `toSvgString()`, `attest()`, `signedValue()`.
accessibility: The canvas carries `role="img"` and is named by `label` — a `<canvas>` has no intrinsic name and no text inside it, so without that a screen reader announces nothing where the signature belongs.
Undo and Clear are real buttons, keyboard reachable, and disabled rather than hidden while there is nothing to act on — a toolbar that appears mid-signature moves the pad under the user's hand.
`touch-action: none` on the canvas stops the browser claiming the gesture for scrolling, which on a phone otherwise turns a signature into a dot and a page scroll.
The baseline and the prompt are DOM siblings rather than painted onto the bitmap, so neither is exported with the signature.
variants: Typing Your Name — because a canvas has no keyboard
Gating a Submit, and Exporting Honestly

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Accessible name for the pad. A `<canvas>` has no intrinsic name and no text inside it, so without this a screen reader announces nothing at all where the signature belongs.

inputs.name: hint
inputs.description: Helper text under the pad.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Height preset for the drawing area.

inputs.name: penColor
inputs.description: Ink colour. Any CSS colour.

inputs.name: penWidth
inputs.description: Stroke width in CSS pixels, before pressure.

inputs.name: pressureSensitive
inputs.description: Vary the stroke with pointer pressure where the device reports it. Off by default: a mouse reports a constant 0.5, so on the commonest input it changes nothing but the arithmetic.

inputs.name: showActions
inputs.description: Show the Undo / Clear toolbar.

inputs.name: showBaseline
inputs.description: Show the baseline the signature sits on.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Nothing can be drawn, and the actions are hidden.

inputs.name: readonly
inputs.description: Show a signature that has already been given: nothing can be drawn, typed, undone or cleared — like `disabled` — but at full opacity, with no "sign here" prompt and a solid border.

inputs.name: customClass
inputs.description: Extra classes on the root element.

inputs.name: allowTyped
inputs.description: Offer a typed name beside the pad.

inputs.name: typedNameLabel
inputs.description: Label for the typed-name field.

inputs.name: typedName
inputs.description: The typed name. Two-way bindable. The attestation wording is the host's. "By typing my name I agree to…" is a legal sentence about a specific agreement, and a component that invents one is writing contracts it has not read. Put it in `hint`.

inputs.name: consentText

inputs.name: signerMetadata
inputs.description: What the host knows about the signer — account id, session, IP, authentication method. Opaque to the component, hashed into the attestation.

components.name: Site Footer
components.description: Multi-column marketing / commerce footer: a brand block (logo, tagline, socials), configurable link columns, an optional newsletter signup, and a bottom bar with copyright, legal links and payment chips. Default, minimal and always-dark variants.
whenToUse: The global footer of a storefront, marketing site or dashboard-adjacent public page.
You want link columns plus a newsletter capture and trust signals (payments, legal) in one block.
Use the minimal variant for app-shell footers where a full sitemap would be too heavy.
Compare with App Shell: its `sv-footer` is the one-line bar inside a dashboard shell; this is the multi-column public footer.

examples.title: Newsletter request state + external links
examples.code:
<sv-site-footer
  brandName="Styloviz"
  [columns]="columns"
  [socials]="socials"
  [newsletter]="true"
  [newsletterStatus]="status()"
  [newsletterMessage]="message()"
  externalTarget="_blank"
  navLabel="Shop"
  legalNavLabel="Policies"
  (subscribe)="subscribe($event)" />

// subscribe(email: string) {
//   this.status.set('pending');
//   this.api.subscribe(email).subscribe({
//     next: () => { this.message.set('Check your inbox to confirm.'); this.status.set('success'); },
//     error: (e) => { this.message.set(e.message); this.status.set('error'); },
//   });
// }

customization: Brand block with optional logo, tagline and social icons.
Any number of link columns, each link with an optional badge.
Optional newsletter block (title / text / placeholder / CTA all configurable).
Bottom bar with legal links and payment chips; default / minimal / dark variants.
Newsletter request state: `newsletterStatus` (`idle` | `pending` | `success` | `error`) plus `newsletterMessage`. Leave it unbound and `subscribe` simply fires, with the field cleared on submit.
Landmark names: `footerLabel`, `navLabel`, `legalNavLabel`.
External-link policy: `externalTarget` (`_self` | `_blank`) and `newTabLabel`.

Variant axes: `variant` is the only APPEARANCE axis (default / minimal / dark). `newsletter`, `newsletterStatus` and `externalTarget` are BEHAVIOURAL. Known limits: `minimal` renders brand, legal links, socials and copyright only — `columns`, `tagline`, `payments` and the newsletter are not shown in it; `dark` ignores the page theme by design.
accessibility: Rendered as a labelled contentinfo footer landmark with nav landmarks for links and legal.
The newsletter field has an associated (visually-hidden) label and native email validation.

Newsletter status is announced through a polite live region that is always present (a region inserted with its text is not reliably announced). On `error` the field is `aria-invalid` and described by the message.
Focus while pending: the field goes read-only and the button `aria-disabled` rather than `disabled`, so the keyboard focus the user submitted from stays where it is; a second submit is ignored.

Each footer, and its heading and email field, gets a per-instance id, so two footers on one page never point their `aria-labelledby` at the first one's heading. The two `<nav>`s carry distinct names (`navLabel` / `legalNavLabel`); a dev-mode warning fires if they match.
Social and payment glyphs are decorative (aria-hidden) with accessible labels / titles on their controls; visible focus states in light and dark mode.

inputs.name: newsletterStatus
inputs.description: Where the host's newsletter request is: `idle`, `pending`, `success` or `error`. While `pending` the field is read-only, the button is `aria-disabled` (not `disabled`, which would strand the keyboard focus the user submitted from) and a second submit is ignored; `success`/`error` are announced politely. Left unbound, `subscribe` fires and the field clears at once.

inputs.name: newsletterMessage
inputs.description: The text announced for the current `newsletterStatus` — typically the server's own reason on `error`. Empty uses a short built-in message.

inputs.name: navLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name of the link-columns `<nav>`. Every `<nav>` on a page needs a DISTINCT name, or a screen-reader landmark list shows two identical entries — so if the page header already has a nav called "Footer" (unlikely) or you render two footers, rename it here.

inputs.name: legalNavLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name of the legal-links `<nav>`. Must differ from `navLabel`; a dev-mode warning fires when they match.

inputs.name: externalTarget
inputs.description: How links to ANOTHER origin open — social links and any absolute `http(s)` column or legal link. `_blank` adds a visually-hidden "(opens in a new tab)" to the name. Either way an external link always carries `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, and any `href` with an unsafe scheme (`javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`) is dropped rather than rendered.

inputs.name: newTabLabel
inputs.description: Suffix appended to an external link's accessible name when `externalTarget` is `_blank`.

outputs.name: linkSelect
outputs.description: Emitted when a column / navigation link is activated (an in-app href is also routed through `SV_LINK_ADAPTER` — don't navigate again from here when the app provides one) — and when a legal link with no rendered `href` (none given, or dropped by the URL policy) is activated, so the host can route it. A legal link WITH an href navigates natively and emits nothing.

outputs.name: subscribe
outputs.description: Emitted with the email when the newsletter form is submitted.

components.name: Skeleton Loader
components.description: Loading placeholders with wave/pulse animations and preset layouts.
whenToUse: Filling space while content loads, preserving the eventual layout.
Cards, lists, tables and profiles where you know the shape ahead of time.
When you can't predict the layout, a Spinner is simpler.

Not sure this is the right wait? Compare spinner, skeleton, progress bar, ring and the fullscreen spinner by duration, known progress and blocking in the “Choosing a feedback pattern” guide under Guides.

examples.title: Escape a load that never finishes
examples.code:
<!-- A stuck skeleton lies in the exact place the data was going: it says
     "the shape of your content is arriving" forever if the request failed
     silently. Both thresholds run from the moment the skeleton appears. -->
<sv-skeleton-loader
  preset="table"
  [slowAfterMs]="8000"
  [stalledAfterMs]="25000"
  stalledMessage="We couldn't load these rows."
  retryLabel="Try again"
  (retry)="reload()" />

customization: Preset layouts (text-block, card, list, table, dashboard…).
Wave or pulse animation.
Custom shapes via composition; `customClass` and `ariaLabel`.

Escalation: `[slowAfterMs]` says "this is taking longer than usual", `[stalledAfterMs]` says the content could not be loaded and can offer a `retryLabel` button wired to `(retry)`; `(escalated)` reports each step. Off by default, and shared with the Spinner — `createWaitEscalation` in `@styloviz/core`.

Delayed show and minimum duration: `[showAfterMs]` keeps a fast response from flashing bones and `[minVisibleMs]` keeps a skeleton that appeared from flickering away (a skeleton visible for 80 ms is a flicker). Bind `[active]="loading()"`, keep it mounted, and swap content in on `(visibleChange)` or with `createDelayedVisibility()` from `@styloviz/core`. Both default to 0 (shown at once).
accessibility: `role="status"` with a configurable `ariaLabel`, which is SAID once through the shared `SvLiveAnnouncer` when the skeleton first renders (politely, browser only, de-duplicated across skeletons) — a status region born with its name and no content is usually never read. Deliberately not `aria-busy`: that attribute tells assistive technology to stop reporting changes from the subtree, so putting it on this element would silence the very region it is here to speak from — and it could never flip back, because the skeleton is destroyed when content arrives rather than updated.
`aria-busy` belongs on the region whose contents are CHANGING — yours, around the swap — not on the placeholder, which IS the busy indicator.

Exactly one owner announces the wait. Leave `announce` on and say nothing yourself, or mark your own region busy, announce the transition, and set `[announce]="false"` so the skeleton becomes `aria-hidden` decoration. Two voices for one wait is worse than one.
Both wave and pulse animations stop under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

An escalation message renders INSIDE the existing `role="status"` wrapper rather than in a region of its own — one wait, one voice, and a region that already existed when the text appeared is what makes the change audible. With `[announce]="false"` the host owns the announcement of the stall too, along with everything else about the wait — but once a stalled skeleton offers its `retryLabel` button the wrapper stops being `aria-hidden`, because a focusable control inside a hidden subtree is reachable by Tab and unnamed to a screen reader.

Seen, not dazzling: bones sit between 1.15:1 and 2:1 against the page and the wave sheen moves them by 1.1–1.5:1 in both themes. Under forced colours the bones are `GrayText` rather than vanishing into the page.

inputs.name: preset
inputs.description: High-level composed preset. Set to `'custom'` (or omit) to control individual bone inputs.

inputs.name: shape
inputs.description: Shape of the skeleton bone.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: CSS width applied to the bone element. Accepts any valid CSS value: `'100%'`, `'8rem'`, `'w-1/2'` (Tailwind class).

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: CSS height applied to the bone element.

inputs.name: rounded
inputs.description: Border-radius override. Accepts Tailwind rounded-* class suffix: `'none'` `'sm'` `'md'` `'lg'` `'xl'` `'full'`. Shape defaults apply when left empty.

inputs.name: lines
inputs.description: Repeat this bone N times stacked vertically. Gaps between repeated lines are automatic.

inputs.name: shortLastLine
inputs.description: When `lines > 1`, make the last line shorter (like a real paragraph ending).

inputs.name: animation
inputs.description: Shimmer animation style.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Overall size multiplier that scales preset bone heights.

inputs.name: customClass
inputs.description: Additional CSS classes merged onto the root wrapper.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible label announced to screen readers while content loads.

inputs.name: announce
inputs.description: Whether this skeleton announces the wait itself.

inputs.name: slowAfterMs
inputs.description: Say "this is taking longer than usual" after this many ms. `0` = never. A stuck skeleton is indistinguishable from a failed request, and it lies in the exact place the data was going. It says "the shape of your content is arriving" — permanently, if the host's request failed silently. There was no timeout, no error and no retry: the placeholder simply outlived the thing it was standing in for. Off by default, because the honest threshold depends on what is loading and because turning it on adds text to every existing layout.

inputs.name: stalledAfterMs
inputs.description: Escalate to a stuck message (with a retry offer) after this many ms. Measured from the same start, not from `slowAfterMs`. `0` = never.

inputs.name: slowMessage
inputs.description: Message shown at the `slow` stage.

inputs.name: stalledMessage
inputs.description: Message shown at the `stalled` stage.

inputs.name: retryLabel
inputs.description: Label for the retry offer shown once the wait is `stalled`. `null` = none. An output cannot be asked whether anyone is listening, so the offer is an input: a placeholder that renders "Try again" and does nothing when it is pressed is worse than one that never offered.

inputs.name: active
inputs.description: Whether the wait is in progress. Bind it — `[active]="loading()"` — and keep the skeleton mounted when using `showAfterMs` / `minVisibleMs`: a skeleton the host removes cannot stay for its minimum.

inputs.name: showAfterMs
inputs.description: Appear only once the wait has lasted this long, in ms, so a fast response never flashes bones. `0` shows at once.

inputs.name: minVisibleMs
inputs.description: Once shown, stay at least this long, in ms — a skeleton visible for 80 ms is a flicker. `0` hides with `active`. Watch `(visibleChange)` (or use `createDelayedVisibility` from `@styloviz/core`) to swap the content in at the same moment.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The user pressed the retry offer on a stalled skeleton.

outputs.name: visibleChange
outputs.description: Emits whenever the skeleton appears (`true`) or leaves (`false`).

outputs.name: escalated
outputs.description: Fires on each escalation: `'slow'`, then `'stalled'`.

components.name: Slider
components.description: Range slider with single-value and dual-handle range mode, tick marks and step control.
whenToUse: Choosing an approximate numeric value within a known range (volume, price, opacity).
You need a price/value band — use `range` for dual handles.
When the exact number matters, pair with or prefer a Number Input.

examples.title: Dual-handle range
examples.description: Enable range to select a min/max band.

customization: Single value (`[(value)]`) or dual-handle range (`[(rangeStart)]` / `[(rangeEnd)]`, `range="true"`).
Configure `min`, `max`, `step`, optional `showTicks` / `tickCount`, and a `prefix` / `suffix` value readout (`showValue`).
Pick a `variant` and `size`; name the control with `label` or `ariaLabel`.
accessibility: Built on the native `<input type="range">`, so it has implicit `role="slider"` and full keyboard support — arrows nudge by `step`, Home/End jump to bounds, PageUp/PageDown step larger.
The single slider associates its `label` via `for`/`id` (or set `ariaLabel`); `prefix`/`suffix` are announced through `aria-valuetext` (e.g. "70%").
Range handles expose `aria-valuetext` and dynamic `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax` (each handle bounded by the other); the thumb shows a clear focus ring.
Implements ControlValueAccessor for the single value — works with `[(ngModel)]` and reactive forms; `formControl.disable()` disables the slider.

Right-to-left is handled by the platform for the keyboard and by CSS for the layout: the native input flips Left/Right and the thumb itself, and the fill, bubbles and insets use `inset-inline-*` so they resolve from the same `direction` rather than a second guess at it. The component adds no key handler of its own — that would have to re-derive the platform's behaviour and would disagree with it somewhere.
`aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` are numbers and do not flip: a screen reader announces 40 of 100 whichever way the track is drawn.
variants: Two Handles, One Track — and a field for the exact number

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Single slider value. Use `[(value)]` for two-way binding.

inputs.name: rangeStart
inputs.description: Range slider lower bound. Use with `range=true`.

inputs.name: rangeEnd

inputs.name: range
inputs.description: Enable range (two-handle) mode.

inputs.name: minGap
inputs.description: Smallest allowed distance between the two handles. `null` uses one `step`.

inputs.name: showInputs
inputs.description: Render a number field bound to each handle.

inputs.name: min
inputs.description: Minimum value.

inputs.name: max
inputs.description: Maximum value.

inputs.name: step
inputs.description: Step increment.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Optional label above the slider.

inputs.name: inputId

inputs.name: valueFormat
inputs.description: Turn a raw value into the text on the bubbles and the min/max labels. A price range slider is the case this exists for. Without it the scale under the track reads `200000 … 4000000`, which is a number a computer wrote; with `formatMoneyShort` it reads `$200k … $4M`. `prefix`/`suffix` cannot do this — they concatenate, they do not format, so no combination of them produces a grouped or abbreviated figure. Pass a STABLE reference (a class field or a bound method), not an arrow written in the template: a new function identity on every change detection pass defeats the memoisation on the computed signals below.
