inputs.name: turn
inputs.description: Where the turn is. Two-way, so the host can drive it from its own recogniser and the component can move it on a user action.

inputs.name: levels
inputs.description: Measured input amplitude, 0–1, oldest first. This is the one input that makes the meter honest. Feed it from an `AnalyserNode` — `getByteFrequencyData`, averaged and scaled — and the bars mean something. Leave it empty and the meter says the microphone is silent, which is the truth about a microphone nobody is measuring.

inputs.name: transcript
inputs.description: The transcript so far, interim segments included.

inputs.name: copyable
inputs.description: Show the settled-transcript copy affordance.

inputs.name: silenceFrames
inputs.description: Quiet frames before the component suggests the turn has ended. Not one. The pause between two words is a quiet frame, and so is the breath before the most important clause.

inputs.name: ambientLevels
inputs.description: Ambient amplitude measured while nobody was talking, for calibration. `SV_SILENCE_LEVEL` is a guess about a quiet office. In a car, a café or a warehouse the ambient floor sits above it, so every frame reads as speech: the auto-stop never fires, `hearing` is permanently true, and the meter claims to hear a user who has not spoken. Feed the first second of capture in here and the threshold is measured instead. Left empty, nothing changes: the default threshold stands, and a floor calibrated from two frames is a floor calibrated from a cough.

inputs.name: lowConfidence
inputs.description: Final segments whose recogniser confidence is below this are marked uncertain ("?" chip, and said in the segment's accessible name). Tune it to your recogniser: confidence scales are vendor-specific. Clamped to 0–1; a non-finite value falls back to the default.

inputs.name: consentRequired
inputs.description: Whether capture needs the user's agreement first. The microphone permission is not consent. The browser asks whether the page may use the microphone; it does not ask whether the user agrees to their voice being transcribed, stored, or sent to a third-party model, and in several jurisdictions that is the question that matters.

inputs.name: consent
inputs.description: The user's answer. Two-way, so a host can persist it. `declined` is a person saying no, which is a different fact from a browser saying no (`turn: 'denied'`) — the difference between "this is not for me" and "fix your settings".

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: Emitted when the user presses the error panel's "Try again" button (retryable errors only); the host should re-run the failed session setup.

outputs.name: action
outputs.description: The user asked to start, stop or interrupt.

outputs.name: silenceDetected
outputs.description: A run of silence has lasted `silenceFrames` while listening, so the turn may be over. Fires once per run of silence — not on every quiet frame of the same pause — and again only after speech has broken the run.

outputs.name: turnChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `turn` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(turn)]`.

outputs.name: consentChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `consent` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(consent)]`.

components.name: Waterfall Chart
components.description: 2 orientations with floating bars, dashed connectors, increase/decrease/total color-coding, data labels, tooltips and per-bar entrance animations. Pure SVG.
whenToUse: Explaining how a starting value reaches an ending value through gains/losses.
Financial bridges (revenue → net), inventory changes, budget variance.
For plain category totals, use a Bar Chart.
customization: Vertical or horizontal orientation.
Increase / decrease / total color coding.
Dashed connectors and data labels.

Every point declares what it is through `kind` — `'delta'` (a step that moves the running total), `'subtotal'` (a running sum drawn from zero that does not advance it) or `'total'`. `isTotal` / `isIntermediate` remain as shorthand for the last two. Nothing is inferred: a point whose `value` is missing is not read as a total, so a row that failed to load never renders a figure the data did not claim in the position a reader trusts most.

`value` on a `subtotal` or `total` is the figure your source **states** for it, and it is optional. The bar is always drawn from the steps before it — the connectors and every preceding bar have to agree with it — and any disagreement is reported: on the bar (`480 ≠ 500` plus a dashed outline), in a sentence under the plot, in the bar's accessible name and in the data table. `totalTolerance` widens the band two figures may sit apart before that happens; it defaults to 0, subject to a floating-point band that scales with the numbers, so `0.1 + 0.2` against `0.3` is not reported as a hole.

`valuePolicy` decides what happens to a step this chart cannot draw — one whose `value` is absent, `NaN` or `Infinity`. A negative is not one of these: a waterfall is built out of falls as much as rises. `clamp` (default) moves the running total by nothing, marks the bar and names it under the plot; `reject` refuses the series and shows the error state. `omit` is not offered, because a bar's position is its place in a sequence and dropping one silently rewrites every total after it. `render` is not offered either — there is no honest way to draw a step of unknown size.

Order is part of the data. Each bar starts where the last one ended, so `[+100, −50, subtotal]` and `[+100, subtotal, −50]` are different statements, and the subtotal reports 50 in one and 100 in the other. Sort before passing the series in; the component will not do it for you, including when the source is an unordered one (a `Map`, an object's keys, a `Promise.all` result).
accessibility: Each bar is keyboard-focusable (`role="button"`, Tab) and its `aria-label` carries the delta AND the running total after it. The running total is drawn as a bar's vertical position and spoken by a hover tooltip, so without it a keyboard reader learned every step and never where the total stood — in a chart whose whole subject is where the total stands.
Tooltip appears on hover and on focus; Enter/Space emits `barSelect`. Color coding is paired with labels.

A visually-hidden table lists every step in order with its step number, type, change and running total — the sequence is the meaning here, so the number is data rather than decoration. It stays when `showLegend` is off: the legend is a display option, the alternative to the plot is not.

Whatever the chart had to alter or could not reconcile is stated in the rendered output, not in `console.warn`. A total that does not add up is the most consequential thing this chart can discover, and the person it matters to is reading a dashboard, not a browser console. The dashed outline in the plot gets a legend key, so the mark is never colour-only.
variants: Waterfall — P&L Bridge, Revenue to Net Income

components.name: Watermark
components.description: A repeating overlay tiled from the ROTATED bounding box, so the marks neither collide nor gap at an angle. Staggered rows, an opacity band that says which way it is wrong, and a signature a host can compare against to detect tampering.
whenToUse: Marking a document, preview or export with its classification or the viewer's identity.
Deterring the casual crop-and-share, which is what almost every real leak actually is.
NOT as a security control — anything rendered in the browser can be removed by somebody with the page source.

examples.title: Measure manually
examples.description: Re-tiling on resize and after web fonts load is automatic. Turn it off to drive measure() yourself.
examples.code:
<sv-watermark #mark text="Confidential" [observeResize]="false">…</sv-watermark>

// after the container changes size
mark.measure();

examples.title: A viewer token instead of a name
examples.description: The id is hashed into an opaque token; the raw id never reaches the DOM. Salt it with a value the client cannot guess, or mint the token on the server.
examples.code:
<sv-watermark text="Confidential" [viewerId]="user.id" [viewerSalt]="deploymentSalt">…</sv-watermark>

// or build the text yourself
import { svViewerToken } from '@styloviz/watermark';
const text = 'Confidential · ' + svViewerToken(user.id, deploymentSalt);

examples.title: Detect a removed or edited mark
examples.description: Capture the signature once, then compare periodically. It checks the configuration, the rendered overlay (present, visible, untransformed, at the configured opacity, carrying the signature) and every mark in it (the expected count, the expected text, none hidden, transparent or zero-size), so an edit in place is caught as well as a deletion. It proves a DOM change in this browser — nothing more.
examples.code:
<sv-watermark #mark text="Confidential" (tampered)="onTampered()">…</sv-watermark>

const expected = mark.signature();
setInterval(() => mark.checkIntegrity(expected), 2000);

customization: Three variants: `tiled`, `single` and `inspect` (which shows the tile arithmetic and the opacity verdict).
Any `text`, `angle`, `fontSize`, `opacity` and per-axis gaps.
Row stagger on or off.
`signature()` + `checkIntegrity(expected)` + the `tampered` output, which reports (it does not restore) a removed, hidden or edited overlay.

Threat model: watermarking is deterrence, not security. `tampered` means a client-side DOM mutation (or configuration change) was observed; it does not mean the content is protected, and it is not a compliance control.

Durable marks are server-side: the only watermark that survives is one burned into the bytes the user receives. Stamp exports, PDFs, images and downloads on the SERVER — the same viewer token, rendered into the file before it leaves your backend — and treat this client mark as a deterrent on screen only. Anything drawn in the browser is removed with the developer tools, absent from a "Save as PDF" made with backgrounds off, and never present in a file fetched straight from your API.

Privacy: `viewerId` + `viewerSalt` append an opaque token (`svViewerToken`, a 32-bit FNV-1a hash — not a secret; salt it or mint it server-side). The mark text also lands in the DOM, the visually-hidden label and `data-sv-signature`.

Measurement: re-tiling is automatic — a ResizeObserver (`svElementSize`, border box, one measurement per frame) re-tiles when the box resizes, and `document.fonts` re-measures the text after web fonts load. Set `[observeResize]="false"` to call `measure()` yourself. The server renders no marks (zero size); the browser tiles on hydration.

Variant axes: `variant` (tiled, single, inspect) and `angle`, `fontSize`, `opacity`, gaps, `stagger` are appearance; `observeResize` and `viewerId` are behavioural and combine with every variant. `single` ignores gaps and stagger.

Containing block: the overlay is `position: absolute; inset: 0` inside the component's own relative box, so it covers what is projected into it — not a scrolled-away part of an inner scroll container, and not a body portal (menus, dialogs) opened from inside it.

Browser limits: `document.fonts` is missing in some embedded webviews (the estimate is kept); forced-colors mode may repaint the marks in system colours; and anything rendered client-side can be removed by somebody with the page source.
accessibility: The overlay is `pointer-events: none`, so it never intercepts a click meant for the content underneath — the commonest way this control ships broken, and one whose symptom (buttons that do nothing) never looks like a watermark bug.
The repeated marks are `aria-hidden`; the mark is announced once, in words, in a visually-hidden label. A screen reader reading "Confidential" forty times is not accessibility.
The marks are `select-none`, so a watermark never lands in the clipboard when somebody copies a paragraph.

RTL: every mark carries `dir="auto"`, so an Arabic or Hebrew mark over an LTR page — or a Latin mark with a viewer token over an RTL page — keeps its words in order. The tiling stays physical on purpose: the overlay covers the whole box whichever way the page runs.
variants: Tiled — Sized From the Rotated Box
Inspect — The Opacity Band, and the Caveat

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Presentation: `'tiled'` across the whole box, one centred `'single'` mark, or `'inspect'` (tiled plus a note on what the mark is and is not).

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The mark. PRIVACY: whatever you put here is published to every screenshot, screen share and support ticket the page appears in — and to the DOM, the visually-hidden label and the `data-sv-signature` attribute. Do not put a viewer's name or email here; bind `viewerId` (or a server-minted token) instead. Dev mode warns once when the text looks like an email address.

inputs.name: viewerId
inputs.description: An id identifying the viewer, hashed into an opaque token by `svViewerToken(viewerId, viewerSalt)` and appended to the mark as `text · token`. The raw id never reaches the DOM. The token identifies the viewer only to whoever can map it back — your server — rather than to every recipient of every screenshot. It is a hash, not a secret: see `svViewerToken` for why a guessable id space needs a salt.

inputs.name: viewerSalt
inputs.description: Salt mixed into the viewer token. Use a per-deployment value the client cannot guess.

inputs.name: angle
inputs.description: Rotation in degrees.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description: 0–1. Outside roughly 0.04–0.25 the mark stops working — see `opacityVerdict`.

inputs.name: fontSize
inputs.description: Font size in px.

inputs.name: gapX
inputs.description: Extra space between marks, in px.

inputs.name: gapY
inputs.description: Extra vertical space between rows of marks, in px.

inputs.name: stagger
inputs.description: Offset every other row by half a tile. A square grid reads as columns, and columns leave clean vertical stripes a screenshot can be cropped to.

inputs.name: observeResize
inputs.description: Re-tile automatically when the box resizes (a `ResizeObserver` through `svElementSize`, throttled to one measurement per frame) and when web fonts finish loading. Turn it off to drive `measure()` yourself — e.g. for a box whose size you already track, or in a test. Without it a resized box keeps the tiling it was measured at — gaps down one edge when it grows, marks stacked past the clip when it shrinks. The observer measures the border box on the first render, so the first paint is already tiled; the server renders no marks (zero size) and the browser tiles on hydration.

outputs.name: tampered
outputs.description: Emitted by `checkIntegrity()` when the mark in the DOM does not match the signature the host captured. What it proves, precisely: that at the moment of the check, in this browser, the rendered overlay was missing, hidden, or carried a different configuration (text, angle, opacity, font size) than the one expected — i.e. a client-side DOM mutation, or a configuration change, was observed. What it does not prove: that the content is protected, that nobody screenshotted it first, that a silent check means the mark was intact (the check runs in the same page an attacker controls; they can stub it, block the event, or copy the content out of the DOM without touching the overlay), or anything a compliance control needs — it is not an audit record, not tamper-evident, and not server-verified. The mark is not restored. Watermarking is deterrence, not security: treat this event as a telemetry hint, never as a control. A durable mark is burned in on the server (an exported PDF or image).

components.name: Widget Grid
components.description: A dashboard grid that lays out YOUR widgets — ordered, hideable, reorderable by keyboard, one arrangement per width, layout persisted — with eight ready compositions to start from and your own template inside any card.
whenToUse: Composing a dashboard from mixed widgets: KPIs, charts, funnels, feeds.
You want a ready, responsive grid instead of hand-laying CSS grid.
For a single metric, a Stat Card alone is enough.

examples.title: Your own widgets
Your own content inside a card
examples.code: {{ tile.value }}

examples.title: A layout save that fails

customization: `tiles` is the grid's real input: pass your own widgets and everything the customizable grid does — order, hide, restore, reset, one arrangement per width, versioned persistence, keyboard reorder, the announcements and the alternative summary table — runs over them. Leave it off and it falls back to `variant()`'s demo dashboard, which is what the eight showcase compositions are.

Widget ids must be unique and stable. The id is what a saved layout stores, so an id derived from an array index rearranges the dashboard the next time the array does. Ids in a stored layout that name no widget are ignored, so adding and removing widgets between releases is safe.

Project `<ng-template svWidgetBody="<id>" let-tile>` to fill a card with your own content — a chart, a table, a feed. `svWidgetBody="*"` catches every widget with no template of its own. The card's frame stays the grid's (label, move/remove controls, position announcement, `role="listitem"`), because a host that had to rebuild the chrome to get custom content would be rebuilding the accessible part.

A projected body replaces the KPI card, not the widget: the alternative summary table still reports the tile's value, change and trend, so choosing a custom rendering never drops the widget from the one place a screen reader can compare the widgets against each other.
Eight ready dashboard compositions (set via `variant`).
Mix KPI, chart, funnel and feed widgets.

Set `customizable` for an interactive KPI grid — remove/restore/reorder widgets; add `persistKey` to save the layout to `localStorage` as a versioned `sv-widget-grid/layout` envelope, so a blob from an older release is migrated where it can be and ignored where it cannot rather than restoring a dashboard that is subtly wrong.
Listen to `(layoutChange)` to sync the layout (order + hidden widgets) to your own backend — it fires on every change regardless of `persistKey`.

`(layoutChange)` carries `requestKey` and `rollback()`: the grid rearranges optimistically, so the payload is also the way back if the write fails. `rollback()` restores both order and hidden set, and unwrites the `persistKey` copy so a reload does not resurrect the failed layout.
`savingLayout` locks every customize control while a change is being written; `layoutError` reports a failed save above the grid, full width, since the change could have been anywhere in it.
Two-way `hiddenWidgetIds` and `widgetOrder` let a host seed the layout from its own backend. `localStorage` only ever seeds an empty layout, so a bound layout always wins.
Reset appears as soon as the layout differs from the variant's own — after a reorder, not only after a removal.
Responsive reflow across breakpoints; name the dashboard with `ariaLabel`.
On touch screens the interactive tile controls (reorder / remove) are always visible instead of hover-only, so they stay usable without a pointer.

One arrangement per width, not one arrangement stretched. Four tiles in a row and four tiles in a column are different arrangements of the same dashboard, so a customization is filed under the width it was made at — `base`, `sm` (640px) or `xl` (1280px), matching the three column counts the grid actually renders. Rearranging on a laptop leaves the phone arrangement as it was.

A width with no arrangement of its own inherits from the nearest WIDER one, then from the last arrangement made anywhere. A dashboard gets arranged on the big screen, so a phone opening it the first time should start from the user's own layout rather than from a variant default nobody chose.

The saved blob only grows a `byBreakpoint` member once a second width is customized, so a layout stored by an earlier release still restores unchanged and the schema version does not move. A resize deliberately does NOT emit `(layoutChange)` — nothing the user did changed, and a host saving on resize would overwrite one width's arrangement with another's.

Read `activeBreakpoint()` to see which width the grid is laid out at. It is read-only on purpose: it is a fact about the viewport, not a setting, and a bound value fighting the media queries would put the grid in an arrangement the CSS is not rendering.
Reset clears every width, not just the current one — it is the only route back to the variant's own layout, and one that left the phone rearranged would not do what it is called.
accessibility: Row/column placement and span ARE the layout, so the grid publishes a metrics table — one row per visible tile with its value, change and a described trend — plus an overview saying how many of the total are shown and how many are down on the previous period. A hidden tile is absent from both, so the summary can never claim a figure that is not on screen.

The change cell joins the number to its `changeLabel` ("+12% vs last month"). On screen the chip shows a bare "+12%" and the period it is measured against is a separate span beside it; out of that layout the two have to be one phrase or the number means nothing.
The sparkline gets a described shape rather than being dropped, so the trend column says something a listener can use.
Each composition is a labelled `region` (`ariaLabel`) with a logical reading order.

In customizable mode, reorder and remove controls are keyboard-operable buttons named per widget AND per position — "Move Revenue later, position 2 of 8", not eight identical "Move widget later"s. The position is how a listener knows the press did anything.

Every customize gesture is announced through an `sr-only` `role="status"` live region: where the tile went, how many are shown after a removal, where a restored one landed. The controls were always real buttons, so the gesture always worked — a keyboard user simply had no way to tell that it had.

Focus survives every gesture. A browser blurs a control the instant it is `disabled`, and removing a tile destroys the button that was pressed, so each gesture re-focuses an ordered fallback list: the same control if it still exists, else its sibling, else the grid.

Focus survives the SAVE too, which is the case a host actually hits. `savingLayout` disables every control at the instant the gesture changes the layout, so there is nothing to land on yet — the target is held and honoured when the save releases the controls, however long the backend takes. And because a rejected save rolls back exactly the control the gesture aimed at (a removal aims at the restore chip; the rollback puts the tile back and the chip goes), each fallback list carries both sides, so the failure path lands on the widget too. Focus you moved elsewhere during the save is never pulled back.

A removed widget is recoverable. The restore chips sit in a `role="group"` labelled "Hidden widgets", each named "Restore <widget>", and focus after a removal lands on that widget's own chip — so the way back is the next thing you meet, not something to go hunting for. A restored widget returns to its original slot rather than the end.
With everything hidden, the empty state names the control to press instead of pointing "above", which is not a direction a screen reader has.
While `savingLayout` is set, every customize control is `disabled` and carries `aria-busy="true"`, so a screen-reader user is told the layout is being written rather than finding dead buttons.
A failed save is announced: `layoutError` renders as `role="alert"` above the grid, so it reaches assistive tech without stealing focus.
Trend chips convey direction with text ("increased/decreased by"), not color alone; decorative charts/sparklines are hidden from assistive tech.
variants: Rearranging a Dashboard, and a Save That Fails

inputs.name: tiles
inputs.description: The widgets to lay out. Supply this and the grid is a grid of *your* widgets; leave it and it renders `variant()`'s demo dashboard. Every id must be unique and stable — it is what a saved layout stores, so an id derived from an array index rearranges the dashboard the next time the array does. Ids in a stored layout that name no widget here are ignored, so adding and removing widgets between releases is safe. Only `[customizable]` mode reads this; the eight variant dashboards are static compositions with their own content.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Dashboard composition variant (saas-kpi, analytics, ecommerce, crm-pipeline, fintech, devops, glassmorphism, hr-analytics).

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name for the dashboard region.

inputs.name: customizable
inputs.description: Enables an interactive, customizable KPI grid over the active variant's tiles: users can remove, restore and reorder widgets. Off by default: the grid renders its tiles as a static layout.

inputs.name: persistKey
inputs.description: When set, the customizable layout (order + hidden widgets) is persisted to `localStorage` under this key and restored on load.

inputs.name: savingLayout
inputs.description: True while a layout change is being written to the host's backend. Every customize control stops responding, so a second change cannot start on top of the first and leave `rollback()` holding a layout that predates it.

inputs.name: layoutError
inputs.description: The last layout change did not save. Reported above the grid; the tiles stay where the user put them, because that is what they are looking at and the component cannot know whether the host means to retry.

inputs.name: hiddenWidgetIds
inputs.description: Widget ids the user has removed (two-way). A `model` because `persistKey` could only ever store the layout on *this* device: a host with a server-side dashboard layout had `(layoutChange)` to observe it and no way at all to put it back. Binding a value wins over whatever `localStorage` holds.

inputs.name: widgetOrder
inputs.description: Widget ids in display order (two-way); ids missing from it follow in the variant's own order, so a partial list is valid. See `hiddenWidgetIds`.

outputs.name: layoutChange
outputs.description: Emitted whenever the user changes the layout (remove / restore / reorder / reset), so a parent can sync it to its own backend. Fires regardless of `persistKey`; not emitted on initial load. Kept alongside the two-way `hiddenWidgetIds` / `widgetOrder` rather than replaced by them: this carries both halves of the layout in one atomic snapshot, which is the shape a host PUTs to its backend. The models emit separately (a reorder touches only one of them), so they answer "what is the order now", not "the layout changed".

outputs.name: hiddenWidgetIdsChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `hiddenWidgetIds` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(hiddenWidgetIds)]`.

outputs.name: widgetOrderChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `widgetOrder` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(widgetOrder)]`.

components.name: Workspace Switcher
components.description: The current workspace of a multi-tenant dashboard and the one place it changes. A body-portalled panel lists favourite and recent workspaces and every workspace grouped by organization, with a search across all of them, a favourite star per row, locked workspaces that say why, and Create / Manage actions. The switch itself is an explicit state: a pick sets `switchingTo`, the trigger goes busy and announces it, and the host commits by setting `currentId` — so the old tenant's data never stays on screen under the new tenant's name.
whenToUse: Job: context — a multi-tenant dashboard where the same screens show a different organization, project or account depending on the workspace.
The user belongs to several workspaces, across organizations, and switches often enough to want favourites and recents.
For moving between pages of one workspace, use Sidebar Nav or Mega Menu; for a one-off choice in a form, use Select.

examples.title: Commit or abandon a switch
Server-loaded list, and a collapsed rail

customization: `groupBy` `org` (the default) or `none`; `searchable`, `favoritesEnabled`, `canCreate`, `canManage`.
Per-workspace `initials`, `tone`, `role`, `description` and `badge`.
`compact` shows only the avatar, for a collapsed sidebar rail.
`loading`, `error` and `(retry)` for a list loaded from a server; an empty list offers Create.
`surfaceId` names it in the navigation-analytics stream (`provideSvNavTelemetry()`).
accessibility: The trigger is a button with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`; its accessible name says which workspace is current and that it switches.
The panel is a labelled dialog: focus goes to the search field, ↑/↓ move through the rows (locked rows are skipped), Home/End jump, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger, Tab leaves.
Rows are grouped (`role="group"`, labelled by their heading); the current row carries `aria-current`; a locked row is `aria-disabled` and described by its reason.
Favourite stars are toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`) with a per-workspace name; every target is at least 32 px.
Switching, switched and a failed switch are announced through the shared live region, and the element is `aria-busy` while a switch is in flight.
variants: Switch with an Explicit Loading State

inputs.name: workspaces
inputs.description: Every workspace the user can see, in display order within each organization.

inputs.name: currentId
inputs.description: The id of the workspace the user is in now (two-way — the host commits a switch by setting it).

inputs.name: switchingTo
inputs.description: The workspace being switched to while the host loads it (two-way). Set by a pick; the host clears it on failure, and it clears itself when `currentId` arrives at it. Blank stale views while it is non-null.

inputs.name: favoriteIds
inputs.description: Ids of the user's favourite workspaces, in the order shown (two-way; the stars write it).

inputs.name: recentIds
inputs.description: Ids of recently visited workspaces, most recent first — the first three (other than the current one) are shown.

inputs.name: groupBy
inputs.description: Group the full list by `org` (`'org'`) or show one flat list (`'none'`).

inputs.name: searchable
inputs.description: Show the search field.

inputs.name: favoritesEnabled
inputs.description: Show the star toggles and the Favourites section.

inputs.name: canCreate
inputs.description: Show the "Create workspace" action — hide it for users who may not create one.

inputs.name: canManage
inputs.description: Show the "Manage workspaces" action.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: The workspace list is loading — the panel shows a skeleton.

inputs.name: error
inputs.description: The workspace list failed to load — the panel shows the error and a retry.

inputs.name: compact
inputs.description: Show only the avatar on the trigger (for a collapsed sidebar). The name stays the accessible name.

inputs.name: surfaceId
inputs.description: Names this switcher in the shared navigation-analytics stream — a static name, never a record id.

outputs.name: switchRequest
outputs.description: The user picked a workspace. Perform the switch, then set `currentId` (or clear `switchingTo` on failure).

outputs.name: favoriteChange
outputs.description: A favourite star was toggled (`favoriteIds` has already been updated).

outputs.name: create
outputs.description: "Create workspace" was chosen.

outputs.name: manage
outputs.description: "Manage workspaces" was chosen.

outputs.name: retry
outputs.description: The error state's Retry was pressed — reload the workspace list.

outputs.name: openChange
outputs.description: The panel opened (`true`) or closed (`false`).

outputs.name: currentIdChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `currentId` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(currentId)]`.

outputs.name: switchingToChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `switchingTo` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(switchingTo)]`.

outputs.name: favoriteIdsChange
outputs.description: Emits the new `favoriteIds` whenever it changes — the output half of `[(favoriteIds)]`.

templates.title: Styloviz Account Template
templates.description: Profile, security and notifications in tabs, a team roster with role filters and pending invites, and plan & billing with seats, payment method and invoices — a drop-in account area for any app. Teal/cyan shell.

templates.title: Styloviz Admin Panel Template
templates.description: Ready-to-use SaaS admin panel — 49 pages across 10 dashboards and 8 app modules, with a self-contained Midnight Pro shell (sidebar, header, dark mode).

templates.title: Styloviz AI Ops Console Template
templates.description: Dark-first admin for AI/LLM products — chat playground, agent run monitor, token spend analytics, model comparison, RAG knowledge base, workflow builder, and a prompt library.

templates.title: Styloviz Auth Template
templates.description: The complete set of pre-session screens — sign in with providers, register with a live policy checklist, two-step verification with recovery codes, single sign-on discovered from the email domain, a lock screen that knows who it locked, and the forgot / reset-password pair. Indigo/sky shell, mock-or-live data switch.

templates.title: Styloviz Blog / Agency Site Template
templates.description: A blog-first site for a small agency — a home page led by the featured post, a searchable index with tag, author and month filters kept in the URL, articles with a table of contents, series and related posts rendered by the kit's safe Markdown renderer, three services with indicative pricing, an enquiry form and a newsletter sign-up.

templates.title: Styloviz Bookings Template
templates.description: Appointments for a clinic, studio or salon — a schedule by practitioner that refuses double booking, a booking flow on sv-slot-picker with the same availability rules, check-in to completion with no-show and cancel-with-reason, a live waiting room, practitioners' hours and leave, and invoices. Stores no clinical records. Berry/cyan shell, mock-or-live data switch.

templates.title: Styloviz Calendar Template
templates.description: A working calendar — month, week, day and agenda views, calendars you can switch on and off from the rail, search across titles, locations and attendees, clash detection shown before you save rather than after, and create / edit / delete against a mock-or-live API. Blue/violet shell.

templates.title: Styloviz Team Chat Template
templates.description: A working team messenger — public and private channels, direct messages, threads in a side panel, presence with each person's local time, mention autocomplete that warns when someone cannot see the room, failed sends that offer Retry, and an unread divider where you left off. Plum/emerald shell, mock-or-live data switch.

templates.title: Styloviz CRM Template
templates.description: A working sales CRM — a deal pipeline where the column is the stage (drag, or Space and the arrow keys; a move to Lost asks why), deal pages with an activity timeline, a leads inbox with CSV import, follow-ups as a list or a calendar, quotes in integer cents, and a forecast by month and by owner against quota. Orange/emerald shell, mock-or-live data switch.

templates.title: Styloviz CRUD Blocks Template
templates.description: Create, read, update and delete for one resource through four surfaces — a table, a create modal, an edit drawer and a naming confirm — with one form component and one set of validation rules behind both the modal and the drawer.

templates.title: Styloviz Developer Portfolio Template
templates.description: A software engineer's personal site — an interactive terminal hero you can actually type into, ⌘K command-palette navigation, case studies that show the real diff and the number it moved, a contribution year, a skills radar and a career timeline. Dark by default, lime signal accent, mock-or-live data switch.

templates.title: Styloviz Documentation Site Template
templates.description: A documentation site — guides, an API reference and a changelog, with each article's table of contents built from its headings, previous / next in the sidebar's order, search by section, a broken-link and review-date check on the home page, and a not-found page that suggests near misses. Green/orange shell, mock-or-live data switch.

templates.title: Styloviz Errors Template
templates.description: Fourteen system pages — every common 4xx and 5xx, plus offline, maintenance and coming-soon — each drawn from one catalogue entry, so adding a page is a five-line change. Slate/amber shell.

templates.title: Styloviz Real Estate Template
templates.description: A working property portal — map-and-list search with live filters, a listing page with gallery, floor-plan comparison, price history and a mortgage estimator, side-by-side compare, saved searches and an agent pipeline. Olive/brass shell, mock-or-live data switch.

templates.title: Styloviz File Manager Template
templates.description: A working drive — folder tree, breadcrumb, list and grid views, sort with folders first and natural number order, multi-select with move/delete, a recoverable Trash, and a move that refuses to detach a folder into its own subtree.

templates.title: Styloviz Help Desk Template
templates.description: A working support desk — a ticket queue sorted by how much SLA time is left, first-response and resolution clocks that pause while a ticket waits on the customer, agent assignment, canned replies filled from the ticket, and a threaded conversation with internal notes. Sky/amber shell.

templates.title: Styloviz HRMS / People Template
templates.description: People operations — a directory whose employment status is derived from hire and end dates, an org chart built from manager links that lists anyone it cannot place, leave counted in half-days across working days, attendance from an append-only punch ledger, and payroll drafts that freeze when posted. Ink-navy/emerald shell, mock-or-live data switch.

templates.title: Styloviz Invoicing Template
templates.description: Invoicing and light accounting for a studio or agency — invoices with gap-free numbering, part payments and void with a reason; quotes that convert to invoices; expenses with receipts; recurring schedules; client statements; a double-entry ledger derived from every document; and a client portal with a mocked card payment. Not certified accounting software; tax rates are examples.

templates.title: Styloviz Launch Template
templates.description: A SaaS marketing site — hero with a working sign-up, feature grid, a numbered how-it-works, social proof, an FAQ accordion and a pricing page whose annual prices, savings and discount badge are derived from one monthly figure per plan. Fuchsia/indigo shell, scroll reveals that degrade to nothing without JavaScript.

templates.title: Styloviz LMS / Course Platform Template
templates.description: A course platform — lesson progress is the union of the stretches actually watched, so skipping to the end credits nothing; grades are weighted over what has been marked, with the floor and ceiling beside the average; marks freeze at submission; and the instructor studio shows what a curriculum change does to enrolled learners before it saves. Oxford-teal/saffron shell, mock-or-live data switch.

templates.title: Styloviz Mail Template
templates.description: A working mailbox — folders with live unread counts, label filters, search, a resizable list/reading-pane split that remembers where you put it, bulk archive and mark-read, and a rich-text compose window that lands in Sent.

templates.title: Styloviz Portfolio Template
templates.description: A design studio's public site — editorial masonry work index with discipline filters, long-form case studies with before/after comparison and a plate lightbox, a studio page whose figures are counted from the catalogue, and a contact form that arrives knowing which work the visitor opened. Ink-and-bone shell, rose accent, mock-or-live data switch.

templates.title: Styloviz POS / Inventory Template
templates.description: A point of sale and inventory app — barcode scanning into a live basket, four tenders with split payments and change, held tickets, printable receipts with a Code 128 barcode, refunds priced from the receipt, and purchase orders. On-hand stock is the sum of an append-only movement ledger, never a stored number. Graphite/emerald shell, mock-or-live data switch.

templates.title: Styloviz Project Management Template
templates.description: A working project workspace — a sprint board where the column is the status, a gantt timeline that previews a drag before it is saved (dependents move, Apply or Undo), a ranked backlog with a dependency editor that refuses cycles, and per-person weekly load. Critical path, float and blocked are computed, never stored. Cyan/sky shell, mock-or-live data switch.

templates.title: Styloviz Store E-Commerce Template
templates.description: A complete e-commerce storefront — home, category (PLP), product (PDP), search, compare, cart, multi-step checkout, order tracking, account and auth. Light-first "Fresh Market" emerald shell with signal-based cart / wishlist / catalog state.

templates.title: Styloviz AI Support Site Template
templates.description: A customer-facing help centre with an AI assistant — search as you type, topics, articles with section anchors, and an assistant on every page that answers only from the help articles, cites the sections it used, says when it does not know and hands off to a person as a ticket. In demo mode it retrieves from the bundled articles — no model, nothing sent.

templates.title: Styloviz Trading Desk Template
templates.description: A trading desk over a seeded, simulated market — markets with a watchlist and sparklines, a stock chart with SMA, EMA, Bollinger, RSI and MACD, an order book and an order ticket (market, limit or stop), open orders and fills, a portfolio with P&L, a wallet and price alerts. Simulated prices — no real exchange, no custody, not financial advice.

import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component } from '@angular/core'; import { SvIconComponent, registerSvIcons } from '@styloviz/icons'; import { bellIcon } from '@styloviz/icons/glyph/bell'; import { checkCircleIcon } from '@styloviz/icons/glyph/check-circle'; import { databaseIcon } from '@styloviz/icons/glyph/database'; let nextId = 0; /** * A bento grid of five feature cards in varying spans — a wide card and a * narrow one on top, three equal cards below — each with a small * Tailwind-drawn visual. One column on mobile. */ @Component({ selector: 'app-feature-bento', standalone: true, changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush, imports: [SvIconComponent], template: `

Platform

One ledger for every revenue question

  • @for (bar of revenueBars; track $index) {
    }

    Live revenue, reconciled nightly

    MRR, ARR and ARPA rebuilt from the invoice ledger every night, with yesterday's numbers frozen for comparison.

  • 114%

    Net retention at a glance

    This year's revenue from last year's customers, expansion included.

  • @for (source of sources; track source) { {{ source }} }

    Twelve billing sources

    Stripe, Paddle, Chargebee, Recurly or a Postgres table you already have.

  • Churn up 1.8 pts in the EMEA cohort
    October books closed · 0 variances

    Alerts worth reading

    Thresholds on any metric, sent to Slack or email — never more than one a day.

  • GET /v1/metrics/mrr
→ {{ apiSample }}

    The same numbers, over an API

    Pull any figure into your warehouse or product with one authenticated call.

`, }) export class FeatureBentoComponent { protected readonly icons = registerSvIcons([bellIcon, checkCircleIcon, databaseIcon]); protected readonly uid = `feature-bento-${nextId++}`; protected readonly sources = ['Stripe', 'Paddle', 'Chargebee', 'Recurly', 'Postgres'] as const; protected readonly apiSample = '{ "mrr": 482190, "currency": "USD" }'; protected readonly revenueBars: readonly string[] = [ 'h-[30%]', 'h-[34%]', 'h-[33%]', 'h-[40%]', 'h-[44%]', 'h-[42%]', 'h-[51%]', 'h-[55%]', 'h-[60%]', 'h-[58%]', 'h-[66%]', 'h-[72%]', 'h-[78%]', 'h-[84%]', 'h-[92%]', ]; }

import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, model, output } from '@angular/core'; import { SvPricingTableComponent, type SvPricingBilling, type SvPricingFeature, type SvPricingPlan, type SvPricingPlanSelect, } from '@styloviz/commerce'; /** * Plan comparison — a real `` of features by plan, grouped under row * headings, with the price row and a monthly / annual toggle on top. * * Each feature's `values` is keyed by plan id: `true`, `false` or a short text. * Bind `(planSelect)` to start checkout. */ @Component({ selector: 'app-pricing-comparison', standalone: true, changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush, imports: [SvPricingTableComponent], template: `

Compare every plan

Every plan reconciles against your invoices. The difference is how many sources, entities and people you bring.

`, }) export class PricingComparisonComponent { /** The billing period shown; two-way bindable. */ readonly billing = model('monthly'); /** The chosen plan and the period it was chosen under. */ readonly planSelect = output(); protected readonly plans: readonly SvPricingPlan[] = [ { id: 'starter', name: 'Starter', price: { monthly: 49 } }, { id: 'growth', name: 'Growth', price: { monthly: 149 }, highlighted: true }, { id: 'scale', name: 'Scale', price: 'Custom', cta: { label: 'Talk to sales' } }, ]; protected readonly features: readonly SvPricingFeature[] = [ { id: 'sources', group: 'Data', label: 'Billing sources', values: { starter: '1', growth: '3', scale: 'Unlimited' } }, { id: 'history', group: 'Data', label: 'Historical import', values: { starter: '12 months', growth: '5 years', scale: 'All time' } }, { id: 'fx', group: 'Data', label: 'Multi-currency roll-up', values: { starter: false, growth: true, scale: true } }, { id: 'mrr', group: 'Reporting', label: 'MRR, churn and LTV', values: { starter: true, growth: true, scale: true } }, { id: 'cohorts', group: 'Reporting', label: 'Cohorts and retention', values: { starter: false, growth: true, scale: true } }, { id: 'recon', group: 'Reporting', label: 'Invoice-level reconciliation', values: { starter: false, growth: true, scale: true } }, { id: 'entities', group: 'Reporting', label: 'Multi-entity consolidation', values: { starter: false, growth: false, scale: true } }, { id: 'seats', group: 'Team & security', label: 'Team members', values: { starter: '3', growth: '15', scale: 'Unlimited' } }, { id: 'sso', group: 'Team & security', label: 'SAML SSO', values: { starter: false, growth: false, scale: true } }, { id: 'audit', group: 'Team & security', label: 'Audit log', values: { starter: false, growth: '90 days', scale: '7 years' } }, { id: 'support', group: 'Support', label: 'Support', values: { starter: 'Email', growth: 'Priority', scale: 'Dedicated analyst' } }, ]; }
